places.name: 金龍ラーメン 道頓堀店 (Kinryu Ramen Dotonbori)
places.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: wheat noodles in a pork-bone broth with a secret tare.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: pork-bone and chicken-feet broth, chashu.
places.hours_raw: Open 24 hours, every day (Tabelog; may change). Number tag: collect your bowl when called.
places.neighborhood: Dotonbori 1-chōme, under the giant dragon on the canal side — 5 min from Namba Stn exit 14
places.cuisine: 24-hour Minami ramen under the giant dragon · pork-bone and chicken-feet tonkotsu · ramen or chashu ramen only (ramen ¥900) · free kimchi, garlic and garlic chives · tatami seating
places.notes: [Ramen · the 24-hour bowl under Dotonbori's giant dragon] Minami's famous all-night ramen stand, known for the huge dragon sculpture over the shop. There are only two choices, ramen (¥900 in October 2026, after a ¥200 rise) or chashu ramen, in a tonkotsu the listing describes as rich, made from pork bones and chicken feet with a secret tare. Most 2026 diners found it surprisingly light, with medium-thin, slightly curly noodles. The fun is the free kimchi, garlic and garlic chives to load in. Take a number and carry your bowl from the counter to tatami or counter seats. Queues are mostly overseas visitors late at night but move fast. Opinions vary: a nostalgic finish to a night out for many, lukewarm and thin for one critic.

chef_bio.background: Multi-shop Minami brand (a reviewer notes the main shop is being rebuilt).
chef_bio.specialty: Tonkotsu ramen with free kimchi and garlic chives.

anecdotes.text: "The broth is pork bone-based but quite light. The noodles are thin, and the added garlic chives and kimchi gave it a nice spicy kick." — October 2026, ramen ¥900 after a night out.
"I remember it being JPY 600 back in my twenties, but now it's JPY 900." — October 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: 金龍ラーメン 道頓堀店、大阪市中央区道頓堀1-7-26、なんば駅14番出口徒歩5分、24時間営業、予約不可、カウンター・座敷、子ども可。店の紹介: 巨大な龍のオブジェで知られるミナミの24時間営業の名物店、豚骨と鶏ガラ(もみじ)を煮込んだ濃厚豚骨に秘伝のタレ、自家製のストレート麺、キムチ・にんにく・ニラ入れ放題。2026年の口コミ: インバウンド客が多い、中細のやや縮れ麺、醤油ベースの豚骨で塩気は控えめ・ぬるかったとの声、メニューはラーメンとチャーシューメンのみ、あっさりした豚骨、無料のキムチとニラが辛い、胡椒が合う、ラーメン900円(200円値上げ、20代の頃は600円)、本店は工事中、鶏と豚のブレンドで切れのある味、ラー油の香り、番号札で呼ばれて自分で運ぶ、回転が早い。

noodles.notes: House-made noodles (listing); diners describe them as medium-thin with a slight curl and lower water content (2026).

ramen.signature_bowl: ラーメン (ramen) — ¥900 in October 2026; チャーシューメン also offered.
ramen.chashu: Two kinds, sliced and cubed, on the sweet side (one 2026 review).
ramen.pantheon: Dotonbori after midnight: a light pork-bone bowl under the giant dragon, made your own with free kimchi, garlic and garlic chives, carried to the tatami on a number tag.

richness: "The broth is pork bone-based but quite light"; another: "surprisingly light" (https://tabelog.com/en/osaka/A2701/A270202/27001495/dtlrvwlst/B536645572/); the listing itself calls it rich.
oiliness: "Surprisingly light even after finishing my meal"; "lacks richness, it has a sharp finish" (https://tabelog.com/en/osaka/A2701/A270202/27001495/dtlrvwlst/B536670125/).
clarity: "The broth was a light tonkotsu" — a pork-bone broth; no source says it is clear.
tare_strength: "The seasoning is also sharp"; another found it "on the milder side in terms of saltiness" (https://tabelog.com/en/osaka/A2701/A270202/27001495/dtlrvwlst/B409489189/).
noodle_firmness: "Medium-thin with a slight curl, cooked just right… a lower water content"; the listing calls them firm.
aroma_punch: "The smell of tonkotsu broth was strong"; free kimchi and garlic chives add spice (https://tabelog.com/en/osaka/A2701/A270202/27001495/dtlrvwlst/B536384620/).

cultural_comfort.note: Number tag; carry your own bowl.

places.name: どうとんぼり神座 道頓堀店 (Dotonbori Kamukura)
places.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: wheat noodles; the broth recipe is secret, and sides include kara-age and gyoza.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: pork slices and soft-boiled egg on the ramen; the secret broth is not described.
places.hours_raw: Daily 10:00–08:00 next morning (Tabelog). Order on the table tablet.
places.neighborhood: Dotonbori 1-chōme (1-7-25), next to Kinryū Ramen — 5 min from Namba Stn
places.cuisine: Dotonbori-born light ramen chain · secret broth with crunchy napa cabbage and fine-sliced pork · "delicious ramen" ¥850 · small chashu and soft-egg ramen ¥1,270 · seasonal hot-and-sour noodles · open 22 h
places.notes: [Ramen · Kamukura's light cabbage ramen on its home street] The Dotonbori shop of Kamukura, now a nationwide chain that long-time fans still call a local treasure, with 71 seats and open from 10:00 to 08:00 the next morning. The signature "delicious ramen" (¥850 in October 2026) is a light, gently sweet, secret-recipe broth heaped with crunchy napa cabbage and thin-sliced pork. The most popular version adds small chashu and a soft-boiled egg (¥1,270); there's kara-age (¥430), gyoza and seasonal bowls such as a hot-and-sour soup with Zhenjiang vinegar and cilantro. Order on the table tablet. It's easy to eat and veg-heavy, though one diner found it too salty, and the noodles are soft, almost udon-like.

chef_bio.origin: Dotonbori 1-chōme; a 2026 reviewer calls this the main branch
chef_bio.background: National chain (kamukura.co.jp).

anecdotes.text: "Every time I visit, I ponder the mystery of the secret broth while enjoying the crisp napa cabbage and finely sliced pork that are its signature features." — September 2026, a fan since student days 35 years ago.

"I ordered the Most Popular Small Chashu and Soft-Boiled Egg Ramen (JPY 1270) along with Kara-age (JPY 430) using the tablet at my table." — September 2026, a first visit to what the reviewer calls the main branch.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: どうとんぼり神座 道頓堀店、大阪市中央区道頓堀1-7-25、なんば駅徒歩5分、71席、毎日10:00〜翌8:00、予約不可、公式サイト kamukura.co.jp。2026年の口コミ: 独特のあっさりスープに白菜、セットは大盛りで満腹、塩気が強すぎたとの声、本店と呼んで訪問、小チャーシュー煮玉子ラーメン1,270円と唐揚げ430円をタブレットで、旨みと甘みのスープとシャキシャキの白菜、観光客で賑わう、店舗により副菜が違う、隣の金龍の行列の横で空いていた、おいしいラーメン850円とハイボール430円、全国チェーン、35年前の学生時代から、秘伝のスープ・白菜・薄切り豚肉、大阪では女性客が多い、うどんのような麺、季節の酸辣湯麺(鎮江香酢・パクチー・蒸し鶏)と餃子。

noodles.notes: Soft noodles "with a texture similar to udon" (October 2026); another diner found them "nothing special".

ramen.signature_bowl: おいしいラーメン (delicious ramen) — ¥850 in October 2026; 小チャーシュー煮玉子ラーメン ¥1,270 (September 2026).
ramen.chashu: Thin-sliced pork in the bowl; small chashu on the popular version.
ramen.pantheon: Dotonbori's gentle bowl: a light, faintly sweet secret broth buried under crunchy napa cabbage and thin pork, served nearly round the clock and loved precisely for not being heavy.

richness: "The ramen is loaded with vegetables, and the broth is light and easy to drink"; "light, sweet flavor" (https://tabelog.com/en/osaka/A2701/A270202/27001562/dtlrvwlst/B536755192/).
oiliness: "An easy-to-eat type of ramen without heaviness."
clarity: No source describes the broth's look; placed mid-scale from repeated "light and easy to drink" descriptions.

aroma_punch: "A healthy ramen with a gentle flavor."

places.name: 金久右衛門 道頓堀店 (Kinkuemon Dotonbori)
places.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: wheat noodles in soy-sauce (shoyu) broths.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: chicken stock with seafood, chashu.
places.hours_raw: Mon–Thu 11:00–08:00 next morning; Fri, Sat, Sun and holiday eves open 24 hours; closes early if sold out; open year-round (Tabelog). Ticket machine outside.
places.neighborhood: Dotonbori 1-chōme (1-4-17), a little off the main strip next to Kinryū — 5 min from Namba Stn
places.cuisine: Osaka Black shoyu ramen · jet-black soy broth with chicken stock and seafood umami · King Shoyu and clear Kinjou Shoyu · thin or thick noodles · extra noodles · ¥1,000–1,200 · open through the night
places.notes: [Ramen · Osaka Black, the jet-black shoyu, through the night] Since 2011 the Dotonbori branch of Kinkuemon, a shop famous for sharp shoyu ramen, set just off the main strip by the Kinryū queue. It has 41 seats over two floors and is open through the night (24 hours Friday to Sunday). The signature Osaka Black is a glossy jet-black soy broth with chicken stock and a seafood edge, buttery chicken-fat aroma and a faintly bitter soy finish. Choose thin noodles (most recommend them) or thick, topped with chashu, menma, green onion and a soft egg; extra noodles are extra. Also on the menu: Red Shoyu, King Shoyu, and Osaka Kinjou Shoyu, a clear chicken-and-light-soy broth that one 34-visit regular likes at 8 am. Buy a ticket at the machine outside; garlic on request. ¥1,000–1,200 a bowl; a few found it pricey for tourists or the service curt.

chef_bio.background: Branch of the Kinkuemon brand (king-emon-dotonbori.com).

anecdotes.text: "The aroma of the rich black soy sauce combined with seafood in the jet-black broth was absolutely delightful! The straight, chewy thin noodles soaked up the black soy sauce soup." — October 2026, Osaka Black ¥1,200 at 5 am.
"The clear broth, made with chicken stock and light soy sauce, is perfect for a refreshing morning ramen." — September 2026, 34th visit, Kinjō Shoyu.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: 金久右衛門 道頓堀店、大阪市中央区道頓堀1-4-17、41席(1階カウンター23、地下カウンター6・テーブル12)、月〜木11:00〜翌8:00、金土日祝前日24時間営業、売り切れ次第終了、年中無休、2011年12月29日開店、公式サイト king-emon-dotonbori.com。2026年の口コミ(英語版): 34回目の朝ラーメンで「Osaka Kinjou Shoyu」(鶏ガラと薄口醤油の澄んだスープ、細麺、にんにく、ねぎ、メンマ、半熟の味玉)、「Osaka Black」の大盛りと豚丼は2,000円超で観光客向けに高いとの声、店前の券売機、「Osaka Black」味玉なし1,000円、艶のある黒、ほろ苦い醤油と鶏油のバターのような香り、細麺がおすすめ、替え玉あり、基本1,200円、スタッフの対応がそっけないとの声、「Red Shoyu」、「King Shoyu」、豚骨の香りを感じたとの声、魚介の旨みのある「Osaka Black」、金龍の隣の行列のない店、朝5時に「Osaka Black」1,200円・細麺かため。

noodles.notes: Choice of thin (most recommended; straight and chewy) or thick noodles; firmness can be ordered (2026).

ramen.chashu: Chashu with menma, green onion and a seasoned soft egg.
ramen.pantheon: Minami's night-owl shoyu: a glossy jet-black soy broth with chicken stock and a seafood edge, buttery chicken fat, faintly bitter soy, and thin straight noodles that drink it all in.

richness: "Rich flavor with seafood umami… the broth has a delightful balance of soy sauce and seafood flavors, providing a refreshing taste."

noodle_firmness: "Thin noodles and a firm texture… The straight, chewy thin noodles."
aroma_punch: "The aroma of the rich black soy sauce combined with seafood in the jet-black broth was absolutely delightful!"

cultural_comfort.note: Ticket machine outside.

places.name: らぁ麺 はやし田 道頓堀店 (Ramen Hayashida Dotonbori)
places.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: whole-wheat-flour noodles in shoyu, paitan and tsukemen bowls.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: duck and Daisen-chicken broth, chashu, egg.
places.hours_raw: Daily 11:00–23:00 (Tabelog; may change). Ticket machine at the entrance.
places.neighborhood: Dotonbori Kankō Bldg B1F, right under the Glico sign by Ebisubashi — 3 min from Namba Stn
places.cuisine: Tokyo Shinjuku shoyu ramen brand under the Glico sign · duck and Daisen-chicken clear shoyu (¥900; special ¥1,200) · chicken paitan · tsukemen · seasonal yuzu cold ramen · TKG and oyakodon sides
places.notes: [Ramen · Tokyo's Hayashida right under the Glico sign] The first Kansai branch, opened in 2022, of Ramen Hayashida, a Shinjuku shop famous for queues and run by INGS Co. It's a 16-seat counter one floor below the Glico running man, southwest of Ebisubashi. The signature is a clear shoyu broth of duck and Daisen-dori chicken (¥900; the special with a "Maximum Koitama" egg ¥1,200) on firm, thin whole-wheat noodles, with pork-shoulder and chicken-breast chashu. There's also a creamy chicken paitan, a refined tsukemen (special ¥1,250), mazesoba with truffle-sauce egg, and summer yuzu cold ramen (¥950) with yuzu jelly. Add a TKG or oyakodon (¥350–400). Buy tickets at the entrance machine. Light and quick, with friendly staff: a handy fast lunch when Minami's big names are queuing.

chef_bio.origin: Opened 11 February 2022 (Tabelog); first Kansai branch of the Shinjuku shop (2026 reviews)
chef_bio.background: Brand of INGS Co., Ltd. (Shinjuku); franchise (July 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: "'ralamen hayashida' is a brand of INGS Co., Ltd., headquartered in Shinjuku, Tokyo, and this is their first franchise location in the Kansai region… right under the towering 20-meter 'Dotonbori Glico Sign'." — July 2026, shoyu ramen ¥900.

"Special Shoyu Ramen (JPY 1,200)… firm, thin noodles made with whole wheat flour, topped with a rich flavored egg made from the premium 'Maximum Koitama' brand, and tender chicken chashu." — October 2026.

places.name: ラー麺ずんどう屋 道頓堀店 (Ramen Zundoya Dotonbori)
places.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: wheat noodles in a pork-bone soy broth; sides include gyoza and kara-age.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: pork-bone broth with back fat, pork-belly chashu.
places.hours_raw: Open 24 hours, every day (Tabelog; may change). Ticket machine in front; seating upstairs.
places.neighborhood: Sōemonchō 7-6, just east of Ebisubashi — 3 min from Namba Stn
places.cuisine: Himeji-born back-fat tonkotsu shoyu chain · motomi ramen ¥860, ajitama ¥980, all-toppings ¥1,360 · pick back-fat level (light to extra rich) and thin or curly noodles · table pickled ginger, garlic, takana · 24 h
places.notes: [Ramen · Himeji back-fat tonkotsu, round the clock] The Dotonbori branch, opened 31 October 2025, of Zundōya, a Himeji-founded chain with over a hundred shops (about 106 in Japan and 4 in Shanghai, per a December 2025 visitor). It sits just east of Ebisubashi and is open 24 hours. The broth is pork bone with a slightly creamy soy seasoning and as much back fat as you choose (light, regular, rich or extra rich). Noodles are house-made: ultra-thin straight (recommended) or curly. The motomi (original) ramen is ¥860, ajitama ¥980, and all-toppings up to ¥1,360; summer brought a cold ramen with grated daikon. Season at the table with pepper, pickled ginger, garlic, chili oil, sesame and takana. Buy a ticket outside (transit IC accepted) and head upstairs. A Kansai-friendly tonkotsu with a hint of sweetness.

chef_bio.background: Chain founded in Himeji (zundouya.com).

anecdotes.text: "The broth is made from pork bone, featuring a slightly creamy soy sauce soup with added back fat… The noodles are house-made, straight, and thin, providing a pleasant texture with just the right amount of chewiness." — October 2025, opening day.
"The broth is rich and fatty, yet not overwhelming, packed with meaty flavors… The firm noodles pair perfectly with the large seaweed." — May 2026, late night.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: ラー麺ずんどう屋 道頓堀店、大阪市中央区宗右衛門町7-6、なんば駅から277m、24時間営業、予約不可、2025年10月31日開店、公式サイト zundouya.com。口コミ(2025年10月〜2026年9月): 姫路に本店のチェーンの新店、元味らーめん860円(豚骨醤油に背脂)、極細ストレート麺2.00mm、豚バラのチャーシュー、ねぎ、海苔、メニュー(チャーシュー1,400円、味玉980円、ねぎ980円、HOT930円、全部のせ1,360円、野菜1,060円、バターコーンなど)、替え玉150円、背脂は4段階(あっさり・ふつう・こってり・こってり増し)、細麺か縮れ麺を選べる、卓上に胡椒・紅生姜・にんにく・ラー油・ごま・高菜、国内106店と上海4店、全部のせチャーシューと祭りセット(餃子と唐揚げ)、宗右衛門町、戎橋の東、関西向けの姫路豚骨でほんのり甘い、深夜にこってりでもくどくない、硬めの麺と大きな海苔、券売機で交通系ICで冷やしおろしらーめん960円、2階の店内。

noodles.notes: House-made ultra-thin straight noodles (2.00 mm), or curly noodles on request (2025–26).

ramen.signature_bowl: 元味らーめん (motomi ramen) — ¥860; 味玉らーめん ¥980 (October 2025).
ramen.chashu: Pork-belly chashu, thick and tender on the all-toppings bowl.
ramen.pantheon: Himeji's answer to Hakata on Dotonbori's east side: a pork-bone soy broth whose back fat you set yourself, ultra-thin house noodles, and a table of ginger, garlic and takana, all night.

richness: "A rich pork bone-based soy sauce broth with added back fat."
oiliness: "The broth is rich and fatty, yet not overwhelming"; back fat chosen from four levels (https://tabelog.com/en/osaka/A2701/A270202/27152648/dtlrvwlst/B516387909/).

places.notes: [Gyoza · Osaka Ohsho's main shop on Dotonbori] The Dotonbori main shop of the Osaka Ohsho gyoza chain: 189 seats over two floors, with back tables upstairs looking over the canal, and touch-panel ordering and payment. The gyoza are the reason to come: juicy enough that one fan skips the dipping sauce. Sets pair them with fried rice (generous chashu), kara-age or a hoikoro set meal (¥1,320 with gyoza). The menu also has mapo tofu, green-pepper beef, chilled Chinese noodles and the punchy lu-su fried rice (¥1,200 as a gyoza set). Plain gyoza are ¥700 here, which one visitor found steep, and the service at the flagship disappointed another. Fast and easy, with a take-out counter.

places.notes: [Ramen · Ichiran's pork-free "no tonkotsu" shop] The one Ichiran operating under its "100% no tonkotsu used" concept: the familiar experience (booth counters with partitions, an order sheet, Arita-ware bowls) but a broth developed from beef bones and chicken, so people who can't eat pork can have Ichiran. Diners call it surprisingly rich and creamy, very like tonkotsu, with the signature red secret sauce. One found it lacked real tonkotsu's punch. Instead of pork chashu there's sweet-spicy seasoned beef (gyūyarō), plus soft salted egg, extra garlic and a matcha pudding. The 100% pork-free ramen was ¥1,280 in July 2026. Expect 30–80-minute waits (scan a QR code and return); a 9 am weekday arrival walked straight in. 25 seats, many overseas visitors.

places.notes: [Ramen · Kinryū's standing yatai on Midōsuji] One of Kinryū's several Namba shops, under a big dragon sign on Midōsuji. It's done in a food-stall style: buy a ticket, then mostly stand at the counter or use the tables by the pavement, with the kitchen in full view. Like the Dotonbori shop, it serves a simple tonkotsu ramen (¥900) that most find lighter than its strong pork aroma suggests, plus free kimchi, garlic and garlic chives to pile on. A seven-time visitor praises the old-school simplicity of a shop that has served for over 35 years; a first-timer was underwhelmed. Turnover is quick and it's open 24 hours, handy at 2 am. Smoking is allowed (Tabelog).

places.notes: [Ramen · Zundōya by Ebisubashi, all night] A bright, busy 24-hour branch, since 2021, of Himeji's back-fat tonkotsu chain Zundōya, a few steps south of Ebisubashi. The chain's site says its broth simmers pork heads, backbones and whole bones over high heat for about ten hours. Diners describe it as rich and creamy yet not overly heavy, deepened by back fat. You choose thin or curly house-made noodles, the back fat (light to extra) and firmness (soft to very firm). An ajitama large was ¥1,070 in 2026, with wood-ear mushroom extra. Regulars add the spicy HOT version with bean sprouts, half fried rice and spicy takana, or a summer chilled ramen. Popular with a younger crowd after drinks.

places.notes: [Ramen · Kamukura on Midōsuji] A newer Kamukura (opened January 2025) on Midōsuji beside Kinryū, open until 7 am on Friday and Saturday nights. Its heavy entrance door may be why it's often the one shop without a queue. The "delicious ramen" (¥820 in October 2026) is the chain's light pork-and-vegetable broth, not tonkotsu, sweet from crunchy napa cabbage, with pork belly, thick bouncy chashu and chewy medium-thin straight noodles. Sets add half fried rice and gyoza (¥1,370) or kara-age, and there are seasonal spicy-sour noodles (with a black-vinegar version) and a chilled ramen. Help yourself to garlic chives and chili.

places.cuisine: Kamukura’s Sennichimae counter shop · light, slightly sweet broth with plenty of napa cabbage · vegetable ramen ¥1,110 · ramen, kara-age and rice set ~¥1,350 · cold pork-shabu ume-shiso ramen (summer) · open 22 h
places.notes: [Ramen · Kamukura on the Sennichimae side] A 40-seat, counter-only Kamukura across from Ichiran on Dotonbori's Sennichimae end, open 9:00 to 7:00 the next morning. The narrow room has a one-way flow, so it's not for lingering. Fans call it Osaka soul food from before the chain went national: a light, slightly sweet, almost Western-style broth loaded with napa cabbage, the kind people want after drinking instead of heavy tonkotsu. One diner insists it tastes different from other branches. Try the vegetable ramen (¥1,110) or the ramen, kara-age and rice set (about ¥1,350); summer brought a cold pork-shabu ramen with ume, shiso and grated daikon (¥1,250). Buy a ticket at the machine out front. Service can be flat late at night, and one summer visitor found the cabbage bitter.

places.notes: [Chinese · build-your-own malatang in Shinsaibashi] A busy branch of the Yang Guo Fu malatang chain, open since 2022, with 31 seats and queues even mid-afternoon. With tongs you fill a bowl from a spread of vegetables, mushrooms, mountain jellyfish, wood ear, meat, squid, quail eggs, fish cakes and noodles (including vermicelli). The cashier weighs it to set the price, and you pick the spice level and broth. One diner prefers the tomato broth, which tastes almost like tomato ramen; another tamed the heat with sesame sauce. Even spice level one is quite spicy. Choose and pay before you join the seating line. Staff are largely from overseas, so Japanese may be limited.

places.notes: [Gyoza izakaya · late-night gyoza and a Jirō-style bowl in Minami-Senba] A casual 34-seat gyoza izakaya, since 2021, with tables and three private rooms, open late and busy with overseas visitors. Order Osaka-style gyoza, dressed in sauce, mayonnaise, green onion and bonito flakes, or shiso, garlic or plain gyoza, with dashimaki and shrimp chilli-mayo. There's also a Jirō-style ramen (¥1,100): a rich pork-bone miso broth with thick, flat, high-hydration noodles under pork belly, cabbage and bean sprouts. Set meals are cheap (ginger pork ¥900), and dishes come fast. One diner found the food more "not bad" than delicious. Smoking is allowed inside. Tabelog's listed hours (18:00–11:00) don't match the lunch visits reviewers describe, so check.

places.notes: [Ramen · beef-bone white soup, all night] An 18-seat counter, since 2011, three doors east of Mitsudera, serving Makotoya's beef-bone "gyū-paitan" around the clock. Regulars go when they want something that isn't miso, shoyu or shio. The beef broth is rich and smooth but not heavy, with a beefy aroma and sweetness that clings to thin noodles (choose your firmness). The favourite is the spicy red version with soft-boiled egg, chashu, wood ear, bean sprouts and green onion in a red bowl. Doctor it at the table with fresh garlic, garlic chips, pickled ginger and white sesame. Morioka cold noodles were ¥1,010 in August 2026. Buy a ticket at the machine by the door; one visitor found the street queue was for the malatang shop nearby.

It makes its own gluten-free sauces, including soy sauce and ponzu. Celiac reviewers on FMGF (14 recent ratings) describe staff who confirm gluten-free at the table, swap single items in a set and change the grill between gluten-free and regular dishes. One 2025 diner was brought regular sauces by a different server and caught it by asking. It is not a gluten-free kitchen. Say you are celiac when you book and again when you sit down.

places.cuisine: Matsusaka-beef yakiniku · grill it yourself · house gluten-free soy sauce and ponzu · every dish can be made GF with notice · set courses and omakase · shoes off, semi-private tables
places.notes: [Yakiniku · gluten-free Matsusaka beef by Hōzenji] The "hanare" annex of Yakiniku M's Hōzenji branch: a second-floor room off Hōzenji Yokochō where you take your shoes off at the door, with seven tables, six of them semi-private and one a private room. Matsusaka beef is grilled at the table. It is a celiac favourite: the restaurant says any dish can be made gluten-free with notice, and it makes its own gluten-free soy sauce, ponzu and dipping sauces, so the marinated beef and garlic rice can be done too. Celiac reviewers rave about the staff ("Best GF meal we've had in Japan"). It is pricey: one diner put it at ¥8,800–12,000 a head, another had the ¥12,000 premium course. When it was full, staff walked guests to another branch nearby. Book and mention gluten-free when you do.

chef_bio.background: Part of the Matsusakagyu Yakiniku M group of Osaka yakiniku restaurants (official site); one FMGF reviewer counted four locations.

anecdotes.text: "I explained I am a coeliac and also have a garlic intolerance and they were able to substitute sauces and provide recommendations." — FMGF review, October 2026.
"After countless yakiniku meals, this is the first time I've ever been able to have GF sauce at one." — FMGF review, June 2026; the manager's reply credits "our homemade gluten-free sauces".
"They gave me gluten free soy sauce to dip and swapped out the grill between gluten free and gluten dishes." — FMGF review, 2024.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式(matsusaka-projects.com): 松阪牛焼肉M 法善寺店 はなれ、大阪市中央区難波1-5-24 だるまビル2F、06-6211-2904。2026年6月21日から平日12:00〜15:00(L.O.14:30)・17:00〜23:00(L.O.22:30)、土日祝12:00〜23:00、定休日なし。入口で靴を脱ぐ、テーブル7(半個室6、個室1)、「グルテンフリー」のタグ。FindMeGlutenFree: 店の説明「グルテンフリーは事前予約が必要。すべての料理をグルテンフリーにできる」、予約時に申告を。セリアック病の客の口コミ: 自家製のグルテンフリーのたれ、醤油、ポン酢、席でも何度も確認、網を替える、別のスタッフが通常のたれを持ってきたことが一度(2025年)、1人8,800〜12,000円、プレミアムコース12,000円、満席のとき近くの別店舗に案内。マネージャーの返信: ヴィーガンメニューもある。

cultural_comfort.note: FMGF reviewers describe English-speaking staff used to overseas celiac guests; book online or by phone.

gf_cross_contamination.text: "One time a different waitres brought new sauces, which were not gf. But I asked before I ate them…" — FMGF review, 2025.
A shared yakiniku kitchen: regular soy sauce and marinades are in use alongside the gluten-free versions.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Regular soy sauce and sauces contain wheat; ask for the house gluten-free soy sauce, ponzu and dipping sauces.

staff_allergy_handling.text: "Advance reservation required for gluten-free dining. All food menu items can be prepared gluten-free upon request." — the restaurant, on FMGF.
"Advance notice allows us to prepare gluten-free alternatives whenever possible and take extra precautions to minimize cross-contact." — the restaurant, on FMGF.

positives.text: Celiac reviewers repeatedly report no symptoms; staff ask about allergies on arrival and confirm gluten-free dishes at the table.
The official branch page tags the restaurant グルテンフリー (gluten-free).

places.name: 源氏蕎麦 法善寺参道店 (Genji Soba)
places.gf_detail: The soba is hand-made from 100% buckwheat (juwari). The menu marks gluten-free dishes, and celiac reviewers on FindMeGlutenFree (101 recent ratings) describe a separate, celiac-labelled section. On the official menu, the tempura is made with buckwheat and rice flour and "Fried in a Dedicated Gluten-Free Fryer". Gluten-free dipping sauce and soy sauce are made for gluten-free orders, while the regular sauces are also in use, so ask. FMGF flags that it is NOT a dedicated gluten-free facility. Several reviewers say the celiac-safe tempura and menu are dinner only. Staff ask whether you are celiac. Tell them, and reserve the set courses ahead.
places.vegan_detail: The set courses note: "Gluten-Free & Vegan options are available upon advance request." There is a vegan soba on the à la carte menu, but in September 2026 a reviewer was asked whether egg was OK after ordering it, so it may only be vegetarian. Ask about the dashi and egg.
places.hours_raw: 11:30–21:30 (L.O. 21:30), break 14:30–17:00; closed some Wednesdays (水曜不定休) (official site). Lunch and dinner set courses by reservation, upstairs. Reviewers say the celiac-safe tempura is dinner only. The original shop at Namba 4-5-8 is closed for now; this Hōzenji Sandō shop opened in March 2026.
places.neighborhood: Namba 1-2-19 on the Hōzenji Sandō approach, a stone-paved lane off Dotonbori — 7 min from Namba Stn
places.cuisine: 100% buckwheat soba, hand-cut in the window · cold zaru and hot soba · prawn and vegetable tempura from a dedicated GF fryer · beef and duck soba · lunch and dinner set courses (¥3,300 / ¥4,800) · since 1929
places.notes: [Soba · 100% buckwheat and gluten-free tempura on Hōzenji Sandō] A soba house founded in 1929 that moved in March 2026 into a new shop on the stone-paved Hōzenji approach; the old shop is closed for now. The noodles are hand-made from 100% buckwheat (you can watch them being cut in the front window), which makes it a celiac favourite. The menu marks gluten-free and celiac-safe dishes, and the prawn and vegetable tempura is made with buckwheat and rice flour in a dedicated gluten-free fryer. The classic order is cold zaru soba with a big wild prawn and vegetable tempura (¥2,950). There are also grated-daikon, yam and Tamba black-bean natto soba, beef and duck soba, a two-soba lunch (¥1,850), and set courses upstairs by reservation. Some find the broth fishy. You order by QR code at the table, and dinner waits can stretch at busy times.

chef_bio.background: Genji Soba ran at Namba 4-5-8; in March 2026 it opened on Hōzenji Sandō, and the new-shop letter is signed 「源氏蕎麦法善寺参道本店 鳥倉 荘一」. The site describes soba-making demonstrations in Melbourne (2023) and Canberra (2024–2026) and soba sold through Takashimaya and other department stores.
chef_bio.philosophy: 「変わらぬ手打ちと、蕎麦本来の味を大切に、日本の文化を食べるお店として」 (new-shop letter, March 2026).

anecdotes.text: "We sat at the bar, where we could watch the food being prepared, while the noodles were being hand made in the front window." — FMGF review, October 2026.
"Celiac-friendly Tempura is available, which has been the only place we've come across in Japan that offers Tempura that's fried separately to be celiac safe." — FMGF review, December 2025.
"The waitress asked me if egg was ok after I order the vegan soba so I think it was just vegetarian." — FMGF review, September 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式(genjisoba.co.jp): 源氏蕎麦、大阪市中央区難波1-2-19 法善寺参道、06-6633-5402、地下鉄なんば駅徒歩7分、11:30〜21:30(L.O.21:30)、14:30〜17:00は休憩、水曜不定休、1,300〜3,000円、禁煙。現在は新店舗(法善寺参道店)で営業、旧店舗(難波4-5-8)はしばらく休業(完全移転ではない)。2026年3月の新店舗のお知らせ、創業1929年、源氏蕎麦法善寺参道本店 鳥倉 荘一。メニュー: お昼の源氏御膳3,300円・夜の源氏御膳4,800円(予約制、2階席、グルテンフリー・ヴィーガンは事前リクエストで対応)、十割ざるそば1,300円、親田大根辛み十割蕎麦1,620円、とろろ十割蕎麦1,920円、丹波黒豆納豆十割蕎麦1,620円、法善寺Aランチ1,850円(十割蕎麦2種、小どんぶり、サラダ、香の物、豆乳プリン)、天然大海老と野菜の天ざる十割蕎麦2,950円(蕎麦粉と米粉の衣、グルテンフリー専用フライヤー)。FindMeGlutenFree(最近の評価101件): グルテンフリーの表示、セリアック向けの欄、専用フライヤーの報告30件、セリアック向けは夜だけという声、QRコードで注文、窓で蕎麦打ち、だしが魚っぽいとの声、ヴィーガン蕎麦で卵を確認された(2026年9月)。

cultural_comfort.note: English menu descriptions, QR-code ordering; staff ask about celiac disease.

gf_cross_contamination.text: FMGF: "This establishment is NOT a dedicated gluten-free facility"; regular dipping sauces are also served — "make sure that you ask" (FMGF review, June 2026).
"Their menu states that celiac safe option is only available during dinner time." — FMGF tip, November 2025; "GF tempura is only available at night" (February 2026).

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Gluten-free soy sauce and dashi dipping sauce are provided for gluten-free orders (FMGF reviews); the regular sauces are not described as wheat-free.

vegan_cross_contact.text: A vegan soba order prompted a question about egg (September 2026), so it may be vegetarian rather than vegan; the dashi is usually fish-based.

staff_allergy_handling.text: "The staff is very well informed and asks if you have celiacs specifically since they take extra precautions." — FMGF review, October 2026.

positives.text: Official menu: the tempura is "Made with Buckwheat & Rice Flour" and "Fried in a Dedicated Gluten-Free Fryer".
Soba is hand-made from 100% buckwheat (十割蕎麦).
FMGF: dedicated gluten-free fryer reported 30 times; many celiac reviewers report no symptoms.

places.name: Naki vegan sweets
places.gf_detail: The shop calls itself a specialist in vegan, gluten-free sweets: 「ヴィーガングルテンフリースイーツの専門店」. FindMeGlutenFree marks it "Reported to be dedicated gluten-free", and celiac reviewers (30 recent ratings) report no symptoms. Reviewers mention rice flour, coconut oil and almond crusts. One caveat: in January 2026 a reviewer found the oat milk for drinks labelled "may contain gluten" and switched to soy milk. Ask about the milk in drinks.
places.vegan_detail: Fully vegan. The shop says it uses no eggs, dairy or other animal ingredients, only selected plant ingredients (「卵・乳製品など動物性の食材を使用せずに厳選した植物性食材で作る」).
places.hours_raw: Not listed on the official site. An FMGF reviewer (August 2026) found it open 13:00–20:00. Check before going. About four seats; takeaway available; also sells online.
places.neighborhood: Namba 1-5-5, on a side street just south of Dotonbori
places.cuisine: Vegan, gluten-free cakes, tarts and cookies · mango, berry, chocolate-pistachio and matcha tarts (~¥1,000) · cashew cream, almond crusts · rice-flour cookies · espresso · four seats, takeaway
places.notes: [Sweets · vegan and gluten-free tarts off Dotonbori] A tiny, quiet cake shop on a Namba side street with about four seats. Everything is vegan and gluten-free, and it is a celiac favourite (FMGF marks it reported dedicated gluten-free). Expect small tarts and cakes, around ¥1,000 each: mango, mixed berry cheesecake, chocolate pistachio, matcha and white chocolate, strawberry chocolate. Reviewers single out the cashew cream on a coarse almond crust, and the rice-flour and coconut-oil cookies, which one family bought to take home after being given some free. There is Italian espresso and peach cream soda. Service is gentle, once by a host in a kimono, though one 2026 diner found it unfriendly. Takeaway, and an online shop.

chef_bio.background: A vegan, gluten-free sweets specialist with an online shop (naki-vegansweets.com); no source names the owner or pastry chef.
chef_bio.philosophy: 「誰でも食べられる優しいお菓子」 — gentle sweets anyone can eat (official site).

anecdotes.text: "The cashew cream was especially good, paired with the coarse almond crust. Then after we finished our cake, they brought out free cookies! They had great texture (rice flour and coconut oil)." — FMGF review, July 2026.
"Dedicated gluten free and vegan cafe. Everything tasted amazing - a bit expensive though (1 tart was ¥1000)… Seating is limited to four but takeout is an option." — FMGF review, September 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式(naki-vegansweets.com): 「誰でも食べられる優しいお菓子」、卵・乳製品など動物性の食材を使用せずに厳選した植物性食材で作るヴィーガン・グルテンフリースイーツの専門店、ケーキ・クッキー・焼き菓子、オンラインショップ。FindMeGlutenFree(最近の評価30件): 大阪市中央区難波1-5-5、080-6217-5050、グルテンフリー専門と報告、席は4つほど、持ち帰り可、タルト1個1,000円(2026年9月)、マンゴー、ミックスベリーのチーズケーキ、チョコピスタチオ、抹茶とホワイトチョコ、カシューナッツのクリームとアーモンドの生地、米粉とココナッツオイルのクッキー、イタリアのエスプレッソ、13時〜20時に営業していた(2026年8月)、着物の接客、オーツミルクに「グルテンを含む可能性」の表示があり豆乳に変えた(2026年1月)、無愛想だったとの声(2026年4月)。

cultural_comfort.note: Tiny counter shop; point at the case.

places.name: Gluten-Free Vegan OKONOMIYAKI Vim
places.gf_detail: A gluten-free okonomiyaki restaurant. FindMeGlutenFree marks it "Reported to be dedicated gluten-free", and celiac reviewers (through October 2026) call it entirely gluten-free and safe for coeliacs, with Kirin gluten-free and organic gluten-free beer. Reported features include a dedicated gluten-free fryer and kitchen. The restaurant itself publishes nothing beyond its name, so this rests on community reports. Confirm when you book.
places.vegan_detail: Despite "Vegan" in its name, the menu also has meat and seafood: reviewers ate pork-belly okonomiyaki, grilled scallops, fried chicken and pork noodles. The vegan options include battered tofu and rice balls ("some vegan options"). Ask whether the batter, sauce and dashi for the vegan dishes are plant-based.
places.hours_raw: No hours published. Reviewers: opens at 17:00 (June 2026); closed Thursdays (April 2026); once closed an hour early (October 2026). About six seats. Reservation strongly advised (booking online needs a Japanese phone number); queue before opening otherwise. No children under 18 (FMGF tip, June 2026). One meal and one drink per person (May 2026).
places.neighborhood: Namba 1-3-13, up a tiny alley just off Dotonbori
places.cuisine: Gluten-free okonomiyaki (pork belly and vegan) · stir-fried noodles and pasta · oyster mushrooms · battered tofu · grilled scallops · fried chicken · Kirin gluten-free beer · six seats
places.notes: [Okonomiyaki · gluten-free okonomiyaki off Dotonbori] A tiny gluten-free okonomiyaki spot up a narrow alley off Dotonbori, with a counter downstairs and one table upstairs (about six seats). For celiac travellers it is a rare safe way to eat Osaka's signature dish. Reviewers order pork-belly okonomiyaki, stir-fried noodles and pasta, oyster mushrooms, tempura, battered tofu with rice balls, grilled scallops and fried chicken, with a Kirin gluten-free beer. The name says vegan, but meat and seafood are on the menu, so ask. Book ahead (online booking needs a Japanese phone number) or queue before the 5 pm opening. Several were turned away. Portions are small and prices high, one meal and one drink per person is expected, under-18s are not admitted, and it is reported closed on Thursdays. One reviewer mentions a sister restaurant around the corner.

chef_bio.background: A gluten-free okonomiyaki restaurant; the official page (nanbavim.biz-option.com) gives only its name, phone and links. One reviewer names the host-chef as Miyo.

anecdotes.text: "Tiny restaurant with a counter downstairs and a single table upstairs… oyster mushrooms, stir fried pasta, and of course the okonomiyaki." — FMGF review, October 2026.
"First time trying Okonomiyaki, and it was delicious! Miyo was a great host (and chef!). We had the Pork Belly Okonomiyaki, grilled scallops and fried chicken." — FMGF review, June 2026.
"I had the battered tofu which is like a chicken equivalent with the rice balls." — FMGF review, March 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式ページ(nanbavim.biz-option.com): 「【公式】Gluten-Free Vegan OKONOMIYAKI Vim」、電話、Instagram、HappyCowへのリンクのみ。FindMeGlutenFree: 大阪市中央区難波1-3-13、06-4963-3034、グルテンフリー専門と報告。セリアック病の客の口コミ(2026年): 1階カウンターと2階に1テーブル、約6席、エリンギ、焼きパスタ、お好み焼き、豚バラのお好み焼き、ホタテ焼き、唐揚げ、揚げ豆腐とおにぎり、キリンのグルテンフリービール、予約必須(オンライン予約には日本の電話番号が必要)、17時開店で開店前から満席、木曜定休との声、1時間早く閉まった、18歳未満は入店不可、1人1品1ドリンク、量が少なく高い、近くに姉妹店、すべてベジタリアンという声と肉やシーフードがあるという声の食い違い。

cultural_comfort.note: Tiny and often full; overseas celiac guests are the core crowd. Booking is hard without a Japanese phone number.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Meat and seafood (pork belly, scallops, fried chicken) are cooked in the same small kitchen as the vegan dishes.

"I appreciate it being entirely gluten free and coeliac safe." — FMGF review, May 2026.

places.name: 一蘭 道頓堀店別館 (Ichiran Dotonbori Annex)
places.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: thin wheat noodles. Tabelog notes allergy information is available.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: pork-bone (tonkotsu) broth, chashu.
places.hours_raw: Flavour-concentration counter open 24 hours; table seats 8:00–23:00 (official page, which warns seats and hours can change at short notice). Open year-round (Tabelog). Buy a ticket and fill in the order sheet while you queue.
places.neighborhood: Dotonbori 1-4-16, Sennichimae end — 3 min from Namba Stn exit 14
places.cuisine: Ichiran Hakata tonkotsu · order sheet for richness, garlic, onions, red sauce and noodle firmness · booth counter (24 h) and table floors · natural tonkotsu ramen ¥1,180 · extra noodles ¥210 · soft salted egg ¥160 · souvenirs
places.notes: [Ramen · Ichiran's big Dotonbori annex, open all night] Ichiran's 82-seat annex at the Sennichimae end of Dotonbori, since 2015. The 30-seat booth counter runs 24 hours, and the table floors run 8:00–23:00. It is the familiar ritual: buy a ticket while you queue, then tick richness, fat, garlic, green or white onion, the red secret sauce and noodle firmness on the order sheet. The bowl is Hakata-style tonkotsu with firm, very thin noodles. One diner found it light and not greasy, another rich with no off-odour. The natural tonkotsu ramen was ¥1,180 and extra noodles ¥210 (August 2026), with a soft salted egg at ¥160. Queues can reach an hour (October 2026), even 10 minutes at 2 am. The table floors suit groups and families: one August visitor noted an adult can bring up to five children free. Souvenirs are sold on the way out.

chef_bio.background: Ichiran chain (ichiran.com), which calls itself a company that researches tonkotsu ramen more than anyone in the world and serves only tonkotsu ramen.
chef_bio.philosophy: 「とんこつラーメンを世界一研究する会社」 (official site).
chef_bio.specialty: Natural tonkotsu ramen with the red secret sauce.

anecdotes.text: "I filled out the order sheet with my preferences: standard richness, extra creamy, one clove of garlic, chashu included, a mix of green and white onions, the signature red sauce at the standard level, and firm noodles." — September 2026, at 8:20 am; natural tonkotsu ramen ¥1,180, soft salted egg ¥160.
"At 2 AM, even at this 24-hour restaurant, I had to wait 10 minutes." — July 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: 一蘭 道頓堀店別館、大阪市中央区道頓堀1-4-16、なんば駅14番出口徒歩3分、82席(味集中カウンター30、テーブル52)、24時間営業・年中無休、予約不可、禁煙、カード・電子マネー可、アレルギー情報あり、2015年4月16日開店、公式 ichiran.com。公式: 味集中カウンター24時間、テーブル席8:00〜23:00、席数・営業時間は急に変わることがある。2026年の口コミ: 朝8時台でも人が多い、天然とんこつラーメン1,180円、半熟塩ゆで玉子160円、オーダー用紙(こってり度、にんにく、ねぎ、赤い秘伝のたれ、麺の硬さ)、博多とんこつの手本、極細麺、あっさりで脂っこくない、臭みのないとんこつ、替玉210円、深夜2時でも10分待ち、10月は1時間待ちも、並びながら券売機で食券と用紙、3階のテーブル席、大人1人で子ども5人まで無料、ミニサイズ、おみやげ販売。

noodles.notes: Very thin noodles; firmness chosen on the order sheet; extra noodles ¥210 (August 2026).

ramen.signature_bowl: 天然とんこつラーメン (natural tonkotsu ramen) ¥1,180 (August–September 2026).
ramen.chashu: Thin chashu ("meaty and had a nice chew", September 2026); optional on the order sheet.

places.cuisine: Abura-soba (soupless oil noodles) · thick chewy noodles, chashu, menma, shredded nori and sesame · soft egg, kimchi, extra meat toppings · vinegar and chili oil on the table · chashu rice bowl · kara-age and rice set · under ¥1,000 · cash only
places.notes: [Ramen · late-night abura-soba on Sennichimae] A two-floor, 26-seat Kirinji shop on the Sennichimae shopping street, since 2023, serving soupless abura-soba. Thick, chewy noodles come coated in an oil-and-sauce base under chashu, menma, plenty of shredded nori and sesame. Add a soft-boiled egg, kimchi or extra meat, then mix well and doctor it with the vinegar and chili oil on the table, as the wall instructions suggest. One fan says it becomes addictive by the third visit. It's cheap: a regular with soft egg came in under ¥1,000 in March 2026. A chashu rice bowl and a kara-age and rice set round it out. Regulars come after drinks or a live show, and lines of overseas visitors are common. Cash only.

chef_bio.background: Kirinji abura-soba chain (Suzume group site, suzume-group.co.jp).

anecdotes.text: "The freshly boiled noodles are mixed with oil and sauce, following Kirinji's unique style. On the table, vinegar and chili oil are available." — July 2026, around 3 pm on a weekday.
"I ordered the regular size with a soft-boiled egg topping. In this day and age, it's truly appreciated to find something under JPY 1000." — March 2026, late at night.

places.notes: [Ramen · the old-school Naniwa tonkotsu counter on Sennichimae] A long-running 11-seat L-shaped counter on the Sennichimae shopping street under a "Ganso Naniwa Tonkotsu" sign, open from 5 am to late, and round the clock at weekends. Its Osaka-style tonkotsu is light and slightly sweet, with thin straight noodles, chashu, naruto, menma and green onion (¥1,080; ¥1,250 with a scalp-tingling spicy miso), and the first kaedama is free. Season it with the pickled ginger, sesame and garlic on the counter. The mountainous chashu ramen is ¥2,200. Several diners say the ¥100 gyoza with a ramen beat the ramen itself. Summer brings a chilled yuzu-lemon shio ramen with ginger (¥1,380), and there's a shrimp-miso abura-soba and tantan tsukemen. Some find it pricey for what it is. Buy a ticket out front. Smoking is allowed.

chef_bio.background: Its sign reads "Ganso Naniwa Tonkotsu"; an August 2026 reviewer calls it said to be the birthplace of Osaka-style light soy-sauce tonkotsu, "though there are various theories".

places.notes: [Ramen · frothy chicken paitan between Namba and Shinsaibashi] A 9-seat shop with five counter seats and a table, since 2022, on the first floor of a mixed-use building with no street sign. Follow the map, or the queue. The chicken paitan is whipped espuma-style into a fluffy, mousse-like broth, creamy and rich yet clean on the finish, over flat, chewy noodles. The special toripaitan (¥1,705, August 2026) adds a seasoned egg, chicken and pork chashu, purple onion and wood ear. The mentaiko version stirs spicy cod roe through the cream. Seasoned-egg rice goes well alongside. Expect waits even off-peak, as turnover is slow. One June diner waited over two hours on a Saturday, and another found it competent but characterless.

chef_bio.background: Instagram @men_wa_tomoare (per a July 2026 review). A June 2026 diner calls it a sister shop of a well-known restaurant, without naming it.

anecdotes.text: "The espuma-style broth was fluffy and smooth, with a rich flavor that truly highlighted the deliciousness of the chicken. It paired perfectly with the chewy noodles." — July 2026.
"I ordered the Special Toripaitan Ramen (JPY 1,705)… Toppings included a seasoned egg, chicken chashu, pork chashu, purple onion, and wood ear mushrooms." — August 2026.

places.notes: [Ramen · the Shōwa-style chuka soba with the long queue] The Namba shop of Fujii, a small chain selling "nostalgic Shōwa flavour" chuka soba from Tokyo to Osaka. A sharp, easy-drinking shoyu broth comes with back fat you can scale down, and one diner was reminded of Onomichi ramen. Watch the fried rice being made at the counter: fluffy, and one regular's favourite anywhere. The ramen, kara-age and fried rice set is a generous ¥1,100 (October 2026). Nira soba piled with garlic chives arrived on 1 July 2026, served with a perforated ladle to catch them. Add garlic powder or vinegar halfway. Queues are the catch: 40 minutes to an hour and a half in October 2026, once 45 groups ahead on a Saturday. Take a number at the shop and wander until your phone pings. Closed Tuesdays; open to 3 am on Fridays and Saturdays.

chef_bio.background: Chuka Soba Fujii (ra-men.co) lists shops in Shinbashi and Shin-Nakano in Tokyo and Ashiharabashi, Namba and Noda-Hanshin in Osaka.
chef_bio.philosophy: 「昔懐かし昭和の味」 — nostalgic Shōwa-era flavour (official site).

anecdotes.text: "I decided to try the newly released Nira Soba, available from July 1, 2026. I chose the regular broth, very firm noodles, and added an egg (free of charge)… The ladle had holes in it, allowing me to enjoy all the nira." — October 2026, after a one-hour wait.

"I went on a Saturday at 11:30 AM and saw there were 45 groups ahead of me with a 120-minute wait… I ordered my ramen with less back fat, so it wasn't too heavy." — October 2026; called after about 50 minutes.

places.notes: [Ramen · a basement counter by Nankai Namba] A small counter along a basement corridor of the Namba Hips building, next to a pachinko parlour, since December 2024. It is usually run by one person, so expect to wait while earlier orders go out. Two lines: a tonkotsu with one big slab of tender chashu, looking thick but drinking easily, and a back-fat shoyu with black pepper that is lighter than it looks. The umami miso tonkotsu (¥1,550 in May 2026) gets an accent from marinated onions, and the back-fat shoyu was ¥1,350. Add a tsukimi chashu rice bowl (¥500). The thin noodles run soft, which may divide people, and one diner tasted oden in the broth. It's cashless (card or PayPay), the only drinks are alcohol, and there's no restroom nearby. Often quiet, with no queue (September 2026).

chef_bio.background: No source names the operator.

places.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: wheat noodles in a pork-bone soy broth; champon, gyoza, fried rice.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: pork-bone broth, pork toppings, naruto fish cake.
places.hours_raw: Open 24 hours, every day (official page: 24時間営業・年中無休; Tabelog lists a year-end closure). Ticket machine taking various payment methods (August 2026). Restroom up narrow stairs on the 2nd floor.
places.neighborhood: Namba 1-2-1, on the shopping street by Hōzenji — 5 min from Namba or Nippombashi Stn
places.cuisine: Pork-bone shoyu ramen · signature "torokotsu" ramen with two big pieces of pork · free kimchi · garlic tonkotsu (new 2026) · champon · fried rice · gyoza · 24 h, 17 seats
places.notes: [Ramen · Minami's 24-hour pork-bone shoyu with free kimchi] A 17-seat, mostly counter shop on the shopping street by Hōzenji, open 24 hours and run by Arakawa Food Service. For years it was a late-night ritual for locals (one did "the sauna at Amza, then Hanamaruken"). The base is a pork-bone soy broth, rich but not heavy, with medium-thin noodles. The signature torokotsu ramen comes with two big pieces of tender pork, nori, menma, naruto and green onion. Free kimchi on the counter cuts the richness. Newer additions include garlic tonkotsu ramen (April 2026) and champon, and the fried rice has a following. Regulars say the old queues have eased, the crowd is now largely overseas visitors, and the regular bowl tastes lighter than before. The restroom is up narrow stairs.

chef_bio.background: Hanamaruken shop of 株式会社アラカワフードサービス (Arakawa Food Service), which runs ramen shops and franchises and a meat wholesale business (arakawa-fs.jp).
chef_bio.philosophy: 「こだわりの独自レシピで作るラーメンを24時間・年中無休でご提供」 (official page).

anecdotes.text: "My personal go-to was the golden route of 'Amza for the sauna, then Hanamaru Ken for ramen.'… I think the free kimchi is a signature touch of Hanamaru Ken." — August 2026.
"It used to have long lines, but recently it feels much calmer… The regular ramen was lighter and had a more balanced flavor than before." — September 2026.

places.name: 無限ラーメン 千日前店 (Mugen Ramen Sennichimae)
places.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: wheat noodles; soy-sauce kaeshi.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: beef-bone and chicken broth, back fat, chashu.
places.hours_raw: Daily 11:00–22:00 (Tabelog; check before visiting). Cards (VISA) and electronic payments accepted, per Tabelog and a September 2026 review.
places.neighborhood: Namba 1-2-2, on the Sennichimae side by Hōzenji
places.cuisine: Creamy, frothy beef-bone and chicken paitan with shoyu kaeshi and back fat · thin straight noodles · two kinds of chashu · tonkotsu ramen · limited bowls over ¥2,000 · strip-loin rice bowl sets · mala chili condiment
places.notes: [Ramen · beef-bone white soup on Sennichimae] A ramen shop since 2023 on the Sennichimae side of Hōzenji, full of overseas visitors even on weekdays. The draw is a frothy beef-bone and chicken white soup: rich and creamy but easy to finish, built on chicken carcass and beef knuckle with a soy kaeshi and back-fat finish over thin straight noodles. It comes with two chashu, one charred and one tender, plus a runny seasoned egg, menma and green onion. There's also a lighter tonkotsu and a mala-style chili condiment on the table. Prices are high: a limited bowl topped ¥2,000 in September 2026, and the strip-loin rice bowl in the set ran salty. One diner flagged cleanliness. Cards and electronic payment accepted.

chef_bio.background: Sennichimae branch (Tabelog listing name); no source names the operator.

anecdotes.text: "The broth was covered in fine bubbles, conveying its richness even at first glance. The chashu (braised pork) came in two varieties: one with a beautifully charred surface and another that was tender and moist." — October 2026.
"The limited-edition ramen surprisingly costs over JPY 2000. The beef bone broth was incredibly delicious, and I found myself drinking it all." — September 2026.

places.name: 松阪牛焼肉M 道頓堀千日前店 (Matsusakagyu Yakiniku M Dotonbori Sennichimae)
places.gf_detail: Replying to reviews on FindMeGlutenFree, the general manager says every one of the house sauces is gluten-free, and staff show diners the labelled gluten-free soy sauce bottle. Celiac reviewers (August–October 2026) report non-GF items in set courses swapped out. One says the restaurant is "almost completely gf (except soup)", so ask about soups. The restaurant also says a staff member who serves here has celiac disease. This is a shared yakiniku kitchen, not a gluten-free one. Say you are celiac when you book.
places.vegan_detail: A Matsusaka-beef yakiniku restaurant; no vegan dishes are described. FMGF users tag it "good vegetarian options", but nothing specific is reported.
places.hours_raw: Dinner daily 17:00–23:00 (L.O. 22:30); lunch Sat, Sun and holidays 12:00–15:00 (L.O. 14:30). No fixed closing day, but it may close depending on circumstances (official page). Book online.
places.neighborhood: Sennichimae 1-7-11, Kamigata Bldg 2F, just off the Sennichimae shopping street — 3 min from Namba Walk exit B20
places.cuisine: Matsusaka-beef yakiniku courses · all house sauces gluten-free (per the manager) · labelled GF soy sauce · private and semi-private rooms, hall for up to 32 · lift, wheelchair access
places.notes: [Yakiniku · gluten-free Matsusaka beef off Sennichimae] The Dotonbori-Sennichimae branch of Yakiniku M, on the second floor of a building just off the Sennichimae shopping street, about 100 m east of its Hōzenji Yokochō sister. It is larger than its sisters: 14 tables, seven of them in private rooms, curtained semi-private seating, a hall for groups of up to 32, a lift, and wheelchair access to the table. Matsusaka-beef courses are grilled at the table. For celiac diners the draw is the sauces, which the general manager says are all gluten-free. Staff even bring out the labelled soy sauce bottle, and one server who is celiac comes up again and again in reviews. Reviewers had non-GF set-course items swapped, though one notes the soup is the exception. Dinner daily, plus weekend lunch.

roles: general manager and chef (signs the FMGF owner replies)

places.name: ABENO HUB
places.gf_detail: The okonomiyaki is gluten-free, per the restaurant: 「国産米粉を使用したグルテンフリーのお好み焼き」, made with 100% Koshihikari rice flour and cooked in olive oil. The yakisoba uses Akitakomachi rice-flour noodles. FMGF reviewers say it is made with gluten-free soy sauce and that a flyer explains the gluten-free options. The gyoza are made with wheat, and in October 2026 a celiac reviewer saw them cooked on the same griddle as the gluten-free food. FMGF marks it NOT a dedicated gluten-free facility. Skip the gyoza and ask about the griddle.
places.vegan_detail: Ask. The restaurant describes a vegetable-based sauce, but okonomiyaki batter usually contains egg and often dashi, and no vegan option is described.
places.hours_raw: Tue–Fri 17:00–23:00; Sat 14:00–23:00 (one block of the official page says Sat 17:00); food L.O. 22:00, drinks 22:30; closed Mon and Sun (official site). Online booking gets priority.
places.neighborhood: Namba 2-3-26, Nakatani Bldg 1F — 3–8 min from the Namba stations, about 5 min from the Glico sign
places.cuisine: Gluten-free rice-flour okonomiyaki (100% Koshihikari) · rice-flour yakisoba · cooked in olive oil with a vegetable-based sauce · okonomiyaki ~¥1,100 · GF potato salad and pudding · organic wine, British organic tea · smoking on the terrace
places.notes: [Okonomiyaki · gluten-free rice-flour okonomiyaki near the Glico sign] A casual bar-restaurant about five minutes from the Glico running man, with what it calls British roots: organic wine, European-style chūhai and British organic tea alongside beer and whisky. The okonomiyaki is made from 100% domestic Koshihikari rice flour, cooked in olive oil with a vegetable-based sauce, and gluten-free, and the yakisoba uses rice-flour noodles. Celiac reviewers love it ("the best okonomiyaki I've ever had – really good ginger flavour and only 1100 yen", October 2026), along with a GF potato salad and pudding. The gyoza are wheat and share the griddle, so skip them. Usually there's no queue when nearby okonomiyaki places have long lines. The chef-owner speaks good English, and ordering is by app. Smoking only on the outside terrace.

chef_bio.background: Describes itself as having British roots (英国にルーツを持つ当店); FMGF reviewers describe a chef-owner who speaks good English, sometimes running the room alone.
chef_bio.philosophy: 「グルテンフリーで、食後も軽やかな粉もんです」 (official site).

anecdotes.text: "We had the best okonamyaki I've ever had - really good ginger flavour and only 1100 yen. The gf was clearly explained on a flyer at the start. Note that the gyoza are made with wheat flour." — FMGF review, October 2026.
"The place is not 100% gluten free but the okonomiaki is and its made with gluten free soy sauce, and instead of wheat flour… rice flour." — FMGF review, 2025.

places.name: OKO - Fun Okonomiyaki Bar
places.gf_detail: A one-person okonomiyaki bar with a clearly marked gluten-free menu (about five GF okonomiyaki plus GF gyoza, fries and beer) and gluten-free soy sauce. FMGF reviewers (about 145 reviews) report gluten-free stickers on dishes and separate griddles and utensils, and some call it coeliac safe. It is NOT a dedicated gluten-free facility (FMGF), and in April 2026 a symptomatic celiac reported a bad reaction after eating only items from the GF menu. Tell the owner-chef you are celiac and weigh the risk.
places.vegan_detail: Reviewers report vegan options and a choice of vegetable and mixed-bean toppings for the okonomiyaki (August 2026). Ask whether the batter and sauce for the vegan version are free of egg and dashi.
places.hours_raw: No hours published. Reviewers: opens around 18:00 (a 40-minute wait at 18:05 in September 2026). Queue before opening; a single person cooks and serves. Self-service drinks ¥100 (bring coins). An FMGF tip from December 2025 said "permanently closed", but reviews continue through October 2026.
places.neighborhood: Dotonbori 2-4-13, the western end of Dotonbori near Namba Stn; tables upstairs
places.cuisine: Gluten-free okonomiyaki (about five choices: beef and onion, triple meat, mushroom and sausage …) · choose vegetable and bean toppings · huge portions (a medium feeds most) · GF gyoza and fries · GF beer · ¥100 self-service drinks · one-woman show
places.notes: [Okonomiyaki · a one-person gluten-free okonomiyaki bar on Dotonbori] A small, wildly decorated okonomiyaki bar at the western end of Dotonbori, run single-handed by its owner-chef, Shiho, and one of the most-collected gluten-free spots in Osaka on FMGF (59 public collections). Order at the counter from a clearly marked menu, find a table upstairs (some have a view), clear it yourself, and listen for your number. Drinks are self-service for ¥100 a go. There are about five gluten-free okonomiyaki (beef and onion, triple meat, mushroom and sausage), or build your own with vegetables and beans. Portions are huge, so a medium is plenty. The GF gyoza and fries are favourites. Queue before the roughly 6 pm opening. One woman does everything, so waits of 40 minutes or more are normal. One symptomatic celiac reacted in 2026, so it is not risk-free.

chef_bio.background: FMGF reviewers describe an owner who runs the whole restaurant alone — cooking, the counter and the room.

anecdotes.text: "The owner Shiho is so fun! The food was absolutely delicious. The owner / chef knows exactly what is and isn't GF. Food came out clearly labeled… Bring 100 yen coins for drinks!" — FMGF review, October 2026.
"I ordered the mushroom and sausage size medium, MASSIVE serve for medium… we arrived at 6:05pm and had a 40 minute wait to order." — FMGF review, September 2026.
"I ordered from a GF menu, just the items that were supposed to be safe… Got a bad glutenning." — FMGF review, April 2026; the reviewer adds that separate utensils and grill are used.

places.notes: [Sweets · gluten-free steamed matcha cake south of Namba] A small matcha-sweets shop from the ROMAN TALE restaurant group, using organic matcha (rare in Japan) from the group's own Kagoshima farm. The signature is the 抹茶ふかしパウン, a lightly sweet, chewy yet fluffy steamed matcha cake served hot from the bamboo steamer and made without wheat flour, so it is gluten-free. Celiac visitors keep coming back for it: one ate it every day of a stay, another three times on one trip. There are also gluten-free ice cream cones, soft serve and an excellent matcha latte, with soy milk and no oat milk. Takeaway too. Hours aren't published in the sources we found, so check.

places.notes: [Tsukemen · clam tsukemen after midnight in Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A 12-seat, second-floor tsukemen shop that opens at midnight (8 pm on Fridays and Saturdays) and runs to 5 am. A rich shijimi-clam broth, lighter than the usual thick tsukemen, feeds a smooth dip for silky noodles. There's a clam cream version and a shijimi paste, the noodles can be warmed, and a broth is poured in to finish. The other signature is rice topped with egg and freshly shaved truffle. One diner credits the concept to a charismatic figure from the Shinshu (Nagano) ramen scene. Regulars come after drinking, and queues form late. Expect ¥2,000–3,000 a head. Cash only. It changed its name before March 2025.

chef_bio.background: A February 2026 reviewer says it is "produced by a charismatic figure in the Shinshu ramen scene" — not named in any source.

anecdotes.text: "The tsukemen here is unlike any other, the flavor of the shijimi clam broth is rich and satisfying! The shijimi paste is also incredibly tasty!" — May 2025.
"You can enjoy a rice bowl topped with freshly shaved truffles and eggs… The light and refreshing broth is perfect after a night of drinking." — June 2026.

places.cuisine: Kyushu tonkotsu with thin Hakata-style noodles · thick, melting "toro chashu" · tomato ramen and tomato tsukemen · red miso chashu ramen · salt tonkotsu "Kio ramen" · Kyushu abura-soba · hot gyoza · multilingual menus · smoking allowed
places.notes: [Ramen · Kyushu tonkotsu and tomato ramen on Dotonbori] A 15-seat branch of the Kio chain on the western stretch of Dotonbori, open until 2 or 4 am, where queues are often entirely overseas visitors (lately many from Korea). The menus come in several languages. Its pride is a thick, melting "toro chashu", which even a diner unmoved by the plain noodles called exceptional. The base is a standard Kyushu tonkotsu with very thin Hakata-style noodles. Alongside it are red miso chashu, a salt tonkotsu, and the house favourite, tomato ramen or tomato tsukemen: bright acidity, gentle sweetness and umami, closer to soup pasta than ramen, as one diner put it. There's also a Kyushu-style abura-soba and hot, juicy gyoza. Smoking is allowed, and cards are not.

places.cuisine: Horumon (offal) ramen bubbling in a clay pot · red (spicy, most popular) or white · tender, fluffy horumon · corn topping · finish with rice as risotto or porridge · kalbi rice bowl · 24 h · cash only
places.notes: [Ramen · offal ramen in a bubbling clay pot, round the clock] A small, 24-hour Sennichimae-arcade branch of Horumon Ramen 8910, whose main shop is in Shimoshinjo, Higashiyodogawa. The bowl arrives bubbling in a clay pot that keeps it hot to the end, loaded with tender, fluffy horumon in a hearty broth with no off-odour. Choose red (spicy, the popular one) or white. One diner liked it topped with corn. The shop nudges you to finish with rice in the broth, risotto- or porridge-style. A salt-seasoned kalbi rice bowl is the alternative. It's like a one-person hot pot, good after drinks or, as one inspector found, for an early breakfast. Rarely crowded. Cash only.

chef_bio.background: Sennichimae branch; a September 2026 reviewer says the main shop is in Shimoshinjo, Higashiyodogawa Ward.

anecdotes.text: "I could choose between red and white, and since red is the most popular, I went with that… The ramen was bubbling away! The high heat retention kept the ramen warm, and the Horumon was incredibly tender." — October 2026.

"The atmosphere suggested that making a risotto or porridge with the ramen broth was highly recommended… I enjoyed the rich flavor of the broth without any unpleasant odor from the Horumon." — August 2026.

places.name: 宮崎麺屋 からから 東心斎橋店 (Miyazaki Menya Karakara)
places.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: wheat noodles by default, and the broth is not described as wheat-free. Konjac noodles can be chosen, but ask about the soup.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: minced meat and egg in the karamen; meat broth.
places.hours_raw: Open 24 hours; closed only over New Year (Tabelog and a September 2026 review). QR payments accepted; no cards or e-money (Tabelog).
places.neighborhood: Higashi-Shinsaibashi 2-7-8 (Sōemonchō) — 10 min from Shinsaibashi or Namba Stn
places.cuisine: Miyazaki-style karamen: red, spicy broth with fluffy egg, garlic chives and minced meat · spice levels (up to 100) · konjac noodles option · tender pork topping · Hokkaido "100-year" miso ramen · omurice · 24 h, two floors
places.notes: [Ramen · Miyazaki karamen round the clock in Sōemonchō] A 24-hour, two-floor, 23-seat karamen shop in the Sōemonchō nightlife streets, since 2011. The signature karakara noodles arrive bright red under fluffy scrambled egg, garlic chives and minced meat, with real umami behind the heat and the egg adding creaminess. Pick your spice level, up to 100 (regulars brag about levels 30, 50 and 100), and your noodles, including konjac. Add tender pork if you like. For milder tastes there's a Hokkaido "100-year" miso ramen, and a cult omurice that one 2 am regular orders instead of noodles. It is kept cool inside, anticipating the heat. A post-drinks staple. The street outside can feel rough late at night.

chef_bio.background: Higashi-Shinsaibashi branch of Miyazaki Menya Karakara (Tabelog listing name).

anecdotes.text: "A bright red bowl filled with fluffy eggs! It also had chives and minced meat… Unlike ramen that relies solely on spiciness, this one had a rich umami flavor." — September 2026.
"I could choose the type of noodles and the level of spiciness, so I opted for konjac noodles with a spiciness level of 50 and added some tender pork as a topping." — September 2026.

places.cuisine: Shellfish-broth shoyu ramen (oyster, asari and shijimi on chicken bones) · rich shoyu (chicken and bonito) · house-made whole-wheat noodles · rare pork-shoulder chashu · special ¥1,300 · seared rare chashu mayo rice bowl ¥400 · chilled shellfish noodles in summer · 8 pm–8 am
places.notes: [Ramen · shellfish shoyu all night in Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A 10-seat, white-and-grey counter tucked into a building beside one of Minami's liveliest clubs, open from 8 pm to 8 am, since 2023. The star is a golden shellfish broth: oyster, asari and shijimi over chicken bones, with a mild soy sauce and chicken oil. It's gentle and gradually deepening, with a pleasant shellfish bitterness, over house-made medium-thin noodles of whole-wheat flour. The special (¥1,300, September 2026) adds rare pork-shoulder and belly chashu, a soft egg, mizuna, menma and red and white onion. There's also a rich shoyu on chicken and bonito with thin noodles, and a chilled shellfish ramen in summer. Pair it with the seared rare-chashu mayo rice bowl (¥400). One colleague group said to skip the sudachi rice. Buy a ticket at the machine inside.

anecdotes.text: "The soup is a soy sauce base made from a blend of oyster, clam, and shijimi clam broth. It has a golden color, with the rich umami of shellfish and a pleasant bitterness… The noodles are homemade, straight, medium-thin, and made with whole wheat flour." — September 2026, special ¥1,300.
"It's based on chicken bones and flavored with clams, shijimi, and oysters. The taste is gentle and gradually seeps in." — August 2026, around 9:30 pm on a Sunday, no wait.

places.notes: [Ramen · hangover-cure shijimi ramen after midnight] A 22-seat, second-floor late-nighter, since 2013, serving "recovery ramen" made with plenty of Yamato shijimi clams from Lake Shinji in Shimane. The broth is light yet deep (one diner compared its depth to tonkotsu), with a touch of butter for richness, in shio, shoyu or miso. The signature rich shijimi shio is ¥1,200, and the shop puts it at 496 kcal. Chashu is ¥200 extra and the salt gyoza ¥400. In summer, a clear chilled shijimi ramen with Morioka-style noodles, rare chashu, half an egg and rice crackers. The walls are covered in autographs: kabuki actors, Yoshimoto comedians, baseball players and Brian May of Queen. One diner found ¥1,200 for a plain bowl steep. Open 8 pm to 5 am, cash only.

places.gf_detail: Ask. You pick your own ingredients, including vermicelli and other noodles, but the beef-bone broth is finished with a sesame-and-peanut sauce whose ingredients are not described. Fish balls, dumplings and many noodles contain wheat.

places.notes: [Chinese · build-your-own malatang in Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A bright, recently renovated 38-seat branch of a malatang chain from China, popular with Chinese visitors and recognisable by its big red sign. Use tongs to fill a bowl from the chilled case: vegetables, meat, horumon, shrimp, octopus, fish balls, xiaolongbao, panda-shaped fish cakes, and noodles from vermicelli to beef-tendon noodles. It's weighed at ¥380 per 100 g (October 2026). The signature broth is beef bones simmered for 8 hours and finished with a fragrant sesame-and-peanut sauce, creamy enough that one diner had it with no spice at all. Others found level 2 plenty hot, with real numbing mala. Stir in sesame sauce or cilantro black vinegar at the table, and add fried bread for dunking, sesame balls or chicken wings.

chef_bio.background: Branch of a malatang chain with many locations in China (May and June 2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "The broth, made by simmering beef bones for 8 hours and finished with a special sauce of fragrant sesame and peanuts, was rich and creamy like a velvety soup." — October 2026, ¥380 per 100 g, "Not Spicy".
"The spiciness and numbing sensation were quite authentic! It had more punch than other places." — March 2026.

places.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: wheat noodles; soy-sauce grilled rice balls.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: sea-bream fish-bone broth, sakura shrimp.
places.hours_raw: Mon and Wed–Sun 18:00–1:00 (L.O. 0:30); closed Tuesdays (Tabelog). Tabelog gives an opening date of 20 July 2026; an October 2026 reviewer says it opened on 12 September. No membership needed here (unlike the Fukuoka original). Cards and e-money accepted.

places.cuisine: Sea-bream fish-bone (gyokotsu) ramen and tsukemen · creamy white broth · fried sakura shrimp · spicy versions · tsukemen with mini rice and broth to finish risotto-style · ramen ¥1,450, spicy ¥1,550 · night-only medicinal hot pot and eel-liver skewers · modern Japanese room
places.notes: [Ramen · Fukuoka's fish-bone ramen, no membership needed] The third shop of Gyokotsuya, famous in Fukuoka as a members-only ramen bar. Here, as in Ginza, anyone can walk in. Upstairs in a Sōemonchō building, a chic black room with vermilion lattice feels more kaiseki than ramen shop. The broth is a creamy white soup from sea-bream bones, under chewy noodles and crunchy fried sakura shrimp, part of the shop's pitch for a "sixth flavour". Fish-bone ramen and tsukemen are ¥1,450, and the spicy versions ¥1,550. Tsukemen comes with a mini rice and a flask of broth to turn the leftovers into risotto. At night there are a medicinal hot pot and grilled eel-liver skewers. Not everyone is sold: one diner found the broth watery and sparse for ¥1,450. Closed Tuesdays.

chef_bio.origin: Dotonbori shop (Tabelog opening date 20 July 2026; a reviewer says 12 September 2026)
chef_bio.background: Third location of Gyokotsuya, a members-only ramen shop in Fukuoka; the Ginza and Dotonbori shops need no membership (October 2026 review).
chef_bio.philosophy: A "sixth flavor" beyond the five basic tastes (October 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: "The broth is a blend of sea bream and creamy white soup, creating a rich flavor that spreads beautifully in your mouth… The topping of deep-fried sakura shrimp adds a strong shrimp flavor." — October 2026.

places.notes: [Takoyaki · gluten-free soybean-flour takoyaki in Higashi-Shinsaibashi] An upstairs takoyaki spot from the people behind OKO Fun Okonomiyaki Bar on Dotonbori, with the same casual, hostel-style, slightly punk feel, run by one person. Order and pay at the window, find a seat, and wait for your number on the speaker. Opinions split: cheap, plentiful and "greatest meal my coeliac daughter has had since being in Japan" (July 2026), but others wanted more seasoning or preferred the okonomiyaki branch. Not a dedicated GF facility.

chef_bio.background: A sister shop of OKO (Fun Okonomiyaki Bar), per an August 2026 FMGF review; run by one person.

places.notes: [Ramen · Osaka's old-school Kotan under Namba] A bright, 33-seat Kotan in the Namba Walk underground mall, steps from the Midōsuji Line, and for many Osakans the taste of childhood. The Kotan ramen comes in shoyu (soy-forward but not heavy) or shio (a light yet rich white broth), with thin noodles, chashu, bean sprouts, carrot and green onion. Regulars shower it in sesame from the table. The pork-belly Kotan is ¥950, a seasoned egg adds ¥120, and the spicy cold noodles with kimchi are ¥980 (September 2026). There are wonton noodles, and lunch sets with fried rice, gyoza or a croquette. Food comes fast, often in two minutes. A brisk hall manager in thick Osaka dialect keeps it moving.

"The 'Kotan Ramen (Salt)' featured a light yet rich white broth filled with bean sprouts, carrots, green onions, and plenty of chashu. The gentle saltiness paired perfectly with the thin noodles." — August 2026.

places.notes: [Ramen · Kappa's 24-hour back-fat shoyu tonkotsu on Sennichimae] The main shop of Kappa Ramen Honpo, a 27-seat counter on Sennichimae-dōri, open around the clock. places.notes: [Ramen · Jirō-style mazesoba in Amerikamura] The 15-seat head shop of Menya Gaten, since 2013, built on a Jirō-style "MAZE soba": thick, chewy, firm noodles (150 g up to 300 g) under vegetables, thick-cut chashu, fat and garlic, all scaled when you hand over your ticket. Mix it hard (one diner flipped it, "tenchi gaeshi"), and add mayo halfway. There's a curry mazesoba with a decent kick, and a DX chicken paitan ramen (¥1,400, August 2026) with tender thick chashu that won over a paitan fan. Kimchi and egg soup are free and self-serve, when they haven't run out. Some find the mazesoba merely salty without Jirō-style depth. Cash only, smoking allowed.

anecdotes.text: "When I handed over the ticket, I made my order with extra noodles, lots of vegetables, extra fat, and garlic… I managed with a technique called 'tenchi gaeshi' (flipping it over)." — October 2026, curry mazesoba.

places.cuisine: The original Kinryu: light Osaka tonkotsu · chashu ramen piled with pork · free kimchi, garlic and garlic chives · free rice instead of kaedama · 24 h · standing space
places.notes: [Ramen · the original Kinryu at the east end of Dotonbori] The main shop of the Kinryu dragon-sign chain, a 38-place counter with standing space at the Sakaisuji end of Dotonbori, open 24 hours. The bowl is Osaka's light tonkotsu, much lighter than Kyushu-style and easy to finish, with generous chashu. Even the plain ramen carries several slices and trimmings, and the chashu ramen piles it on. The ritual is unchanged for half a century, as one diner put it: free kimchi, garlic and garlic chives to load in as you like, plus free rice in place of extra noodles. Waits run 10–30 minutes at busy times. Buy a ticket first. Cash only, smoking allowed.

chef_bio.background: Main shop of Kinryu Ramen; a September 2026 reviewer says the free garlic, chives and kimchi have "remained unchanged for half a century".
chef_bio.specialty: Light Osaka tonkotsu with free kimchi and garlic.

anecdotes.text: "Unlimited toppings of garlic, chives, and kimchi have remained unchanged for half a century." — September 2026, after a 10-minute wait.
"This famous tonkotsu ramen shop in Osaka offers a lighter flavor compared to Kyushu-style tonkotsu ramen… Instead of extra noodles, you can enjoy all-you-can-eat rice." — November 2025.

places.notes: [Chinese · an all-night, Chinese-run kitchen off Sennichimae] A slightly run-down, 28-seat Chinese restaurant in a back alley off Aioibashi-suji, open from 5 pm to 5 am, where Chinese is spoken all round and the menu is hard to decipher. Regulars come back for the spicy pork spare ribs, garlicky stir-fried water spinach and big shrimp in chili sauce, with beer. Cheap evening set meals (mapo tofu, chive and liver) come with cabbage and pickled mustard greens. places.notes: [Ramen · lobster ramen in Amerikamura] A lobster-broth ramen and tsukemen shop in Amemura, since 2023, with a Japanese and English menu and plenty of overseas diners. The broth is rich and creamy with concentrated lobster, which one diner likened to a tonkotsu, over thick, chewy, curly noodles with plenty of vegetables and burdock chips. Pick a spice level from 0 to 4. Basic bowls started around ¥1,000–1,100 in 2025, and the showpiece adds a whole lobster for ¥4,200. The other half of the menu is bluefin tuna: a rice bowl with crab miso soup (¥1,550) or a tuna cutlet set. You pay after eating. Some found the ramen broth less rich than the tsukemen dip. Recent reviews date from 2025, so check it is still open.

places.cuisine: Tonkotsu ramen ("moto-aji") · ajitama ramen with black garlic oil · light meat soba ¥880 with grated daikon · abura-soba with three chashu, nori, chili oil and vinegar · spicy miso · pork rice bowl · 10-seat counter, open to 4 am
places.notes: [Ramen · late-night tonkotsu on Aioibashi-suji] A 10-seat counter on the Aioibashi-suji shopping street, part of the Fukuchan group, open from lunch to 4 am and often run by a single cook. The standard is a straightforward tonkotsu ("moto-aji"). The ajitama ramen adds a slick of dark black garlic oil that gives the broth depth. For something lighter, the meat soba (¥880, July 2026) has a clear, refreshing broth with thin straight noodles, pork bits, onion and grated daikon. The abura-soba comes with three big slices of chashu, nori, and chili oil and vinegar at hand. There's also a spicy miso and a well-liked pork rice bowl. Buy a ticket out front.

chef_bio.background: Tenchijin, a Fukuchan-group ramen brand (fukuchan.co.jp).
chef_bio.specialty: Tonkotsu ramen with black garlic oil.

anecdotes.text: "The white tonkotsu broth was topped with dark black garlic oil, which really whetted my appetite… The black garlic oil was doing wonders, adding depth to the rich and somewhat monotonous tonkotsu flavor." — December 2025, ajitama ramen.
"I ordered the Meat Soba for JPY 880 (tax included)… The broth was light and refreshing, paired with thin straight noodles, and there were bits of pork scattered throughout." — July 2026.

places.cuisine: Osaka kasu udon: clear dashi with crispy abura-kasu and green onion · plum and tororo-kombu kasu udon · spicy seasoning to stir in · 8-seat counter · 80s–90s hard rock · 6 pm–1 am
places.notes: [Udon · late-night kasu udon in Amerikamura] An 8-seat counter up a graffiti-covered corridor in Mitsudera Kaikan, the pink-lit building that is one of Amemura's deep-drinking landmarks. It serves Osaka's kasu udon: a clear, refreshing dashi enriched by crispy, fragrant abura-kasu (fried beef offal) and green onion, with firm udon. A spicy seasoning deepens as it melts in. Try the plum and tororo-kombu version. A regular of more than ten years says prices have risen to around ¥1,000, but the taste hasn't changed. It's a classic finish to a night out. The owner plays 80s and 90s hard rock (Guns N' Roses, Van Halen), and young crowds fill it by 10 pm. Closed Wednesdays. It plans to move by June 2027.

chef_bio.background: A kasu-udon counter; no source names the owner.

anecdotes.text: "I've been coming here for over 10 years. While the prices have increased from a few hundred yen to the thousand-yen range, the taste remains unchanged, with the rich umami of the kasu and a clear, refreshing broth." — June 2026.
"I had the plum kasu udon topped with kombu kelp… Due to building renovations, they are planning to relocate by June 2027." — August 2026.
