places.cuisine: Chuka soba (shoyu) with plenty of chicken oil, medium-thick chewy noodles, rare chashu · shio ajitama ramen · chilled soba in summer: kombu and bonito dashi with kumquat and minced chicken · half fried rice set · kara-age, two for ¥150 · Friday izakaya from 15:00: toro liver ¥400, chicken sashimi ¥400, yukhoe, grilled rare chashu, dashimaki, green-onion chijimi, highball ¥350 · 20 seats
places.notes: [Ramen · chicken-oil shoyu and a Friday izakaya near Sakaisuji-Honmachi] A clean, stylish ramen shop two minutes from Sakaisuji-Honmachi, open since 2021. The chuka soba is a rich shoyu glossy with chicken oil, on medium-thick, firm, chewy noodles with rare chashu; one diner drank every drop. In summer there was a chilled soba of kombu and bonito dashi topped with kumquat and minced chicken. Opinions on other bowls vary: one diner found the shio too oily and salty, another found the broth lukewarm at opening. Fridays it stays open to 20:00 and adds an izakaya menu from 15:00, with fresh chicken at bargain prices: toro liver and chicken sashimi ¥400 each, kara-age ¥150 for two, highballs ¥350. Weekdays only; cash only.

chef_bio.background: Ramen shop with a Friday izakaya menu (Tabelog, staff-maintained; 2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "The broth was rich with a generous amount of chicken oil and a delightful soy sauce aroma—it was incredibly delicious. I ended up drinking it all. The noodles were medium-thick with a chewy texture and had a strong bite." — September 2026, chuka soba with half fried rice set.

"Personally, I found that the umami of the kombu came through first, followed by a subtle hint of bonito… The firm, medium-thick noodles had a smooth texture and a nice chew." — September 2026, chilled soba with kumquat.

places.cuisine: Tabelog Tempura 100 (2025) · omakase tempura course fried in extra-virgin olive oil at low temperature, light and not heavy · opens with a katsu sandwich · several kinds of shrimp, body, heads and roe · seasonal fish, e.g. young ayu; sea urchin; seaweed · vegetables direct from growers: carrot, sweet potato, broccoli, mushroom, lotus root · Kagawa Olive Beef · tencha (tempura rice tea) to finish · about ten seasonal sakes, beer, wine · 8-seat hinoki counter
places.notes: [Japanese · a Tabelog 100 tempura counter frying in olive oil] A calm basement counter of hinoki wood just off the Soemoncho nightlife strip, open since 2021 and picked for Tabelog's Tempura 100 in 2025. The chef and the chef's wife are both very kind. The difference is the oil: extra-virgin olive oil at low temperature, which the shop says soaks in less and drains well, so even a long course stays light. The omakase opens with a surprise katsu sandwich, then runs through seasonal seafood and growers' vegetables: several kinds of shrimp including heads and roe, young ayu, sea urchin, sweet carrots and sweet potato, plus Kagawa Olive Beef, and finishes with tencha. Diners describe the chef as friendly and talkative about the ingredients. About ten seasonal sakes. One seating nightly at 18:00, plus Sunday lunch; book ahead.

chef_bio.background: Tempura counter (official site tenpura-ando.com; Tabelog, staff-maintained); Tabelog Tempura 100 2025. The chef and the chef's wife are both very kind (August 2026 review).
chef_bio.philosophy: Extra-virgin olive oil and low-temperature frying to keep the umami, sweetness and aroma of the ingredients (Tabelog listing).

anecdotes.text: "The tempura, fried in olive oil, has an astonishingly light batter that doesn't weigh you down at all. I was impressed by the precise cooking techniques used for each ingredient. The carrots and sweet potatoes were exceptionally delicious." — August 2026.
"The course starts with a surprising katsu sandwich, followed by a parade of delicious tempura." — September 2026.

places.cuisine: Refined oden and seasonal Japanese plates · oden: daikon, konnyaku, clams with kuzukiri, green onion with abura kasu, tuna negima, whale saezuri, yuba · oden-broth soup with wild mushrooms and free-range chicken · shime-saba sandwich · hairy crab in the shell · umazurahagi with its liver · junsai with shirasu · yellow garlic chives with beef tongue · sardine tsukune · grilled eel · sashimi · sake and bottled beer · 7 counter seats, 1 table for four
places.notes: [Japanese · refined oden and sake hidden in Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A quiet, old-Shinsaibashi-style oden counter at the very back of a building's second floor, open since 2014, with classical music playing. The oden is the heart of it, delicately seasoned: daikon, konnyaku, big clams with kuzukiri, green onion with abura kasu, tuna negima, whale saezuri and yuba. Around it come seasonal plates: an oden-broth soup with wild mushrooms and free-range chicken, a shime-saba sandwich, hairy crab packed in its shell, umazurahagi with its liver, a fluffy sardine tsukune that converted a sardine skeptic, crisp grilled eel. Good sake to match. Dinner runs about ¥10,000–20,000 with a 10% service charge, and one table waited a long time for dishes. Book ahead, especially in winter; closed Mondays.

chef_bio.background: Oden and Japanese restaurant (official site yoshitaka-osaka.jp; Tabelog, staff-maintained).

anecdotes.text: "First, we have the oden broth soup infused with the umami of natural mushrooms. One sip, and the rich flavor spreads pleasantly." — October 2026, seventh visit.
"From the oden, we enjoyed the Japanese radish, konnyaku (konjac), clams, and kuzukiri (starch noodles) which were all flavorful… The grilled eel was perfectly crispy on the outside." — May 2026.

places.cuisine: Long-established sushi, Kamigata roots now serving Edomae · omakase with appetizers and 12 nigiri, or à la carte · torigai, lightly grilled nodoguro, chutoro · abalone with its liver sauce over rice · anago · sea urchin · 8 seats at an L-shaped white-wood counter
places.notes: [Sushi · a century-old Minami sushi counter by Aioibashi] An eight-seat counter of pale wood near Aioibashi, a long-established sushi house that one diner dates back more than 100 years, which began with Kamigata (Osaka-style) sushi and now serves Edomae. Founded more than 100 years ago, it is now run by the fourth-generation owner. Book the omakase of appetizers and 12 nigiri, or order à la carte; one diner found the prices reasonable. Highlights in reviews: crisp torigai, thick lightly grilled nodoguro, abalone with its liver sauce over rice, a refined anago, and sea urchin that melts away. Seasoning is balanced, neither too sweet nor too sour. Not every visit lands: one diner found some pieces fishy or too salty. Enter by 21:30; closed Sundays.

chef_bio.origin: Founded over 100 years ago, per a July 2026 review.
chef_bio.background: Long-established sushi restaurant; Kamigata sushi roots, now Edomae (July 2026 review; Tabelog, staff-maintained). Founded more than 100 years ago, it is now run by the fourth-generation owner (July 2026 review).
chef_bio.specialty: Edomae nigiri; abalone with liver sauce.

anecdotes.text: "Originally, it was known for Kamigata sushi, but over time it has evolved to serve Edomae sushi… The abalone is served with liver sauce on top of the rice… The anago (conger eel) was exquisite." — July 2026.
"The Nodoguro was slightly grilled, cut thickly, and left a memorable impression… The seasoning was just right—not too sweet, nor too sour." — August 2024.

places.notes: [Sushi · a young omakase counter with a sweet-shrimp signature in Sennichimae] A seven-seat hinoki counter in a basement off Sennichimae, open since October 2023, which one regular says has been a Michelin Guide Kyoto-Osaka selected restaurant in 2025 and 2026. The chef trained at two-star sushi restaurants in Osaka and in Kobe (Sushi Ikko). The omakase (about ¥25,000) opens with clam soup and the signature: sweet shrimp spread paper-thin, eaten with rock salt and sudachi. Appetizers are inventive, such as eel and cucumber wrapped Peking-duck style, kue or kinmedai shabu-shabu, abalone with liver sauce, before nigiri of seasonal fish the chef sources directly from producers and Toyosu. The chef seems reserved at first but warms up; the host is friendly. Three seatings a day; book well ahead.

chef_bio.background: Omakase sushi counter (Tabelog, staff-maintained); Michelin Guide Kyoto-Osaka selected restaurant 2025 and 2026, per an October 2026 review. The chef trained at two-star sushi restaurants in Osaka and in Kobe (Sushi Ikko) (September 2026 review).

places.notes: [Sushi · a busy, generous Minami sushi bar regulars rebook] A popular 19-seat sushi bar a block off Dotonbori, usually full, with regulars who book the same day and come back often. The shop describes itself as run by a husband-and-wife team. Portions are big: oversized toppings, huge rolls and sashimi platters piled with toro, kazunoko, scallops, flounder and geoduck. The favorite is the toro-taku roll (only one toro item per table, so choose between it and the toro tekka); aburi salmon, rare and juicy, comes close behind, with eel and anago. Start with the crab-claw sunomono in sweet vinegar or the kani miso, which pull you toward sake. There's no price list, but two diners paid about ¥17,000 with drinks. Popular items sell out; one diner found the rolls unevenly cut. Closed Mondays.

places.notes: [Ramen · a homey shoyu chuka soba with sets by Uehommachi] A red-neon, graffiti-windowed ramen shop a minute from Osaka-Uehommachi, open since 2016, with the broad menu and sets of a neighborhood Chinese diner and a loyal crowd of regulars. The staff, of Chinese descent, are polite. The shoyu chuka soba is a chicken-and-seafood broth with a strong, nostalgic soy edge, gentle rather than salty, on medium-thin low-hydration noodles with three slices of chashu, menma, sprouts and green onion; at lunch, extra sprouts and onion are free. For more richness there's a back-fat version. Sets add gyoza or a small soy-dark fried rice (¥1,200 with gyoza), and evenings bring a beer set with fatty chashu. Grated garlic is on the table. Service is attentive. Closed Sundays.

The Asari Rapasu (¥1,230; the SP version ¥1,580) is a mild, Western-leaning broth of clam dashi and chicken paitan on flat, wide, chewy noodles, with chashu, tender chicken, clams, yuzu and a squeeze of lemon; diners compare it to a Western-style mazesoba. places.notes: [Ramen · a beginner-friendly Jiro-style bowl by Uehommachi] A Jiro-style shop two minutes from Osaka-Uehommachi, open since February 2025, with a relaxed atmosphere that diners call easy for first-timers. Sizes start big: the small is 250 g of thick, chewy, wheaty noodles (¥1,100), the large 375 g (¥1,200), the extra-large 500 g. Buy a ticket, then call your garlic, vegetables and fat; vegetables run a bit light by Jiro standards unless you ask for more. The broth leans soy over pork, with a touch of sweetness, under thick pork, bean sprouts and cabbage. Garlic mayo (+¥100) and spicy fried garlic push it further into junk-food territory, and the back-fat rice bowl is a guilty side. One diner could not add garlic on a daytime visit. Busy at lunch; open daily.

places.notes: [Ramen · Osaka's benchmark Nagoya Cochin shoyu and tsukesoba by Nishinagahori] The main shop of Kadoya Shokudo, open since 2001 and on Tabelog's ramen 100 every year since 2018, one of Osaka's most famous bowls (the Crysta Nagahori branch is also in this guide). Everything rests on Nagoya Cochin chicken. The tsukesoba (¥1,880 for 200 g) is the order to make: a dip of intense chicken umami with soy, a tang of vinegar and a little chili, with glossy, smooth house-made medium-thick noodles; the larger sizes add more to the dip. The shoyu chuka soba and the handmade wonton noodles (shio or shoyu) are the alternatives, and the Cochin seasoned egg is ¥350. On weekends there's a limited Cochin chicken rice. Lines run 30 minutes to two hours; the shop lends umbrellas for shade. Lunch only; closed Tuesday and Wednesday; cash only.

places.notes: [Ramen · a Tabelog 100 Nagoya Cochin shoyu by Sakaisuji-Honmachi] A seven-seat counter a few minutes from Sakaisuji-Honmachi, open since 2013 and on Tabelog's ramen 100 lists in most years since 2017, yet on two October 2026 visits there was no wait. The chuka soba (¥1,000) is built on Nagoya Cochin chicken: a clear amber broth with a rich soy aroma and long finish, firm, slightly wavy medium-thin noodles with real wheat flavor, two slices of chashu, menma and a seasoned egg included. The chicken soba (¥1,100) is a robust chicken paitan glossed with chicken oil and sharpened with raw onion; one diner found the chicken edge too strong, another the finish a bit sweet. The shio soba sells out first. Add a chashu rice bowl. Lunch only on Wednesday and Saturday; closed Sundays; cash only.

places.notes: [Ramen · rich seafood tsukemen with a curry option near Tanimachi 6-chome] A busy, stylish tsukemen shop near Tanimachi 6-chome, open since 2014 and on Tabelog's Ramen OSAKA 100 from 2023 to 2025, filling up fast at lunch. The rich tsukemen (¥1,200) pairs house-made thick, chewy, slightly sweet wheat noodles with a dip so thick it clings, built on pork, chicken, sardine flakes and niboshi; order it soy or curry, the curry adding a gentle spice. Large noodles are free, but the dip is strong and a small rice comes at the end to mix with the leftover dip and yuzu kosho, so regular may be enough. Lemon halfway brightens it. The mazesoba (¥1,150) adds cheese, fried onion and garlic chives. One regular has eaten here twenty times. Buy a ticket outside; open daily; cash only.

places.notes: [Sushi · a showy tuna omakase counter just off Dotonbori] A six-seat counter on a third floor near Namba, calm despite the crowds below, built around tuna and theatre. The omakase (¥12,000 in October 2026) opens with a bowl heaped with uni, ikura and otoro that the chef sears in front of you, then the "Dragon Roll" of otoro, negitoro, uni and egg yolk, and a tuna flight of akami, chutoro and otoro. Shira-ko with ponzu, a gold-leaf uni tofu, nigiri of shrimp, sea bream, scallop and salmon, and an unagi dog handed straight across the counter round it out. Reviews call it visually spectacular and, past the show, well made. Open from noon, so it works for a splurge lunch too. Book ahead.

"While the initial impression was the vibrant presentation, I was pleased to find that the quality of the ingredients was excellent, and every dish was delicious." — October 2026, omakase ¥12,000.

places.notes: [Sushi · a lively ¥4,400 omakase in two seatings on Soemoncho] A counter sushi bar from the 881 ("Yabai") Group, open since June 2025, whose idea is authentic counter sushi made approachable and fun. The head chef, Hibiki, is a former sumo wrestler, just 21 when reviewed, who trained at Sushi Yamato; the chanko on the course is the chef’s own. There's one omakase (¥4,400), or ¥6,600 with all-you-can-drink, served to eight guests at a time in two seatings at 17:30 and 20:00, opening with a group shout-out. The course runs about 15 items: Tosa katsuo, chawanmushi, seasonal fish sandwiches, kamasu, yuan-yaki, tuna, unadon, then chanko and a ramen made from the broth of the sushi fish. Diners love the warm, playful atmosphere and the head chef's friendliness; one found only six nigiri and no chutoro, and the shaved-ice dessert plain. The door shows only a QR sign. Reservation only.

One diner found service slow and the room noisy, another found it calm and suited to business dinners. Book ahead; closed Sundays.

Its signature Fuku Ryu ramen (¥930) is a chicken paitan shoyu whipped into a creamy, cappuccino-like foam, topped with rare chashu, green onion, mizuna and a slightly tangy foam that blends in as you go; thin straight noodles stay firm. One regular prefers the niboshi shoyu with onions and thick chashu, lighter than it looks; others order the Mazenibou niboshi mazesoba, best with vinegar and a few pieces of meat saved for the rice. Fills by noon on weekdays. Open daily; bring cash.

The marudori (whole-chicken) chuka soba looks dark but drinks light and refreshing, with medium-thin noodles, rare chashu and tender menma; the special (¥1,300) adds a well-seasoned egg. places.notes: [Ramen · a ¥750 shoyu with mitsuba, and ¥500 morning ramen, by Ebisucho] A ten-seat counter a few minutes from Ebisucho, open since 2021 and loved for good ramen at a low price. The shoyu ramen (¥750) is a seafood dashi deepened with chicken bones and chicken fat, easy to drink, on thin but chewy noodles, with thin chashu and an unexpected sprig of mitsuba; there's a shio too. The classic order is the half-and-half set (¥1,400 with a large fried rice), picking a ramen: the rich kote shiro shoyu one regular always orders, a shio scallop, a spicy miso full of vegetables and minced meat, or dan dan noodles with a subtle Sichuan-pepper note that come with a side of rice. places.notes: [Sushi · a relaxed one-chef sushi counter in Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A sushi counter where the chef works alone and quietly, a rare place in Minami to order serious sushi à la carte as well as by the course. Start with a platter of six appetizers and about five kinds of sashimi, then nigiri on small, red-and-white-vinegar rice that lets the fish lead: sweet shrimp straight from the tank, chutoro (one regular's pick of the tuna), eel, raw anago with a crunchy bite, standout ikura and a beautifully presented sea urchin. Tamago is Kansai-style, and dessert is a homemade pudding. Diners call the balance of quality and price unusually good for this level. With one chef, order slow dishes early. Closed Sundays.

chef_bio.background: Sushi counter run by the owner alone (January 2026 review; Tabelog, staff-maintained).
chef_bio.specialty: Sushi courses and à la carte.

anecdotes.text: "This place offers a great balance of quality ingredients, taste, presentation, and price. Since the owner prepares everything… it's best to order time-consuming dishes with some patience in mind." — January 2026, fifth visit.
"The sweet shrimp was incredibly fresh, taken straight from the tank, and had a delightful, firm texture. The medium fatty tuna, eel, and sea urchin were all of high quality." — January 2026.

places.cuisine: Creative kushiage counter · Harusai course: 12 signature and seasonal skewers chosen by the chef, about ¥5,000, served one by one as they fry · asparagus cut into easy bites · quail egg · Japanese-style pho and ice cream to finish · carefully poured draft beer · 9 counter seats
places.notes: [Japanese · a quiet nine-seat kushiage counter by Namba Station] A small second-floor counter a minute from Namba exit 13, open since 2024 in a quieter corner of Namba, good for an unhurried dinner or a low-key business meal. The owner-chef is Vietnamese, and the course ends with a Japanese-style pho. The Harusai course (about ¥5,000) brings 12 of the chef's skewers, classics and seasonal ones, fried to order and handed over one at a time; details like asparagus cut into easy bites show the care. Add a quail egg if you have room. It ends unusually with a Japanese-style pho and ice cream. The draft beer is poured with real attention to the foam. The owner-chef is friendly and creative, and staff are attentive. Open for lunch too.

chef_bio.background: Kushiage counter (Tabelog, staff-maintained; 2026 reviews). The owner-chef is Vietnamese, and the course ends with a Japanese-style pho (July 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: "This course allows you to enjoy 12 of the restaurant's signature skewers, ranging from classic favorites to seasonal flavors, all selected by the chef… for dessert, we had Japanese-style pho and ice cream." — August 2026, Harusai course.
"The freshly fried kushi-katsu is served one by one, and the asparagus kushi-katsu is cut into easy-to-eat pieces, showcasing the care put into each dish." — August 2026.

places.notes: [Japanese · game-meat yakiniku of deer, bear and boar in Sennichimae] A retro-modern yakiniku room near Nippombashi, sister to the Ueda Shoten in Harinakano, that grills wild game rather than beef. The list depends on the season and the hunt: Ezo deer tataki and meaty ribs, crunchy Japanese deer tongue and heart, black bear thigh and sweet bear belly, wild boar loin, belly and top sirloin, and badger now and then. Diners are struck by how little gaminess there is. The ¥11,000 course (book ahead) opens with a small boar hot pot before the grill. Staff explain each cut while grilling, and service is slow when one person is working the room, so give it time. Many cuts sell out. Closed Sundays.

chef_bio.background: Game-meat yakiniku, sister shop of Ueda Shoten in Harinakano (July 2025 review; Tabelog, staff-maintained).

places.notes: [Japanese sweets · a wagashi house since 1868, known for chestnut steamed yokan] A long-established wagashi shop in Higashi-Shinsaibashi, dating to 1868 and picked for Tabelog's wagashi and sweets 100 lists, with a calm, old-fashioned front and a small sweets café inside. The star is the autumn kuri mushi yokan, red-bean steamed yokan packed with moist chestnuts and only gently sweet, sold whole (about ¥6,000) or half (about ¥3,000); there's a white-bean version too. The monaka is the most popular item and sells out first; in summer the mizu yokan and mizu manju are smooth and refined. Go early, as much is gone by late afternoon. It works as well for gifts as for an afternoon treat. Closed Sundays.

chef_bio.background: Wagashi maker (official site angetsu.co.jp, as 御菓子司 庵月堂); Tabelog Wagashi WEST 100 2023 and 2026, Sweets WEST 100 2019.

anecdotes.text: "You can see from the cross-section of the yokan that it is packed with chestnuts. When you take a bite, the red bean yokan has a chewy texture, while the chestnuts are crunchy and moist, delivering a strong chestnut flavor!" — October 2026, kuri mushi yokan.

places.notes: [Japanese · mentaiko-and-tororo hot pot to 1 am in Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A calm hot-pot izakaya in Higashi-Shinsaibashi, open since 2021 and featured on TV, open until 01:00 every night. The signature is the Hakata mentaiko tororo nabe: pork belly, chicken, fish balls and tofu in a good broth, crowned at the table with a heap of creamy grated yam and salty, spicy mentaiko, then finished as a cheese risotto. Sides are drinking food with flair: avocado yukke, a theatrically long toro-taku roll wrapped in thick nori, potato salad with truffle flakes, fresh oysters. All-you-can-drink is ¥1,500, so three drinks or more makes it worth it; one table spent just over ¥6,000 each. Staff finish the pot for you. A second branch, Bettei, is upstairs.

chef_bio.background: Hot-pot izakaya with a Bettei branch upstairs (Tabelog, staff-maintained).

anecdotes.text: "The Hakata Mentaiko Tororo Nabe had a stunning appearance with plenty of tororo and mentaiko on top! The creaminess of the tororo combined perfectly with the saltiness and umami of the mentaiko." — August 2026.

"The hot pot ingredients included not only the pork belly… but also chicken, fish balls, and tofu… the total bill was just over JPY 6000 per person. Since the all-you-can-drink option was JPY 1500, it's definitely worth it." — September 2026.

places.notes: [Ramen · clam and jidori clear ramen with a butter-risotto finish near Tanimachi 4-chome] A calm, roomy second-floor ramen shop in a building of eateries near Tanimachi 4-chome, open since 2021, easy to walk into alone. The Choro raa men (¥950) is a clear broth of clam and jidori chicken with strong umami and an elegant, gentle finish, in original shio (the staff's suggestion) or shellfish shoyu; pick melt-soft braised pork or rare chashu, and regular or smooth whole-grain noodles. At lunch the bigger "Choro-mori" portion and a small rice are free. Half the fun is the self-serve butter, grilled nori and Okuizumo sansho: add them midway, then drop the rice, the rest of the egg and a pat of butter into the broth for a risotto. Those wanting a big punch may find it subtle. Open daily; cards accepted.

places.notes: [Ramen · a seafood-only chuka soba with house noodles near Tanimachi 4-chome] A cozy, wood-fronted nine-seat counter near Tanimachi 4-chome, open since 2015 and lunch only, whose soup uses no meat stock and no chemical seasonings. The chuka soba (¥1,000) is a deep, slightly oily broth of niboshi, katsuobushi and kombu; choose rich or light soy (rich is the punchier pick). House-made medium-thin noodles, flecked with whole wheat, pick up the broth well, and the two rare chashu (beef chuck roll and chicken breast) are tender. For something bigger, one regular swears by the mazesoba, oyster with nori or horumon with sweet-spicy colon (¥1,400), finished with rice like a risotto. The owner is attentive. One diner found the light version unremarkable. Lunch Monday to Saturday, until sold out.

"This time, I ordered the oyster mazesoba. The seaweed adds a nice accent and enhances the ocean flavor. It's rich but incredibly delicious. At the end, I added rice, and it felt like a risotto." — April 2026.

places.cuisine: Garlic ramen open until 05:00 · ramen ¥1,100: light tonkotsu-shoyu of pork head, chicken feet, pork belly and vegetables, fresh minced garlic to taste, medium-thick curly noodles, thick, sweet, melting pork-belly chashu · set A +¥350: stir-fried takana, kimchi and rice · miso ramen ¥1,150, miso chashu B set · wakame ramen · "W vinegar" ramen ¥1,250 with black and balsamic vinegar, peppers, onion, ginger and garlic · hyaku-negi ramen ¥1,300 with 100 g of Kujo green onion · tsukemen ¥1,150 with fish powder · gyoza ¥450 · 21 counter seats
places.notes: [Ramen · garlic tonkotsu shoyu until 5 am by Taisho and Kyocera Dome] A lively local garlic-ramen shop under a yellow sign a few minutes from Taisho Station, open until 05:00 and busy after Kyocera Dome events. The base ramen (¥1,100) is a surprisingly light tonkotsu-shoyu, made, the shop says, from pork head, chicken feet, pork belly and vegetables; it comes alive when you load on the fresh minced garlic, adjustable when you order. Medium-thick curly noodles hold it well, and the thick pork-belly chashu melts. Add set A (+¥350) for stir-fried takana, kimchi and rice. Variations include a miso, a hyaku-negi bowl heaped with Kujo green onion, a tangy-spicy "W vinegar" ramen, and tsukemen. The same garlic-ramen name has a Shinmachi shop in this guide. Staff are friendly. Smoking allowed; AMEX only for cards.

chef_bio.philosophy: House tonkotsu of 40% pork head, 40% chicken feet, 10% pork belly and 10% vegetables (October 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: "The tonkotsu-based broth is surprisingly mild and not overly rich, offering a light texture. However, the addition of robust garlic gives it a powerful punch… The medium-thick curly noodles hold the broth well." — October 2026, ramen ¥1,100.
"The ramen itself lacks a bit of punch. However, when you add a generous amount of the separately served minced garlic, the flavor explodes." — October 2026.

places.notes: [Ramen · rich back-fat tonkotsu shoyu by JR Taisho Station] A small ramen shop seconds from JR Taisho, open here since 2017 and carrying on a bowl that late-night drinkers once loved at its former Kyobashi shop, with Orix memorabilia and signatures on the walls. The chuka soba is a thick soy tonkotsu glossed with back fat and a strong pork-bone aroma, nostalgic and indulgent but with a clean finish; the rich ajitama version is ¥1,000, and the special adds thick chashu. Choose thin straight noodles or thicker Chinese-style noodles; large is free. Add the moyashi chashu rice bowl (¥360). The pork aroma isn't for everyone, and one diner had cleanliness concerns. Handy before a Kyocera Dome event. Open to 23:00; closed Mondays.

places.notes: [Ramen · a ramen-and-set-meal diner by Tanimachi 6-chome] A casual ramen diner near Tanimachi 6-chome, open since 2012, where you can have a quick lunch set or settle in for beer, gyoza and fries at night, with the TV on. The lunch ramen set (¥990) pairs a rich soy tonkotsu with gyoza and rice. The spicy miso (¥1,140 with rice) is mild and creamy rather than fiery, with crunchy mizuna. There are chicken paitan bowls in shio or shoyu, rich and punchy, and a garlic-butter chicken ramen with thin noodles as a ¥1,600 set. Smaller mini-ramen sets suit lighter appetites, and garlic powder on the counter perks things up. One diner found the noodles a little soft. Short waits at lunch; open late most nights.

places.notes: [Sushi · sushi and tempura in one omakase, drinks included, in Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A seven-seat wooden counter in Higashi-Shinsaibashi, open since October 2025, whose omakase combines Edomae sushi with fresh tempura and makes the price easy: ¥15,000 with free-flow soft drinks, or ¥18,000 with alcohol. The chef has more than 25 years of experience. Expect a clear hamo soup, sawara sashimi, a striking mackerel "prosciutto," then crisp tempura of abalone, anago or nodoguro and maitake with yuzu-kosho salt, and a chawanmushi topped with Hokkaido sea urchin, before nigiri on lightly pressed red-vinegar rice, each fish prepared its own way and served at the right temperature: otoro, akami, generous uni. Diners note the knife work at the counter and a calm atmosphere for special occasions. Book ahead.

chef_bio.background: Sushi-and-tempura omakase counter (Tabelog, staff-maintained; 2026 reviews). The chef has more than 25 years of experience (September 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: "The sushi is made with red vinegar rice and seasonal fish, prepared in various styles such as marinated, seared, steamed, and boiled… The abalone tempura has a light batter that gives way to a delightful crunch." — September 2026.

"The standout for me was the mackerel prosciutto… As for the sushi, each piece was served at the appropriate temperature after checking the temperature of the ingredients." — September 2026, ¥15,000 course.

places.notes: [Yakiniku · thick-cut beef sliced to order at a Namba counter] A lively 14-seat yakiniku counter a minute from Namba Station, open since 2024, where staff cut the meat to order and season it in front of you. The thick-cut series is the reason to come: premium salted tongue with lemon and a thick outside skirt with wasabi soy, juicy and generously portioned. Start with kakuteki or cucumber kimchi, order rice even if you usually don't, and finish with a soupy curry ochazuke or curry zosui. The ¥5,000 recommended course is good value. One diner found the menu a little limited. The counter fills quickly, so book on Tabelog. Smoking allowed; open nightly until midnight.

"The style here involves cutting the meat right in front of you and seasoning it on the spot before serving. The meat was fresh, and the seasoning was exquisite." — August 2026.

places.notes: [Japanese · a one-chef counter kappo hidden under Dotonbori] A ten-seat counter in a basement in the heart of Dotonbori, open since 2013 and run by one chef, with a back door onto a terrace over the Dotonbori River. The cooking is creative seasonal Japanese served on fine tableware: chilled chawanmushi with eggplant in summer, sashimi such as bluefin tuna, and in autumn a sanma rice one diner called amazing. One regular never looks at the menu and simply leaves it to the chef; à la carte works too. The sake list is wide, with rarities like a sparkling sake from Okayama, and the value draws praise. Despite the location it feels calm, not touristy, and the counter invites chat with the chef and neighbors. Lunch on Wednesday and Friday to Sunday is an omakase (¥5,800, two or more, book by the day before). Closed Mondays.

chef_bio.background: Counter kappo run by the owner alone (September 2025 review; Tabelog, staff-maintained).

anecdotes.text: "The owner was managing everything alone, but the dishes were presented efficiently, one by one. The tableware was also quite exquisite. The selection of drinks was extensive, and I even got to try a rare sparkling Japanese sake from Okayama." — September 2025, lunch course.
"I usually don't even look at the menu and just let the master prepare dishes for me. It's a hidden gem for creative Japanese cuisine in Minami." — December 2025.

places.notes: [Japanese · grill-your-own dried fish over charcoal off Dotonbori] A basement izakaya under a green lantern in Dotonbori 2-chome, open since 2002, where you grill Shizuoka dried fish and vegetables yourself over a tabletop charcoal brazier. The assorted platter brings mackerel, horse mackerel and shishamo; shiitake come out bursting with juice, and there's a surprisingly good beef platter of thick tongue, wagyu short rib and tenderloin. Summer adds hamo with grated daikon and ponzu. Order the kamameshi when you sit down, since it's cooked to order and takes over 30 minutes; the salmon and ikura is the pick. Ingredients are mostly domestic, and the sake and shochu lists are strong. The room is calm, with a counter and tatami tables. Book a day ahead for weekend lunch or a 17:00 start.

chef_bio.background: Charcoal-grill izakaya (Tabelog, staff-maintained).
chef_bio.philosophy: Safe ingredients, mainly from domestic producers (Tabelog listing).

places.notes: [Okonomiyaki · a hidden teppan izakaya open until 3 am in Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A teppan izakaya at the very end of a narrow corridor in a Higashi-Shinsaibashi building, running for about 27 years, whose sliding door opens onto a cozy counter and a cheerful owner. The Chinese-style fried rice comes from a recipe shared by Nakamura, a friend of the owner's mother. One regular has lost count of visits; the draw is drinking food from the griddle: kasu hari (abura kasu with crisp mizuna, ¥770), ten cheese, sautéed scallops, and okonomiyaki such as pork and egg crowned with a runny fried egg. Finish with salt yakisoba with crisp pork fat, or a curry yakisoba. It's often full of reservations, so book or call ahead. Open until 03:00; closed Sundays; cash only; smoking allowed.

chef_bio.background: Teppan izakaya (official site on toxnavi.com; Tabelog, staff-maintained). The Chinese-style fried rice comes from a recipe shared by Nakamura, a friend of the owner's mother (May 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: "This dish features oil kasu and mizuna, giving it a refreshing crunch. The crisp texture of the mizuna combined with the rich flavor of the oil kasu made it delicious." — May 2026, kasu hari ¥770.
"Okonomiyaki with Pork and Egg → It came topped with a fried egg. At first, the combination of the runny egg and the soft okonomiyaki made it easy to eat." — December 2025.

places.notes: [Ramen · chicken paitan and clam shoyu, with wagyu sushi, by Tanimachi 4-chome] A lunch-only shop on the ground floor of the Dia Palace building in Uchihonmachi (the clam-and-chicken ramen shop Choro is upstairs), open since November 2024. Every regular bowl is ¥900. The paitan, the shop says, is a "triple soup" of three chickens, Yamagata pork and Kuroge wagyu tendon; one diner smelled a neighbor's bowl and called the aroma "comparable to tonkotsu ramen." For something lighter, the chicken and clam shoyu comes with thin noodles and yuzu. Add the ¥400 wagyu roast sushi, seared in front of you, or the ¥300 seared chashu-mayo rice bowl. A soy-milk cold tantanmen with yodare-dori chicken ran in summer 2026 and drew raves, though one diner found it bland. Lunch only, closed Sunday and Monday, cash only; one diner found it closed before last order.

places.cuisine: Miso ramen specialist (chain) · Hokkaido 100-year miso ramen: aged, salty Hokkaido red miso, seared to deepen it · butter-corn version, with half fried rice ¥1,500 · samurai ramen with egg, katsu and thick chashu · spicy miso ¥980, three heat levels · gin no maro miso: mild Kyushu barley miso · kin no aburi miso: three-year red miso seared with white wine, almond and sansho, katsu option · beef-offal miso · medium-thick egg noodles or whole-wheat noodles · lunch sets about ¥900 with fried rice or rice · gyoza · kids' miso ramen · 20 seats
places.notes: [Ramen · miso ramen specialist facing Utsubo Park] A branch of a miso-only ramen chain in front of Utsubo Park, open since 2021 with plenty of tables. The base is the chain's Hokkaido 100-year miso, a salty aged red miso it sears to draw out depth; one diner found it rich and robust, "perfect for when you're craving a rich bowl." If that's too strong for you, the silver miso uses a milder Kyushu barley miso, though one diner found it too mild. The gold miso is seared with white wine, almond and sansho; a spicy miso (¥980) comes in three heats. Lunch sets run about ¥900 with fried rice or plain rice, though one diner found the set ramen too simple and another warned off the fried rice. There's a kids' miso ramen too. Lunch can draw a short line.

chef_bio.background: Branch of the miso-ramen-only chain Menya Kunimaru (official site kunimaru.net).
chef_bio.philosophy: "Miso is a health food": four base misos, seared to draw out richness and aroma; medium-thick egg noodles and whole-wheat noodles (official site).

anecdotes.text: "The broth has a rich and robust flavor, showcasing the depth and umami of the miso… Despite its strong seasoning, the ramen is well-balanced." — October 2026, Hokkaido 100-year miso ramen.
"It has a mild miso flavor, and if you're looking for a rich and deep miso ramen… I recommend the 100-Year Miso Ramen instead." — June 2026, silver miso ramen.

places.notes: [Ramen · chicken paitan and big chashu set meals in Uchihonmachi] A small counter of about 10 seats a few minutes from Sakaisuji-Honmachi, running since 2011 and specializing in chicken paitan. The ajitama paitan (¥1,000) is rich yet relatively light, with thick-cut pork-belly chashu; at lunch you get a free large serving of noodles or rice. The other draw is the chashu set meal: 150 g or 250 g of chashu with mayonnaise and black pepper, a neatly rounded mound of rice, kimchi and soup, ¥1,300 for the large. There are also a classic ramen one diner found nostalgic, and Taiwanese mazesoba. Buy tickets at the machine outside; it takes ¥1,000 notes only. Snug, so not for groups. Cash only.

places.cuisine: Shoyu ramen, open late · signature shoyu ramen ¥950: clear, gentle broth with a slightly sweet shoyu, chashu, menma, red onion and chili; flat noodles +¥100; garlic served on the side · "umakara" spicy ramen ¥990: slightly sweet shoyu with chili · choose noodle firmness, yuzu peel, garlic, green onion and onion · seafood shoyu ramen · tantanmen; chilled tantanmen in summer · miso ramen with flat noodles · free rice at lunch · counter and tables
places.notes: [Ramen · clear, slightly sweet shoyu until 6 am Fri–Sat in Honmachi] A busy office-district ramen shop near Sakaisuji-Honmachi with good turnover at lunch and late hours: until 23:00 most nights and 06:00 into Saturday and Sunday. The signature shoyu ramen (¥950) is a clear, gentle broth with a hint of sweetness in the soy, with chashu, menma, red onion and chili; flat noodles are ¥100 more, and the garlic comes on the side; one diner found it changed the bowl a lot. You choose noodle firmness and add-ons like yuzu peel and onion. The "umakara" (¥990) adds a stronger chili kick to that sweet shoyu. There's also a seafood shoyu, a tantanmen one diner came back for four times (chilled in summer), and a miso ramen. Free rice at lunch.

anecdotes.text: "The broth was indeed clear and gentle, with a hint of sweetness in the shoyu flavor… I added a bit of garlic, but it significantly changed the taste, so I prefer it without. I'm glad it was served separately." — August 2026, shoyu ramen ¥950.
"The spiciness from the chili was stronger than I expected. The base broth seems to use a slightly sweet soy sauce." — September 2026, umakara ramen ¥990.

places.cuisine: Light Hakata-style tonkotsu · tonkotsu ramen ¥700: milky, light, creamy pork-bone broth, straight thin noodles cooked to your firmness, grilled chashu, green onion, bean sprouts · variations on the same base: tonkotsu shoyu, garlic with sliced garlic, butter, spicy, tomato ramen with halved tomatoes, tantanmen · extra noodles ¥100 · lunch: any regular ramen + mentaiko rice, diced chashu rice or white rice ¥800 · two tables and about seven counter seats
places.notes: [Ramen · light Hakata tonkotsu for ¥700 in the Dia Palace basement] A small, one-person ramen shop in the basement of the Dia Palace building in Uchihonmachi, the same building as Choro and Menya Odashi to Niku to, open since 2021. The tonkotsu ramen (¥700) is a milky but light, creamy pork-bone soup with very little odor, on straight thin Kyushu-style noodles cooked to the firmness you ask for. Everything else is a variation on that base: tonkotsu shoyu, sliced-garlic, butter, spicy, a tomato ramen and tantanmen. At lunch, ¥800 gets any regular ramen with mentaiko rice, diced chashu rice or plain rice, though the rice sometimes runs out. One diner found the staff attentive in explaining things to overseas visitors. It's light rather than heavy, so one diner wished it were more filling. Cards and QR accepted.

anecdotes.text: "It had a milky broth, three slices of grilled chashu, green onions, and bean sprouts… it was a light and creamy tonkotsu soup… straight thin noodles, quite a generous portion!" — May 2024, tonkotsu ramen ¥700.
"The richness is kept in check, resulting in a creamy pork bone soup without any heaviness or unpleasant odors… The noodles were thin with a nice snap." — June 2025, tomato ramen.

places.cuisine: Lunch-only ramen counter · shoyu ramen: salty seafood-and-pork broth, thick grilled chashu, egg · shio ramen: strong salt and pepper, two slices of chashu, menma, wood ear, green onion, egg, spinach, nori · vegetable noodles, large ¥950: crab sticks, wood ear, roast pork · tantanmen ¥900, mild heat · sour-spicy noodles ¥900 topped with fresh tomato · rice the only side · about 15 counter seats facing the wall
places.notes: [Ramen · salty shoyu and shio, vegetable noodles and tantanmen at lunch in Honmachi] A bright, clean lunch-only counter of about 15 wall-facing seats under Chinese-style lanterns, a little inside its building near Sakaisuji-Honmachi, open since 2019. The ramen runs salty: the shoyu is a seafood-and-pork broth "for those who enjoy bold flavors" with thick grilled chashu, and the shio hits hard with salt and pepper, which one diner likened to a much-upgraded Sugakiya. Beyond those there are vegetable noodles (¥950 large) with crab sticks and wood ear, a mild tantanmen (¥900) for the heat-shy, and sour-spicy noodles (¥900) topped with fresh tomato. Buy the ticket at the machine outside; water is self-service. Lunch is quieter by about 12:30. Cash only.

chef_bio.background: Ramen counter (Tabelog; 2025–2026 reviews).
chef_bio.specialty: Shoyu and shio ramen; vegetable noodles; tantanmen.

anecdotes.text: "The broth seemed to be a seafood and pork blend. It had a relatively strong salty taste, but it wasn't overwhelming… Those who enjoy bold flavors might like it!" — September 2025, shoyu ramen.
"I found the saltiness to be quite strong with a noticeable pepper kick… While the salt flavor hits hard, it was nice that it didn't leave an unpleasant aftertaste." — March 2026, shio ramen.

places.cuisine: Chicken paitan, one chef · chicken paitan ramen ¥850: thick, velvety, concentrated paitan on smooth straight thin noodles, tender chashu, long menma, soft-boiled egg (+¥150), red onion, crisp green onion, bonito flakes; spicy miso on the side · an even richer, thicker paitan · chuka soba · warm mazesoba ¥850 · summer: chilled sea bream shio ramen ¥850 with chicken breast, egg, naruto, kaiware and yuzu salt (limited) · rice ¥100 · about 8 counter seats
places.notes: [Ramen · thick chicken paitan from a one-chef counter by Uehommachi] A clean, eight-seat counter a few minutes from Uehommachi where one chef cooks fast, open since 2020. The chicken paitan (¥850) is thick and velvety, "rich yet not overwhelming" to one diner, with smooth straight thin noodles, tender chashu, long menma, red onion and bonito flakes. Stir in the spicy miso on the side little by little; it's hot. For more, there's an even richer, thicker paitan; a chuka soba one diner prefers; and a warm mazesoba. In summer, a chilled sea bream shio ramen with yuzu salt sells in limited numbers. Finish the soup with ¥100 rice. Mark your order on the sheet at the counter and pay cash after. One diner hit clumps of salt. Lunch only on Wednesday and Saturday.

anecdotes.text: "The rich, creamy broth with a concentration level of 8 was thick and velvety, a truly luxurious white soup… The scattered bonito flakes added a vibrant aroma." — October 2024, rich chicken paitan.
"The rich flavor of the chicken broth paired perfectly with Menya Teikaku's smooth, straight, thin noodles… my preference still leans towards the 'Chuka Soba.'" — August 2026, chicken paitan ¥850.

places.notes: [Ramen · tantanmen in several flavors near Sakaisuji-Honmachi] A tantanmen shop behind a neon sign, opened in October 2025, that one diner learned is a sister shop of the Honmachi Chinese restaurant Koyouju. Start with the "Moto-Aji" original (¥950): a rich, only mildly spicy soup under a generous minced-meat sauce, bean sprouts and greens, on fairly thin noodles; one diner couldn't stop drinking the soup, which changes as the meat sauce mixes in. There are also "Shin-Aji" and miso versions, a shoyu tanmen and a sour-spicy suanshu tanmen; in summer a chilled spicy tantanmen (¥1,200) ran, though one diner wanted more heat. It also works as a casual Chinese spot: one diner had mapo tofu, pork and bean-sprout stir-fry, a half tantanmen and two lemon sours at 8 pm for under ¥2,500. Counter, tables and a terrace. Cards and QR accepted.

chef_bio.background: Tantanmen shop; one diner learned it is a sister shop of the Chinese restaurant Koyouju in Honmachi (September 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: "It was topped generously with meat sauce… it's interesting how the flavor of the soup changes depending on where you drink it from. When I scooped some meat sauce and drank it, the richness of the meat added a different dimension." — September 2026, Moto-Aji ¥950.
"It had a distinctive aroma that was a bit unusual, but it quickly blended into a harmonious flavor. On the other hand, the noodles were quite thin." — October 2026.

places.cuisine: Edomae sushi omakase on red-vinegar rice · omakase ¥19,800 (September 2026): Hokkaido oysters with ponzu, boiled octopus, bonito tataki, grilled eel with crisp skin, otoro, chutoro and soy-marinated akami of natural bluefin, steamed abalone with liver sauce and rice to mop it up, ikura chawanmushi, squid, sea bream, kohada, Hokkaido sea urchin with caviar, Kumamoto prawn, simmered anago, red miso soup of fish bones, iburigakko and toro-taku hand roll, a pudding-like tamago to finish · firm 10-year-aged akazu rice, white vinegar for some toppings · 8 seats at a single hinoki counter
places.notes: [Sushi · red-vinegar sushi omakase at an eight-seat counter with a Namba night view] An eighth-floor, eight-seat counter of single-board hinoki in Soemoncho, open since February 2025, a sister shop of Sushi Akazu in Shinsaibashi. The omakase (¥19,800 in September 2026) runs in two seatings and builds around firm rice seasoned with aged red vinegar; one diner who worried it wouldn't suit loved it. Expect Hokkaido oysters in ponzu, a tuna trio of otoro, chutoro and marinated akami, steamed abalone whose liver sauce you finish over a little rice, sea urchin crowned with caviar, soft simmered anago, then a smoked-daikon toro-taku hand roll and a pudding-like tamago that plays dessert. One diner mentions the friendly chef, others the Minami night view, and two call it an anniversary or date place. BYO costs ¥5,000 a bottle.

chef_bio.background: Red-vinegar sushi counter; sister shop of Sushi Akazu in Shinsaibashi (Tabelog).
chef_bio.philosophy: Firm rice of 10-year-aged red vinegar, white vinegar for some toppings (September 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: "The sushi was made with a firm 10-year aged akazu rice, with white vinegar used for certain toppings… after finishing it, I placed the leftover liver sauce on the rice… what surprised me was the additional liver sauce!" — September 2026, omakase ¥19,800.
"…I was honestly a bit nervous about whether it would suit my taste, but I was pleasantly surprised by how much I loved it." — September 2026, on the red-vinegar rice.

places.cuisine: Aged-fish sushi omakase · aged sushi omakase ¥14,800 (October 2026): about 18 dishes, 10–12 nigiri with sashimi, grilled and simmered dishes and soup · sea bream with Tosa-vinegar jelly finished over binchotan · aori squid flash-frozen and finely scored, with Himalayan salt and sudachi · shima aji aged 7 days · chawanmushi with king and snow crab · Kesennuma bonito seared with ginger · dry-aged chutoro on rice kept at 42°C · Densuke anago shabu-shabu · signature botan ebi with shrimp roe and sea urchin · Saikyo-miso yuan-grilled yellowtail · kinmedai aged 6 days · kanpachi roll with gari, green onion and honey ume · fish-bone soup · "noble cocktail" of the day's trimmings with alum-free sea urchin · marinated akami · vanilla pudding · counter and private rooms, 18 seats
places.notes: [Sushi · aged-fish sushi omakase by Dotonbori] A reservation-only sushi counter on the third floor of a new building in Nishi-Shinsaibashi, open since May 2025, built around fish aged for different lengths of time. The ¥14,800 omakase runs to about 18 dishes: sea bream under a Tosa-vinegar jelly finished over binchotan, aori squid flash-frozen and finely scored, seven-day shima aji, dry-aged chutoro on rice kept warmer at 42°C so the fat melts, Densuke anago swished as shabu-shabu, and the signature botan ebi topped with shrimp roe and sea urchin. A fish-bone soup simmered for hours and a vanilla pudding close it. Diners praise the explanations and playful touches; one was surprised with a birthday plate. One diner noticed many overseas guests. There's a 5% service charge. Lunch on weekends.

chef_bio.background: Reservation-only aged-sushi counter (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
chef_bio.philosophy: "Ultimate umami with time as an ally": different aging days for each fish and rice temperature varied by topping (October 2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "The medium fatty tuna, aged for 14 days, was served with rice at 42 degrees Celsius, the perfect temperature for melting the tuna's fat… The signature dish, botan ebi (sweet shrimp), was topped with uni (sea urchin) and egg." — October 2026, aged sushi omakase ¥14,800.
"A rich soup made by roasting fish bones for about 20 minutes and simmering for 4 hours." — October 2026.

places.notes: [Shabu-shabu · Okinawan Agu pork shabu-shabu in Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A clean, reservation-only shabu-shabu room near Shinsaibashi that serves Okinawa's Agu pork, sliced and arranged like a rose; repeat diners come back for meat that is sweet and "not greasy at all." The ¥5,280 course opens with crunchy mozuku vinegar, then the hot pot, with homemade ponzu heaped with green onion, a sesame sauce and yuzu-kosho; wrap the pork around green onion or pickled island garlic. Staff explain the pot and serve the first round. Finish with zosui or Okinawa soba made with Ishigaki noodles, and add the sweet purple sweet potato tempura. One repeat diner always buys the ponzu to take home. Order a course or the hot pot per person, or a per-head charge applies. There's a second branch in Namba.

anecdotes.text: "The meat was beautifully arranged in the shape of a rose… You can enjoy it with a dipping sauce filled with plenty of green onions and ponzu, along with yuzu pepper." — August 2026.

places.notes: [Standing bar · horumon and game, from kangaroo to badger, by Nippombashi] A retro standing bar behind a plastic-sheet door just off Sennichimae-dori, picked for Tabelog's tachinomi 100 in 2025, where 1980s and 90s J-pop plays on a big screen and you mix your own highball from bottled soda. The owner runs the shop with two female staff members. The draw is fresh offal and game: Matsusaka beef garlic small intestine (¥580), a seared Miyazaki beef yukhoe with egg yolk (¥980), and a kangaroo tenderloin steak (¥720) diners find tender, juicy and not gamey. Venison and wild boar are staples; pheasant, badger (as a winter hot pot), camel and sea lion turn up when in stock, camel announced on the shop's Instagram. Liver and the rarer cuts go fast, so come at opening; there can be a line. The weekend curry wins praise from the few who order it. Portions are small and prices exclude tax. Cash only.

chef_bio.background: Standing bar for horumon and game; Tabelog tachinomi 100, 2025 (Tabelog). The owner runs the shop with two female staff members (October 2026 review).
chef_bio.specialty: Horumon of Matsusaka and Miyazaki beef; game meats.

places.notes: [Ramen · cafe-style ramen with coffee on the ground floor of My Dome Osaka] A big, calm, 100-seat ramen cafe on the ground floor of the My Dome Osaka exhibition hall, opened in August 2025 by the company behind Choro. The bowls are light: a chicken-based shoyu on straight thin noodles with thin slices of duck chashu, a niboshi shoyu (¥950) and a miso, with seasonal changes. The popular lunch set pairs shoyu ramen with yakimeshi and a drip coffee for ¥1,000; others come with lu rou fan or seasoned rice, and there's a kara-age set (¥900) and Basque cheesecake. Two diners found the shoyu on the salty side. With Wi-Fi, outlets, raised tatami seating and a kids' menu, it suits families and laptop lunches. Order at the touch-panel ticket machine and clear your own table.

places.notes: [Ramen · chicken-tonkotsu paitan, tsukemen and abura soba by Tanimachi 4-chome] A small counter of about seven seats near Tanimachi 4-chome, with tables upstairs when it fills after noon, running since 2018. The ramen (¥900) is a chicken and pork-bone paitan that one diner found hearty, with short medium-thin noodles and thin, well-seasoned pork-belly chashu; add the A set (+¥150) for two kara-age and rice. The tsukemen (¥980) pairs medium-thick chewy noodles with a chicken, pork-bone and seafood dip, light in body but oily on top, with a little acidity. The abura soba (¥890) comes regular or Japanese-style, dressed in soy and shrimp oil over thick glossy noodles; at lunch ¥1,070 adds kara-age and rice. One diner found the menma flat and the welcome cool. Dinner on weekends depends on the soup.

anecdotes.text: "The soup is a chicken and pork bone white broth, and after taking a sip, I could taste the richness of the chicken combined with the depth and umami of the pork bone… The noodles are short, medium-thin, with a nice chewiness." — September 2025, ramen ¥900.
"The dipping sauce was made from chicken, pork bones, and seafood. It had a light consistency with a generous amount of oil on the surface… a hint of acidity." — September 2025, tsukemen ¥980.

places.cuisine: Lunch-only shio ramen in an Italian restaurant · shio ramen ¥1,000: chicken and aromatic-vegetable broth with herbs and spices, thin Menya Teikaku noodles, rare chashu, lemon on the side · shoyu ramen · smaller noodle portion · toppings: umeboshi, yuzu-kosho, menma · chashu rice bowl, rice · 19 seats
places.notes: [Ramen · herb-scented shio ramen at lunch in an Italian restaurant, Awajimachi] A stylish room between Honmachi and Yodoyabashi that serves Italian food at night and turns into a ramen shop at lunch, open since March 2025. The shio ramen (¥1,000) is the bowl to get: a rich chicken and aromatic-vegetable broth drawn out with herbs and spices, which one diner likened to Italian dressing, with rare chashu and thin noodles. A lemon wedge comes on the side; squeeze it in midway for a brighter, almost pho-like finish. Add umeboshi or yuzu-kosho for more changes. One diner brought a 2026 Kansai ramen guide that gave the shio a semi-grand prize. There's also a shoyu, and a chashu rice bowl that sells out. A small noodle portion is very small. Lunch only; a line formed after noon one April day.

chef_bio.background: Ramen at lunch in a restaurant that serves Italian at night (2026 reviews; Tabelog).
chef_bio.philosophy: Shio broth drawn with herbs and spices, per a 2026 Kansai ramen guide cited by a diner (June 2026).

anecdotes.text: "The broth, infused with the aroma and flavor of herbs typical of Italian cuisine, was rich and savory… a lemon for flavor enhancement is provided by default, and squeezing it… gives a slightly Asian twist, reminiscent of pho broth." — May 2026, shio ramen.
"I added umeboshi (pickled plum), yuzu pepper, and menma (bamboo shoots) as toppings. I really liked the thin, smooth noodles that paired well with the broth." — June 2026.

places.cuisine: Thick chicken-and-vegetable "doro" soba · doro soba with richness level to order: soup of chicken and vegetables simmered until they dissolve, thin flat or medium wavy noodles, chashu, fried green onion, fried eringi, green onion · lunch doro soba + mini chashu rice bowl set · spicy "extreme" doro soba ¥1,500 · "Oni Kyoku" extra-thick doro soba ¥1,600 · doro tsukemen · lunch mini kara-age rice bowl +¥100 · pink pickled ginger on the counter · 11 counter seats and a table for four
places.notes: [Ramen · thick chicken-and-vegetable "doro" soba near Kitahama] A small office-district counter between Kitahama and Sakaisuji-Honmachi, open since 2020 and, one diner says, one of the chain's last two shops along with Nara, serving doro soba: a soup of chicken and vegetables simmered until they dissolve, so thick it clings to the noodles "like a purée." Two diners were surprised how easy it is to drink and how clean the finish is; one found the flavor ordinary beneath the texture. Choose your richness, from the basic bowl up to the extra-thick Oni Kyoku (¥1,600), or a spicy version (¥1,500). Toppings of fried green onion and eringi add aroma, and pink pickled ginger from the counter sweetens and shifts the soup. At lunch there's a doro soba set with a mini chashu rice bowl, or add a mini kara-age bowl for ¥100. Buy a ticket first; staff help if you're unsure. Cash only.

places.notes: [Ramen · niboshi chuka soba with back fat, on Tabelog's Ramen 100 since 2017, in Kyomachibori] A seven-seat counter near Awaza, open since 2012 and picked for Tabelog's Ramen 100 every year from 2017 to 2025, with early-morning hours from Thursday to Sunday and late nights most days. The niboshi ramen (¥950) is gentler than the name suggests: a mild soy base with floating back fat and a pleasant niboshi bitterness, on medium-thick curly noodles; one diner thought of Yamagata ramen. The special niboshi mazesoba (¥1,300) is the other draw: sweet-savory soy and concentrated niboshi over wide, chewy curly noodles from Kyoto's Menya Teigaku, piled with block and rare chashu; one diner said the regular version would do. There can be a line at night, with chairs outside. Cards, e-money and QR accepted. A second shop is in Nakazakicho.

places.notes: [Ramen · shoyu on medium-thick curly noodles and karasumi mazesoba, by Shitennoji] A tiny eight-seat shop near Shitennoji, open since 2022 and picked for Tabelog's Ramen 100 in 2024 and 2025. The noodles are the point: robust, flat, medium-thick and curly, which one diner was "a bit moved" to find. The shoyu ramen is light with niboshi umami (¥1,250 with wontons and egg); the rich shoyu adds a strong garlic hit, aosa seaweed and fish powder to stir in. For heat, the Inazuma chuka soba and mazesoba layer chili, sansho and black pepper over sweet soy and back fat. A repeat diner's favorite is the chilled mazesoba with karasumi, green onion and niboshi, finished with a warm egg sauce, though the shio with beef tendon, clams and niboshi may top it. Seats are few, so expect a short wait at noon. Pay first, cash only.

anecdotes.text: "It was light yet flavorful, with a nice umami from the niboshi (dried sardines). Then came the medium-thick curly noodles. I was a bit moved to encounter such a perfect noodle." — October 2026, shoyu ramen with wontons and egg ¥1,250.

"With a combination of chili peppers, sansho pepper, and black pepper, the spices amplify the flavors, while the sweetness of the soy sauce and back fat accelerates the stimulation." — October 2026, Inazuma chuka soba.

places.notes: [Ramen · rich tonkotsu with free rice at lunch near Higobashi] A second-floor ramen shop near Higobashi with flashy decor, open since 2012 and the main branch of its name. The tonkotsu ramen (¥950) is a rich, slightly grainy pork-bone soup with a pleasant pork aroma, deep but not too salty, on thick, firm noodles; one diner tasted seafood in it too. Two chashu come with it: a smoky, sweet-fatted belly block and a meaty loin. At lunch the rice is free and self-serve, with pickled greens, tsukudani and takana; one diner had two bowls, and when it sold out the staff found some leftovers. Add garlic and chili powder from the table. The black tonkotsu seemed the more popular order to one diner. Open until midnight Monday to Thursday, lunch only Friday to Sunday.

"There were two types of chashu: the belly block was tender and had a pleasant sweetness from the fat, while the loin was packed with robust meat flavor." — September 2026.

places.notes: [Ramen · thick chicken paitan and full toppings at lunch in Kitahama] A bright basement ramen shop in the Kitahama office district, open since 2020 for lunch Monday to Saturday; one September day it was full by 11:15. Arrive by 11:30 for a free mini rice bowl. The chicken nikomi ramen (¥900) is a thick, creamy chicken paitan with a sweet chicken-fat finish that doesn't feel heavy afterward; pick thin or medium-thick noodles. The chicken and seafood (¥900) is flavorful but not too heavy. For +¥300 the full toppings bury the noodles in grilled and rare chashu, egg, nori and green onion. Tsukemen and a chicken shoyu round out the menu. After 13:30 you get almond tofu or a black coffee on the house. Cash only.

No fixed closing time; one diner joined the line at 16:00 and waited two hours (October 2026). Lines of about 40 by opening and waits of 1¾–2 hours (October 2026). Takeaway only. places.cuisine: Ohagi, made to order, takeaway only · box of 6 ¥1,170: choose up to two of koshian (smooth red bean), tsubuan (chunky red bean) and kinako (roasted soybean flour) · small pieces of soft, lightly crushed glutinous rice · gentle sweetness with a hint of salt in the anko; fine kinako · kinako best the same day, anko until the next morning
places.notes: [Sweets · made-to-order ohagi with a two-hour line, by Nippombashi] A small, long-standing ohagi shop off Sennichimae-dori (often called Tamaseiya), picked for Tabelog's sweets lists from 2017 to 2026, that opens at 14:00 four days a week and closes when it sells out. There's one thing to buy: a box of six small ohagi (¥1,170), choosing up to two of smooth red bean, chunky red bean and kinako, made fresh after you order, so the line is slow; October diners waited one and three-quarter to two hours, and about 40 people were queued by opening. The anko is gently sweet with a touch of salt, the kinako fine, the rice soft and lightly crushed, and even people who dislike ohagi like them. Eat the kinako ones the same day; anko keeps until the next morning. Takeaway only, cash only.

chef_bio.background: Ohagi shop; Tabelog sweets 100 (2017–2022) and Japanese sweets WEST 100 (2023, 2026) (Tabelog).

anecdotes.text: "I arrived at 1:20 PM, 40 minutes before opening, and there were already about 20 people in line… by opening time, around 40 people were waiting." — October 2026.

"The soybean flour is pleasantly sweet, and the red bean paste has a gentle sweetness with a hint of salt. The soft texture… combined with the chewy, slightly crushed glutinous rice is simply delightful!" — October 2026.

places.name: PIENO vivace (ピエーノヴィヴァーチェ)
places.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: pasta and pizza are the core; baguette with the ajillo; spring-roll wrappers.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: uni cream pasta, carpaccio, prosciutto, burrata, beef.
places.hours_raw: Wed–Mon 17:00–24:00 (L.O. 23:00); closed Tue (Tabelog). Small: reserve for Friday and Saturday evenings and for tables; call for the counter with three or more (Tabelog; 2026 reviews). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners) and PayPay accepted (Tabelog).
places.neighborhood: Namba 4-8-2, Daiko Center 1F, at the end of the street by the Hanshin Expressway — 2 min from Namba Stn exit 21
places.cuisine: Italian bar · signature uni cream pasta ¥1,188 · three-fish carpaccio (sea bream, yellowtail, salmon) ¥1,298 · seasonal fruit and mascarpone prosciutto spring rolls ¥1,078 · beef skirt teppan steak ¥1,408 · oyster ajillo with baguette · prosciutto salad · burrata · pizza with a runny egg · roast beef tartare · Genovese, tomato-cream and other pastas cooked firm · handwritten daily specials · homemade sangria; wine list with descriptions · 10 counter seats and a semi-private room for about 10
places.notes: [Italian · uni pasta, carpaccio and wine in a tiny Ura-Namba bar] A small, nearly always full Italian bar at the end of a backstreet in Ura-Namba, open since 2009 and one of several PIENO shops. It shares the main shop's menu, so start with the three-fish carpaccio (¥1,298) and the fig, mascarpone and prosciutto spring rolls, add the oyster ajillo or a skirt steak, and finish with the signature uni cream pasta (¥1,188). Pasta comes firm; one diner came back ten years on for the unchanged Genovese. Handwritten specials change daily, the wine list explains itself, and the sangria is homemade. One diner spent about ¥5,000 with drinks, another about ¥8,000 with two bottles of red between two. It's cramped, so skip it with big luggage and reserve for Friday or Saturday evenings.

chef_bio.background: One of the PIENO Italian bars run by the Yasumaru group, which lists several PIENO shops in Namba and one in Kochi (official site yasumaru.co.jp).

anecdotes.text: "The basic menu is the same as the main Pieno location, but there are many handwritten daily specials. The signature dish at Pieno is the sea urchin pasta… The carpaccio here is a standout, made with fresh seafood." — August 2026.

"I particularly recommend the Genovese pasta. I used to come here just to eat this pasta ten years ago. I was really happy to see it still on the menu and that the taste remained the same." — October 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式 yasumaru.co.jp: PIENO vivace、大阪市中央区難波4-8-2 大幸センター 1F、20席(カウンター10、半個室約10)、15名以上で貸切可、系列にPIENO、PIENO villa、PIENO di cibo、PIENO festa、高知のPIENO settimo、ENO cafe、肉屋まるはち。食べログ: なんば駅21番出口から徒歩2分、毎日17:00〜24:00(L.O. 23:00)、火休み、3名以上のカウンター利用は電話で、カード・PayPay可、2009年10月4日開店。口コミ(2025年2月〜2026年10月): 裏なんばの通りの突き当たり、阪神高速の見える場所、ほぼ満席、金土の18時半〜19時は予約なしでは難しい、本店と同じ基本メニューに手書きの日替わり、名物の雲丹パスタ、カルパッチョ、アヒージョ、生ハムサラダ、自家製サングリア、パスタは固めの茹で加減、アクアパッツァ、ブッラータ、半熟卵のピザ、トマトクリームパスタ、3号店、高知にも店、ローストビーフのタルタル、一人5,000円ほど、ジェノベーゼを10年前から、赤ワイン2本で一人約8,000円、ワインの説明付き、鮮魚3種のカルパッチョ1,298円(鯛、鰤、サーモン)、季節のフルーツとマスカルポーネの生春巻き1,078円(生ハム、無花果)、牛ハラミの鉄板焼き1,408円、牡蠣のアヒージョとバゲット、雲丹のパスタ1,188円、狭いカウンター、ワインが豊富、量が多い。

places.name: わびすけ 難波本店 (Wabisuke Namba Honten)
places.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: dashi-soy seasoning throughout; kara-age, ham katsu, fried horse mackerel and tempura; spaghetti salad.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: dashi in the obanzai and omelet; beef, pork miso soup, seafood.
places.hours_raw: Mon–Sat 11:30–15:00 (L.O. 14:30; lunch ends when sold out) and 17:30–23:30 (L.O. 23:00); Sun 17:30–23:30 (Tabelog). Lunch lines of 10–20 from before opening; staff take orders in the line (September–October 2026). Evenings are easier. PayPay accepted; no cards or e-money (Tabelog).
places.neighborhood: Namba 4-8-3, in the Ura-Namba backstreets — 80 m from Osaka-Namba Stn
places.cuisine: Obanzai counter izakaya · lunch set ¥900: one main from six (niku dashimaki — fluffy dashi omelet topped with beef — kara-age and others) with 3–4 obanzai, a little sashimi, tonjiru and rice with refills; beer set swaps rice for a draft · evening: assorted obanzai "5 kinds" (often six) · dashimaki or wagyu tamagoyaki · thick-cut ham katsu · chikuwa tempura with shibazuke tartare · squid tentacles with aosa mayo · fried horse mackerel · mentaiko and aosa spaghetti salad · red shrimp with vinegar miso · niku tofu · tongue steak · onigiri and tonjiru set · highballs, Hachijo-jima shochu · 12 counter seats
places.notes: [Izakaya · obanzai counter with a ¥900 niku dashimaki lunch in Ura-Namba] A twelve-seat counter in the Ura-Namba backstreets, open since 2020, that is two places in one. At lunch the line forms before opening for the ¥900 set: pick one of six mains, most famously the niku dashimaki, a fluffy, freshly rolled dashi omelet topped with sweet-savory beef, with obanzai, a little sashimi, a big bowl of tonjiru and rice refills; or swap the rice for a draft beer. Staff take your order in the line. At night it's an easier, friendly izakaya: the "five" obanzai platter that one regular says usually comes with six, thick-cut ham katsu, chikuwa tempura with shibazuke tartare, the dashimaki again, and highballs. It's the main shop of its name. PayPay or cash.

chef_bio.background: Obanzai izakaya, main shop (Tabelog; 2020–2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "The meat dashimaki set meal is priced at JPY 900 and includes the main dish, four types of daily obanzai, pickles, and a hearty pork miso soup… The fluffy dashimaki, perfectly cooked without any burnt edges, pairs wonderfully with the richly flavored beef." — November 2025.
"As usual, the assorted obanzai came with 6 types instead of 5, which was a nice surprise!" — October 2026, a ninth visit.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: わびすけ 難波本店、大阪市中央区難波4-8-3、なんば駅から徒歩3分、大阪難波から80m、月〜土 11:30〜15:00(L.O. 14:30、売り切れ次第終了)・17:30〜23:30(L.O. 23:00)、日 17:30〜23:30、予約可、カード・電子マネー不可、PayPay可、カウンター12席、2020年8月1日開店。口コミ(2020年8月〜2026年10月): 裏なんばのカウンターの居酒屋、おばんざい5種盛り(いつも6種)、厚切りハムカツ、ハイボール、明太子とあおさのスパゲッティサラダ、ちくわ天のしば漬けタルタル、おにぎりと豚汁のセット、げそ天のあおさマヨ、だし巻き、肉吸い、赤海老の酢味噌、アジフライ、白身魚のゆかりとかつお節、肉豆腐、タン焼き、八丈島の焼酎、昼は行列、マスターとスタッフが気さく、名物のだし巻き、Kuro Kirishimaのソーダ割り、肉だし巻き定食900円(メイン、日替わりおばんざい4種、漬物、豚汁)、30分待ち、日曜11時45分に約20人で40分待ち、並んでいる間に人数と注文を確認、6種のメイン、刺身少し、ご飯おかわり可、夜は待たずに入れた、和牛の玉子焼き、土曜11時10分に8人、ご飯の代わりにビールのセット、唐揚げビール定食900円、開店10分前に10人。

places.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: wheat-flour tempura batter is the meal; tentsuyu dipping sauce; curry finish option.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: shrimp, fish, wagyu and sea urchin in the course; ikura rice.
places.hours_raw: Wed–Thu 17:30–22:00 (food L.O. 20:30); Fri–Sun and public holidays 11:30–14:00 (food L.O. 13:00) and 17:30–22:00 (L.O. 20:30); closed Mon and Tue (next day if a holiday) (Tabelog). 10% service charge; same-day cancellation fee (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners) accepted; no e-money or QR (Tabelog).
places.neighborhood: Shinsaibashi-suji 1-5-3, Hoei Bldg 1F — 3 min from Shinsaibashi Stn exit 6
places.cuisine: Counter tempura courses · lunch courses ¥7,700 (with a drink) and ¥10,000; spend up to ¥15,000–20,000 (reviews) · the day's ingredients shown first · course opens with two shrimp, crisp shrimp heads · seasonal fish and vegetables, sweet potato (Beni Haruka), autumn matsutake as tempura or dobin-mushi with scallop and ginkgo · three salts and tentsuyu, with a suggestion for each piece · finish: four choices incl. tendon and curry; freshly cooked rice with ikura · dessert: fluffy shaved ice of slow-frozen house ice and dandelion coffee · 8 counter seats and a table for four
places.notes: [Tempura · counter tempura courses with a shaved-ice finish in Shinsaibashi] A calm twelve-seat tempura counter on Shinsaibashi-suji, open since 2018, the second shop of Tempura Osakaya Kusatetsu in Fukushima. The chef, Shin Tamura, trained at the Nikko Hotel and has 32 years in Japanese cuisine. Courses begin with a look at the day's ingredients, then two shrimp, fried one piece at a time in front of you, with three salts and tentsuyu and a suggestion for each. In autumn there's matsutake as tempura or a dobin-mushi with scallop and ginkgo, and one diner called the Beni Haruka sweet potato the best tempura sweet potato ever eaten. Finish with tendon, curry or rice with ikura, then a fluffy shaved ice and dandelion coffee. Lunch on Friday to Sunday is the way in: courses from ¥7,700 with a drink, or ¥10,000; reviewers' spend ran up to ¥15,000–20,000. Explanations are thorough. 10% service charge.

chef_bio.background: Second shop of Tempura Osakaya Kusatetsu in Fukushima, Osaka (August and October 2026 reviews). The chef, Shin Tamura, trained at the Nikko Hotel and has 32 years in Japanese cuisine (Tabelog listing).
chef_bio.philosophy: Ingredients such as Nagasaki live shrimp, A5 wagyu fillet, Nemuro sea urchin and young ayu; house-treated water adjusted per ingredient; shaved ice from house ice frozen over two days (as listed by an October 2026 reviewer).

anecdotes.text: "First, they present the tempura options for the day… There are three types of salt and a dipping sauce available… The course began with two shrimp… The dessert was quite unique, featuring shaved ice and dandelion coffee." — September 2026, lunch course ¥7,700.

"I was offered a choice between tempura and dobin mushi for the matsutake mushroom… the sweet potato (today it was Beni Haruka) was the best tempura sweet potato I have ever had!" — October 2026, lunch.

places.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: tare on skewers; ponzu; fried gizzards and tulip wings; noodle finish.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: chicken in every course; chicken-bone mizutaki broth.
places.hours_raw: Mon–Sat and days before/after holidays 18:00–24:00, from 17:00 with a reservation; closed Sun and public holidays; may close early when ingredients run out (Tabelog). Seating limited to 2½ hours when busy; three-item otoshi ¥660 (Tabelog). Cards incl. UnionPay, QUICPay and QR accepted (Tabelog). Lively and loud (October 2026).
places.neighborhood: Higashi-Shinsaibashi 2-4-19, Tamayamachi Galaxy Bldg No. 3 1F, down an alley — 5 min from Nipponbashi Stn, 7 min from Shinsaibashi or Namba
places.cuisine: Hakata mizutaki and yakitori · Hakata mizutaki (reserve ahead): rich, creamy collagen broth that arrives as a solid block and melts, yuzu-kosho and ponzu on the side, zosui or noodles to finish · chicken sashimi, five kinds · chicken tataki · salt-grilled skewers; tsukune with egg yolk · fried tulip wings · fried gizzards · grilled rice balls · otoshi of three ¥660 · 7 counter seats, 12 at tables
places.notes: [Yakitori · Hakata mizutaki and yakitori down a Higashi-Shinsaibashi alley] A busy chicken restaurant tucked down an alley in Higashi-Shinsaibashi, running since 2007 and often hard to book. The hot pot is the reason to come: a Hakata mizutaki whose rich, creamy collagen broth arrives as a solid block and melts in the pot, deep and gentle with tender chicken; finish with zosui or noodles, and reserve it ahead. Around it, there's a five-kind chicken sashimi plate with no off flavors, tataki, salt-grilled skewers, tsukune with egg yolk, fried gizzards and fried tulip wings the size of a KFC piece. Portions are big. Service is quick and the room loud enough that one diner couldn't hear the table. Seating is capped at 2½ hours when busy; ¥660 otoshi.

chef_bio.background: Yakitori and mizutaki restaurant (Tabelog; 2025–2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "The recommended hot pot features a broth rich in chicken flavor, delivering a deep and gentle taste from the very first bite… worth visiting primarily for the hot pot." — April 2026.
"The broth for the hot pot comes in a solid block! As it melts, it transforms into a rich and flavorful broth. I also love the fried chicken gizzards here." — September 2025.

places.notes: [Ramen · Jiro-style MAZE soba and Taiwanese mazesoba in the Yodoyabashi office district] A twelve-seat office-district shop between Yodoyabashi and Kitahama, open since 2015 and open daily. The MAZE soba is the order: flat, thick, chewy noodles in a rich soy dressing, under vegetables, back fat, garlic and a punch of black pepper, all adjustable from less to extra, with 200 g of noodles for the price of 150 g. The Taiwanese mazesoba (¥1,050) has its own repeat diner, and the creamy chicken paitan (¥1,000) is the lighter way in. Self-serve kimchi is free, and a stamp card leads to a gold card with free rice. One diner asked for extra fat and got extra garlic. Cash only.

anecdotes.text: "The rich soy sauce dressing paired perfectly with the hearty flat thick noodles… You can choose between 150g and 200g of noodles, and customize the amount of vegetables, fat, and garlic from less to extra." — March 2025, MAZE soba.
"The chicken paitan ramen costs JPY 1000, and the chashu (braised pork) is tender and delicious." — October 2026, ninth visit.

places.notes: [Ramen · Agu pork and Tanba black chicken shoyu and shio, with inventive limited bowls, by Kujo] A nine-seat counter near Kujo, open since 2019 and picked for Tabelog's Ramen 100 in 2024 and 2025, with lines at the 11:00 opening. A husband-and-wife team runs it; the owner trained at ramen shops before opening. The base is an additive-free double soup of Agu pork and Tanba black chicken with a layered fish dashi; the ajitama shoyu (¥1,250) floats Agu back fat over flat noodles from Tsurumi Seimen, with juicy Agu belly chashu. The shio is clear and mellow, its umami building as you go. For the simplest taste of broth and noodle, there's a kake-style shio or shoyu soba with only onion. Repeat diners come for the limited bowls: a stir-fried chicken-shoulder noodle tossed in a cast-iron pan, an Onomichi-style back-fat shoyu, chilled ramen in summer. Add the seasonal takikomi rice. Ticket machine, cash only; closed Mondays.

places.notes: [Ramen · rich miso on thick curly noodles near Kitahama] A fifteen-seat counter in the Kitahama office district, open since 2020 and run by the same people as the nearby Tsukemen Ide, with a lunch line that some diners call routine. The miso ramen (¥1,000) is rich and slightly gritty, with a pork-bone base beneath, on thick, chewy curly noodles of whole wheat, brightened by chopped purple onion and white negi with yuzu peel. Two variations stand out: the spicy miso, with five heat levels and the first three free, where the miso stays the star; and the "Wasan sansho" miso (¥1,100), whose aroma greets you at the door and gives a refreshing finish. Buy your ticket inside before you line up. Cards and PayPay accepted.

chef_bio.background: Miso ramen shop; sister of Tsukemen Ide (2021 and September 2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "The broth is quite rich in miso flavor. You can taste the pork bone flavor beneath the miso, but there's a slight graininess… The noodles are thick, curly, and made from whole wheat, strong enough to stand up to the broth." — October 2026, miso ramen ¥1,000.
"The broth had a rich miso flavor without being heavy, and the fragrance and mild spiciness of the sansho created a refreshing aftertaste." — March 2026, Wasan sansho miso ramen ¥1,100.

places.notes: [Ramen · thick pork-bone and seafood tsukemen in Kitahama since 2011] A busy fifteen-seat tsukemen shop in the Kitahama office district, open since 2011, where lunch means buying a ticket, a short wait outside and often a shared table. The tsukemen (¥1,100) pairs glossy, chewy thick noodles with a strong wheat flavor and a thick, rich dipping soup of pork bone and seafood, "rich without being overly heavy," with chashu and menma already in it; one October diner got 300 g for ¥1,100. Finish with soup-wari from the table. Add all the toppings (¥600) or a rice bowl of shredded pork or niku-miso. There's also a curry tsukemen. One diner found it simply average. Its sister shop, Miso Noodle Koji, is a few blocks west. Cards and PayPay accepted.
