places.notes: [Ramen · fried rice and light chuka soba by Tenmabashi] A small shop right by Tenmabashi Station, open since 2024, whose banner and name put the fried rice first. Buy a ticket downstairs (cash, no big notes), then climb a steep, narrow staircase to the seats. The usual order is the set (¥1,280–1,290): a light shoyu chuka soba on thin, straight noodles with a soba-like bite, rare chashu and thick menma, plus half a plate of fragrant, fluffy fried rice. Opinions split: several diners call the fried rice the reason to come, while others found both mild, and one saw the set cost ¥980 a week earlier. Water and dish return are self-service.

chef_bio.background: Fried rice and chuka soba shop (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).

places.notes: [Chinese · a station-front local Chinese since 1985, Tsuruhashi] A long-running local Chinese restaurant a minute from Tsuruhashi Station, with a classic red counter downstairs and tables upstairs, open since 1985. The specialty is a sauce yakisoba in the style of Osaka's Imazato yakisoba (¥1,000): thick noodles in a rich sauce with pork, shrimp, squid, green pepper and a fried egg on top. Lunch sets are the other draw, such as set B (¥1,080) with standout sweet and sour pork, kara-age and a crab omelet. There's also crab fried rice (¥800), gyoza (¥370) and noodle soups. One diner found the kara-age batter tempura-like, another the portions small. Cards accepted; smoking allowed. Closed Wednesdays and Saturdays.

chef_bio.background: Local Chinese restaurant (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
chef_bio.philosophy: Yakisoba with roots in Imazato yakisoba (May 2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "This local specialty, 'Imazato Yakisoba,' features pork, cabbage, onions, and custom thick noodles stir-fried in a rich sauce, topped with green peppers, large shrimp, small shrimp, a fried egg, shredded nori, and squid." — May 2026, special sauce yakisoba ¥1,000.
"I was impressed by the high level of the sweet and sour pork! The sauce was so rich that I felt it was the star of the set." — May 2026, set B ¥1,080.

places.cuisine: Inventive ramen · Shoyu Animal ¥1,600: rich, sweet umami from an animal-based broth · iriko soba shoyu ¥1,000 · shio ramen ¥1,000 · Antoki no Shio ¥1,600 with tangy red onion · Neo Shio Ramen Apple (when available) · curry ramen with seafood stock and beef fat · homemade flat, thick "fettuccine" noodles · rotating limited tsukemen, e.g. Aka Buta DDX autumn pear tsukemen ¥1,600, black pork and unagi dashi wasabi tsukemen ¥1,400, fig and octopus summer salt tsukemen ¥1,600, tantan tsukemen · chicken paitan now and then · Aka Buta DDX chashu, 2 slices ¥500 · Ajitama Arokana ¥200 · Kurobuta rice ¥400 · Rainbow wonton · large +¥200 · 6 seats
places.notes: [Ramen · inventive six-seat ramen on homemade fettuccine noodles, Momodani] A six-seat shop with a storefront that doesn't look like a ramen shop, five minutes from Momodani, open since 2020. The menu has a steady core and a stream of playful limited bowls. The standout for several diners is the Shoyu Animal (¥1,600), a deep, sweet, umami-heavy animal broth; the iriko shoyu and shio (¥1,000 each) are simpler. The limited tsukemen use homemade flat, thick fettuccine-style noodles, such as a pear and Aka Buta DDX pork tsukemen, an unagi dashi version or a fig and octopus salt dip. Staff suggest trying the noodles first with just salt and lemon. Check Instagram for the current menu. Order on the tablet. Closed Thursdays.

chef_bio.background: Ramen shop with a rotating limited menu (Tabelog; 2025–2026 reviews).
chef_bio.philosophy: Homemade flat, thick fettuccine-style noodles; recommends tasting them with salt and lemon first (October 2026 reviews).

The seasonal limited bowls show the most care, even chilled ones in October: an autumn sanma and mushroom chilled ramen (¥1,580) on a Rausu kombu, sanma-bushi and shiitake broth with mushrooms cooked four ways. Kimchi is free and good, and chicken plates with beer make it an evening stop too. Short lines at lunch. Cards and QR accepted.

It's linked to Jinrui Mina Menrui. The signature Witch's Red (¥957) is a sweet, shellfish-rich shoyu on chewy, medium-thick whole-wheat noodles with thin chashu that breaks up into each bite; there's also a light bonito-broth bowl. Gyoza are five for ¥200, though one diner found them greasy and the ramen heavy by the end. Order on your phone at the table. Open all day; cash only.

places.notes: [Ramen · creamy clam shio ramen in Via Abeno Walk] A busy shio ramen shop in the Via Abeno Walk mall near Tennoji, open since 2021. The Asari SiO ramen blends pork bone, chicken and asari clam into a creamy, milky soup whose salt stays gentle, on thin, straight, supple noodles with crunchy chopped onion and kaiware. The special version adds a pink rare chashu draped over the rim and a thick slice grilled just before serving. Play with the salts from around the world on the counter. One diner found it oily and the clam faint, another light and clean. Many order the SiO lemon mazesoba. Short waits at lunch. Ticket machine; QR payments only. Closed Wednesdays.

places.notes: [Ramen · Daniel Punch sansho shoyu soba and big kara-age by Tamatsukuri] A long-running fifteen-seat ramen shop two minutes from Tamatsukuri, open since 2011 until 23:00, with a menu that runs from gentle to punchy. The long-standing Daniel Punch (¥1,000) is a rich shoyu laced with sansho over flat curly noodles, meat miso, tenkasu and onion; stir in the raw egg, then finish with rice. The rich chuka soba is a thick chicken paitan with seafood and fish powder; the Men-Ta soba (¥950) a sweet Osaka shoyu with wontons. The kara-age is a specialty in its own right, often taken away. Summer brings chilled bowls. Weekday specials before 19:00 include a ¥800 shoyu ramen. Cash only.

places.notes: [Yakitori · a calm Hinai-chicken course counter above its lively sister, Ura-Namba] Up the stairs from the busy yakitori Bird, a minute from Namba Grand Kagetsu, this quiet white-wood counter surrounds a central grill, open since 2022. Skewers of Hinai chicken come plump and juicy, salted boldly, alongside Kawachi duck with melon, Awaodori chicken neck, a giant red eggplant grilled in front of you, and playful extras like liver pâté monaka and a mini croquette burger. Finish with oyakodon or ramen; the Basque cheesecake is worth saving room for. Good for entertaining. Cards and QR accepted.

places.notes: [Sushi · a relaxed reservation-only sushi course in a Ura-Namba basement] A ten-seat counter plus a few sunken tables below street level near Namba, open since 2014, serving one long omakase course by reservation. Three different broths are matched to the ingredients. Beyond the classics (tender octopus, thick fried tofu, whale), try the creative pieces: a potato ball wrapped in egg, jaga-butter, wagyu cooked shabu-shabu style in the broth, and the house daikon in white miso with pork belly. Finish with clay-pot rice. Lunch is the bargain: a seasonal tempura set with oden for ¥2,480. Portions are delicate. 10% service charge at dinner. Closed Wednesdays.

places.notes: [Ramen · light chicken chuka soba by day, obanzai and drinks by night, Tsuruhashi] A small, welcoming spot down a side alley three minutes from Tsuruhashi, open since 2022 and run single-handed on one February visit, cooking ramen and stirring fried rice at once. The owner, a woman, trained at Men FACTORY JAWS; the Ganso Chuka Soba was developed by the owner's father, who served it at a street stall. The Ganso Chuka Soba (¥890) is a surprisingly clear, low-oil soy broth of Tosa Hachikin chicken that clings to thin, smooth noodles; the Akayoroshi soba (¥1,200) goes the other way, heavy on garlic and vegetables, finished with rice like a risotto. Tomato, sesame and horumon ramen round it out. At night it's an izakaya with obanzai lined up on the counter and oden, and the ramen makes a gentle finish. Open until 2:00 on Fridays and Saturdays. Closed Wednesdays and Thursdays.

places.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: wheat and egg noodles; shoyu and miso tare; kara-age.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: meat broth; chashu; egg noodles; egg.

places.cuisine: Shoyu and miso ramen · Nakanoshima Straight: rich but not greasy shoyu, medium-thick straight noodles with a wheat aroma, large chashu, small menma; negi version · Nakanoshima Curve: Sapporo-style miso ramen with egg noodles and seasoning blended in Sapporo, a little richer · Kamisori Drop: warm chilled noodles with a special salt sauce, egg and a mountain of green onion · garlic topping ¥80 · kara-age and kara-age rice set · highball set
places.notes: [Ramen · "Straight" shoyu and Sapporo-style "Curve" miso in Nakanoshima] A clean, busy basement branch in Festival Tower West, opened in June 2025 by a popular ramen shop from Tenjinbashi-suji 6-chome. Two bowls frame the menu: the Nakanoshima Straight, a rich but not greasy shoyu on medium-thick straight noodles with a big slice of chashu, and the Nakanoshima Curve, a miso ramen on curly egg noodles that since a recent update tastes close to Sapporo, with seasoning blended there. The Kamisori Drop, a warm-chilled noodle bowl with salt sauce, egg and heaps of green onion, is the sleeper. Add kara-age or a highball set. One diner found the shoyu's noodles too heavy for the soup. Cards and PayPay accepted.

chef_bio.origin: Opened 16 June 2025 (Tabelog); a branch of a popular ramen shop in Tenjinbashi-suji 6-chome (June 2025 review).
chef_bio.background: Ramen shop (Tabelog; 2025–2026 reviews).
chef_bio.philosophy: Miso seasoning blended in Sapporo (September 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: "After the renovation, the Miso Ramen has become closer to the authentic Sapporo style… The menu mentioned that the seasoning was blended in Sapporo. The noodles are egg noodles too!" — September–October 2026, Nakanoshima Curve.
"The noodles were medium-thick and straight, with a nice chewiness. The broth was rich and had a strong flavor. The chashu was large and satisfying." — April 2026, shoyu ramen.

places.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: wheat noodles; shio tare; wontons; mapo tofu sauce.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: chicken paitan; chicken chashu; wontons; egg.
places.hours_raw: Daily 11:00–23:00; closing days follow Abeno Q's Mall (Tabelog). Lunch sets until 17:00 (July 2026). Lines from about noon on holidays (September 2026). Cards, e-money and QR accepted (Tabelog).
places.neighborhood: Abenosuji 1-6-1, Abeno Q's Mall 4F (Abeno-ku) — 2 min from Tennoji Stn exit 12
places.cuisine: Chicken paitan ramen · toripaitan shio soba: rich, creamy but light chicken paitan on medium noodles, with lemon to squeeze in halfway and yuzu at the bottom · special version: vegetables, wontons, soft-boiled egg, chicken chashu, dried chili, leafy greens, onion chips · rice into the last of the soup · lunch sets until 17:00: half ramen with Sichuan-style mapo tofu or yurinchi · evening value set with mapo tofu rice bowl · 27 seats
places.notes: [Ramen · chicken paitan shio soba with lemon in Abeno Q's Mall] A Jiyugaoka Kageyama branch on the fourth floor of Abeno Q's Mall near Tennoji, open since 2017 from 11:00 to 23:00, handy for families and groups. The toripaitan shio soba is rich and creamy yet light, with a strong chicken aroma; squeeze in the lemon halfway, find yuzu at the bottom, and finish by dropping rice into the soup. The special adds wontons, chicken chashu, vegetables and onion chips. Lunch sets (until 17:00) pair a half bowl with mapo tofu or yurinchi; the mapo tofu struck two diners as salty. One diner found the whole bowl too mild. Lines form at noon on holidays. Cards and QR accepted.

chef_bio.background: Branch of the Jiyugaoka Kageyama chicken paitan ramen group (Tabelog; 2025–2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "The Toripaitan Shio had a rich broth that was surprisingly light in flavor, perfectly complementing the slightly thicker noodles… I squeezed some lemon provided on the side… and at the end, I added a spoonful of rice to the soup…" — October 2025, special toripaitan shio soba.
"The Toripaitan Ramen was a rich bowl with a strong chicken broth aroma. The thick soup clung perfectly to the medium noodles…" — September 2026, half noodle mapo tofu set.

places.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: wheat noodles; shoyu and shio tare; mayo rice bowl sauce.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: chicken broth and chicken oil; katsuobushi dashi; pork and chicken chashu; egg.
places.hours_raw: Daily 11:00–21:30; hours may change (Tabelog). Ticket machine (2026). Cash only (Tabelog). Run by two people (October 2026).
places.neighborhood: Tamatsukuri-Motomachi 3-30 (Tennoji-ku) — 111 m from Tamatsukuri Stn
places.cuisine: Kombu-water tsukemen and chicken shoyu · kombu-water tsukemen, shoyu or shio: noodles served in kombu water, a chicken-and-salt or refined shoyu dip, warm honkatsuo dashi to pour in, lemon; eat the noodles first with just salt · special version ¥1,430: pork and chicken chashu, seasoned egg, menma · chicken shoyu ramen ¥890: clear soup of ground chicken with chicken oil and a sharp soy edge, thin straight noodles, pork and chicken-breast chashu, thick menma, kaiware, white negi · grilled chashu mayo rice bowl with two kinds of chashu · 8 high counter seats
places.notes: [Ramen · kombu-water tsukemen and clear chicken shoyu by Tamatsukuri] A small, casual eight-seat counter a minute from Tamatsukuri Station, opened in November 2025 and run by two women, including the owner. The star is kombu-water tsukemen: noodles bathed in kombu water that you first taste with just salt, then dip in a chicken shio or refined shoyu sauce, with warm honkatsuo dashi to stretch the dip and lemon for brightness (special ¥1,430). The chicken shoyu ramen (¥890) is a clear modern bowl with chicken oil and thin straight noodles. Don't skip the grilled chashu mayo rice bowl. One diner found the chashu a little plain, another the noodles uneven on an early visit. It gets tight when full. Cash only.

chef_bio.background: Tsukemen and ramen counter run by two people (October 2026 review). A ramen shop with a female owner, run by two women (October 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: "I love starting with just salt. The noodles are smooth, and the flavor of the wheat is nicely enhanced by the salt… I also enjoy adding the broth for a flavorful drink." — January 2026, kombu-water tsukemen (shoyu).

"The piping hot soup has a rich soy sauce color with a layer of chicken fat floating on the clear surface, offering a delightful blend of depth and sharpness in flavor." — October 2026, chicken shoyu ramen ¥890.

places.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: wheat noodles; soy-based sauces; wontons.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: meat sauces and chicken paitan; chashu; egg.
places.hours_raw: Mon–Fri 11:00–15:00 and 18:00–22:00; closed Sat and Sun; hours may change (Tabelog). Ticket machine to the right of the entrance; chilled tsukemen ordered verbally (June 2026). Rice included with mazesoba at lunch (June 2026). Cards, e-money and QR accepted (Tabelog).
places.neighborhood: Nakanoshima 3-2-30, MINAMO B1F (Kita-ku) — inside Keihan Watanabebashi Stn
places.cuisine: Mazesoba and ramen · mazesoba in original, shoyu, Sichuan and sea-bream salt (best cold), 100–500 g, garlic or none, spice levels; rice at lunch · exquisite shoyu ramen: classic shoyu, medium-thin straight noodles, three chashu, thick menma, wontons · blended shoyu ramen · chicken paitan ramen with a sweet soy edge · Nakanoshima black ramen · chicken paitan tsukemen, spicy tsukemen · sweet or spicy tantanmen · seasonal stamina ramen and chilled tsukemen · ramen in normal or DX size · 4 counter seats and tables
places.notes: [Ramen · weekday-only mazesoba by the gram in Watanabebashi Station] A twelve-seat shop in the MINAMO dining area inside Keihan Watanabebashi Station, open since 2018 on weekdays only, with a lunch line from office workers. Mazesoba is the core: original, shoyu, Sichuan or sea-bream salt (staff suggest the last one cold), from 100 to 500 g, with or without garlic and rice included at lunch. The menu also runs to a classic shoyu ramen with wontons, a sweetish chicken paitan, a Nakanoshima black ramen, tsukemen and tantanmen. Two diners found the mazesoba and the paitan on the sweet side, and one found spice level 3 mild. Ticket machine by the door. Closed weekends.

chef_bio.background: Weekday-only noodle shop (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "The menu features a variety of noodle dishes including Mazesoba (original, soy sauce flavor, Sichuan style, and sea bream salt flavor), exquisite shoyu ramen, blended shoyu ramen, chicken paitan ramen, Nakanoshima black ramen…" — June 2026.

"I initially requested the noodles to be served warm, but was advised that the cold version pairs better with the sea bream salt flavor, so I switched to cold. It was delicious!" — August 2026, 300 g.

places.name: 中華そば 鯵右衛門 (Chuka Soba Ajiemon)
places.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: homemade wheat noodles; shoyu tare; fried aji.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: horse-mackerel and niboshi broths; pork chashu; naruto; egg.
places.hours_raw: Mon, Tue, Thu, Fri, Sat 7:00–15:00 (last order 14:30); Sun 11:00–15:00; closed Wed; hours may change (Tabelog). Hours revised to early morning in 2026; an evening-only tsukemen was also reported in September 2026; check the shop social media (2026). Cash only (Tabelog).
places.neighborhood: Tsuruhashi 2-14-10 (Ikuno-ku), on the Tsuruhashi shopping street — 4 min from Tsuruhashi Stn
places.cuisine: Horse-mackerel (aji) chuka soba · aji fresh-fish shoyu ¥980: a creamy, rounded aji-bone soup with savory soy · aji niboshi shio ¥930, aji niboshi shoyu ¥900 (sharp soy, low oil) · limited aji ramen ¥980: rich, cloudy aji soup · Tsuruhashi 2-chome Black Tsukemen ¥1,250: aji niboshi and aji-bushi dip with re-brewed Shimane soy, Rausu kombu and Mongolian rock salt, yuzu-kosho; 200 g, 300 g free · homemade medium-thick noodles of Miyake Seifun flour from Ikuno · Kagoshima Sanmi pork chashu, menma, naruto · aji meshi ¥350–380 (fresh aji on rice with wasabi), fried aji made to order, TKG · ajitama +¥180, chashu +¥300, extra +¥150 · 7 counter seats
places.notes: [Ramen · horse-mackerel chuka soba with Tsuruhashi-market fish, Tsuruhashi] A seven-seat counter on the Tsuruhashi shopping street, open since March 2026 and already well covered, built around aji (horse mackerel) from the local market. The owner trained at Himeji Mentetsu, Kinkyuemon and Fuse Hosomi Shoten before opening, and still buys horse mackerel from a fishmonger who has helped since those training days. The aji fresh-fish shoyu (¥980) is a creamy, rounded bone broth; the aji niboshi shoyu and shio are sharper and leaner, and a limited aji ramen goes rich and cloudy. Noodles are homemade from flour milled in Ikuno, chewy and wheaty, under Kagoshima pork chashu. Order the aji meshi: fresh aji over rice with wasabi, so good it rivals a sushi bar. The menu changes often, and hours have moved to 7:00 openings, so check social media. Cash only. Closed Wednesdays.

chef_bio.background: Chuka soba shop on the Tsuruhashi shopping street (Tabelog; 2026 reviews). The owner trained at Himeji Mentetsu, Kinkyuemon and Fuse Hosomi Shoten before opening, and still buys horse mackerel from a fishmonger who has helped since those training days (October 2026 review).
chef_bio.philosophy: Ingredients from around Tsuruhashi: aji from a Tsuruhashi market fish shop, flour from Miyake Seifun in Ikuno, vegetables from a local grocer (October 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: "The noodles are made from a special blend of flour from Miyake Seifun in the same Ikuno Ward, using a vacuum mixer… resulting in a homemade noodle with a chewy texture and rich wheat flavor." — September 2026, Tsuruhashi 2-chome Black Tsukemen ¥1,250.
"I was amazed by the freshness of the aji itself. Since it's sourced from a local fish market in Tsuruhashi, it's no surprise…" — July 2026, aji don.

places.cuisine: Tantanmen · soupless black-sesame tantanmen: near-black sesame paste, minced meat, chewy flat noodles, plated like pasta; spice levels; rice to finish · white-sesame tantanmen with a chicken-based soup · limited chilled white-sesame tantanmen with chili oil and Sichuan pepper · small size · toppings such as steamed chicken · yodare chicken, bite-size gyoza · Horo Yoi drink set and a long drink list · counter seats in a renovated old house
places.notes: [Ramen · black-sesame tantanmen in a renovated old house, Nishi-Tenma] A calm, stylish tantanmen shop in a renovated old house down the narrow Oimatsu alley in Nishi-Tenma, easy to mistake for a home, open since 2018. The order is the soupless black-sesame tantanmen: a nearly black, intensely fragrant sesame paste with minced meat over chewy flat noodles, plated like a pasta dish, with spice to your level and rice to finish. The white-sesame tantanmen is the soup version, and a chilled white-sesame bowl appears in summer. Yodare chicken, small gyoza and a drink set make it an evening stop too. One diner found the soup mild. Small sizes available. AMEX and PayPay accepted.

chef_bio.background: Tantanmen shop in a renovated old house (Tabelog; 2020–2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "The rich aroma of black sesame fills the air, and the perfect balance of spiciness and sweetness from the sesame creates a delightful bowl. The noodles have just the right thickness and a strong chewiness." — July 2026, soupless black-sesame tantanmen.

"The glossy white sesame soup, vibrant chili oil, and colorful toppings… The depth and nuttiness of the white sesame spread across my palate, followed by the pleasant spiciness of the chili oil and the refreshing numbing sensation of Sichuan peppercorns." — July 2026, limited chilled tantanmen.

places.cuisine: Yakitori · omakase yakitori set ¥2,800: appetizers, three small dishes and four skewers (by reservation) · Ume no Yu course ¥4,500: eight skewers, a dish, small bowl, salad, main and mini curry · six-skewer set · Kyoto Akadori thigh, breast lightly rare, gizzard, neck, bone-in wings with rock salt, tsukune, negima · liver sashimi ¥660, Kyoto Akadori tataki ¥1,100 · fried tomato with mascarpone · mozuku, potato salad, Camembert · grilled Tochio aburage with ginger soy · shochu selection · 17 counter seats
places.notes: [Yakitori · a Showa-era bathhouse-themed yakitori counter, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A seventeen-seat counter behind a bathhouse-style noren near Shinsaibashi, with Showa pop on the speakers. Ume no Yu once served horse meat, and has returned as a yakitori shop. Start with the omakase set (¥2,800, reserve), four skewers with appetizers and small dishes, or the ¥4,500 course that ends with a mini curry. The grilling is precise: Kyoto Akadori thigh with crisp skin, breast left lightly rare, bone-in wings with rock salt. Order the fried tomato with mascarpone, the mozuku and the potato salad, plus a grilled Tochio aburage. Plenty of shochu. Some skewers sell out, so reserve. Cards accepted.

chef_bio.origin: Listed from 1 November 2006 (Tabelog); reopened as a yakitori restaurant after serving horse-meat dishes (2025–2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "The meal consisted of appetizers, small dishes, and four skewers, all served one by one… One standout dish was the grilled thigh of Kyoto Akadori chicken. The skin was crispy, and the meat was juicy." — August 2025, omakase yakitori set ¥2,800.
"The chicken breast was perfectly grilled, lightly salted, and slightly rare inside… the chicken wings had crispy skin, and they were best enjoyed with rock salt!" — November 2025, six-skewer set.

places.cuisine: Charcoal robatayaki izakaya · appetizer of grated daikon with shirasu · sashimi platter (tuna, hamachi, squid, swordfish, sea bream) · grilled sanma with grated daikon and ponzu · charcoal-grilled vegetable platter · nagaimo grilled with butter and soy · spear squid with sea urchin · charcoal-grilled sirloin cap · straw-grilled dishes · zucchini wrapped in meat with Kaneyama miso · dashimaki tamago with mentaiko, grilled anago · kamameshi in several kinds · lightly pickled cucumber, water eggplant and tomato · pasta, omurice · wide drink list · 12 counter seats and 2 tables
places.notes: [Izakaya · charcoal robata open until 5:30 am, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A stylish third-floor robata izakaya near Nagahoribashi, open since 2023 from 18:00 until 5:30, which draws a late-night Minami crowd. The owner is a former fishmonger from the Central Wholesale Market and a charcoal-grilling expert. Everything comes off the charcoal or straw fire in front of the counter: whole sanma with grated daikon, a big grilled vegetable platter, butter-soy nagaimo and sirloin cap. The sashimi platter is fresh (one diner waited a while for it), and the mentaiko dashimaki with grilled anago is a standout. Finish with one of several kamameshi or a buttery omurice. Smoking is allowed at the table. Not cheap, but seasonal and carefully made. Closed Wednesdays.

chef_bio.background: Charcoal robatayaki izakaya (Tabelog; 2025–2026 reviews). The owner is a former fishmonger from the Central Wholesale Market and a charcoal-grilling expert (Tabelog listing).
chef_bio.specialty: Charcoal-grilled seasonal fish, meat and vegetables; kamameshi.

anecdotes.text: "The skin was crispy and the flesh juicy, with a hint of bitterness in some parts. Paired with grated daikon and ponzu sauce, it was a perfect match for drinks." — September 2026, grilled sanma.
"The dashimaki tamago (Japanese rolled omelette) was the most delicious dish. It was fluffy and tender with mentaiko… and I enjoyed it with grilled conger eel!" — August 2026.

places.cuisine: Robatayaki izakaya and seafood lunch bowls · lunch: Bakudan don ¥1,800 (¥1,400 in 2024): salmon roe, tuna, negitoro, sea bream, takuan, shiso, nori and wasabi, with sesame-sauce sashimi, a small dish, tororo, miso soup and white or mixed-grain rice; eat it with dashi soy, then the sesame sashimi, then the tororo · Gobu Gobu don ¥1,800: Wakayama shirasu half raw, half boiled · Senshu anago tempura don ¥1,700 · hon-maguro don with tororo · seasonal sanma set; large rice free · weekend breakfast 7:00–11:00 · dinner: anago nigiri, sashimi platter under a smoking lid, potato salad, nut salad, soft-roe mapo tofu, Manganji peppers, gratin, grilled rice balls
places.notes: [Izakaya · robata izakaya with a famous seafood lunch bowl, Ura-Namba] A popular robatayaki izakaya in the Ura-Namba back streets, open since 2012, where lunch lines form for seafood bowls. The signature Bakudan don (¥1,800) heaps salmon roe, tuna, negitoro and sea bream over rice; eat it in three stages, first with dashi soy, then with the sesame-dressed sashimi on the side, then with tororo. Seasonal bowls rotate, like a Wakayama shirasu half-raw, half-boiled bowl or a Senshu anago tempura don. Dinner is robata and a sashimi platter served under a cloud of smoke, plus anago nigiri and soft-roe mapo tofu. Weekend breakfast from 7:00. No lunch reservations; arrive early. 5% service charge at dinner.

chef_bio.background: Robatayaki izakaya with seafood lunch bowls (Tabelog; 2024–2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "The restaurant has a recommended way to enjoy it… First, drizzle some dashi soy sauce over it… Next, enjoy it with the sashimi drizzled with sesame sauce… Finally, mix in the yam tororo for a hearty finish." — August 2024, Bakudan don.

"When I opened the lid, it was like opening a treasure box, with smoke rising dramatically—such a stylish presentation! Not only was it visually impressive, but the sashimi was also incredibly fresh…" — September 2026, dinner.

places.notes: [Yakitori · binchotan chicken on plates until 5 am, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] The main shop of SASAYA, tucked into an alley near Shinsaibashi, grilling morning-fresh chicken over Kishu binchotan and serving it off the skewer on colorful Japanese plates. Try the seseri with green onion, the heart, and the chicken tataki of liver and heart with sesame on a Kutani-style plate; the chicken sashimi and seasonal duck with wasabi are other picks. The counter is friendly and chatty. One diner found it good rather than special. Only two tables, so reserve for groups. ¥418 appetizer charge. Smoking allowed.

places.cuisine: Creative salmon ramen, "with a French twist" · salmon tantanmen with spice levels, colorful, like a soup pasta · white salmon ramen: creamy broth under an espuma, thin chashu, thick smoked salmon, mizuna, carrot, croutons, burdock chips, balsamic and chili powder, slightly wavy flat noodles · summer chilled salmon ramen with firm noodles · Genovese mazesoba with basil and cheese on flat noodles · salmon rice set (pour the ramen broth over it) · basil aedama side · seasoned egg · counter, terrace and tables, 33 seats
places.notes: [Ramen · "French-twist" salmon ramen in a bar-like room, Tenma] A stylish shop near the Okawa river that looks like a bar from outside, open since 2022, from a group with shops in Tokyo and Kyoto. The bowls look like plated pasta. The white salmon ramen floats an espuma over a creamy broth, then piles on smoked salmon, thin chashu, croutons, crisp burdock chips and balsamic, over slightly wavy flat noodles; the salmon tantanmen is the spicy signature. The Genovese mazesoba, rich with basil and cheese, is a good second dish, and the salmon rice set comes alive with broth poured over. One diner found the white salmon broth more salty than salmony. Staff explain the menu patiently. Lunch-led hours; closed Tuesdays.

chef_bio.origin: Opened 15 December 2022 (Tabelog); the group also has shops in Tokyo and Kyoto (February 2026 review).

places.notes: [Ramen · graded-spice chige ramen in the Abeno HOOP food hall] A spice-focused counter of the Jinrui Mina Menrui group in the basement food hall of Abeno HOOP, open since 2023. Two bowls carry the name: the 50 (¥1,100), ramen in a flavorful chige soup heavy with chili oil and minced meat on medium-thick noodles, and the soupless 30 (¥1,000). There's also a yukgaejang ramen that one diner likened to Mongolian Tanmen Nakamoto. Spice runs from none through levels 1–4 to Over and the fierce END, which staff suggest only after you've eaten Over; level 2 is already properly hot, and level 1 suits most. The thick chashu soothes the heat, as does a pork rice bowl (¥350). Order, take a buzzer, sit anywhere in the hall.

"When I asked for the 'END,' [staff] asked, 'Have you tried the OVER? I only recommend the END to those who have eaten the OVER. It's quite spicy!'" — September 2026, 50 at END.

places.notes: [Ramen · Jiro-style ramen with a Takaida soy edge in the Abeno HOOP food court] A six-seat partitioned counter in the HOOP basement dining court, open since 2024, serving Jiro-style ramen that leans toward Osaka's Takaida style, with a tangy, stronger soy than usual. Order at the kiosk, pick your garlic, back fat and vegetables, and collect a bowl of extra-thick, chewy noodles under sprouts, cabbage, heaps of green onion and thick chashu. The shio Jiro is powerfully salty; the soupless version is heartier still. Cheddar cheese is the surprise topping that works, and black oolong tea comes free. It's milder than many Jiro shops, which suits newcomers. Under ¥1,000 for a regular. Open until 23:00.

places.notes: [Tsukemen · thick whole-wheat tsukemen in kombu water by Tamatsukuri] A tsukemen and mazesoba shop two minutes from Tamatsukuri's north exit, open since 2021; one diner prefers its relaxed pace to the busier JET600 nearby. The noodles are the draw: thick, golden, homemade with whole wheat and served in kombu water, chewy and bouncy, best taken two strands at a time. The house dip is a rich tonkotsu-and-seafood soy with back fat, katsuobushi oil and a whisper of yuzu; spicy (levels 1–3, level 2 is hotter than it sounds) and shio versions too. Finish by diluting the dip with the citrus-scented soup at the counter, or with rice. Tsukemen 200 g is ¥1,000, and large sizes cost a little more. PayPay accepted.

places.notes: [Ramen · ultra-rich chicken paitan tori soba by Tamatsukuri] A branch of Ramen Jinsei JET from Fukushima, open here since 2011 and known for lines. The signature tori soba is an ultra-rich chicken paitan, simmered over ten hours with seafood for depth, on homemade medium-thick noodles of domestic wheat with thin chashu, naruto, white onion and mitsuba: intense, yet balanced enough that it doesn't wear you out. A lighter shoyu ramen (special ¥1,400) and an aburi buta soba (¥950) are the alternatives, and limited bowls like the Royal Pork chashu noodle (¥1,700) come and go. One diner found the shoyu good but pricey. Ticket machine by the door; cash only.

places.notes: [Ramen · spoon-standing rich chicken soba by Momodani Koreatown] A clean, stylish eight-seat counter facing Koreatown near Momodani, open since January 2025, lunch hours only, with lines of 20 at opening on holidays. The rich chicken soba (¥1,050) is so thick the ladle stands upright, dark with sharp soy and deeply chicken, clinging to every noodle, brightened by diced onion and green pepper; add chopped Aomori garlic. The kombu-water tsukemen and monthly limited bowls (grilled sanma soba, chilled mackerel niboshi, a curry version on the 20th) are worth chasing. Free Tsuruhashi kimchi on the side. Two diners found the noodles too soft. One diner noted a Bib Gourmand. Cash only. Closed Wednesdays.

chef_bio.background: Rich chicken ramen counter (Tabelog; 2025–2026 reviews); one diner mentions a Michelin Bib Gourmand listing (May 2026 review).

places.notes: [Ramen · chicken-and-pork white broth in many versions, Momodani] A small eleven-seat neighborhood ramen shop between Tsuruhashi and Momodani, open since 2015 and run by two people. Everything builds on a creamy, milky chicken-and-pork paitan: plain, with fish, spicy, garlic-loaded, with vegetables (¥1,060) or as a curry ramen (¥1,000) whose spices sit nicely on the broth; there's also a curry tsukemen and a light shoyu. Homemade medium-thick noodles are chewy, the chashu is tender, and the menma is unusually good. One diner found the spicy version short on broth flavor and recommends the plain. Add a chashu rice bowl. One ramen per person. Cash only. Closed Tuesdays.

"As soon as the bowl arrived, the aroma of garlic filled the air… The broth, rich with the flavors of chicken and pork, paired perfectly with the garlic." — June 2026, chicken-and-pork garlic ramen.

places.notes: [Chinese · a 60-year-old alley Chinese counter with ¥500 ramen, Kujo] A seven-seat counter tucked into an alley off the Kujo shopping street, about 60 years old by one diner's count and run by an elderly couple whose easy banter is part of the charm. The gyoza are made after you order, wrappers rolled on the spot, ten bite-size pieces with crisp bottoms. The ramen (¥500) is a light, peppery bowl with thick chashu; the yakisoba (¥550) is cooked in a sauce made first, so it's moist rather than fried. There's also fried rice, wonton noodles, a chuka-don and, in summer, a chilled chuka with jellyfish and real mustard. Prices are remarkably low. Short hours; look for the red noren. Cash only.

chef_bio.background: Local Chinese counter run by two people (2026 reviews). A small counter-only shop run by an elderly couple (July 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: "The gyoza is made fresh after the order is placed, with the skin rolled out and the filling wrapped inside… The crispy sear and the chewy outer skin make it another dish that pairs well with drinks." — July 2026.

"A classic bowl topped with bean sprouts, green onions, menma (bamboo shoots), and chashu (braised pork). The broth has a light flavor with a hint of black pepper, which paired well with the thin noodles." — August 2026, ramen ¥500.

places.notes: [Yakitori · a Kumano jidori course counter with two clay-pot rices, Nishi-Shinsaibashi] A calm, stylish ten-seat L-shaped counter at the back of a passage near Shinsaibashi, open since 2023 and named to Tabelog's Yakitori WEST 100 for 2025. There's one course (¥13,200) of Kumano jidori and Date chicken over charcoal, each skewer grilled and seasoned differently: crisp-and-juicy seseri, heart, tsukune with mustard, Kinkan with liver. Between skewers come plates like wood-smoked thigh tataki, sweet liver pâté on baguette and dashi-soaked tomato. It ends with two seasonal clay-pot rices, refills allowed, plus pickles and soup. One diner found the heart more burnt than smoky. Reserve; weekend lunch too.

places.notes: [Curry · spice curry in an old wooden house down a Higashi-Shinsaibashi alley] A curry house in a back-alley wooden house near Nagahoribashi, easy to miss, lit by bare bulbs and hung with cute illustrations and Asian odds and ends. The curries rotate daily: eggplant keema, butter chicken, shrimp coconut, pumpkin butter, squid green curry. Each is distinct, deep and well balanced rather than fiery, though you can ask for more heat. Lunch is a two-curry combination; on Sundays, a three-curry plate (¥1,380) comes with turmeric-scented rice, dal, raita and pickles. Add a fried egg and a cardamom chai. Cash only. Closed Wednesdays; Tuesday is lunch only.

"On Sundays, you can order either a la carte or a three-dish plate. I opted for the three-dish plate, which included squid green curry, keema, and pumpkin curry, served with saffron rice, pickles, and dal for JPY 1380." — October 2026.

places.notes: [Tonkatsu · brand-pork tonkatsu fried low and slow, Shimanouchi] A clean, Japanese-modern ten-seat counter in Shimanouchi, open since 2024, serving tonkatsu of premium brand pigs fried at low temperature until rosy inside. Myojin pork from Mie comes out tender and juicy, the loin sweet with fat; Dorobuta from Hokkaido is richer still. Eat it first with rock salt and wasabi, then the sauces. The seasonal soup is a treat: canola-flower miso in spring, chilled dashi with yuba over nyumen in summer, red miso in autumn. It's expensive for tonkatsu, with Dorobuta loin at ¥5,500, but diners rate the quality highly; one wished for free cabbage refills.

chef_bio.philosophy: Brand pork fried at low temperature and drained carefully (August 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: "The beautiful rose-colored cross-section of the Hirakatsu immediately showcases the delicate cooking technique… When enjoyed with the accompanying rock salt and wasabi, the umami flavor becomes even more pronounced." — August 2026, Myojin pork hirakatsu 120 g.

It is family-run, homey and loved by locals. Start with the gyoza: small, thin-skinned and garlicky, good enough to have a reputation of their own (six for ¥450; frozen to take home too). Then the okonomiyaki, crisp outside and fluffy inside, served cut, or the ebi-tama with eight plump shrimp (¥900) and the suji negi-tama, plus stir-fried beef with ponzu. Evenings only, four days a week. Cash only; reserve for groups.

chef_bio.background: Teppan okonomiyaki restaurant run by two people (2026 reviews). It is family-run, homey and loved by locals (July 2026 review).

places.notes: [Ramen · black-shoyu ramen piled with stir-fried vegetables, Teradacho] A big, busy ramen shop a minute from Teradacho's north exit, open since 2010 and part of the Wasshoi group. It looks Jiro-style, but the house kuro shoyu ramen is its own thing: a light chicken-and-soy soup under a mound of hot, sweet stir-fried cabbage, sprouts and meat, on thick chewy noodles, sized up from Danjiri to Danjiri MAX. There's also mazesoba, Taiwan mazesoba, tsukemen and a monthly limited bowl (October's was a salty "junk" mazesoba with fried garlic and a fried egg). Add half fried rice or gyoza. Order on your phone. One diner found the large mazesoba heavy, another waited 15 minutes between rice and ramen.

places.cuisine: Niboshi specialist · Tomio niboshi soba ¥1,200: balanced niboshi, generous chashu · rich niboshi chuka soba: a thick, "cement"-grey soup · niboshi tsukemen ¥1,000, with narutomaki, onion, menma and chashu in the dip; soup to dilute · summer Ibuki iriko cold noodles ¥1,150–1,250: Ibuki iriko, saba-bushi and other fish flakes with kombu water and salt tare, dashi ice, Morioka-style elastic noodles, chicken chashu, vinegared sardine, pickled cherry tomatoes, kaiware, menma, egg and an iriko "cement" paste · two-week limited Shodoshima iriko cold ramen: rich cement soup on thick flat noodles with seaweed and onion · meat shumai · tamago-kake gohan with house soy · table: furikake, kombu tsukudani and spices · 12 counter seats
places.notes: [Ramen · niboshi specialist with summer iriko cold noodles, Teradacho] A twelve-seat niboshi ramen counter on Route 25 by Teradacho, open since January 2020, where the smell of dried sardines greets you at the door. The house Tomio niboshi soba (¥1,200) is balanced rather than brutal; the rich niboshi chuka soba goes thick and cement-grey with a pleasant bitterness for true fans. Summer is its showcase: the Ibuki iriko cold noodles, an icy iriko-and-kombu soup with dashi ice and springy Morioka-style noodles, plus a two-week Shodoshima iriko cold ramen. Niboshi tsukemen (¥1,000) and meat shumai too. One diner found the shumai soft and the tsukemen noodles plain. Order by QR code or out loud.

chef_bio.background: Niboshi chuka soba specialist (Tabelog; 2024–2026 reviews).
chef_bio.specialty: Niboshi chuka soba; iriko cold noodles.

anecdotes.text: "The broth is made from a blend of Ibuki iriko (dried sardines), saba (mackerel) flakes, and soya flakes, combined with kombu water and a salt-based sauce… The noodles are specially sourced from Morioka, boasting a chewy texture…" — September 2024, Ibuki iriko cold noodles ¥1,150.

"While many cold ramen dishes tend to be refreshing and light, this one had a rich flavor with a noticeable bitterness from the niboshi (dried sardines)." — September 2026, Shodoshima iriko cold ramen.

places.notes: [Ramen · thick chicken paitan with rare chashu, Teradacho] A clean two-floor shop thirty seconds from Teradacho's north exit, open since 2023 as a branch of Tori ni Koishita Hi. Its chicken paitan is the thick kind rather than the light modern style, with four slices of house-made rare chashu over thin noodles; the special miso version (¥1,200) adds spice and depth. The chicken paitan tsukemen (from ¥1,000) pairs thick, chewy noodles with yuzu and kaiware. Summer brings a run of chilled bowls (¥1,000), from a gentle clam-broth ramen to a niboshi-kombu shio, and a 20-a-day clam chilled tsukemen. Kara-age and fried rice on the side. One diner found the portion small.

places.notes: [Ramen · chashu chuka soba and spicy mala jangmen by Teradacho] A compact counter by Teradacho Station from the team behind Ramen Shuki in Tsuruhashi, reopened in April 2026 under this name, open until midnight, often with a few groups waiting. Cold tantanmen and a sesame soy-milk version appear seasonally. Students get free extra noodles. Half fried rice at lunch. Pay on the way out.

places.notes: [Ramen · tom yum tantanmen with a play board of toppings, Abeno] A small, lively shop near Abenobashi that fills within minutes of its 11:00 opening, serving one thing above all: tom yum tantanmen (¥1,100 at lunch). The broth is spicy, numbing, sour and a little sweet, with a strong Sichuan-pepper tingle, on thin, flexible noodles with meat miso. Ordering is a game: slot colored menu chips into a board and hand it over, adding cilantro, egg or onion, or a whiteboard special like shredded pig's feet. Then work through the flavor-changers and the fragrant chili oil, on spare plates provided. Staff walk first-timers through it. It's properly hot. Lunch only, until sold out; closed Sundays. Cash only.

"Instead of a traditional menu, there are plastic chips with the menu items printed on them. You insert one into an order board and hand it to [staff]." — September 2026, tom yum tantanmen with three toppings, ¥1,660.

places.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: wheat noodles; tare; miso; gyoza.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: pork-bone soup; chashu; egg.
places.hours_raw: Mon–Thu 18:00–02:00; Fri–Sat 18:00–03:00; closed Sun; hours may change (Tabelog). One April 2026 diner noted it now closes at 23:00, so check. Cash only; smoking allowed (Tabelog).
places.neighborhood: Daido 4-10-4 (Tennoji-ku), under a yellow awning with red lanterns — in front of JR Teradacho Stn
places.cuisine: Garlic ramen · ninniku (garlic) ramen: light pork-bone soup loaded with chopped garlic, smooth, curly medium-thick noodles · miso chashu ramen ¥1,100 · chashu ramen ¥1,100 · kimchi ramen ¥900 · boiled egg · extra noodles ¥300 · gyoza ¥300 · small rice ¥150, served with kimchi · cucumber kimchi (oi kimchi) · a "no-noodle set" of chashu, sprouts, kimchi, rice and broth · counter
places.notes: [Ramen · late-night garlic ramen by Teradacho Station] An old-school, evening-only garlic ramen shop right in front of Teradacho, behind a yellow awning, red lanterns and a red noren, often full after 22:00. The house ninniku ramen is a surprisingly light pork-bone soup under a heap of chopped garlic, on smooth, curly noodles, a classic finish after a night out; there's also miso chashu (¥1,100) and kimchi ramen (¥900). Order the cucumber kimchi: addictive and the real star for one diner. Rice comes with kimchi, and gyoza are ¥300. Several diners wanted even more garlic, so ask. Hours have reportedly shortened, so check before going late. Cash only; smoking allowed.

chef_bio.background: Garlic ramen shop open in the evening (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "The broth is rich with pork bone and plenty of garlic, yet surprisingly light. But the real star is the cucumber kimchi, which I believe is a type of oi kimchi—it's delicious and addictive!" — June 2026, garlic ramen.
"The ramen was packed with garlic and had a light pork bone broth. The noodles were smooth and curly, and it was delicious!" — October 2026.

places.cuisine: Kiritama and tsukemen · Kiritama (Kirimen) ¥1,000: homemade flat noodles with a special salt sauce and a raw egg underneath, mixed like kama-tama; served cold too (Kiritama cold); 1.5 servings at no extra charge · rich tsukemen, 1.5 servings free; chashu and menma in the dip · Kiridon: chashu, menma and green onion over rice; with Kiritama cold as a set ¥1,480 · chashu topping · counter seats
places.notes: [Ramen · Kiritama egg-and-salt noodles and rich tsukemen, Abeno] A small Tennoji branch of the noodle-focused Kirimen, opened in September 2026 near Abeno Station, with short lines at peak times. The signature Kiritama is noodles first: homemade flat noodles, firm, smooth and wheaty, tossed with a special salt sauce and the raw egg hidden underneath, kama-tama style; taste the noodles alone, then mix. It comes hot or cold, and 1.5 servings cost the same. The rich tsukemen, also free at 1.5 servings, has chashu and menma in the dip. The Kiridon chashu rice bowl finishes it off. One diner found the egg-and-sauce mix uneven and another the chashu fatty. Ticket machine first, then queue. Closed Thursdays.

chef_bio.origin: Opened 14 September 2026 (Tabelog); a branch of Kirimen (October 2026 review).
chef_bio.background: Ramen and tsukemen shop focused on its homemade noodles (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).

"The noodles had a delightful wheat aroma and were delicious! When I tried the dipping sauce, it was rich and satisfying…" — October 2026, rich tsukemen, 1.5 servings.

places.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: pasta; bread; fried hamo and cutlet.

places.cuisine: Italian courses · lunch course with a drink ¥5,200: assorted antipasti and bread with olive oil; the signature chilled capellini with snow crab and fruit tomato; a main of Mochi pork or fried hamo; dessert plate · dinner course: e.g. long shrimp, a cutlet, hamo and karasumi pasta · wines incl. Sardinian Vermentino · 19 seats
places.notes: [Italian · refined Italian with a chilled snow-crab capellini, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A popular second-floor Italian restaurant two minutes from Shinsaibashi, known for a delicately flavored, carefully built cooking that rewards slow attention. Lunch is the easy way in: four courses with a drink for ¥5,200, starting with antipasti and bread, then the signature chilled capellini, where the acidity of fruit tomato meets the richness of snow crab, then Mochi pork or fried hamo, then dessert. Dinner courses run to dishes like hamo and karasumi pasta, matched with Sardinian Vermentino. One diner found the baguette hard. Reserve for lunch. Closed Sundays and Mondays.

chef_bio.background: Italian restaurant (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "The acidity of the fruit tomatoes and the richness of the snow crab created a perfect balance. The extremely thin pasta, 'Capellini,' had a smooth yet chewy texture…" — September 2026, lunch course with a drink, ¥5,200.
"Each dish had a delicate flavor, and while it initially felt a bit lacking… as I continued eating, the rich flavors gradually emerged!" — October 2026, lunch course.

places.name: 循誠 (Junsei)
places.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: homemade pasta and bread; brioche; curry with a pork cutlet.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: seafood, jamón, beef and pheasant throughout; sea urchin; Comté.
places.hours_raw: Tue–Sun and public holidays, reservation only, lunch from 12:00 and dinner from 18:00; closed Mon except private bookings (Tabelog). Dislikes asked in advance (March 2026). Cards accepted; no e-money or QR (Tabelog). Formerly Karato (July 2026 review).
places.neighborhood: Higashi-Shinsaibashi 1-19-15, Unagidani Block 1F–2F, behind an intercom door — 3 min from Shinsaibashi Stn exit 2
places.cuisine: Innovative, genre-free courses · special omakase course ¥22,000, built daily on the best ingredients: appetizers such as caviar with karasumi, lotus-root chips, kensaki squid and shiso; aged wagyu tartare on homemade bread; fried bone-in Daisendori chicken with honey and red-wine gastrique; fish marinated in aged Shaoxing wine; 48-month Iberico bellota jamón sliced in front of you · corn soup · homemade hand-rolled pasta (e.g. crab and sweet shrimp; asparagus and clams) · sea urchin on brioche · pheasant soup · charcoal-finished mahata · chateaubriand with tuna soup · European-style beef curry with a Kobe pork cutlet · a choice of five desserts, e.g. Mont Blanc or a vegetable dessert of celeriac mousse and burdock caramel · fruit juices (pear, melon, peach) as a non-alcoholic pairing · 8–10 counter seats, tatami, shoes off
places.notes: [Innovative · a hidden-door counter of genre-free courses, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] Ring the intercom at a hidden door, climb to the second floor, take off your shoes and step into a modern Japanese room with tatami and a counter of about ten. The young owner-chef, Iwao, is passionate and experienced, and the chef's wife is also at the shop. Formerly Karato, now Junsei, it serves one omakase course (¥22,000) set each day by the ingredients: caviar layered with karasumi, aged wagyu tartare, 48-month Iberico jamón sliced at the counter, a fresh corn soup, homemade pasta, sea urchin on brioche, then a charcoal-finished fish and a beef curry with a Kobe pork cutlet. Choose your dessert from five; fruit juices such as pear and melon make a non-alcoholic pairing. Dishes are explained carefully. Reservation only; closed Mondays.

chef_bio.origin: Opened 2 August 2019 (Tabelog); renamed from Karato to Junsei (July 2026 review).
chef_bio.background: Reservation-only innovative counter (Tabelog; 2026 reviews). The young owner-chef, Iwao, is passionate and experienced, and the chef's wife is also at the shop (June 2026 review).
chef_bio.philosophy: The menu is decided by the day's ingredients, each cooked the best way for it (September 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: "Entering this restaurant begins with a playful touch, as you press the intercom of a hidden door. Located on the second floor, the interior features a modern Japanese space with tatami flooring." — June 2026.

places.notes: [Chicken nanban · a one-dish chicken nanban lunch spot in Ura-Namba] A popular little counter shop in Ura-Namba that serves only chicken nanban, the crisp-battered chicken with sweet vinegar and tartar sauce. The set is ¥1,700: choose classic sweet vinegar, lemon basil or spicy mala, or pay ¥600 more for a double portion with two sauces. The clay-pot rice, a black-pepper pasta side, pickles and the egg-rich tartar sauce are all bottomless, so the set is filling. Food comes fast, but expect a short wait at weekend lunch. Daytime only; closed Wednesdays and Thursdays. No cards.

places.cuisine: Japanese fish and seasonal dishes, à la carte or course · every table starts with sea bream dashi and small dishes · assorted sashimi of wild fish (e.g. bluefin tuna, seared Spanish mackerel, yellowtail, sweet shrimp with salt and sudachi) · autumn eggplant with hairy crab sauce · simmered octopus and vegetables · matsutake dobin-mushi · shrimp cream croquettes · lotus root manju with crab · grilled oysters on kombu · shrimp and sake-lees gratin · duck breast, wagyu dishes · Kue hot pot with rice porridge in winter · Korean and Chinese dishes too: cold noodles, Horumon Chige, sweet and sour pork, spring rolls · clay-pot sea bream rice · sake such as Dewazakura and Tenpo Ichi · 10 counter seats and two sunken tables
places.notes: [Japanese · wild-fish sashimi and seasonal small dishes, Shimanouchi] A calm, quietly tucked-away Japanese restaurant near Nagahoribashi with a counter and two sunken tables. Every table begins with a gentle sea bream dashi and small seasonal dishes (charged ¥1,650–2,200), then you order à la carte or take a course. The assorted sashimi of wild fish is the reason to come, cut with care; after that the menu runs from autumn eggplant in hairy crab sauce, matsutake dobin-mushi and crab-filled lotus root manju to Kue hot pot in winter, plus a few surprise Korean and Chinese dishes such as cold noodles and sweet and sour pork. Attentive, friendly service suits solo diners at the counter. One diner found portions modest. Closed Mondays.

chef_bio.background: Japanese restaurant of fish and seasonal dishes (Tabelog; 2025–2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "When visiting Nanairo, you must try the sashimi assortment. The sweet shrimp served with salt and sudachi was simply exquisite…" — October 2026.
"Unusually for a Japanese restaurant… Korean and Chinese dishes, and the sweet and sour pork and Korean cold noodles are of restaurant-level quality…" — April 2026.

places.cuisine: Counter French built on Wakayama ingredients · lunch course around ¥10,000, e.g. carrot mousse with ikura; barracuda, turnip and olive; homemade bread; octopus quenelle with scallops, mussels and clam chowder; Iwate duck with fig, eggplant and Kaneyama miso; fromage blanc with rum raisin ice cream; tea and petits fours with fresh brown-sugar financiers · dinner: e.g. Kumano Beef & Foie Gras Course ¥18,700, 7-glass pairing ¥9,900 · a seasonal miniature-garden opener · meat finished on a shichirin over Binchotan · homemade plum soda; Colombian Geisha coffee · 12 seats: counter and a semi-private table for 4
places.notes: [French · counter French with Wakayama ingredients, Nagahoribashi] A white, calm second-floor counter near Nagahoribashi, easy to miss from the street, that builds its French courses around Wakayama produce: Kumano beef, Nanko plums, Kaneyama miso and Binchotan charcoal for meat finished on a shichirin in the open kitchen. The chef is from Wakayama Prefecture, and the shop is featured in the Michelin Guide Kyoto-Osaka 2025. Meals open with a miniature garden that changes with the season. Lunch (around ¥10,000) might bring carrot mousse with ikura, an octopus quenelle in clam chowder and Iwate duck with Kaneyama miso; dinner runs to the Kumano Beef & Foie Gras Course with a wine pairing. Save room for the warm brown-sugar financiers, and try the homemade plum soda. Courses by reservation; 10% service.

chef_bio.background: Counter French restaurant (Tabelog; 2025–2026 reviews). The chef is from Wakayama Prefecture, and the shop is featured in the Michelin Guide Kyoto-Osaka 2025 (Tabelog listing).
chef_bio.philosophy: Courses built around Wakayama ingredients (2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "…right in front of me was a shichirin (charcoal grill) in the open kitchen! I had never seen a shichirin in a French restaurant before! They used Binchotan charcoal from Wakayama…" — January 2026.
"The use of Wakayama ingredients, such as the plum in the soda and the Kaneyama miso, left a strong impression on me as they were key to the dishes' flavors." — September 2026, lunch course.

places.notes: [Tonkatsu · thick, tender tonkatsu with free refills, Namba] A busy tonkatsu shop a few minutes from Namba, one of several New Babe branches, serving thick, tender cutlets: a loin over 2 cm thick with sweet fat (¥2,800) or lean Hire (¥3,200), and sets pairing a cutlet with garlicky ginger pork. places.cuisine: Oden in a light, drinkable Osaka-style broth · assorted five-piece oden platter: daikon, beef tendon, egg, thick fried tofu, mochi pouch · also fresh yuba, corn, duck, green onion pouch, shirataki, sea bream with salt and lemon, shiitake, takoyaki · shumai floating in the broth with black pepper · freshly fried fish cakes (e.g. with wood ear mushroom) · dashimaki wrapped in cherry leaves · ginger tempura, corn tempura · firefly squid in soy · chilled Chinese noodles or chazuke to finish · seasonal sake; apple vinegar sour · 9 seats: 7 at the counter
places.notes: [Oden · a small oden counter with freshly fried fish cakes, Nipponbashi] A calm, clean nine-seat oden shop near Kintetsu Nippombashi, sister to a fish-cake maker, so the freshly fried fish cakes are the thing to order: chewy and full of umami. The broth is the light Osaka kind you can drink, and it soaks into a daikon tender enough to cut with chopsticks; start with the five-piece platter, then try shumai floating in the broth with black pepper. Beyond oden there's dashimaki wrapped in cherry leaves and chilled Chinese noodles or chazuke to finish. Orders go through your phone; check with staff if anything goes missing. Good for solo diners. Open until 1:00.

chef_bio.background: Oden shop (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).

places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: bonito flakes over the kamaage udon; dashi; mentaiko and meat toppings.

places.cuisine: Udon from a noodle maker in business since 1910 · signature kamaage udon ¥680: thin homemade noodles in their hot water under a heap of bonito flakes, seasoned yourself with Yuasa soy sauce and ground sesame · cold mentaiko nama-shoyu udon ¥830 with shiso and nori · grated daikon udon, plain dashi udon, curry udon, meat udon; soba too · noodles thin, extra thin, thick or kishimen; sizes up to 1.5 · small rice balls; weekly rice, e.g. bamboo shoot rice · free homemade tenkasu and green onion on the table · 16 seats
places.notes: [Udon · a noodle factory's own udon shop by Kuromon Market] A clean, calm little udon shop just outside Kuromon Market, run by a noodle maker founded in 1910, open only a few days a week. The shop belongs to a noodle maker with more than 100 years of history and has appeared on many TV shows and in magazines. The owner, a woman, runs the shop with the owner's husband; both are very kind. The thing to order is the kamaage udon (¥680): thin homemade noodles in their own hot water, buried under bonito flakes, which you season with Yuasa soy sauce and fresh-ground sesame — a dish that began as the factory's staff meal. The cold mentaiko nama-shoyu udon (¥830) is a good summer choice, and you can pick thin, extra-thin or thick noodles or kishimen. Add the free homemade tenkasu and green onion. Cash only; open Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday and Saturday.

chef_bio.origin: Run by the Futaba Seimenjo noodle factory, founded 1910 (May–July 2026 reviews).
chef_bio.background: Udon shop of a noodle maker (Tabelog; 2026 reviews). The owner, a woman, runs the shop with the owner's husband; both are very kind (May 2026 review). The shop belongs to a noodle maker with more than 100 years of history and has appeared on many TV shows and in magazines (Tabelog listing).

places.notes: [Curry · a spice-curry lunch that turns into a bar at night, Kozu] A small Nipponbashi-side curry shop near the National Bunraku Theatre that serves spice curry at lunch and becomes a bar in the evening. Lentil and spinach or salmon and potato curries round out the menu, and combination sets add a hamburger steak. Three sizes. One diner noticed cigarette smoke at lunch. Closed Mondays.

places.notes: [Kushiage · fried skewer courses and big-shrimp lunches by Yotsubashi] A quiet, modern kushiage restaurant under a big shrimp sign just south of Yotsubashi Station. At night, order a course of 10 or 15 small, carefully fried skewers (you can change the count along the way): seasonal conger eel, juicy shrimp, tomato with cheese, chicken with shiso, beef, even a takoyaki skewer in broth and dessert skewers, paced to how fast you eat, with six condiments from sauce to rock salt. The knife work stands out, changing how each piece of fish feels and melts, and a wall of wine faces the counter, so wine and sake pair easily with the nigiri. Weekend lunch is the gentle way in at ¥6,600 for omakase nigiri. Conversation at the counter is relaxed and friendly. One diner found the rice a bit dry and one the chawanmushi weak. Closed Mondays.

places.notes: [Taiwanese · Taiwanese fried-chicken bento and lu rou fan, Shimanouchi] A small, cute Taiwanese street-food shop on the edge of Shimanouchi, done up like a Taiwanese school lunchroom, with aluminium bento boxes and a menu in the style of a school notebook. It is run by two women, and the friendly staff are Taiwanese. The order is ji pai, a big, thin cutlet of pounded chicken breast fried crisp and juicy, in salt-pepper or the sweet special sauce, as a bento over rice with lightly seasoned vegetables, thick fried tofu and egg. The shredded-pork lu rou fan is just as good, and the radish cake and apple soda round it out. Order by QR code; lots of takeout and delivery. Open every day.

places.notes: [Omurice · demi-glace omurice topped with dote-ni, Minami-Senba] A tiny six-seat counter on a back street near Shinsaibashi that puts an Osaka spin on omurice. The Naniwa Omurice sets fluffy egg in a rich demi-glace and crowns it with tender, slow-cooked beef-tendon dote-ni and green onion, so the sweet egg, deep sauce and savory tendon melt together. Add cheese if you like, choose your rice amount and toppings, and note that even the SS size fills you up. There's a handmade hamburg steak and a side of dote-ni too. Busy at lunch; expect a short wait. Cash only.

places.notes: [Italian · an adult-oriented trattoria and wine bar, Kitahorie] A trattoria near Nishi-Ohashi in its 17th year, billed as a calm place for grown-ups, with house rules set out on the tables and the menu. A small family-run trattoria; one dish carries the chef’s memories of a grandfather cook from Campania. Read them before you go: dinner carries a ¥330 coperto and a per-person minimum order, and the kitchen can be slow on busy nights. In return you get carefully made pasta, a good wine list chosen with the staff, and dishes like fresh fish carpaccio, tripe stew, duck, Sangen pork and a steak of satisfyingly red meat. Lunch is the easy way in: pasta with salad, bread and an Italian omelette for ¥1,300–1,600, three days a week. Closed Mondays.

chef_bio.background: Trattoria and wine bar (Tabelog; 2026 reviews). A small family-run trattoria; one dish carries the chef’s memories of a grandfather cook from Campania (Tabelog listing).
chef_bio.philosophy: Aimed at calm adults; house notes set out manners and ordering rules (2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "The pasta was delicious, showcasing a great attention to the quality of the noodles." — March 2026.
"We started with the fresh fish carpaccio, followed by gratin and tripe, and for the main course, we had duck and pork from the Sangen breed, both of which were incredibly tasty." — September 2026.

places.name: AWA SUSHI 泡鮨 (AWA SUSHI)
places.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: soy sauce on the sushi; simmered and fried dishes; dobin-mushi dashi. Tell the restaurant when booking and ask.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a fish and shellfish omakase.
places.hours_raw: Daily 17:00–22:30, last entry 20:30, all guests start together; lunch for private bookings only (Tabelog). Reservation only (May 2026). Cards, transit IC, iD and QR (PayPay, Alipay, WeChat Pay) accepted; no service charge (Tabelog).
places.neighborhood: Minami-Senba 2-6-7, inside Cuvée J2 Hôtel Osaka — 1 min from Nagahoribashi Stn via the Crysta Nagahori north 4 elevator
places.cuisine: Sushi omakase paired with champagne · several small dishes and about 10–12 nigiri, soup and a seasonal dessert · e.g. abalone steamed for six hours with liver sauce, finished with a little sushi rice; surf clam; anago; uni; medium-fatty tuna; aged fish; deep-fried young sweetfish; Kamochi Ayu; dobin-mushi · champagne pairing by the glass from over 200 champagnes, with a featured house each month · 10 counter seats
places.notes: [Sushi · sushi omakase with a champagne pairing, Minami-Senba] A sophisticated ten-seat sushi counter inside a champagne-themed hotel near Nagahoribashi, built around one idea: sushi with champagne. The head chef, Kim, previously worked at the two-star Kuruma Sushi and at Sushi Shiro. The omakase runs to small dishes and about a dozen nigiri, with standouts like abalone steamed for six hours in its liver sauce (mixed with a little sushi rice at the end), sweet uni, medium-fatty tuna and anago with a rich sauce. The pairing pours a glass every two or three courses from a list of over 200 champagnes, with a featured house each month, and staff guide non-experts well. Dinner only, all guests start together; reserve for an anniversary night. One diner found a grilled fish watery.

chef_bio.background: Sushi counter in Cuvée J2 Hôtel Osaka (Tabelog; 2026 reviews). The head chef, Kim, previously worked at the two-star Kuruma Sushi and at Sushi Shiro (April 2026 review).
chef_bio.philosophy: Sushi paired with champagne (2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "What stood out the most was the abalone that had been steamed for 6 hours. It was astonishingly tender, and when dipped in the liver sauce, the umami flavor burst forth…" — April 2026, Awa Sushi Omakase Course.
"I requested the champagne pairing, enjoying one glass with every two to three dishes, totaling five glasses." — April 2026.

places.notes: [Curry · a ¥980 chicken katsu curry behind JR Namba, Inari] A small, warm curry shop on a quiet street about ten minutes from JR Namba that stays open through the afternoon. The order is the chicken katsu curry (¥980): the katsu is the surprise, crisp outside and tender and juicy within, over a mild, homestyle European curry sweet with onion. Some diners find the sauce a little sparse for the rice; there's a spicier curry too. It can be slow when one person is cooking at the lunch rush, smoking is allowed and the room gets hot in summer. Closed Sundays.

chef_bio.background: Italian meat bar (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).

places.notes: [Italian · a one-person Italian with a ¥1,200 pasta lunch, Minami-Senba] A small second-floor Italian near Nagahoribashi, run single-handed and still quick, that fills up at lunch. anecdotes.text: "For pasta, you can choose from three sauces: tomato, oil, or cream… The sauce, rich with fresh cream, was decadent yet light, making it very enjoyable." — January 2026, A Lunch ¥1,200, tuna and mushroom cream sauce.

places.cuisine: Creative mushroom cuisine at dinner · Bamboo course: mushroom sashimi of several kinds, shiitake dobin-mushi, grilled mushrooms, tempura, a hot pot of many mushrooms, risotto from the hot pot, ice cream (course only) · à la carte too: mushroom hot pot, maitake tempura, grilled or deep-fried shiitake · mushroom sake and gin · weekday lunch: soup curry · 16 seats: 8 at the counter
places.notes: [Mushroom · creative mushroom courses, Minami-Senba] A small, pleasant restaurant near Shinsaibashi where nearly everything at dinner is mushrooms. The Bamboo course runs from mushroom sashimi (crunchy yet moist, several kinds) and a shiitake dobin-mushi through grilled mushrooms and tempura to a hot pot crowded with varieties, then a risotto made in the broth and ice cream. Staff explain the mushrooms and how to eat each dish. Seasoning is gentle and the umami is deep. Try the mushroom sake or gin. Weekday lunch is a different menu: soup curry only. Reserve for dinner. One diner got soggy tempura.

chef_bio.background: Mushroom-themed restaurant (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "I had never tried sashimi made with mushrooms before, and the crunchy yet moist texture with various types was a refreshing experience." — October 2026.
"The shiitake dobin mushi was especially amazing—I could drink it for a lifetime!" — September 2026.

places.cuisine: Sri Lankan-style spice curry plates · Dekkao Special ¥1,300: bone-in chicken curry plus a daily curry, with sides · Mini Dekkao Special ¥1,250 with three sides · Greedy Dekkao Special ¥1,650: chicken curry, two daily curries and four sides · daily curries (about four or five), e.g. komatsuna and pork keema, spicy coconut tuna, clam and tomato, spicy squid (+¥100), vinegar pork · sides such as coconut furikake, stir-fried eggplant, tomato salad, mizuna with coconut · eat each first, then mix everything · 13 seats
places.notes: [Curry · Sri Lankan-style curry plates, Minami-Senba] A busy, homey second-floor curry shop near Shinsaibashi, easy to miss from the street, serving Sri Lankan-style curry adapted to Japanese tastes: spicy but approachable. Build a plate around the bone-in chicken curry and one or two of the four or five daily curries, such as clam and tomato or spicy coconut tuna; the Dekkao Special is ¥1,300 and the Greedy version adds a second curry and more sides for ¥1,650. Taste each curry and side first, then mix it all together. Warm, smiling staff. Expect a line at opening. Mostly lunch; dinner Tuesdays and Thursdays. Closed Sundays. PayPay, no cards.

chef_bio.background: Sri Lankan-style curry shop (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
chef_bio.philosophy: Sri Lankan curry blended with Japanese cooking to suit Japanese tastes (September 2026 review, citing the owner).

anecdotes.text: "The standard way to enjoy this meal is to first savor each curry and side dish separately, and then mix them together." — September 2026, Greedy Dekkao Special ¥1,650.

"The clam and tomato curry, which I tried for the first time, had a wonderful clam flavor and was delicious. It was perfectly spicy, and it paired well with the chicken curry." — September 2026, Dekkao Special ¥1,300.

places.notes: [Italian · a bright, casual Italian bistro, Kitahorie] A bright, warm Italian in western Kitahorie, a short walk from Yotsubashi, casual enough for families at lunch and lively at dinner. Lunch is pasta with potage, bread and salad, such as a fresh tomato pasta with swordfish and spinach. At night, courses and à la carte run to braised beef cheek, a rich uni cream pasta for mopping up with baguette, melt-in-the-mouth black-haired wagyu, sirloin cap steak and crab risotto, ending with homemade tiramisu. Birthday plates on request; friendly staff. It fills up, so reserve. Closed Mondays.

anecdotes.text: "The braised beef cheek was incredibly tender, and the uni cream pasta was rich and paired perfectly with the baguette." — September 2026, course.
"I had the fig butter baguette, crab risotto, and sirloin cap steak. Everything was absolutely delicious." — October 2026.

places.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: soy sauce throughout; a fried spring roll; miso soup. Tell the restaurant when booking and ask.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a fish and shellfish omakase with beef and egg dishes.
places.hours_raw: Two seatings daily, 18:00–20:00 and 21:00–23:30; irregular closings and New Year break (Tabelog). Omakase ¥28,000 (February 2026). Cash only — no cards, e-money or QR (Tabelog). Gold leaf can be left off on request (March 2026).

places.cuisine: Sushi omakase ¥28,000 · e.g. starters of young bamboo shoot and wakame; ankimo; Miyazaki beef spring roll; flounder sashimi; homemade half-dried karasumi; otoro with ikura and egg yolk; uni with caviar and honey; chawanmushi with cod roe cream; red miso soup; roasted tea ice cream · nigiri such as sea bream, scallop, shimaaji, otoro, kuruma shrimp, fugu milt, charcoal-grilled saba bozushi, anago, tamago, otoro with uni · finale: uni served on the back of your hand with a shower of gold leaf · draft beer ¥1,000; Kyoto highball ¥1,500 · 6 counter seats
places.notes: [Sushi · a six-seat omakase with a gold-leaf finale, Minami-Senba] A quiet, six-seat sushi counter near Nagahoribashi with two seatings a night. The chef talks fluently with overseas guests in each guest’s own language. It's known online for its show-stopping finale, uni served on the back of your hand under a shower of gold leaf, but diners who came for the photos stay for the food: delicate starters, homemade karasumi, a cod roe chawanmushi and nigiri like kuruma shrimp, fugu milt and charcoal-grilled saba bozushi, on slightly soft rice. The omakase was ¥28,000 in early 2026. Hospitality is warm and humble, with humor at the counter. Gold leaf can be skipped if you're heading to work. Cash only.

chef_bio.background: Sushi omakase counter (Tabelog; 2026 reviews). The chef talks fluently with overseas guests in each guest’s own language (February 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: "One standout was the 'Saba Bōzushi' (mackerel sushi) grilled with charcoal. The combination of the fragrant charcoal aroma and the rich flavor of the mackerel was exceptional…" — May 2026.
"…upon entering, I was pleasantly surprised by the calm ambiance and the warm hospitality… The sushi rice was slightly softer than usual…" — March 2026.

places.notes: [Italian · pasta-centred Italian courses, Minami-Senba] A small second-floor Italian near Nagahoribashi with a calm, warm wooden room, run by one person and still quick. Everything is a course built on seasonal ingredients and beautiful presentation, and pasta is the strength: dinner brings two, such as chewy orecchiette with octopus and aonori, and a spaghetti with Ryukyu black pork and beets. Lunch A (soup, three breads, appetizers, pasta, dessert, drink) is already generous; Lunch B adds a main. The vegetables and the desserts, like peach melba, get special mention. Dinner Fridays to Sundays only. Reserve.

chef_bio.background: Italian course restaurant run by one person (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "The pasta, shaped like earlobes, was wonderfully chewy and had an amazing texture." — August 2026.
"Despite being run by just one person, the service was quick, and not only was the taste excellent, but the presentation was beautiful as well!" — September 2026, Lunch A Course.

places.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: soy-based eel sauce; breaded chicken katsu at lunch.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: eel, liver and chicken; fish-based soup likely.
places.hours_raw: Mon–Sat and public holidays 11:30–14:00 and 17:30–20:30; closed Sun (Tabelog). Eel grilled to order (July 2026). Very busy around Doyo no Ushi in late July (reviews). Cards, e-money and QR accepted (Tabelog).

places.cuisine: Eel, Edo style (steamed, then grilled over Kishu Binchotan) · unadon ¥1,800 (half eel) · jumbo / premium unaju with soup and pickles ¥3,600 · Gomori-ju of eel and grilled liver ¥2,200 · sansho from Wakayama, offered at the table · Kimagure weekday lunch: chicken katsu don small ¥700, regular ¥900 (two katsu), large; chicken kara-age ¥900 · charcoal-grilled chicken set · 10 counter seats
places.notes: [Eel · an eel counter since 1946, Kitahorie] A small counter near Nishi-Ohashi that has grilled eel since 1946, Edo style: steamed so the eel is fluffy, then finished over Kishu Binchotan with a sauce kept since the start, light and only gently sweet. A mother and son run it: the owner's son, the third generation, has taken over the grill. The unadon (¥1,800, half an eel) is the everyday order, and the premium unaju (¥3,600) or the Gomori-ju with grilled liver go further; you'll be asked whether you want sansho. Weekday Kimagure lunches are a bargain: a chicken katsu don from ¥700 that overflows the bowl. Eel is grilled to order. Expect crowds around Doyo no Ushi. Closed Sundays.

chef_bio.background: Eel restaurant run by two people (Tabelog; 2023–2026 reviews). A mother and son run it: the owner's son, the third generation, has taken over the grill (July 2026 review).
chef_bio.philosophy: Sauce kept since the restaurant opened (2025–2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "The eel is grilled using Kishu Binchotan charcoal, following the Edo-style (Kanto-style). The tender meat is coated in a sauce that has been passed down since the restaurant's inception." — April 2026, Gomori Ju ¥2,200.
"Since it's steamed, the meat is quite fluffy. The surface is grilled to a crisp, giving it a nice char…" — October 2026, premium unaju ¥3,600.

places.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: a pizzeria; wheat dough; tiramisu.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: cheese, salami and anchovy; a cheese-free marinara base exists — ask about toppings.
places.hours_raw: Tue–Fri and Sun 11:30–14:00 and 18:00–21:00; Sat 18:00–21:00; closed Mon (Tabelog). Busy after 12:00; 11:30–12:00 is quietest (August 2026). Weekday and weekend lunch menus differ (2023 review). Cards (VISA, JCB) accepted (Tabelog).

places.cuisine: Wood-fired pizza · lunch pizzas with salad (e.g. watercress) from just over ¥1,000: about 12 options incl. two daily specials · Margherita ¥1,200; Diavola ¥1,300 (marinara base, spicy salami, chili, garlic; spice level on request); Capricciosa; Quattro Formaggi; Bianca with porcini and smoked mozzarella; anchovy; buffalo mozzarella · three bases: Margherita, Marinara (no cheese), Bianca (no tomato) · marinated octopus, salami · tiramisu ¥500 · beer ¥500, wine · 18 seats: 6 at the counter, 12 upstairs
places.notes: [Pizza · wood-fired pizza in a little house, Minami-Senba] A charming small house near Nagahoribashi with an Italian wood-fired oven at the back, a counter downstairs and tables upstairs, and a stained-glass pizza in the window. Pizzas come out in minutes with a chewy, fragrant crust whose twisted edge is a highlight. The Diavola (¥1,300), a cheese-free marinara with spicy salami, chili and plenty of garlic, is properly hot, so ask for it milder if you like; the Bianca with porcini and smoked mozzarella and the Quattro Formaggi are the cheesy picks. Lunch pizzas come with a salad for about ¥1,000–1,300. Go before noon. Closed Mondays.

chef_bio.background: Wood-fired pizzeria (Tabelog; 2023–2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "The twisted edge has a nice chewiness and a wonderful wheat aroma, the dough itself is very delicious." — August 2026, Diavola ¥1,300.
"I ordered the Bianca Porcini, and as expected from a wood-fired oven, it was served in just a few minutes! The aroma of smoked mozzarella and porcini mushrooms was irresistible!" — August 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: ラ・ゴロセッタ、大阪市中央区南船場2-8-13、心斎橋・長堀橋駅から徒歩、火〜金・日 11:30〜14:00・18:00〜21:00、土 18:00〜21:00、月曜休み、カード (VISA・JCB) 可、18席 (1階カウンター6、2階テーブル12)。口コミ(2023年6月〜2026年10月): かわいい一軒家、奥にイタリアの薪窯、ピザのステンドグラス、数分で焼き上がる、もちもちで香ばしい生地とねじった耳、昼はサラダ (クレソンなど) つきで1,000円ちょっとから、日替わり2種を含め12種ほど、マルゲリータ1,200円、ディアボラ1,300円 (マリナーラにスパイシーなサラミ、唐辛子、にんにく、辛さは調整可)、カプリチョーザ、クアトロフォルマッジ、ポルチーニとスモークモッツァレラのビアンカ、アンチョビ、水牛のモッツァレラ、ベースはマルゲリータ・マリナーラ (チーズなし)・ビアンカ (トマトなし)、蛸のマリネ、サラミ、ティラミス500円、ビール500円、ワイン、12時を過ぎると混む、サラダのドレッシングは塩気が強めという声。

cultural_comfort.note: Staff suggest pizzas and adjust spice (2023–2026).
