places.cuisine: Japanese fish and sake · a monthly course around ¥5,000 with a sake pairing, ending in a fish hot pot rather than meat: e.g. Kinmedai shabu-shabu, sea bream shabu-shabu, abalone shabu-shabu, conger eel sukiyaki with egg, whale Harihari hot pot (Oct 2026) · courses run from a starter (e.g. ikura chawanmushi, nagaimo somen) through sashimi (e.g. Kinmedai, Katsuo, Isaki), grilled and steamed dishes (eel, conger eel, sweetfish, duck with water eggplant) to zosui, udon or noodles · sakes such as Zao, Sasaichi, Kinran · weekday lunch: daily set or bento about ¥1,000 · 13 seats
places.notes: [Japanese · monthly fish hot-pot course with a sake pairing, Minami-Senba] A small, long-running izakaya tucked into the back of a building near Shinsaibashi, with a counter and a few tables. The draw is the monthly course, around ¥5,000 with a glass of sake matched to each dish: a seasonal starter, three kinds of sashimi, grilled and steamed fish, then a fish hot pot as the main, such as Kinmedai shabu-shabu or conger eel sukiyaki, finished with zosui or noodles. The menu changes every month; one diner returns every month. Dislikes are handled if you say so when booking. Weekday lunch is a cheap daily set. Smoking allowed. Closed Sundays.

chef_bio.background: Izakaya of seasonal fish and sake (Tabelog; 2015–2026 reviews).

places.notes: [French · a late-night creative French bistro, Minami-Senba] A cozy counter-and-table French spot near Nagahoribashi that serves until 1:00, with warm service and a sommelier chef for wine. Order à la carte, such as the roast duck breast with bigarade sauce, the seafood pilaf or the inventive consommé daikon, or book the Executive Course of foie gras mousse, lobster and foie gras fricassée and roast Ezo venison, finishing with a duck pilaf. chef_bio.background: Creative French bistro (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).

places.notes: [Bar · a bread-and-drinks bar, Minami-Senba] A stylish little second-floor bar near Nagahoribashi built around bread with wine. Order the CHE Sandwich (¥800), crisp hash browns with gooey cheese and egg, then work through baguettes and toasts topped with aosa butter, salt kombu and cream cheese, or a prosciutto and new onion yukhoe; the water eggplant and prosciutto salad is a cool side. Wines sit in a fridge for you to choose, from ¥3,800 a bottle including domestic labels, plus craft gin and grape beer. With one person on the floor it can be slow. Cash only. Open late Fridays and Saturdays; closed Mondays and Tuesdays.

"The Aosa Butter Sandwich had a delightful fresh scent of the ocean, and the Corn Potage Toast truly tasted like corn potage, which was quite interesting." — June 2026.

places.notes: [Soba · a soba shop that turns into a soba izakaya, Shinmachi] A small soba shop near Yotsubashi that has served thin, fragrant Ju-wari soba for many years, packed at lunch and a relaxed soba izakaya at night. At lunch, try the Iso Karami Soba with seaweed, sudachi and spicy daikon, or a set of cold soba with a miso tempura rice bowl; the grated daikon is fiercely hot, and the soba is good with just salt. In the evening, order the five-piece small-plate platter, a dashi omelette and grilled iwana with sake, then finish with Bokkake soba. Counter seats are tight. Closed Sundays.

chef_bio.origin: Diners recall visits nearly 20 years ago (September 2026 review).

places.notes: [Hamburg steak · a seven-seat hamburg steak lunch, Hakurocho] A tiny lunch-only grill in the Senba textile district with a line most weekdays. The hamburg steak is coarse-ground, seared crisp on a sizzling iron plate and juicy inside, roughly 150–200 g; top it with wasabi grated daikon (one repeat diner's usual order), cheese, bacon or a tangy homemade tomato sauce, in Japanese or demi-glace style. Pay ¥100 more for egg rice made with rich Ran-oh eggs. Rice and a ginger beef-tendon soup are refillable. Friendly staff. Arrive before opening or after 2 pm. PayPay only. Closed Wednesdays.

anecdotes.text: "This hamburg steak has a coarsely ground texture that gives it a satisfying meatiness, crumbling delightfully in my mouth." — August 2026, bacon hamburg steak +70 g with egg rice.
"The wasabi adds a nice touch, making it refreshing and enhancing the flavors of the meat and fat." — September 2026, Wasabi Oroshi Hamburger Steak with Egg Rice.

Two sittings a night; 10% service. places.cuisine: Neapolitan pizza only, wood-fired · Margherita ¥1,000 · Marinara · Ricotta e Cipolla ¥1,500 · served uncut, with a note on how to eat it · Coke ¥300 · ticket machine · 13 counter seats facing the oven
places.notes: [Pizza · a one-person Neapolitan pizza counter, Shinmachi] A clean, thirteen-seat counter near Nishi-Ohashi where the owner, working solo as pizzaiolo, stretches, tops and fires every pizza in a blazing wood oven in front of you, alongside a steady run of takeout orders. It has held a Michelin Bib Gourmand five years running, was ranked 27th in 50 Top Pizza Asia-Pacific 2023, and was named one of the top 100 pizza restaurants in 2017, 2018, 2019 and 2021. Buy a ticket from the machine; the Margherita is ¥1,000 and arrives in a few minutes, toasted outside and chewy within, uncut so you slice it yourself. Try the Marinara or the Ricotta e Cipolla too. No reservations and cash only; go right at opening, as lunch lines form fast. Closed Mondays and Tuesdays.

chef_bio.background: Neapolitan pizzeria run by one person (Tabelog; 2026 reviews). The owner works solo, stretching dough non-stop (September 2026 review). It has held a Michelin Bib Gourmand five years running, was ranked 27th in 50 Top Pizza Asia-Pacific 2023, and was named one of the top 100 pizza restaurants in 2017, 2018, 2019 and 2021 (September 2026 reviews).

places.notes: [Curry · a one-person dashi curry shop, Minami-Senba] A calm, lunch-only curry counter behind a heavy door in Minami-Senba, where the owner cooks alone and calls the style "Ware": thick curries built on Japanese dashi, aromatic rather than hot. places.notes: [Italian · a small Italian with animals hidden in the décor, Minami-Senba] A gentle, café-like twelve-seat Italian at the back of a building near Nagahoribashi, with antique furniture, dried flowers and little animals hidden everywhere, even on the door handles. The chef honed the craft at Michelin-starred restaurants in Italy. Lunch is excellent value: the ¥1,300 weekday set brings a plate of seven carefully made vegetable appetizers and a mini soup before a well-judged pasta, and the ¥3,200 course adds a main such as braised Chami pork. Dinner is a course of about eleven small, elaborate dishes, explained one by one, from homemade ham to straw-grilled wagyu; desserts cost extra and portions are small. Closed Thursdays.

places.notes: [Japanese · seafood lunches and courses in a renovated house, Ikutamacho] A beautifully renovated house on a quiet street near Tanimachi 9-chome, with a counter and tables. Lunch is a choice of grilled or simmered fish, the species a surprise, with side dishes and refillable rice for ¥1,650; the simmered fish is generous and gently seasoned. At night, the ¥5,500 course runs from appetizers and fine sashimi through a dobin-mushi brightened with sudachi and a whole simmered fish to tempura and clay-pot rice, closing with nyumen. Everything is made with care, so it takes time; settle in. Closed Tuesdays and Wednesdays.

chef_bio.background: Japanese seafood restaurant (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "I had the option to choose between grilled fish or simmered fish, so I ordered the simmered fish set meal… The simmered fish was Houbou, and it was tender and flavorful with a light taste." — October 2026, lunch ¥1,650.
"The clay pot was filled with fragrant broth… and then added a squeeze of sudachi for a refreshing burst of flavor…" — October 2026, ¥5,500 course.

places.cuisine: Dashi-based spice curry · pick a base — chicken broth with Shodoshima soy sauce, or katsuobushi dashi with soy milk — and a keema — chicken and pork, or fish (cod) — with sides such as gizzard achar and salmon achar: ¥1,450–1,500 · add-ons ¥200: squid and clam broth Thai curry, homemade egg masala; cilantro · specials: shrimp curry (Thu–Sat), San Gen pork and squid, spicy chicken plate · truffle crackers with homemade cream cheese; potato salad · 10 seats
places.notes: [Curry · dashi-based spice curry, Shinmachi] A small curry counter under a green awning in Shinmachi, run by a couple whose bright, attentive service, remembering returning faces, is half the appeal. The owner was formerly manager of a very famous Osaka curry shop that had a Bib Gourmand. The curry is light and soupy, built on dashi rather than heat: choose a chicken-broth base with Shodoshima soy sauce or a katsuobushi dashi with soy milk, then chicken-and-pork or fish keema, and mix in the sides, such as a crunchy gizzard achar. Add the ¥200 squid and clam Thai curry if it's on. Shrimp curry Thursdays to Saturdays. Open through 4 pm, handy for a late lunch. Cash only. Closed Sundays.

chef_bio.background: Spice curry shop run by two people (Tabelog; 2025–2026 reviews). A couple runs it; the owner was formerly manager of a very famous Osaka curry shop that had a Bib Gourmand (October 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: "The umami of the Japanese-style dashi is irresistible, and I couldn't help but keep eating." — October 2026, Rich Beef and Pork Keema (Japanese-style dashi) with cilantro.
"Among them, the gizzard achar stands out with its satisfying crunch and is absolutely exquisite." — September 2026, fish keema + sides ¥1,450.

places.notes: [Italian · a refined Italian of seasonal courses, Shinmachi] A calm twelve-seat Italian near Nishi-Ohashi, pale blue outside and gray stone and concrete within, where courses of unexpected ingredient pairings arrive on carefully chosen tableware. The chef has 20 years in Italian cooking, and one diner says the chef came out of Ponte Vecchio; the owner is a certified sommelier who picks the monthly sake pairings. The chef trained at a well-known restaurant in Kobe and runs PRESTAU with the chef's wife. The monthly lunch course (¥7,700) is the way in: a squid-ink risotto with cuttlefish and sudachi, delicate sardine with turnip, homemade conchiglie in beef-tongue ragù and charcoal-grilled duck, with a delicate rather than bold hand on seasoning. Desserts come in three stages. Dislikes are handled if mentioned ahead. One diner found drink service slow. Closed Mondays and one Sunday a month.

chef_bio.background: Italian course restaurant (Tabelog; 2026 reviews). The chef trained at a well-known restaurant in Kobe and runs PRESTAU with the chef's wife (July 2026 review). places.notes: [Ramen · rich chicken paitan by Daikokucho Station] A friendly ramen shop seconds from Daikokucho Station, open since late 2024 with a table for four as well as the counter. The young owner has a great smile, and a lively head chef works alongside. The signature is a rich, frothy chicken paitan; the special bowl adds grilled chashu, steamed chicken, an egg and red onion. The paitan also comes as a miso ramen, light enough to finish, and there's a back-fat shoyu with thin tip menma that is lighter than it looks. The mazesoba (¥1,250) comes with a rice bowl of aburi chashu. One diner found the miso broth lukewarm. Open all day at weekends.

places.notes: [Ramen · tom yum noodles and porcini ramen, Shinmachi] A one-person, eight-seat lunch shop in western Shinmachi with ramen unlike anywhere else. The Tom Yum Noodles (¥990) are the draw: creamy, sour, spicy and savory at once, with a mound of cilantro over straight noodles. The porcini mushroom salt ramen has its own fans, and there are dan dan noodles, a sudachi shoyu ramen and tsukemen. Add a small green curry or rice bowl. Cash only, and the ticket machine wants coins or older ¥1,000 notes, so bring change. Lunch only; closed Sundays, with the odd surprise closure.

places.notes: [Ramen · a chashu-heavy neighborhood ramen shop, Zaimokucho] A small, old-fashioned ramen counter near Matsuyamachi, now under a new owner and busy even mid-afternoon. The draw is chashu: the chashu ramen (¥1,200–1,300) carries about five thick, tender slices over thin, soft noodles, in shio, shoyu or miso, with garlic and spicy miso on the counter to sharpen it. For something different, the Harapeko Kizuna-men is a bowl of mixed noodles with chopped chashu and green onion; mix it from the bottom, then add vinegar and chili oil as the owner suggests. The garlic-chive gyoza are worth adding. One diner found the broth lukewarm. Cash only; open all day; closed Sundays.

places.notes: [Ramen · cheap Taiwanese ramen and mazesoba in Den Den Town] A simple ticket-machine noodle shop on a side street of Den Den Town, with a counter downstairs and more seats upstairs. The Taiwanese ramen is a bargain at ¥750: a soy-sauce broth that grows richer as the spicy minced meat seeps in, over thin noodles with good bite, milder than the chain versions and adjustable up to super spicy. The mazesoba comes with minced meat, onion and crunchy peanuts, with free fried onions on the table and rice offered at the end. Not into heat? There's a gentle tonkotsu ramen. Large size is free. Cash only. Open every day.

places.notes: [Ramen · aged-shoyu ramen five ways, Minami-Senba] A bright, roomy ramen shop near Nagahoribashi, open since early 2024, with tables as well as a counter and a family-friendly feel. The house bowl is aged shoyu ramen on a chicken-and-seafood broth, in five styles: plain, with katsuo, with yuzu (¥900), with back fat, or black. The back-fat versions are lighter than they look, and the spicy garlic chives on the table give them a punch. There's also an iekei-style tonkotsu and a thick tantanmen, plus seasonal specials such as a chilled ago-dashi ramen with duck chashu in summer. Ticket machine, cash only; staff are lively and quick.

places.notes: [Ramen · a JoJo-themed performance ramen counter, Hakurocho] Less a ramen shop than an attraction: nine counter seats in a room filled with figures from JoJo's Bizarre Adventure, where the owner drains noodles shouting the manga's catchphrases and serves each bowl in character. Every ramen is ¥2,000 with free extra noodles and toppings; the miso tonkotsu is rich and creamy, the cilantro ramen very strong, and the tomato mazesoba (¥1,500) comes with free rice, cheese and kimchi. A ¥1,000 prize lottery never loses. Groups are served in turn, so expect to queue one to two hours from before 7 pm. Cash only. Closed Sundays and Mondays.

places.cuisine: Malatang · pick ingredients from a chilled case, individually packed at fixed prices: napa cabbage, bok choy, komatsuna, lettuce, okra, lotus root, wood ear, enoki, egg tofu, quail eggs, fish cakes, beef and other meats · noodles: instant, thin or thick Chinese noodles, egg noodles, vermicelli · rich, sesame-heavy broth with separate numbing and spice levels · black vinegar on the table · rice; buns · bottled beer ¥600 · typically ¥1,200–1,700
places.notes: [Malatang · a sesame-rich malatang worth the walk, Motomachi] A pick-your-own malatang shop between Namba and Daikokucho, a little out of the way, so there's rarely a queue. Fill a bowl from the case of individually priced ingredients, from napa cabbage, okra and lotus root to egg tofu, quail eggs and beef, choose your noodles, from instant to chewy thick ones, then set the numbing and spice levels separately. The broth is unusually rich in sesame, closer to dan dan noodles, and a splash of the black vinegar halfway through makes it creamier. A bowl typically runs ¥1,200–1,700. Pay after eating. Open daily until 11 pm.

"The individually packaged ingredients were clearly priced, making it easy to understand. I realized that the fixed pricing, rather than weight-based pricing, is likely what makes it so popular." — October 2026.

places.notes: [Seafood · a fishmonger's lunch counter, Shinmachi] A fish shop in western Shinmachi with a surprisingly roomy counter at the back, where lunch is a good-value seafood meal. The daily sashimi bowl comes heaped with tuna on red-vinegar rice, and the Hokkaido bowl piles salmon, ikura, scallops and crab, each with two side dishes, a rich fish soup and dessert for about ¥1,400. There's an eight-piece sushi set too. Evenings bring a long list of fish dishes and good sashimi. Buy fish, side dishes or a bento on the way out. Closed Wednesdays and the 1st and 3rd Tuesdays.

chef_bio.background: Fish shop with an eat-in counter (Tabelog; 2024–2026 reviews).

places.notes: [Yakitori · aged-chicken yakitori by night, chicken ramen by day, Senba] A quiet, hidden-feeling yakitori counter in the basement of the Senba Center Building, a minute from Honmachi Station. places.notes: [Chinese · a creative Chinese bar of small plates, Azuchimachi] A stylish, busy Chinese bar near Sakaisuji-Honmachi where colorful small plates are sized for two to share. places.notes: [Ramen · an old-style chicken shoyu shop, Minami-Horie] A quiet neighborhood ramen shop in western Minami-Horie with warm, attentive staff. The bowls are light and old-fashioned: a chicken shoyu broth that tastes mild at first and deepens as the tare at the bottom mixes in, medium-thin straight noodles, and tender, well-marinated chashu and good menma, which even diners who found the soup lacking praise. places.notes: [Ramen · a cozy chicken-paitan ramen and Chinese-food spot, Minami-Horie] A café-like ramen and Chinese-food shop facing Takadaibashi Park; one diner has ordered takeout from it for years. The chicken paitan comes in shio or shoyu, rich but not heavy, with a seasoned egg included at no charge, thick melt-in-the-mouth chashu, chopped onion and fried garlic. Pair a half bowl (¥800) with the fluffy small fried rice (¥350) for a cheap loop of rice, soup and chashu. There are also dan dan noodles, Taiwanese mazesoba, gyoza and a long drinks list. Smoking allowed. Hours vary; check before going.

places.notes: [Lanzhou noodles · hand-pulled Lanzhou beef noodles and lamb skewers, Namba-naka] A big, no-frills Chinese noodle house between Namba and Daikokucho. An older review found staff and customers mostly of Chinese descent. The draw is hand-pulled Lanzhou beef noodles in a light, spiced beef-bone broth finished with chili oil and cilantro, with your pick of eight noodle widths, chewy almost like udon at the wide end; Set A (¥1,200) adds small side dishes. Add cumin-spiced lamb skewers, or try the sour-and-spicy vermicelli and a cheap lamb-with-cumin set. Splash in the table vinegar halfway. Open every day. Ask for the non-smoking section.

places.notes: [Ramen · a Kumamoto ramen chain branch with tai-pien, Senba] A weekday-lunch branch of the Kumamoto ramen chain Ajisen, two floors down in the Senba Center Building and connected to Sakaisuji-Honmachi Station. The house tonkotsu (¥950) is satisfying if chain-standard, with fried garlic on the table. The reason to seek out this branch is tai-pien (¥1,100), Kumamoto's light glass-noodle soup loaded with shrimp, pork, squid and vegetables, rare in Osaka. Lunch sets pair ramen with takana rice. Two diners found it a little pricey. Weekdays 11:00–16:00, occasionally Saturdays.

places.notes: [Ramen · Tenri-style garlic stamina ramen, Uehonmachi] The Uehonmachi outpost of Saika, the garlicky stamina ramen from Tenri in Nara, open until midnight every day. places.notes: [Ramen · creative ramen and fruit-heaped kakigori, Tanimachi] A playful shop at the Tanimachi 5 crossing, decorated with anime-film goods, that does two things: inventive ramen and lavish shaved ice. The ramen changes with the season, from a vivid blue chilled seafood ramen to a rich chilled corn-cream bowl topped with rare figs, plus mazesoba to tweak with mayonnaise, chili oil and kombu vinegar; diners split on the boldest pairings. Many reviews are for the kakigori: fruit heaped all the way around, figs, peaches, a chestnut Mont Blanc piped at the table. Order by QR, one dish each; reserve on Instagram. Closed Tuesdays and Wednesdays.

places.notes: [Ramen · a one-person spicy chashu ramen counter, Kitahama] An old-fashioned ramen counter near Kitahama, run single-handed. The house Ramen Man is a pork-bone shoyu heaped with sliced and coarse-ground chili, bean sprouts and green onion, with chopped garlic if you want it; the chili isn't powdered into the soup, so the heat doesn't swamp the broth. The chashu ramen packs eight or nine small, tender pork-belly slices, and order it at spice level 2 or 3. Sets with rice and kimchi run ¥800–1,000. Smoking is allowed, which surprised one diner. Hours aren't listed. Cash only.

places.notes: [Teppanyaki · a 12-seat Dotonbori teppan counter with a river-view room] A small teppanyaki restaurant at street level on Dotonbori: seven counter seats facing the griddle and a semi-private room at the back that looks out on the Dotonbori River. The house course, the Panyo Dinner, runs through seared meat sushi, a Panyo burger and a domestic tenderloin; steaks can be upgraded to Special Wagyu or Matsusaka beef, and shrimp and abalone come live from the tank. A December 2025 course had grilled turnip, pumpkin and green onion and an 80 g tenderloin with salt, garlic and wasabi, then garlic rice with a light chicken soup. Diners have booked lunch courses for celebrations; on request the kitchen cooked the meat sushi through, and a birthday dessert came with fireworks in place of candles and a message. Dinner about ¥8,000–10,000, lunch ¥3,000–4,000 (Tabelog).

places.notes: [Café · a Showa-retro night kissa open until 6 am, Souemoncho] A second-floor night café off Souemoncho, done up in Showa-retro style, that opens at 19:00 on weekdays (13:00 at weekends) and runs until 6 am. The draw is dessert with a drink: pudding with a glass of Macallan, a rich, moist terrine, a banana split, or pancakes with cold coffee; there's also Neapolitan pasta under an omelet, cocktails and wine. One diner praised the cute plating, another the hidden-gem feel; at 4 am it was quiet. No reservations, and at weekend afternoons there's a waiting board at the door. ¥550 table charge; smoking allowed. Cards are listed, but one diner was asked for cash on a small bill.

chef_bio.background: Night café with a staff-maintained Tabelog listing (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
chef_bio.specialty: Pudding and drinks late at night.

anecdotes.text: "I visited this night cafe in Minami around 4 AM, and it was very quiet with a lovely atmosphere… One thing to note is that if your bill is under JPY 5000, [cash is requested]…" — March 2026.
"This time, I had pancakes, which paired perfectly with cold coffee! We also shared a Neapolitan pasta topped with an omelet…" — July 2026.

places.notes: [Teppanyaki · a 10-seat round-counter teppan with its own Gekko-yaki, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A calm, grown-up teppanyaki bar in a corner of a Higashi-Shinsaibashi building, with six seats around the griddle and one table, where the owner cooks in front of you and pours from a short list of red wines. The signature is Gekko-yaki, a fluffy egg-and-cabbage cake with thick pork, and two diners single out the kimchi-cheese version (¥2,700); the seafood yakisoba carbonara (¥2,500) folds shrimp and scallops into thick chewy noodles under a soft egg. Simpler plates: shrimp, squid and scallops grilled with salt, cabbage stir-fried with abura-kasu, grilled asparagus, salty grilled beef intestine. One diner found the seasoning salty overall. Expect about ¥6,000–8,000. Students may be turned away, children by arrangement only, and there's a dress code (no sandals or sweats).

places.notes: [Korean · a two-person basement Korean spot for soy-marinated crab, Sennichimae] A 16-seat basement Korean restaurant off Sennichimae, run by a friendly couple aged 70-something, open from 16:00 to 2 am and busy late; one night it was nearly full at 23:30. Come for the house-made ganjang gejang, crab marinated in soy (¥2,700 small, ¥5,500 large), or the sweet-spicy yangnyeom version, served with gloves; the soy-marinated shrimp is the other draw. Also cheese jeon, tender steamed pork, samgyetang, and an octopus, offal and shrimp hot pot for two that needs booking. Makgeolli comes by the bottle or ladled from a big bowl, and there's bottle keep. One diner found the food average and a little pricey but the service warm; another said it felt like coming home. English and Korean menus (Tabelog). Closed Wednesdays.

chef_bio.background: Korean restaurant run by two people (2025 reviews; Tabelog). A friendly couple aged 70-something runs it (August 2025 review).

anecdotes.text: "The Kanjang Gejang and Kanjang Saeu are just as amazing as I remembered!… It felt like coming home, making it a very comforting place." — November 2025, second visit.

places.notes: [Italian · a 14-seat alley Italian that turns into a late bar, Shinsaibashi] A small second-floor Italian restaurant at the end of a Shinsaibashi back alley, with warm wood, soft light and about 14 seats at the counter and tables. The listing says the chef trained at a top restaurant. Dinner is courses only: a November 2025 seven-course meal ran from seasonal oysters through charcoal-grilled anago and handmade squid-ink tagliolini to Wagyu sirloin cap with truffle sauce, and the house specialty is a Kawachi duck carpaccio. After 21:30 it opens an à la carte menu and works as a bar until 1 am, good for squid-ink pasta and dessert as a second stop. Two diners praise the plating, one the chef's funny conversation; another found the course price on the high side. About ¥8,000–15,000; ¥550 service charge.

places.notes: [Bakery café · puppy-shaped buns and Japanese tea, Amerikamura] A small bakery in Amerikamura whose idea is bread that goes with Japanese tea: buy downstairs, then eat upstairs in a calm, Japanese-style room with cushions, outlets and Wi-Fi. The star is the puppy bun (¥330), custard in the head and chocolate or hojicha cream in the body, with a Shiba Inu version (weekends only, per one diner) and a pink one that one diner took to hold strawberry jam. Also a dango Danish (¥300), a mitarashi dango bun, a clover-shaped Kyoto matcha anpan, a melon bread with a face and a yakisoba bun under a fried quail egg. There's a tea of the day to taste, and Japanese tea ordered with bread is ¥200 off. Buns are small and cheap, so it's easy to try two or three. Claim a seat upstairs before ordering.

chef_bio.background: Bakery with an eat-in floor (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
chef_bio.philosophy: Bread that pairs with Japanese tea (May–June 2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "The concept of this bakery is 'bread that pairs well with Japanese tea.' [There is] a tasting of the tea of the day, and if you order a set with tea, you can enjoy a discount of JPY 200 on your drink." — June 2026.

places.notes: [Venison · a deer-meat izakaya open to 4 am, Sennichimae] A small venison specialist on the Aioibashi-suji shopping street, nearly everything on the menu made from deer, and open for lunch and then from 18:00 to 4 am. The master's second son also works in the room. Several diners say the meat is lean, tender and free of gamey smell. The ¥2,500 lunch course brings a freshly fried venison cutlet, a low-temperature roast and venison fried rice; at night try the venison carpaccio, a juicy roast with salt and fried onions, rillettes on baguette, and the deer bread, roast venison on salty garlic toast. Newer dishes include crisp pleatless venison gyoza and a peppery venison mazesoba with egg yolk. A seven-dish venison yaki-shabu course (¥7,500) needs booking; one diner wished the cuts were explained. One diner noted a generous wine pour. ¥500 dinner charge.

chef_bio.background: Venison izakaya and bar (Tabelog; 2025–2026 reviews). The master's second son also works in the room (April 2026 review).
chef_bio.specialty: Venison cutlet; roast venison; deer bread.

anecdotes.text: "The venison is lean, with no fat… The freshly fried cutlet has a rich flavor, yet no gamey taste at all, and it's incredibly tender and delicious!" — May 2026, Venison Feast Lunch Course ¥2,500.
"The carpaccio had no gamey taste at all, and I felt the meatiness was even stronger than beef. The roast was perfectly cooked and juicy…" — September 2026.

places.notes: [Café · jiggly pancakes up a staircase, Shinsaibashi-suji] A second-floor pancake café off Shinsaibashi-suji, reached by a staircase straight from the door. The pancakes are the tall, wobbling kind, so soft one diner said they eat like a drink: the standard has a crisp caramelized top with custard inside, whipped cream, vanilla ice cream and berry sauce, plus a bitter caramel to adjust the sweetness. Seasonal versions include matcha with matcha custard and mascarpone (¥1,800 + tax), peach and mascarpone, and a summer chocolate-mint. For lunch there's a plate of French toast with bacon and eggs. Pancakes came in about 10 minutes for one diner. One weekday afternoon was quiet; one holiday lunch the two-person tables were nearly full. Order by QR code.

chef_bio.background: Pancake café (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
chef_bio.philosophy: Seasonal, natural ingredients (Tabelog listing).

anecdotes.text: "The freshly made pancakes were incredibly fluffy—so soft that they felt like a drink rather than food… The caramelized surface was crispy, and when I cut into it, I could see a hint of custard sauce inside." — June 2026.
"The lunch plate included French toast, bacon and eggs, chips, salad, and canelé. (The contents may change occasionally.)" — August 2026, 512 Lunch Plate.

places.notes: [Chicken · grill-your-own Tajima chicken over charcoal, Sennichimae] A small chicken specialist a few minutes from Nippombashi where you grill fresh Tajima chicken yourself, yakiniku style, on a charcoal brazier set in front of you. Order neck, thigh, skin, chewy older-hen meat or rarer heart cuts, then fill in with the raw dishes several diners single out: a chicken sashimi platter, liver sashimi and chicken sashimi with tororo. The chicken nanban and salt-stir-fried liver are thick but tender, and there are chicken hot pots and shabu-shabu for groups. The counter at the front lets you talk with the staff; the raised room at the back can be fully booked. It gets smoky, so dress for it. Opens 18:00, closed Mondays; AMEX is the only card.

chef_bio.background: Chicken izakaya with table grills (Tabelog; 2023–2025 reviews).
chef_bio.philosophy: Tajima chicken sourced fresh (Tabelog listing; May 2025).

anecdotes.text: "Yakitori is served on skewers, but the grilled chicken here is prepared in a yakiniku style… However, it does produce a lot of smoke." — June 2024.

The chewy handmade pasta comes up in several reviews: oyster and bottarga pasta with three big oysters, oyster pasta in January. Lunch is ¥1,800, a reserved lunch course ¥2,500, and a fuller ¥4,800 course with a drink runs from crab appetizers and onion-corn soup with fresh onion focaccia to sea bream and coconut tiramisu. Over 30 Italian wines, with pairing suggestions. One cook runs the kitchen, so dishes come at a leisurely pace; tables are close. One diner rated the cooking average but the value excellent. Cash only; closed Tuesdays and the 1st and 3rd Wednesdays.

chef_bio.origin: Opened 9 June 2018 (Tabelog); sister restaurant of SPELLO in Sakaisuji-Honmachi (January 2026 review).

places.notes: [Korean · an 8-seat Showa-retro Korean bar for gimbap and sundae, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A street-level Korean bar in Higashi-Shinsaibashi, run by two people and styled like a 1970s–80s Showa izakaya crossed with a Korean street stall, open until 2 am. The shop is run by Korean twins. Gimbap is the draw, in many varieties; one diner ordered a half roll and got a whole one. One diner calls it a rare find for sundae, Korean blood sausage; there's also bulgogi, jeon and Korean oden that one diner calls a must with Korean beer or Chamisul. One diner found prices well above Korea's. Eight seats around the counter, friendly service, smoking allowed and pets welcome; leftovers can go home with you. English and Korean menus (Tabelog). Opens 19:00 on weekdays, 17:00 at weekends.

chef_bio.background: Korean bar run by two people (November 2024 review; Tabelog). The shop is run by Korean twins (November 2024 review).

anecdotes.text: "It's rare to find a place in Japan that serves sundae… In fact, the gimbap is the main attraction here! There are many different types of gimbap available!" — August 2024.
"The Korean oden is absolutely delicious, so I highly recommend trying it when you go! It pairs perfectly with Korean beer and Chamisul as well." — February 2025.

places.notes: [Izakaya · a 10-seat back-alley counter with set-meal lunches, Shinsaibashi] A quiet 10-seat counter in an alley just off the busy Shinsaibashi-suji arcade, reopened in November 2025 under a new name by the owner of the former Wabisuke, with an Okinawan streak. Lunch is a tray set: pick a main such as the gently seasoned meat tofu (¥1,100) or chicken nanban with both mentaiko and tartar sauce, with rice refills, miso soup, small sides and a raw egg for egg-over-rice. At night order the obanzai assortment (¥990), which one diner saw every table order, plus rafute tacos (¥550) with hot sauce, tako-wasa with nagaimo, crab gratin and shrimp gyoza. Lunch can be reserved, which helps with so few seats.

chef_bio.origin: Opened 15 November 2025 (Tabelog); formerly Wabisuke, same owner (August 2026 review).
chef_bio.background: Counter izakaya with set-meal lunches (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "You can get free refills on rice, and it comes with four types of obanzai (Japanese side dishes) and a raw egg, which I used to make a delicious egg over rice." — August 2026, Meat Tofu Set Meal ¥1,100.

places.cuisine: Tempura counter izakaya (13 counter seats) · course ¥4,400 · classic tempura: jumbo shrimp, a whole anago, autumn eggplant · creative tempura: toro-taku canapé on seaweed, soft-boiled egg with shiba-zuke tartar, Camembert with honey · Carat Roll ¥1,540: salmon, sea bream and roe wrapped with myoga and shiso · niku-sui, beef soup with tofu · ju-wari (100% buckwheat) soba for dipping · sweet-potato tempura with vanilla ice cream and honey · sashimi · six kinds of sake; sparkling sake Mio ¥1,210
places.notes: [Tempura · a 13-seat late-night tempura counter with creative pieces, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A calm, stylish tempura counter in Higashi-Shinsaibashi that stays open until 3 am. The ¥4,400 course is the easy way in: a toro-taku canapé on seaweed tempura, a soft-boiled egg with shiba-zuke tartar, Camembert drizzled with honey, then jumbo shrimp, a whole anago and fan-cut eggplant, all served piping hot, plus the Carat Roll of salmon and sea bream wrapped with myoga and shiso. Two diners say the beef niku-sui soup, with 100% buckwheat soba to dip, stole the show; dessert is sweet-potato tempura with vanilla ice cream. Menus in English, Chinese and Korean, and English-speaking staff (Tabelog). ¥330 seat charge.

places.notes: [Sake bar · a 10-seat Tohoku sake counter with seasonal fish, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A calm second-floor sake bar of ten counter seats in Higashi-Shinsaibashi, open since 2015 and focused on local sake from Tohoku. Tell the staff what you like and a few get poured to try; one diner did a flight of one brewery's range, another paired sake with bonito. The food beats bar snacks: fish bought daily, red shrimp marinated in sake (two diners single it out), Senshu water eggplant as sashimi, squid tentacles with liver mayo, Wagyu sukiyaki-style, even Okinawa soba with squid-ink yakisoba. A sashimi platter from ¥1,500 a head can be ordered a day ahead. Beginners are welcome (Tabelog). Last entry 23:00; closed Sundays and holidays; ¥300 charge.

chef_bio.background: Sake bar with seasonal fish (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
chef_bio.philosophy: Seasonal fish bought daily; local sake from Tohoku (Tabelog listing).

anecdotes.text: "The red shrimp marinated in sake was incredibly delicious! The rich sweetness of the shrimp combined with the flavor of the sake made it the perfect accompaniment for drinks." — January 2026.
"On this visit, I enjoyed a tasting of Rashomon. It was fascinating to realize how the aroma, flavor, and finish can vary so much even within the same brewery…" — July 2026.

places.notes: [Izakaya · rice balls and owner-caught fish until 7 am, Souemoncho] A small izakaya in Souemoncho that pairs rice balls with fish the owner catches each week off Wakayama and Maizuru, and stays open until 7 am on most nights, handy after the last train. Start with a sashimi platter (thick-cut, from the week's catch) or a seafood rice bowl, add an extra-large fried horse mackerel that one diner calls a must, a grilled yellowtail collar or marinated mackerel, then finish with rice balls made from Niigata and Hiroshima rice and the miso soup of the day. Individual hot pots run to the 06:00 food last order. Friendly staff, counter and table seats, and children are welcome. Closed Thursdays (Tabelog).

places.notes: [Teppanyaki · kaiseki-style teppan courses in a hotel, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A calm, chic teppanyaki room on the second floor of a Higashi-Shinsaibashi hotel, with eight counter seats facing the griddle. The chef has more than 40 years in Japanese cuisine. The courses read like kaiseki first: five seasonal appetizers (one diner loved the fugu-skin jelly), three kinds of sashimi, a simmered dish or soup, flounder meunière cooked on the teppan, then Wagyu steak flamed in front of you, eaten with wasabi and rock salt. Garlic fried rice and miso soup close it out before fruit or a parfait. A diner noted that courses now start at ¥6,600, lower than before; two diners chose the ¥8,800 omakase. Dinner only for now, 10% service charge; closed Thursdays.

chef_bio.background: Teppanyaki restaurant in a hotel, with a staff-maintained Tabelog listing (Tabelog; 2026 reviews). The chef has more than 40 years in Japanese cuisine (Tabelog listing).
chef_bio.philosophy: Seasonal seafood, Wagyu and Kyoto vegetables; menu changes with the seasons (Tabelog listing).

"Previously, the restaurant mainly offered high-priced courses, but now you can enjoy an authentic teppanyaki course starting at JPY 6,600…" — August 2026.

places.notes: [Takoyaki · a cash-only takoyaki izakaya open from noon to the small hours, Amerikamura] A small takoyaki bar in Amerikamura, open from noon until 2 am (3 am at weekends), as good for a daytime drink as a late one. The takoyaki has a dashi-rich batter, crisp outside and creamy within; it's good plain, but salt mayo is the topping diners keep naming, with salt butter and sauce mayo as alternatives. Cash only; smoking allowed.

places.notes: [Takoyaki · late-night takoyaki and table teppan, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A branch of the TAKOTAKO KING takoyaki group, just west of the main shop, open from 18:00 to 3 am and still busy around 1 am. Upstairs, each table has its own teppan for reheating and grilling, with a toy train running past and an octopus-shaped smoke machine. Salt garlic takoyaki is the flavor diners keep naming, and a few prefer the hot, crunchy fried takoyaki; a four-flavor sampler lets you try several. Beyond takoyaki: a cheesy tororo-yaki, yam and seafood specials, grilled squid tentacles, extra-large kara-age and even omurice. Staff are usually cheerful, though one October 2026 diner found a new hire couldn't get the table grill hot. Takeout available.

Chicken is fried to order, bone-in or boneless, with a crunchy coating; get it plain-crispy, yangnyeom (sweet-spicy) or soy, or half-and-half (¥1,950 in November 2025), with pickled radish on the side. places.notes: [Sushi · Onodera-group Edomae sushi by the piece, ordered on a tablet, Namba] A casual counter from the Ginza Onodera sushi group, on the ground floor of the Namba Oriental Hotel, where you order authentic Edomae sushi one piece at a time on a tablet, choosing size, rice amount and wasabi, and help yourself to tea like at a conveyor-belt shop. The rice is seasoned with red vinegar and the pieces arrive already brushed, so there's no soy sauce on the counter. Diners single out isaki, anago, hairy crab, akagai and the nara-zuke toro-taku hand roll; one found the featured tuna underwhelming. Shop originals include a Sennichimae Roll and 'Namba Mountain'. Expect ¥5,000–10,000; families welcome; menus in English, Chinese and Korean.

places.notes: [Charcoal grill · seasonal irori courses over binchotan, Shinsaibashi] A calm, upscale charcoal-grill restaurant in a Shinsaibashi back alley, built around sunken irori hearths burning Kishu binchotan, which keeps smoke down. The seasonal courses run through small fish, juicy large clams, live lobster and abalone, Wagyu, wild boar, duck and vegetables, mostly grilled in front of you (one diner grilled at the hearth themselves). The Wagyu is seared with XO sauce for a smoky edge, and a thick-cut Wagyu strip-loin rice bowl is the closer two diners rave about. One diner asked to skip a sauce ingredient and the chef made an abalone-liver sauce on the spot. Expect ¥20,000–30,000 for a full course; ¥1,000 appetizer charge. Closed Sundays.

places.notes: [Standing bar · a Korean-Italian standing bar in Jumbo Yokocho, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A tiny standing bar in the Jumbo Yokocho alley of small bars off Yahata-machi street, open since 2010 and, per the listing, only three nights a week. The cooking leans Korean and properly spicy: generous, well-fermented baechu kimchi (¥350), fiery stir-fried baby octopus (¥780), shrimp jeon, and an extra-hot octopus stir-fry that one diner had made with shirako when octopus was out. Fresh oysters come with three sauces, including a gochujang one, and fruit cocktails are made to order, like a makgeolli cocktail packed with crushed strawberries. Friendly and easy for solo drinkers; one diner found prices a little high for a standing bar. Food notes are mostly from 2023; latest visit July 2025.

chef_bio.background: Standing bar run by its owner, who cooks (Tabelog; 2018–2025 reviews).
chef_bio.philosophy: Korean and Italian dishes from ingredients bought daily (Tabelog listing).

places.notes: [Hot pot · individual sukiyaki pots at a 1978 counter with lunch lines, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A Higashi-Shinsaibashi counter that has served sukiyaki and shabu-shabu since 1978, one pot per guest, and famous for its lunch line. Lunch sukiyaki starts around ¥1,400 (¥2,000 with 1.5× meat): thin-sliced marbled beef to add to a pot of udon, shirataki and vegetables in a rich, slightly sweet sauce, with egg for dipping, rice and oolong tea refilled free. Staff manage the heat if you like. Dinner moves to A5 Wagyu and pork courses, with house ponzu or sesame sauce for shabu-shabu and a signature frozen sake. When it's full you may be seated at the annex nearby. One diner suggests the less fatty cuts. Closed Sundays.

places.notes: [Kappo · a 1999 Osaka kappo known for its dashi, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A calm 15-seat kappo in Higashi-Shinsaibashi, open since 1999 and proud of its dashi, with four courses and about 70 à la carte dishes on Rosanjin-style tableware. Long-time diners return for the Kumamoto horse sashimi, steamed abalone with liver, grilled sesame tofu, crab with crab miso and fried snapper scales, and one now always finishes with the sea bream chazuke in rich sesame sauce. Prices aren't shown on the à la carte list: one diner paid just over ¥16,000; ¥10,000–15,000 is typical. Over a dozen sakes. It asks for quiet: no sandals or shorts, no strong fragrance, and no children below school age.

places.notes: [Spanish · a pintxos counter with Japanese twists, Namba] A small Spanish bar on a side street near Namba Station, the Namba branch of an OPERA in Honmachi, opened October 2025. The pintxos sit in a row at the counter like a sushi display, each on French bread with its own sauce: shiitake, shrimp and zucchini, vongole, sardine with tomato, shirasu and avocado. Order the seasonal seafood paella and the grilled octopus early, since they take time. Thirteen wines by the glass. It's often full and service can be slow; one diner saw a single person running it. Two-hour limit, ¥300 seat charge, no children.

places.notes: [Chinese · a basement creative-Chinese counter open to 2 am, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A cozy basement Chinese restaurant in Higashi-Shinsaibashi with six counter seats and sunken kotatsu tables, open until 2 am most nights. The menu changes daily and leans seasonal and vegetable-rich, with diners comparing it to hotel Chinese at izakaya prices: roast char siu (¥1,100), cuttlefish in Hong Kong sauce (¥1,400), plump spicy stir-fried oysters (¥1,500), sweet-and-sour spare ribs, braised beef, clams with thick glass noodles, and soup noodles two diners single out. Ask and the kitchen will make fried rice or ramen off the menu. Portions suit sharing among two or three. Smoking at every seat. Closed Wednesdays.

places.notes: [Japanese · a signless, reservation-only small-plates course in private rooms, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A deliberately hidden Japanese restaurant with no sign on the street: look for a small red sign on the Yahata-suji side of the Nippo Jumbo Building. Every seat is in a private room, some with sunken kotatsu, some at a counter, and dinner is a reservation-only omakase of many bite-sized seasonal dishes, with very fresh fish, good chicken and a sake list to match. Diners praise the variety and presentation; one was surprised by the konjac with roe. Portions are small, and two diners left wishing for more volume. Expect ¥10,000–20,000. Closed Sundays.

places.notes: [Sweets · Kakegawa-matcha crepes from a Tokyo tea-house chain, Shinsaibashi] The Shinsaibashi branch of Asakusa Chaya Tabanenoshi, a Japanese-crepe chain from Asakusa, on Shimizu-machi-suji across from the Daimaru car park. Everything turns on Kakegawa matcha from Shizuoka: the signature Kakegawa matcha brûlée wraps matcha custard, strawberries and matcha ice cream in a chewy matcha crepe, then torches the top so it cracks. Seasonal versions rotate, such as an autumn Tsukimi brûlée (¥1,250); there's also hojicha with anko butter, matcha soft serve and lattes. You can watch them being made. Only about five tables, so on weekends it fills and takeout is the easy option.

Start with the sashimi platter, then the rolled omelet, brought out on a hot teppan with extra dashi poured on so it bubbles at the table. Diners also praise the fried hatahata, homemade zaru tofu, whitebait with grated daikon and ponzu, mackerel pressed sushi and monkfish liver with nara-zuke. Dishes can take a while, and one diner found many sakes out of stock. Closed Mondays.

places.notes: [Yakitori · a 10-seat charcoal yakitori counter open to 5 am, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A small counter yakitori bar near Shinsaibashi Station, open from 18:00 until 5 am, so it works for dinner or a 1 am second stop. More than 30 skewer cuts, many rare, come from Tanba chicken, Tokushima young chicken and Daisen Jidori, each grilled over charcoal, and some get unusual house finishes such as escargot butter or black truffle oil. The omakase is good value; add vegetable skewers, the garlic edamame and a comforting egg soup with thin noodles to finish. One diner found the duck tataki weaker than the rest. The food is more than snacks: taro dumplings with beef and burdock in a nameko sauce, spring cabbage and prosciutto croquettes, Kagoshima chicken sashimi, fatty bluefin and seared mackerel, and in spring a run of firefly-squid dishes ending in clay-pot rice. The deep-fried house curry bread is a good take-home. Book a course for better value than ordering à la carte. Pretty sake cups and tableware. Rules: one non-alcoholic drinker per group, two-hour limit when busy. Closed Thursdays.

places.notes: [Takoyaki · Amerikamura's 1974 takoyaki stand by Triangle Park] The original shop of Koga Ryu, a takoyaki stand across from Amerikamura's Triangle Park since 1974, now with about nine shops. Ten small balls come per serving, soft and gooey rather than crisp, with a strong dashi flavor and big pieces of octopus. One diner calls the classic sauce-and-mayo (¥600) the most popular; another was told that Koga Ryu was the first to put mayonnaise on takoyaki. The negi versions come buried under green onion, with sauce (¥700) or ponzu. Eat upstairs or take them to the park. Two diners say Osaka locals pointed them here instead of Dotonbori. PayPay or cash only.

places.notes: [Soba · soba-shabu and meat dipping soba on Takashimaya's restaurant floor, Namba] The Takashimaya branch of Naniwa Soba, a small Osaka soba chain (four shops) on the seventh-floor restaurant level, with colorful seats. The signature, trademarked, is soba-shabu: Wagyu swished through the house dashi and eaten with fresh soba, as a course from ¥5,000. For a simpler meal, one repeat visitor always picks the meat dipping soba (¥1,300), pork in a lightly spicy chili-oil dip that becomes a rich soup when you add soba water at the end. Also chilled sudachi soba, ume-and-yam soba and an oyakodon set; diners praise the delicate Kansai-style broth. Open to 21:30 or 22:00, later than many department-store restaurants.

chef_bio.origin: Branch of Naniwa Soba, a local chain of four (September 2026 review); opened 2 March 2010 (Tabelog).

places.cuisine: Mexican tacos and tequila bar (about 20 seats, counter and terrace) · tacos on handmade tortillas: chorizo, braised pork rib (de costilla) ¥880, pulled pork with beans, chicken, cheese-filled · quesadilla with garlic mushrooms, half ¥880 · shrimp and avocado cocktail (cocktail de camarón) ¥1,320 · about 30 salsas, mild to fierce, plus habanero sauce · tequila and mezcal, straight or in cocktails · non-alcoholic Virgin Chichi and cranberry cooler ¥600
places.notes: [Mexican · a late-night taco and tequila bar since 2001, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A small Mexican bar near Shinsaibashi, open since 2001 and late into the night, with a neon 'Tacos' sign, a terrace and a Latin, clink-glasses mood. Tacos come on handmade tortillas: chorizo with tangy salsa, tender braised pork rib (¥880), pulled pork with beans, or cheese-filled. Start with the shrimp-and-avocado cocktail de camarón (¥1,320) and a crisp garlic-mushroom quesadilla. About 30 salsas sit ready for heat-seekers, and the tequila and mezcal list is deep; one diner who doesn't care for tequila found the tequila soda easy to drink. One diner found the chicken taco's mayo-like sauce unexpected. Book ahead: food can run out late. Closed Mondays.

chef_bio.background: Mexican taco and tequila bar (Tabelog; 2025–2026 reviews).
chef_bio.philosophy: Mexican food is about chili aroma and flavor more than heat (Tabelog listing).
chef_bio.specialty: Tacos on handmade tortillas; tequila and mezcal.

anecdotes.text: "Cocktail de Camaron (JPY 1,320, tax included) — Shrimp and avocado marinated with tomato and lime… Tacos de Costilla (JPY 880, tax included) — Tacos made with tender braised pork rib." — June 2026.
"The tacos were authentically delicious, featuring pulled pork and a bean paste, and the tortillas were especially tasty." — September 2026.

places.notes: [Café · thick açaí bowls and Greek yogurt in a bar-like room, Shinsaibashi] A small açaí-bowl and Greek-yogurt shop near Shinsaibashi Station with a dim, bar-like room and plush sofas. The açaí is thick and creamy, piled with fruit and honey, and you can build your own with granola, kiwi, coconut, nuts or mango; the Greek yogurt with comb honey is rich and filling. Bowls run about ¥1,680, which diners call a little pricey. Two diners called it the best açaí bowl ever, but one found a smaller, unripe-mango bowl on a return visit. Tabelog lists vegan options. Hours are unclear (the listing shows evenings to 4 am, reviewers came at lunch), so check before you go.

places.notes: [Pizza · a cheap oven-baked pizza bar, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A small Italian-bar-style pizza place in the Higashi-Shinsaibashi drinking streets, known for cheap, chewy, rustic pizzas that are on the small side, so a group can order several. Diners like the Margherita, a basil pizza, the quattro formaggi with honey and a mentaiko pizza, with ahijo and prosciutto to start and inexpensive wine. There's a one-drink rule. Pizzas were ¥500–600 in older reviews; recent prices aren't reported. Service reports range from attentive (pizzas sent one at a time so each stays hot) to curt, and one diner found the backless stools hard going after an hour. Most reviews are older; the latest is June 2025.

chef_bio.background: Pizza and dining bar (Tabelog; 2018–2025 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "The size of the pizza is a bit smaller, but it's just the right size and has a rustic homemade flavor. There is a one-drink policy. My favorite is the Quattro Formaggi with honey." — June 2025.
"The pizzas were about JPY 600 each, and we enjoyed authentic, oven-baked varieties. They were fluffy and delicious." — February 2020.

places.notes: [Sushi · a quiet 8-seat Edomae counter near Amerikamura, Nishi-Shinsaibashi] A calm, upstairs Edomae sushi counter of eight seats on the quieter edge of Amerikamura, open since 2014 and serving lunch as well as dinner. Each piece arrives already seasoned, with salt, citrus or plum paste instead of soy sauce. The ¥20,000 omakase runs like a small kaiseki: appetizer, three sashimi, grilled fish and chawanmushi before ten nigiri from squid and striped jack to chutoro, sea urchin and eel; there's also a ¥12,000 sushi course and lunch courses that diners call good value. Past highlights include tuna cooked in a salt crust, well-judged kohada and bonito with salt. You can ask for less rice. Closed Mondays.

chef_bio.background: Counter sushi restaurant with a staff-maintained Tabelog listing (Tabelog; 2020–2026 reviews).
chef_bio.philosophy: Fish sourced each morning, seasoned piece by piece (Tabelog listing; April 2026).

anecdotes.text: "'Sushi without Soy Sauce' seasoned for each topping — Delicate flavors enhanced with salt, citrus, and plum paste." — April 2026, Omakase Course ¥20,000.
"That day, we enjoyed tuna done in a salt crust, which was rich in flavor. The kohada (gizzard shad) was perfectly seasoned with vinegar…" — March 2023.

places.notes: [Okonomiyaki · a calm wooden teppan bar off Amerikamura, Nishi-Shinsaibashi] A tidy, wood-lined teppan bar tucked away in Nishi-Shinsaibashi, a quiet alternative to the Dotonbori okonomiyaki queues. Okonomiyaki comes in several styles, pork, oyster, a mixed modern and even Hiroshima-style, served on individual pans; around it, yam-yaki, cheese tonpei-yaki, shrimp mayo, shrimp toast and a salty, well-liked soba-meshi, plus salt-grilled offal and thick beef tongue. One diner didn't care for the sauce. The owner, a woman, runs the kitchen alone, so it can be slow, but diners like the warm touches (a message card on the table, a candy on the way out) and fair prices. Tabelog lists vegan options; ask.

chef_bio.background: Teppan and okonomiyaki bar run by its owner, who cooks alone (September 2026 review; Tabelog). The owner, a woman, runs the kitchen alone, so service can be slow (September 2026 review).

places.notes: [Yakiniku · Ning's thick-cut green-onion tongue in a calm hotel-floor room, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] The second Higashi-Shinsaibashi branch of the yakiniku shop Ning, on the ground floor of an APA Hotel near Nagahoribashi: black-toned, calm, with a long counter and smokeless roasters. The thing to order is the thick-cut tongue wrapped in green onion, garlic and ginger, which the shop calls its own creation; grill it well. The Ning set (¥9,680) is a tour of 11 cuts, and the branch-only special misuji is worth adding. Also tongue yukhoe, yukhoe on gimbap and a gelato that surprised one diner with its quality. One diner had a grill that wouldn't heat on one side and found the beer too icy. 90-minute seating.

places.notes: [Tempura · a 7-seat tempura course counter, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A quiet seven-seat tempura counter a few minutes from Shinsaibashi, where each piece is fried and handed over in front of you. The ¥12,100 dinner course opens with seasonal sashimi (steamed abalone with liver sauce, snow-crab sashimi), then light, crisp tempura, the shrimp especially juicy, with a fresh salad mid-way and a tempura rice bowl or tempura in tea broth to finish. In winter the showpiece is a female crab packed back into its shell and fried whole. Diners praise the warm, joking hospitality and a list of rare sake and wine. A summer lunch set ran ¥1,650–1,980 in 2026. Book ahead; closed Sundays.

places.notes: [Teppanyaki · a relaxed teppan counter for Wagyu, lobster and abalone, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A calm, grown-up teppanyaki restaurant in Higashi-Shinsaibashi with a six-seat counter and two private rooms, more relaxed than one diner expected. Black Wagyu is seared to your chosen doneness and cut, and one diner recommends wasabi; a fuller course adds Ise lobster and abalone, at about ¥24,000. places.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information; food is cakes and sandwiches (Tabelog), with a baked cheesecake the usual pick.
places.vegan_detail: Ask. Black coffee is the core; cakes and sandwiches are not described.
places.hours_raw: Daily 10:00–21:00 (last order 20:30) (Tabelog). Cash only (Tabelog; April 2026). Fully non-smoking, including e-cigarettes, from October 2025 (Tabelog). One diner was told stays are limited to 60 minutes, though the door sign said 90 (April 2026). Beans sold in the shop and by web, phone or fax order (Tabelog).
places.neighborhood: Higashi-Shinsaibashi 1-13-19, NT Bldg 1F, about 20 m north of the FamilyMart corner — 5 min from Shinsaibashi or Nagahoribashi Stn
places.cuisine: House-roasting coffee shop in Showa-kissa and mid-century style (17 seats: 12 at tables, 5 at the counter) · hand-brewed single origins such as Mandheling and a mocha, plus a strong blend · baked cheesecake · coffee jelly · sandwiches and cakes · beans from around the world to take home
places.notes: [Coffee · a quiet house-roasting kissa off the Shinsaibashi bustle, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A calm, dim coffee shop just off the busy Higashi-Shinsaibashi streets, part Showa kissa and part mid-century American, with jazz playing and a counter for solo visits. It roasts its own beans and brews each cup to order: ask the owner for a recommendation (one diner was steered to a freshly roasted Mandheling), or try the mocha with its grapefruit-like acidity or the strong blend. The baked cheesecake is the standard partner, smooth and well balanced; coffee jelly is on the menu too. Not everyone was won over: one diner found the coffee ordinary, the dish-washing loud and the stay limited to 60 minutes. Cash only.

chef_bio.background: House-roasting coffee shop (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "…[the owner] suggested the freshly roasted Mandheling!… The cheesecake was a baked type with a smooth texture, perfectly balanced in cheese flavor, sweetness, and acidity…" — February 2026.

"The atmosphere is a blend of a Showa-era Japanese café and mid-century American style. I ordered the Mocha Tamari. It had a subtle acidity reminiscent of grapefruit…" — December visit, April 2026 review.

places.name: ワインショップ&ダイナー FUJIMARU 東心斎橋店 (Wine Shop & Diner FUJIMARU Higashi shinsaibashi ten)
places.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information; the course includes cod croquettes, bread, a rice or risotto finish and an egg tart.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan in practice: Portuguese seafood, cod, octopus and chicken dishes; nothing described as vegan.
places.hours_raw: 2F Portuguese diner Tue–Sat and holidays 17:00–23:00 (food last order 22:00); 1F wine shop 15:00–22:00; 1F standing bar 17:00–22:00; closed Sunday and Monday (Tabelog). Reservations for the second floor only; often fully booked (September 2026). Cards accepted; no e-money or QR (Tabelog). Non-smoking (Tabelog). Bottles from the shop downstairs can be opened upstairs for a corkage fee (September 2026). When full, the shop points to its sister restaurant RAINDROP near Tanimachi 4-chome (Tabelog).
places.neighborhood: Higashi-Shinsaibashi 1-4-18, Uehara Bldg — 2 min from Nagahoribashi Stn exit 7
places.cuisine: Portuguese diner upstairs (Casa da Andorinha, moved from Honmachi) above a 1,000-bottle wine shop and standing bar (18 seats: 6 at the counter, 12 at tables) · course ¥5,500: assorted appetizers, pastel de bacalhau (cod croquettes), green salad, Tanba chicken piri-piri, seafood cataplana, a rice or risotto finish, pastel de nata · octopus salad; octopus carpaccio · Alentejana (pork and clams) · Portuguese wines, port and Madeira; Minoh craft beer
places.notes: [Portuguese · a Portuguese diner above a wine shop, near Nagahoribashi] Part of the FUJIMARU wine-shop group: downstairs a shop of about 1,000 wines and a standing bar, upstairs Casa da Andorinha, a long-running Portuguese restaurant that moved here from Honmachi. The ¥5,500 course is the way in: appetizers, crisp bacalhau croquettes, Tanba chicken piri-piri, a seafood cataplana, then rice or risotto to finish and a freshly baked pastel de nata. Two diners single out the octopus and the port wine, and you can pick a bottle downstairs and pay corkage. Staff are good at pairing wines. One diner missed Vinho Verde. It fills up, so book. Closed Sundays and Mondays.

chef_bio.origin: Branch of the FUJIMARU wine-shop and restaurant group (Tokyo and Osaka); the upstairs Portuguese restaurant Casa da Andorinha moved from Honmachi (Tabelog listing).
chef_bio.background: Wine shop, standing bar and Portuguese diner (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "Pastel de Bacalhau (Cod Croquettes)… Tanba Chicken Piri Piri… Seafood-filled Cataplana… Risotto to Finish Off… Pastel de Nata (Egg Tart)… The Egg Tart was freshly baked and incredibly tasty." — July 2026, course.
"We ordered the course for JPY 5,500 per person… selected a bottle of wine from the first floor, paying the corkage fee… finished with a tasting of Madeira wine." — September 2026.

places.name: BANCO
places.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information; food is paninis, doria and homemade tiramisu.
places.vegan_detail: Ask. Espresso is on the menu; food and milk options are not described.
places.hours_raw: Daily 12:00–02:00; may change, so check (Tabelog). Cards, e-money and PayPay accepted (Tabelog; April 2024). Smoking allowed inside (Tabelog; March 2025). No restroom in the shop; staff point you to one nearby (2023). Terrace seats; pets seen on the terrace (April 2024).
places.neighborhood: Nishi-Shinsaibashi 1-9-26, Hariju Daihoji Bldg 1F, on Daikokubashi-suji at the north edge of Amerikamura — 2 min from Shinsaibashi Stn
places.cuisine: Espresso café-bar (20 seats, terrace) · espresso solo ¥363; doppio ¥440; cappuccino doppio ¥583 (2024) · homemade tiramisu · paninis; doria · desserts around ¥500 · beer and a long drinks list from noon
places.notes: [Café · an espresso café-bar from noon to 2 am, Amerikamura] A casual espresso bar on the north edge of Amerikamura, by the Hariju building, open from noon until 2 am and as much a day-drinking spot as a café. Order a double espresso, strong and well-roasted, or a cappuccino doppio, at prices one diner called cheap for a city café (¥363–583 in 2024). The homemade tiramisu, light and not too sweet, is the reason two diners came back; paninis and doria cover meals. Tables are well spaced and the style is laid-back: you're left alone. Smoking is allowed inside, there's no restroom, and one diner found the room getting cluttered. Terrace seats.

chef_bio.background: Espresso café-bar (Tabelog; 2023–2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "A solo espresso is JPY 363, and a doppio is JPY 440, which is quite affordable for a café in the city… I ordered a cappuccino doppio for JPY 583…" — April 2024.
"The coffee has a classic taste and is delicious, and the tiramisu is fantastic… You can smoke inside the café, which might be tough for non-smokers." — March 2025.

places.gf_detail: Ask. Steak comes with garlic soy sauce, grated daikon with ponzu and rock salts (June 2026), so request salt; courses also include a quiche, sauces and an optional black curry. The restaurant says it cannot handle allergies to the rose family (Rosaceae) (Tabelog).
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan in practice: Wagyu, live abalone, lobster and seafood courses; nothing described as vegan.
places.hours_raw: Wed–Mon and holidays 11:30–14:30 (food last order 13:30) and 17:30–22:00 (food last order 20:00); closed Tuesday; may take substitute days off after holidays (Tabelog). Course prices include tax and service (Tabelog). Cannot accommodate Rosaceae-family allergies (Tabelog). Cards, e-money and QR accepted (Tabelog). Non-smoking (Tabelog).
places.neighborhood: Minatomachi 1-2-3, Hotel Monterey Grasmere Osaka 22F — 1 min from JR Namba, connected to Osaka Metro Namba
places.cuisine: Hotel teppanyaki at two 6-seat counters on the 22nd floor, with views west toward Kobe and Akashi Kaikyo Bridge · lunch courses (special lunch, A5 steak lunch) about ¥10,000–15,000 · dinner courses such as Maya and Rokko about ¥20,000–30,000 · live abalone with liver sauce; Ise lobster; scallops and shrimp; fish of the day · black Wagyu sirloin cap, ribeye or filet with two sauces and three salts · four seasonal grilled vegetables · garlic rice or black beef curry (+¥500) with red miso soup · dessert and coffee · a special Yonezawa beef course every two months (Tabelog)
places.notes: [Teppanyaki · a 22nd-floor hotel teppan counter with a view, JR Namba] A teppanyaki counter on the 22nd floor of the Hotel Monterey Grasmere by JR Namba, with big windows looking west over Kyocera Dome toward Kobe, the Rokko range and Akashi Kaikyo Bridge. Courses move from small appetizers to seafood (live abalone grilled in front of you, Ise lobster, scallops), four seasonal vegetables, and black Wagyu with a choice of sauces and salts, then garlic rice or a rich black beef curry. Lunch courses are the value play; one long-time diner noted lunch prices have risen and the 80 g steak now feels small. Chefs are happy to chat. Closed Tuesdays.

chef_bio.background: Hotel teppanyaki restaurant with a staff-maintained Tabelog listing (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
chef_bio.specialty: Teppanyaki courses with Wagyu and live seafood.

anecdotes.text: "The fresh abalone was quickly grilled while still alive, served with its liver and an oriental sauce… We had sirloin cap and strip loin, served with garlic soy sauce, grated ponzu, and several types of rock salt." — June 2026, lunch course.
"It's unfortunate that due to rising costs, the price of the lunch special has increased… The 80g steak portion feels a bit small…" — October 2026.

places.name: 天ぷら互生 心斎橋 (Tempura Gosei Shinsaibashi)
places.gf_detail: Not gluten-free in practice: a tempura course that opens with somen noodles; batter is not described as gluten-free.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan in practice: the course includes shrimp, sea urchin, octopus and whitebait; nothing described as vegan.
places.hours_raw: Daily 18:00–24:00; irregular closures (Tabelog). Reservation only; call if running late (Tabelog). Please avoid strong perfume or hair products (Tabelog). Cards and PayPay accepted; no e-money (Tabelog). Non-smoking (Tabelog). English menu; sommelier on site (Tabelog).
places.neighborhood: Nishi-Shinsaibashi 1-8-22, Dai-5 Ace Bldg 2F, on the Amerikamura side — 1 min from Shinsaibashi Stn exit 7 or Yotsubashi Stn exit 5
places.cuisine: Tempura course with wine pairings at an L-shaped counter (12 seats: 8 at the counter, one table for 4) · opens with chilled kuzu somen with sudachi · small dishes such as baby octopus and boiled whitebait with sansho, wild vegetables · uni on rice cooked in a clay pot · tempura: sweet shrimp from Amakusa (heads fried crisp), shiso-wrapped tempura, scallop, vegetables, a shrimp to start · grated daikon between rounds · curry to finish (optional) · wine and sake pairings chosen by the sommelier
places.notes: [Tempura · a 12-seat tempura and wine-pairing counter run by a couple, Shinsaibashi] A small, stylish tempura counter a minute from Shinsaibashi Station, run by a husband-and-wife team: one fries, the wife is a sommelier who pairs affordable wines and sake with each course. The meal opens with chilled kuzu somen sharpened with sudachi, then small seasonal dishes and uni piled on clay-pot rice before the tempura, which diners call light and gentle on the stomach. The standout is sweet shrimp from Amakusa with crisp fried heads; vegetables shine too. A rich curry is an optional finish. One repeat visitor keeps bringing guests to impress. Expect ¥15,000–30,000 with pairings. Reservation only; skip the perfume.

chef_bio.background: Tempura and wine counter run by two people, one a sommelier (September 2026 reviews; Tabelog). A husband-and-wife team runs the counter; the wife is a sommelier and chooses the pairings (September 2026 review).
chef_bio.philosophy: Seasonal ingredients with sommelier-chosen wines (Tabelog listing).

anecdotes.text: "…the cold kuzusomen that came out first was absolutely perfect!… You must try the amaebi (sweet shrimp) here! The moment I took a bite, an incredible sweetness spread throughout my mouth…" — June 2026.
"I always feel that the tempura here is very gentle on the stomach… The wine pairing… was, as usual, outstanding." — September 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ (店舗会員の公式情報): 天ぷら互生 心斎橋、大阪市中央区西心斎橋1-8-22 第5エースビル 2F、心斎橋駅7番出口・四ツ橋駅5番出口から徒歩1分、毎日18:00〜24:00、不定休、完全予約制、香水や整髪料の強い香りは控えて、カード・PayPay可、電子マネー不可、禁煙、12席 (カウンター8、4人テーブル1)、ソムリエ、英語のメニュー、公式サイトあり。口コミ(2026年6〜10月): ふたりで営む店でひとりがソムリエ、L字のカウンター、最初に sudachi の冷たい kuzu somen、小ダコ、sansho の効いた釜揚げ shirasu、山菜、土鍋で炊いたご飯に uni、天草の甘エビの tempura (頭はカリッと)、shiso 巻き、ホタテ、野菜、大根おろし、しめにカレーも、手頃なワインと日本酒のペアリング、胃にやさしい軽い tempura、滋賀の作家の器、予算15,000〜30,000円。

places.gf_detail: Ask. Raw oysters and sashimi come with ponzu or soy; fried oysters and oden are also on the menu.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a seafood and sushi bar.
places.hours_raw: Daily 9:00–16:00; irregular closures (Tabelog; the listing blurb says from 11:00, and diners report being served from about 10:00). No cards or e-money; PayPay, d Barai, Rakuten Pay and au PAY accepted (Tabelog). Non-smoking on the ground floor; smoking only upstairs (Tabelog). Second-floor room bookable from two people (Tabelog). Children welcome (Tabelog). Takeout (Tabelog).
places.neighborhood: Nippombashi 1-21-1, on the main street of Kuromon Market — 3 min from Kintetsu Nippombashi Stn
places.cuisine: Seafood and sushi bar in Kuromon Market, open from the morning (18 seats; room upstairs) · fish bought daily by the owner · oysters raw or grilled, 3 for ¥999 (October 2025) · bluefin tuna; tekka maki under ¥700 · scallops by size, served in parts · fugu with ponzu · five-kind sashimi platter · seafood rice bowl with egg yolk · fried oysters; oden · beer and sake for morning drinking
places.notes: [Seafood · a fair-priced seafood and sushi bar in Kuromon Market] The main shop of Kashin, a bright little seafood bar on Kuromon Market's main street that opens in the morning and welcomes a beer with breakfast. In a market known for high prices, diners single it out as fair: three big raw or grilled oysters for ¥999, tuna tekka maki for under ¥700, large scallops cut so you taste each part, fugu with ponzu, a five-kind sashimi platter and seafood bowls. Fried oysters and oden fill out the izakaya side. The owner buys fish daily and is cheerful company; staff are polite. It gets crowded, and the ground floor is cramped. No cards; QR payments only.

chef_bio.origin: Moved to Kuromon Market's main street in April 2021 (Tabelog listing); main shop of a small group with an Umeda branch (January 2026 review).
chef_bio.background: Seafood and sushi izakaya with a staff-maintained Tabelog listing (Tabelog; 2023–2026 reviews).
chef_bio.philosophy: Fish bought daily by the owner; the owner wants Kuromon to be more than overpriced food (January 2026 review).

places.notes: [Chinese · a 9-seat Chinese bar for mapo tofu, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A tiny Chinese bar in a converted snack-bar space in Higashi-Shinsaibashi, nine seats and open to 1 am, serving serious Chinese food with cocktail-bar style. The mapo tofu (¥1,200) is the signature, meaty, spicy and numbing; the beef-tendon version has its own fan. Also the yodare-dori, whose sauce one diner wanted to drink, grilled shumai of Jinan mochi pork (2 for ¥500), black-vinegar sweet-and-sour pork, shrimp chili and seafood noodles in thick sauce. Pair with a Shaoxing highball or baijiu jasmine highball. The owner travels to research and source ingredients, and the room is friendly. ¥300 charge, one drink, adults only.

places.notes: [Burgers · big Wagyu-and-pork burgers with crisp fries, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A small second-floor burger shop near Shinsaibashi Station, known for thick, juicy patties of black Wagyu blended with domestic brand pork on a well-toasted bun, with a light sauce that lets the meat lead. The burgers are by a former French chef, mixing French technique into burgers. The burgers are big: some diners use a knife and fork, one prefers to wrap them in paper and bite. The fries get nearly as much praise, crisp with a refined sweetness; one diner called them the best fries ever. Get the Classic, the Comple, or the B set (¥2,500 with fries and a drink); a three-patty stack is there if you're hungry. Ten seats; it closes when the burgers sell out.

chef_bio.background: Burger shop (Tabelog; 2026 reviews). The burgers are by a former French chef, mixing French technique into burgers (March 2026 review).

places.notes: [Japanese · a hidden 5th-floor koryori for seasonal small plates and sake, Nagahoribashi] A calm Japanese room on the fifth floor of a building near Nagahoribashi, hard to find but often full, serving Osaka-style small plates with sake and shochu. The head chef trained at Naniwa Kappo Kameji in Nishi-Shinsaibashi. Dinner starts with a run of small dishes and a rich dashi that two diners single out, then a generous sashimi platter. The kitchen makes its own kombu salt for the rare chicken tempura, and the seasonal list runs from lightly boiled or fried conger eel and straw-grilled chicken to stuffed peppers with meat miso and spring rolls of whitebait and perilla. Finish with salted rice balls from an iron pot. Mostly à la carte, with courses too. Smoking allowed; closed Sundays.

places.notes: [Café · a queue-worthy American breakfast café in Minami-Horie] A warm, wood-and-vintage American bakery café among the Horie fashion shops, open for breakfast and lunch since 2013, with a line on weekends. The pancakes are the draw: thin, flavorful, piled with bacon and eggs and plenty of maple syrup (¥1,250). The croque madame on the house natural-yeast bread (¥1,485) makes a hearty breakfast, and the burgers, such as avocado and mozzarella, come with crisp fries; one diner didn't care for the thick truffle fries. Donuts appear only on weekends and holidays. Arrive at 9 am on a weekday to skip the wait; at weekends expect 20–60 minutes.

places.notes: [Kushiyaki · teppan-grilled skewers on Takashimaya's restaurant floor, Namba] A kushiyaki restaurant on the eighth floor of Takashimaya's Namba Dining Maison, where skewers of meat, seafood and vegetables are grilled on a teppan and served on the plate: pork-wrapped asparagus, Wagyu, enoki rolled in meat, shrimp paste, tsukune, plus a monthly limited menu. At dinner, add tonpei-yaki and a punchy garlic fried rice. Reservations on weekday evenings only.

places.notes: [Bar · a Japanese-Italian standing bar to 3 am, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A basement bar near Shinsaibashi Station that ran for years as a meat-sushi and Italian bar and reopened in September 2026 as a standing bar, same chef and team, with the counter stools gone and two tables kept for groups. places.notes: [Crêperie · Parisian crepes and galettes behind Hotel Nikko, Shinsaibashi] A stylish little crêperie behind the Hotel Nikko in Shinsaibashi, with a Paris-styled room and pretty tableware, open from 10 am to 11 pm. A review says the crepes are made by a French chef. The savory side draws the warmest reviews: a Salmon Royal galette loaded with salmon and rich cheese, and a juicy, slightly spicy minced-meat one, both big enough for dinner. Sweet crepes are chewy with crisp edges, from a simple sugar-butter-lemon to chocolate with lightly sweet cream; one diner found the Dubai chocolate too sweet to finish. Eating in requires one drink each, and payment is cashless only. Tabelog lists vegetarian options.

chef_bio.background: Crêperie (Tabelog; 2026 reviews). A review says the crepes are made by a French chef (September 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: "The salmon crepe was filled with salmon no matter where you bit into it, and it was loaded with ingredients. The cheese was rich and incredibly tasty." — September 2026.
"Please note that a drink order is required for in-house dining, and payments are cashless only…" — September 2026.

Diners pick out the Wagyu, the angel shrimp, whiting, Camembert and a marinated tuna skewer, dipped in the house sauce, with the shop's frozen lemon sour alongside. Unusually, there's a good oden pot too. Expect ¥4,000–8,000 with drinks. Diners praise the friendly staff and the owner's sunny manner, though one found orders missed and the bill wrong on a busy night. Smoking allowed.

places.notes: [Coffee · a specialty coffee bar with about 20 beans, Shinsaibashi] A small, bright coffee bar near Shinsaibashi Station, industrial-meets-minimal, with a wall of colorful bean cards and about 20 single coffees from light to dark. Tell the barista what you like and you'll be steered to a coffee, with an explanation of the beans; one diner got a berry-ish Ethiopian, another a fruity light-roast Colombian with Geisha (¥1,700). places.notes: [Korean · soy-marinated crab courses in private rooms, Nagahoribashi] A fifth-floor Korean restaurant by Nagahoribashi Station built around ganjang gejang, raw blue crab marinated in soy sauce, served in quiet private and semi-private rooms (some with sunken kotatsu). The crab is sweet and creamy, good with rice; soy-marinated shrimp comes with lemon. Courses (about ¥6,980) add namul, japchae and jeon, and the nakopsae seafood hot pot ends with noodles under egg yolk, cheese and pepper. A rare-sake list fits the Japanese-leaning seasoning. One diner found portions smaller than expected, and another was hurried out at a two-hour limit nobody had mentioned, so ask when booking.

Every set meal comes with steaming clay-pot mixed rice you can refill, plus house pickles and free tempura bits, and the custom is to finish the rice ochazuke-style with soba broth or tea.
