The owner is Nakagawa of the comedy duo Randies, who still serves customers, and the walls are covered with comedians’ autographs. A thin crepe is topped with crunchy cabbage, little pieces of chicken and minced beef fat, which melts into the batter for a rich but surprisingly light cake; the original is ¥650, so groups order several (green onion, cheese curry, mochi and cheese). Also the hefty western-style modern with noodles, a garlicky udon-soba-offal 'uso-yaki', soba-meshi with natto and good drinking snacks. Open to 2 am; no cards; smoking allowed.

chef_bio.origin: Second shop of the kashimin-yaki specialist Hako (Tabelog listing).
chef_bio.background: Kashimin-yaki bar (Tabelog; 2024–2025 reviews). The owner is Nakagawa of the comedy duo Randies, who still serves customers, and the walls are covered with comedians’ autographs (October 2024 review).
chef_bio.philosophy: A lighter okonomiyaki from the Senshu area (Tabelog listing).

anecdotes.text: "The base is a crepe with plenty of crunchy cabbage, and the batter poured in creates a wonderfully gooey finish. The minced meat is grilled to perfection, and the chicken adds a delightful crunchy texture." — December 2024, Kashimin-yaki original ¥650.
"The amount of batter is minimal, and the seasoning is very rich, making it perfect to enjoy with beer!" — November 2025.

places.notes: [Sweets · crisp Brussels waffles baked to order, by Yotsubashi] A small café a minute from Yotsubashi Station that bakes Brussels-style waffles to order, with unsweetened batter, Belgian butter and Belgian chocolate and toppings. Pick your chocolate, or add pudding and vanilla ice cream. An espresso shake (¥600) surprised one diner as the highlight. One found the cream ordinary. Comfortable for families, with sofa seats; open 10:00–18:00 daily.

chef_bio.background: Belgian-waffle café (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).

"I had the Chilled Sweet Potato Brulee Waffle for JPY 1400 and the Espresso Shake for JPY 600… I was pleasantly surprised by how delicious the Espresso Shake was…" — October 2026.

places.notes: [Coffee · a specialty coffee café where you pick your cup, Minami-Horie] A small, decorated café in Minami-Horie that takes coffee seriously: single origins sorted into dark and fruity, each about ¥999, with staff happy to explain light roasts and match a bean to your taste. You choose your own cup and saucer from the shelf (fine porcelain, one diner noted), and any coffee that doesn't fit is served on the side. Diners single out an Ethiopian for its balance of aroma and acidity and an Indonesian 'dark' that drinks clean with chocolate notes. Ordering can be slow when it's busy. Dog-friendly. Cash only; open until 23:00 on weekdays.

chef_bio.background: Specialty coffee café (Tabelog; 2025–2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "If you choose to enjoy your coffee inside, [you can] pick your favorite cup. If the smaller cup can't hold all the coffee, [the extra is served] separately…" — April 2026, Indonesian ¥999.
"The specialty coffee from Ethiopia left a strong impression on me… the balance of aroma and acidity in the coffee was truly remarkable." — November 2025.

places.notes: [Café · an early-opening surf café for bagels and lattes, Kita-Horie] A small, surf-themed café near Yotsubashi that opens at 8:30, rare for the area, with a feel one diner compared to being abroad. The owner speaks English. Breakfast and lunch are bagel sandwiches packed with fillings (bacon, egg and cheese ¥980; ham and avocado; salmon, prosciutto and cream cheese), messy but filling; one diner found the bagel itself a bit hard. Coffee is hand-dripped from three beans, ground per cup, and takeaway cups get a hand-drawn illustration. The lattes stand out, especially a thick caramel latte; sweets include a tiramisu on a waffle base. Cramped inside, and it can be nearly full on weekend afternoons.

chef_bio.background: Café (Tabelog; 2026 reviews). The owner speaks English (June 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: "I was delighted to see [the beans ground] on the spot and [each cup] carefully drip[ped]… The take-away cup came with a hand-drawn illustration…" — February 2026, Indonesian hand drip.
"It was much richer and creamier than I had imagined, and the milk was delicious... it paired perfectly with the caramel." — February 2026, caramel latte.

places.notes: [Café · a temple café overlooking a garden, Minami-Horie] A calm café tucked into a corner of Banpukuji, a roughly 400-year-old Jodo Shinshu temple in Minami-Horie, open only Thursday to Saturday. Window seats look straight onto the tended temple garden. The sweets are made in-house: a daily sweets set (¥1,650) such as a rich cheesecake with caramel and almonds, or a seasonal wagashi tray of red bean, chestnut, ice cream and chrysanthemum monaka, good with the properly made matcha. Summer brings an ume-syrup kakigori topped with a pickled plum. Prices run high for drinks (matcha about ¥1,400), which one diner put down to the view. Cash only.

chef_bio.origin: Opened 1 April 2017 inside Banpukuji, a Jodo Shinshu Honganji-sect temple (Tabelog; July 2026 review).

chef_bio.philosophy: Original Japanese sweets by an in-house patissier (Tabelog listing).

anecdotes.text: "The cheesecake was rich and creamy, topped with a strong caramel sauce and almond slices that enhanced its flavor." — July 2026, Today's Sweets Set ¥1,650.

"On the tray, there was a delightful array of sweet red bean paste, chestnuts, ice cream, and adorable chrysanthemum-shaped monaka and wagashi!… the authentic matcha was simply outstanding!" — October 2026.

places.notes: [Shaved ice · a summer-only old-style kakigori stand, Yotsubashi] A long-running ice shop by Yotsubashi Station that sells kakigori only in summer, shaved from big clear blocks into a fluffy pile that doesn't bring on brain freeze, then soaked through with syrup. There's just a three-person bench; many eat standing on the pavement, often with families and a short line on hot afternoons. It closes on rainy days. The 2026 season ended on 23 September; check again next summer. Cash only.

chef_bio.background: Long-established ice shop open in summer (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "In a world where desserts often exceed JPY 1,000, this fluffy kakigori is available for just JPY 360." — August 2026.
"Using pure ice, it's less likely to give you a brain freeze and has a fluffy texture." — September 2026, Strawberry ¥360.

places.notes: [Café · a Taiwanese-style soy milk café for breakfast, Namba] A cheerful little café near Edion Arena decorated with cartoon soybeans, serving soy milk made the Taiwanese way: lighter and more refreshing than Japanese soy milk, with a stronger bean taste. Choose plain, oolong-tea, black sesame or mixed berry (¥660), and set the sweetness level yourself; one diner found 25% just right. A fluffy, juicy Taiwanese meat bun (¥320) makes it breakfast, and the bun-plus-soy-milk combo was ¥500. Summer adds shaved ice with tapioca, and you get sunflower seeds to crack while you sit. Opens at 8:00; closed Mondays.

chef_bio.philosophy: Taiwanese-style soy milk (October 2025 reviews).

places.name: 和かろん専門店 和果 (Wacaron Senmon Ten Waka)
places.gf_detail: Not gluten-free in practice: dorayaki-style pancake wrappers around cream, red bean paste and mochi; no gluten-free item described.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan in practice: cream, custard and cheese-cream fillings; nothing described as vegan.
places.hours_raw: Mon, Tue, Thu–Sun 11:00–18:00; closed Wednesday; may change (Tabelog). Mainly takeaway; four counter seats listed, and one diner ate on a bench by the door (Tabelog; May 2026). Wacaron are handed over frozen and thaw to eating temperature (May–August 2026). Cards and QR accepted; no e-money (Tabelog). Opened 10 September 2020 (Tabelog).
places.neighborhood: Kita-Horie 1-11-6 — 2 min from Yotsubashi Stn exit 6
places.cuisine: Japanese-sweets shop for "wacaron," fresh dorayaki filled with cream, plus mochi rolls (mostly takeaway; 4 counter seats) · wacaron: blueberry cheese cream ¥480; custard; matcha with red bean; hojicha with red bean; sweet potato · mitarashi roll, a dango wrapped in pancake, ¥580 · roll with red bean and mochi ¥400 · roasted sweet potato and red bean roll · Anno sweet-potato mitarashi roll ¥900 (event, October 2026)
places.notes: [Sweets · fresh-dorayaki 'wacaron' and mitarashi rolls, Kita-Horie] A small Japanese-sweets shop near Yotsubashi that turns dorayaki into 'wacaron': thin, soft pancakes sandwiching a thick layer of cream in flavors like blueberry cheese (¥480), custard, or matcha and hojicha with red bean. They're handed over frozen and soften to eating temperature as you walk. The other draw is the mitarashi roll (¥580), a soft dango in a freshly cooked pancake with sweet-savory sauce, which one diner came back for; another wished for more sauce. Also red-bean-and-mochi and roasted-sweet-potato rolls. Mostly takeaway, with a bench by the door. Closed Wednesdays.

chef_bio.background: Japanese-sweets shop (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "It features a thin, soft dorayaki skin with a thick layer of cream in between. It was handed to us frozen solid, and after carrying it around… it melted to the perfect eating temperature." — August 2026, blueberry cheese cream ¥480.
"During my last visit to Osaka, I couldn't forget the deliciousness of the 'Mitara-shi Maki,' so I returned on this trip!" — August 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: 和かろん専門店 和果、大阪市西区北堀江1-11-6、四ツ橋駅6番出口から徒歩2分、月・火・木〜日11:00〜18:00、水曜休み、カード・QR可、電子マネー不可、禁煙、カウンター4席、テイクアウト、2020年9月10日開店、公式サイトあり。口コミ(2026年5〜10月): 写真に「和かろん(生どら焼き)ブルーベリーチーズクリーム(税込480円)」、薄くやわらかいどら焼きの生地に厚いクリーム、凍った状態で渡され歩くうちに食べごろに、カスタード、抹茶と小豆、ほうじ茶と小豆、さつまいも、mitarashi の巻き (パンケーキでdango を包む) 580円、あんこともちの巻き400円、焼き芋の巻き、イベントでAnno 芋の mitarashi の巻き900円、また買いに来たという声、たれが少なめという声、入口のベンチで食べられる、ショーケースはなくメニューから選ぶ。

cultural_comfort.note: Order from the menu; mostly takeaway (2026).

places.name: GUFO
places.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information; flavors change daily, some with mix-ins (fig and cheese, cookies), and cones are offered.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan in practice: milk-based soft serve and gelato; no dairy-free flavor described.
places.hours_raw: Mon, Tue, Thu–Sun 12:00–18:00; closed Wednesday; may change (Tabelog). Cards (JCB, AMEX) and e-money accepted; no QR (Tabelog). Non-smoking. Children and strollers welcome; takeout (Tabelog). Small lines form quickly at weekends (October 2026). Opened 29 April 2016 (Tabelog).
places.neighborhood: Kita-Horie 1-11-9, U+ Bldg 1F, glass-fronted — 2–3 min from Yotsubashi Stn
places.cuisine: Soft serve and gelato shop (6 counter seats; eat-in space) · very airy soft serve: milk ¥420; Japanese chestnut ¥540; hazelnut cup ¥520 · daily gelato ¥420: salt vanilla; dried fig and cheese; pumpkin; hojicha; Earl Grey chocolate; pistachio · cup or cone
places.notes: [Sweets · featherlight soft serve and daily gelato, Kita-Horie] A glass-fronted ice cream shop near Yotsubashi with wood-and-white-tile decor, known for a soft serve so full of tiny air bubbles it eats like whipped cream. The milk flavor (¥420) is lightly sweet; seasonal ones like Japanese chestnut (¥540) and hazelnut taste strongly of the real thing, and portions are generous enough that one diner suggested sharing. The gelato case changes daily (¥420), with flavors such as salt vanilla, dried fig and cheese, pumpkin, hojicha and Earl Grey chocolate. There's a little eat-in space; weekend afternoons bring short lines. Closed Wednesdays.

chef_bio.background: Soft serve and gelato shop (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "Compared to regular soft serve, it contains a lot of tiny air bubbles, making it incredibly light. You can also taste the rich chestnut flavor." — October 2026, Soft Serve Chestnut ¥540.
"The salt flavor was more pronounced than I expected, enhancing the sweetness of the vanilla. It was rich yet refreshing…" — October 2026, Salt Vanilla ¥420.

places.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information; the menu is pudding, cheesecakes, gelato and matcha drinks.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan in practice: puddings, cheesecakes, gelato and milk lattes; plain sencha is on the menu.
places.hours_raw: Mon–Thu 10:30–19:00 (last order 18:30); Friday–Sunday and holidays 10:30–23:00 (last order 22:30); check Google Maps for changes (Tabelog). Order at the counter, then choose a seat (October 2026). Cards, e-money and QR accepted (Tabelog). Non-smoking. Outlets and Wi-Fi; takeout (Tabelog). Opened 4 May 2026 (Tabelog).

places.cuisine: Uji-matcha and Japanese-tea café (20 seats) · Uji matcha rich pudding ¥900, firm and dense; add rich matcha gelato +¥250; matcha sauce · matcha Basque cheesecake; hojicha baked cheesecake · Uji matcha latte "Zuiun" ¥850, unsweetened; mango matcha latte; matcha strawberry latte · iced sencha · peach pudding in season
places.notes: [Café · an Uji-matcha café for dense pudding and gelato, Shinsaibashi] A calm, wood-accented matcha café near Shinsaibashi Station, opened May 2026 and open until 11 pm at weekends. The signature is a firm, rich Uji matcha pudding (¥900); add a scoop of the intensely bitter matcha gelato (+¥250) and a drizzle of matcha sauce. A matcha Basque cheesecake and a hojicha baked cheesecake are just as rich. Lattes are unsweetened, so the matcha comes through (the 'Zuiun' is ¥850), with mango and strawberry versions too. Diners call prices high and touristy, and one waited a long time, but matcha lovers rate it. Order first, then sit.

chef_bio.background: Matcha café (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "Pairing the dense and firm matcha pudding with the rich matcha gelato was simply the best! When I added matcha sauce, the matcha flavor intensified…" — October 2026, Uji Matcha Rich Pudding ¥900, gelato +¥250.
"The matcha latte had no syrup, allowing me to truly enjoy the authentic taste of matcha… Since it's priced for tourists, I hope it becomes a bit more affordable." — October 2026.

places.gf_detail: Ask. The shop says its galettes are made from buckwheat flour, water and salt only (Tabelog listing), but its crepes use French wheat flour and are cooked in the same kitchen; fillings and griddle sharing are not described.
places.vegan_detail: Ask. The galette batter is buckwheat, water and salt (Tabelog listing), but fillings use ham, cheese, egg and butter; no vegan filling is described.

places.cuisine: Nordic-style crêperie with a terrace (20 seats: table, counter, sofa, terrace) · buckwheat galettes (buckwheat flour, water and salt): Complete with ham, cheese, egg, tomato, avocado and pesto, set ¥1,900; prosciutto · chewy crepes of French VIRON flour with Échiré butter · chocolate crepe platter with cocoa cookies, almonds, cream and chocolate ice cream · banana juice; café latte; Iced Americano ¥690 · wine and cocktails · crepes for dogs
places.notes: [Crêperie · buckwheat galettes and chewy crepes with a dog-friendly terrace, Kita-Horie] A wood-lined, Nordic-styled crêperie near Yotsubashi, open into the evening. Galettes are made from just buckwheat flour, water and salt; the Complete set (ham, cheese, egg, tomato, avocado and pesto, ¥1,900) changed one diner's view of galettes. The sweet crepes use French flour and Échiré butter, crisp at the edges and chewy, though one diner found the cream excessive. Order by QR at your table. Dogs are welcome on the terrace, and there are even crepes for them. Indoor seats are few, so book; reservations need food, not just drinks. Diners find the drinks pricey.

chef_bio.background: Crêperie café (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
chef_bio.philosophy: Galettes of buckwheat flour, water and salt; crepes of French VIRON flour (Tabelog listing).

anecdotes.text: "A. Complete (ham, cheese, egg, tomato, avocado, pesto) crepe set for JPY 1,900… The crepe was made with thick Echire butter, crispy on the outside and chewy on the inside!" — August 2026.
"The atmosphere is nice, and the crepes are chewy and delicious, but there is just way too much whipped cream and cream!!!" — August 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ (店舗会員の公式情報): PALM Cafe&Creperie 堀江、大阪市西区北堀江1-9-14 PAN1914ビル 1F、四ツ橋駅4・6番出口から徒歩2分、月・火・木・日・祝・祝翌日11:00〜22:00 (L.O. 21:30)、水11:00〜18:30、金・土・祝前日11:00〜22:30、休みは変わることも、ドリンクのみの予約不可 (ガレットかクレープを人数分)、カード・PayPay可、電子マネー不可、店内禁煙 (17:30以降は電子たばこ可)、テラスは喫煙可、20席 (テーブル8、カウンター6、ソファ3、テラス3)、そば粉・水・塩だけのガレット、フランスの VIRON の小麦粉のクレープ、バナナジュース、ワンちゃん用のクレープ。口コミ(2026年8〜10月): 北欧風の木の店内、テラスは犬連れ可、QRで注文、コンプリート (ハム・チーズ・卵・トマト・アボカド・ジェノベーゼ) のセット1,900円、生ハムのガレット、エシレバターのクレープ、チョコレートのクレープ、アイスアメリカーノ690円、もちもちの生地、クリームが多すぎるという声、ドリンクが高めという声、駐車場が見つからなかったという声。

places.name: otto. coffee and sweets
places.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information; sweets include puddings, crepes, tarts, mille-feuille and cheesecake, and there are tacos.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan in practice: egg-rich puddings, custard and cream desserts; nothing described as vegan.
places.hours_raw: Daily 9:00–19:30; may change (Tabelog). No cards or e-money; PayPay accepted (Tabelog). Non-smoking. A covered, terrace-like room facing Shinsaibashi-suji, air-conditioned (June 2026). Dog cookie add-on +¥250 (October 2026). Opened 19 March 2022 (Tabelog).

places.cuisine: Terrace-style café on the arcade (12 seats: 6 at the counter, 6 at tables) · firm egg pudding with bitter caramel; pudding with vanilla ice cream or Mont Blanc cream · seasonal sweets: sweet-potato ice cream pudding ¥780 (autumn); purple sweet-potato Mont Blanc mille-feuille with mochi and custard; sweet-potato tart · sugar-butter crepe · soufflé cheesecake · tacos with Corona · coffee from two beans; hojicha latte; Earl Grey ¥550 · brunch menu · dog cookies +¥250
places.notes: [Café · a bright café on the Shinsaibashi-suji arcade for pudding and seasonal sweets] A light, white café up a few steps from the Shinsaibashi-suji arcade, with a covered, terrace-like room facing the street that's a calm break from the crowds. Open from 9 am for brunch through evening. The pudding is firm and eggy with a slightly bitter caramel, and the seasonal menu goes all in: an autumn sweet-potato pudding with ice cream (¥780), a purple sweet-potato Mont Blanc mille-feuille layered with mochi and custard, a cinnamon sweet-potato tart. There's a sugar-butter crepe, soufflé cheesecake, and even tacos with a Corona. Coffee comes from a choice of two beans. Drinks from about ¥500. No cards or e-money; PayPay accepted.

chef_bio.background: Café on Shinsaibashi-suji (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "The pudding had a nice, soft texture with a slightly bitter caramel, giving it a sophisticated touch." — August 2026.

"The purple sweet potato Mont Blanc mille-feuille… features mochi and custard layered within the flaky pastry, creating an indescribably delicious combination of chewy and crispy textures." — October 2026.

places.name: OSARU Coffee
places.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information; the upstairs plates are sandwiches, croque monsieur, French toast, croissants and cheesecake.
places.vegan_detail: Ask. Black coffee (Americano, iced dark roast) is on the menu; the food plates use egg, ham, cheese and béchamel.
places.hours_raw: Daily 8:00–17:00; may change (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners), e-money and QR accepted (Tabelog). Non-smoking; 11 seats; no reservations (Tabelog). The 1F stand serves coffee only; plates are served in the café on the 2F of the building next door (September 2026). About 15 people were waiting before the 8:00 opening on a Saturday, and the stairs fill with a line at busy times; don't line up in front of the neighboring Kumon (October 2026). places.neighborhood: Motomachi 1-7-15, Naniwa — about 4 min from JR Namba, 10 min from Namba Stn Exit 6; entrance a little hard to find
places.cuisine: Specialty coffee stand and upstairs café (11 seats) · 1F stand: coffee only, wooden box seats where you take off your shoes · dark-roast "Slow Boat" iced coffee; "Magic Hour" iced coffee; hot Ethiopian; Americano; café latte · 2F café next door: onion and bacon croque monsieur ¥1,400; hot coffee ¥700; ham and egg sandwich plate with salad, potato salad and honey yogurt; French toast; croissants; cheesecake
places.notes: [Café · a dark-roast coffee stand with a busy breakfast café next door, Motomachi] A small specialty coffee spot a few minutes from JR Namba, open from 8 am every day. The ground-floor stand serves only coffee: a cozy wooden room with box seats where you take off your shoes, and coffees like the dark-roast 'Slow Boat' iced coffee, 'Magic Hour', a hot Ethiopian and a light, low-acid Americano. For food, go up to the café on the second floor of the building next door, where one diner had a creamy onion and bacon croque monsieur (¥1,400) with a dark hot coffee (¥700) and another a ham and egg sandwich plate with a well-dressed salad and honey yogurt. Expect a line: about 15 people were waiting before opening one Saturday, and the line runs up the stairs; don't queue in front of the Kumon next door. When the stand is busy, orders can take a while.

chef_bio.background: Specialty coffee stand with a separate café upstairs next door (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
chef_bio.specialty: Dark-roast coffee; croque monsieur and sandwich plates.

anecdotes.text: "The Croque Monsieur was generously filled with béchamel sauce, cheese, bacon, and onions. It was creamy, with the sweetness of the onions perfectly balancing the saltiness of the bacon." — October 2026, Onion and Bacon Croque Monsieur ¥1,400.
"The first floor serves only coffee, while the second floor offers plates with croissants, Croque Monsieur, French toast, and cheesecake. The entrance was a bit hard to find!" — September 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: OSARU Coffee (オサル コーヒー)、大阪市浪速区元町1-7-15、JR難波駅から308m、毎日8:00〜17:00、カード (VISA・Master・JCB・AMEX・Diners)・電子マネー・QR可、禁煙、11席、予約不可、2016年8月22日開店、公式サイトあり。口コミ(2026年9〜10月): 1階はコーヒーのみのスタンドで、靴を脱いで座る木の箱の席、深煎りの「Slow Boat」のアイスコーヒー、「Magic Hour」、ホットのエチオピア、酸味のない軽いアメリカーノ、カフェラテ。隣の建物の2階のカフェでプレート: 玉ねぎとベーコンのクロックムッシュ1400円、ホットコーヒー700円、ハムと卵のサンドのプレート (サラダ、ポテトサラダ、はちみつのヨーグルト)、フレンチトースト、クロワッサン、チーズケーキ。土曜の開店前に15人ほどの列、階段に並ぶ、隣の Kumon の前に並ばないように、混むと注文に時間がかかる、入口が少しわかりにくい。

cultural_comfort.note: Coffee-only stand on 1F; plates in the 2F café next door; expect a line (2026).

places.cuisine: Creative European cooking and natural wine (19 seats, open kitchen) · ¥8,000 course and anniversary course: "American dog" in binchotan-charcoal batter with spiced meat; buri carpaccio with seaweed sauce; charcoal-grilled sawara with spinach sauce; sweet-potato soup with stracciatella; sansho Bolognese; charcoal-grilled Kyoto Hiyoshi pork; black fig and canelé · à la carte: crab miso toast; porcini omelette; grilled vegetable salad; pork sauté · non-alcoholic gin and tonic; homemade lemonade · birthday plate
places.notes: [Creative · natural wine and seasonal plates from an open kitchen, Namba] A wood-toned second-floor restaurant beside the railway near Nankai Namba, open until midnight, where the cooking is ingredient-led and the wine list leans natural. Courses (from ¥8,000, plus an anniversary course) run from a playful 'American dog' in jet-black binchotan-charcoal batter to buri carpaccio, charcoal-grilled sawara, a sweet-potato soup with stracciatella, sansho Bolognese and low-temperature Kyoto Hiyoshi pork, ending with black figs and canelé. You can also go à la carte: crab miso toast, a porcini omelette, grilled vegetable salad and a pork sauté that won over one seafood eater. Good non-alcoholic drinks too. It suits celebrations, and a birthday plate can be arranged. Sofa seats are first-come even if you've booked. Table charge ¥550. Closed Sundays.

places.notes: [Café · a specialty coffee stand with a roadside bench, Minami-Senba] A tiny coffee stand east of Shinsaibashi with two seats inside and a tented bench along the road outside. The coffee is the point: a piping-hot, rich long black, a refreshing low-acid cold brew (M ¥750), Americanos and a creamy iced latte, with beans to take home. There's a hot dog if you're hungry. Weekday hours are 9 am–6 pm; check weekend hours, which the listing gives two ways.

places.notes: [Pasta · homemade meat sauce on chewy fresh pasta, Minami-Senba] A small counter pasta shop near Shinsaibashi built around its meat sauce, slow-simmered from the beef cut senbon-suji. The classic version is rich and clings well to chewy fresh pasta without any meaty smell; the listing also highlights a cream meat sauce with Australian grain-fed beef meatballs, and there are limited sauces like a dashi meat sauce topped with bonito flakes, a monthly avocado cream, carbonara and arrabbiata. Choose fresh or whole-wheat noodles. Weekday lunch includes a free large size and a side of soup, and drinks are just +¥200. Ordering is by QR code. One diner found the oyster and karasumi pasta bland and disliked being pushed to add the shop on LINE. Six terrace seats allow smoking and pets.

places.cuisine: Sichuan Chinese eatery (16 seats) · lunch sets ¥1,000: mapo tofu set with plenty of Sichuan pepper; fried rice set with two pieces of yurinchi; sweet and sour pork; +¥200 for two pieces of fried chicken · evening: 2-item assorted platter set ¥1,500 (mapo tofu, yurinchi, pickles, soup and rice with refills); dry dandan noodles (small) ¥500; steamed chicken with Hong Kong sauce ¥300; spicy shrimp with mayonnaise (small) ¥500; century egg tofu with sesame sauce; shrimp omelet; yodare-dori; shumai; xiao long bao · courses with 90-min all-you-can-drink
places.notes: [Chinese · numbing Sichuan mapo tofu and set meals, Yotsubashi] A small, calm Sichuan eatery in the basement of a building you reach straight from Yotsubashi Station's Exit 2 stairs. The owner formerly ran Meigen, a popular Chinese restaurant in Honmachi, so its signature mapo tofu lives on here; the listing also cites experience at Osaka's Koshin. Every lunch set is ¥1,000, and mapo tofu is the house signature: boldly Sichuan, with a generous hit of numbing pepper that one diner calls addictive and another found too spicy to finish. Unusually, set meals continue at night, like a ¥1,500 two-item platter of mapo tofu and yurinchi with refillable soup and rice. In the evening there are small plates for drinking too: dry dandan noodles (small ¥500), steamed chicken with Hong Kong sauce (¥300), a spicy shrimp mayo and century egg tofu with sesame sauce. One person runs the place, so expect to wait a little for orders. Closed Sundays; Saturday dinner is by reservation only.

chef_bio.background: Sichuan Chinese eatery (Tabelog; 2026 reviews). The owner formerly ran Meigen, a popular Chinese restaurant in Honmachi, so its signature mapo tofu lives on here; the listing also cites experience at Osaka's Koshin (October 2026 review).

places.notes: [Sweets · light mousse cakes and chocolate, Kita-Horie] A small, stylish patisserie a minute from Nishi-Ohashi Station, with a showcase of seasonal cakes and just four counter seats to eat in. One diner notes that most cakes are mousse-based and made airy, so fruit and chocolate come through without heaviness: the Écrin (¥700) layers strawberry and mascarpone mousse around a passion fruit centre, and one diner compared its texture to a premium Aero bar. In autumn there is a chestnut roll (roulé au marron, ¥680) with Hokkaido cream and a Japanese-chestnut Mont Blanc; the soufflé au chocolat (¥680) is surprisingly light. Kouign-amann to take away, and café au lait (¥600) or a creamy cappuccino to drink. Eat-in seats can't be booked, so come soon after the 11:00 opening; cakes can be reserved by phone. Closed Mondays and Tuesdays.

chef_bio.background: Patisserie and chocolatier (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
chef_bio.specialty: Light mousse cakes; chocolate; seasonal fruit cakes.

anecdotes.text: "When you take a fork to it, the mousse is surprisingly light, filled with air… The tang of the passion fruit adds a refreshing kick, ensuring the sweetness doesn't overwhelm." — October 2026, Écrin ¥700.

"The sponge cake was moist and chewy, paired with Hokkaido cream and chestnut chantilly… The soufflé chocolate was surprisingly light and easy to eat, despite being chocolate." — October 2026, Roulé au Marron ¥680, Soufflé au Chocolat ¥680.

places.vegan_detail: Not vegan in practice: the one daily plate has a meat or fish main with egg and dashi-based sides; no vegan option described.

places.cuisine: Tea-room café with antique furniture and stained glass (20 seats, counter and a few tables) · lunch is one daily plate, "Honeysuckle rice" ¥1,100 (¥1,300 with a drink, February–March 2026): a main such as Japanese-style hamburg steak with grated daikon and ponzu, three or more small sides (vegetable tempura, simmered dishes, coleslaw, omelet), white or mixed-grain rice and soup · tea, yuzu tea, café au lait · mini parfait or cake with lunch
places.notes: [Café · a retro tea room with a home-style daily lunch plate, Minami-Senba] A dimly lit café near Nagahoribashi that feels like an old Western-style house or British tea room, with antique furniture and stained glass. A reviewer describes it as run by a lovely elderly couple. It opens only Tuesday to Thursday for lunch and serves one thing: the daily 'Honeysuckle rice' plate (¥1,100, ¥1,300 with a drink), a main such as a light Japanese-style hamburg steak with grated daikon and ponzu plus several small vegetable sides, white or mixed-grain rice and soup. Several diners value it as a balanced, home-style meal that changes every day; a mini parfait or cake can be added. One diner was served hot water on arrival in winter. Cash only, and smoking is allowed inside.

chef_bio.background: Tea-room café serving a daily lunch plate (Tabelog; 2023–2026 reviews). A reviewer describes it as run by a lovely elderly couple (January 2023 review).

House rules: each guest orders at least one food item, parfaits come as a drink set, and pricier drinks cost extra. One diner found the bowls smaller than in the photos. places.notes: [Japanese · tempura bowls at lunch and seasonal courses at night, Minami-Senba] A cozy 10-seat Japanese restaurant hidden at the back of a building just off Shinsaibashi-suji. The shop says it is run by a couple both born in the Year of the Rabbit. Weekday lunch is a short run of tempura bowls and set meals, from a ¥700 tempura bowl to a two-shrimp special bowl (¥1,000) with a light batter and a dashi-rich Kansai-style sauce; rice can be made large for free, miso soup comes alongside, and you pay first. Lunch ends when the rice runs out, and one diner saw it fill up soon after noon. At night it becomes a place for seasonal Japanese courses built on fish bought at Kuromon Market, with a good sake list; one diner was served a warming sake-lees soup on a cold night. Courses need booking by the day before; à la carte diners pay a ¥550 charge. Smoking is allowed. Closed Sundays.

places.cuisine: Bistro-style teppanyaki with French technique, ordered à la carte and served course-style (15 seats) · pork rillettes with red cabbage and baguette · Canadian lobster and scallops with salted onion mousse and lobster consommé jelly ¥3,960 · wild red shrimp and snow crab with carrot mousse · cabbage steak with Gorgonzola (half portions possible) · sautéed cod milt with Shimonita leeks and port-wine onion sauce · Black Wagyu sirloin cap steak 100 g · wagyu tendon and garlic rice · mixed seafood okonomiyaki to finish · chocolate cake with vanilla ice cream · wine
places.notes: [Teppanyaki · French-leaning teppanyaki that ends in okonomiyaki, Yotsubashi] A calm, wood-toned counter near Yotsubashi Station that cooks teppanyaki with French technique and still finishes the Osaka way, with okonomiyaki. You order à la carte and dishes arrive course-style: pork rillettes with red cabbage, lobster and scallops with salted onion mousse and lobster consommé jelly (¥3,960), the signature cabbage steak under a Gorgonzola sauce (mop it up with baguette), cod milt with Shimonita leeks, a 100 g Black Wagyu sirloin cap steak, then garlic rice or a mixed seafood okonomiyaki. Portions suit two, and one pair of diners was allowed to take leftovers home. Run by a couple, so service can be slow; one diner felt pressed to order a full run from appetizer to dessert. Book ahead; ¥550 appetizer charge; JCB or AMEX only.

chef_bio.background: Teppanyaki and okonomiyaki restaurant using French techniques (Tabelog; 2025–2026 reviews). A couple runs it, so service can take a little time (January 2026 review).
chef_bio.specialty: Cabbage steak with Gorgonzola; seafood starters; okonomiyaki finish.

anecdotes.text: "The lobster meat was plump and elastic, paired with a fluffy, sweet salted onion mousse. On top, a consommé jelly made from simmered lobster shells added depth…" — November 2025, Canadian Lobster, Scallops, Salted Onion Mousse and Lobster Consommé Jelly ¥3,960.
"The specialty here was delicious, featuring a Gorgonzola sauce. I recommend dipping the leftover sauce with a baguette." — August 2026, cabbage steak.

places.notes: [Sweets · homemade ice cream with sorbets, oat-milk flavors and quiche lunches, Minami-Horie] A bright ice cream café tucked a little off the main road in Minami-Horie, whose name means 'satisfied' in Swedish. The case holds about 14 homemade flavors, and you can taste before you choose: matcha with salted black cocoa cookie, pistachio and caramel walnut, a creamy caramel banana made with oat milk, and seasonal sorbets like mango and cardamom (one diner found the spice faint). Scoops run ¥640–840. It's also a lunch spot: the quiche plate (¥1,950 with a dessert plate) comes with a thick soup and a dill salad, and on Friday and Saturday mornings there's a breakfast plate with rice-flour bread or pancakes and Tanba vegetables (¥1,190). Tabelog lists vegan and gluten-free options; ask at the counter. Closed Tuesdays.

places.notes: [Bakery café · curry bread and a curry cabbage dog, Minami-Horie] A friendly, unpretentious bakery with an eat-in café on a stylish Minami-Horie street, known for its curry breads. The crispy minced-meat curry bread looks ordinary until you bite into a filling closer to a minced cutlet; there's an egg curry bread too, and the curry cabbage dog piles curry-spiced cabbage around a sausage. A curry lunch is served, and the shelves hold breads like mixed nuts (¥268), cheese fromage (¥328), bacon French bread and anpan, plus sandwiches and a breakfast menu from 8 am. Eating in requires a drink; the coffee gets praise. One diner found prices have crept up. Closed Tuesdays.

places.notes: [Café · Minami-Senba, open until 10 pm with a dog-friendly terrace] A stylish café between Honmachi and Shinsaibashi that sells goods (brand-name bags and wallets) alongside coffee, and stays open until 10 pm every day. places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: fresh cream, egg and dairy across the cakes, cream puffs, pudding and panna cotta; no vegan statement.

places.cuisine: Osaka patisserie, flagship of four LE PINEAU shops, with a 9-seat café · Mont Blanc (seasonal pumpkin version) · classic chocolat · Gâteau Fraise · strawberry tart on pie crust · soufflé fromage and soufflé chocolat · cream puffs · fig shortcake · "Kuro" chocolate cake · berry panna cotta · Iyo-orange rare cheesecake · "Sunao" pudding · chocolate cookie (bitter, 60% cacao) ¥270 · morning sets with avocado or tuna-and-cheese toast · chai · Halloween and Christmas sweets
places.notes: [Patisserie · Kita-Horie, the flagship of an Osaka cake house] A neighborhood cake shop near Nishi-Ohashi Station, Tabelog Sweets WEST Top 100 in 2020, 2022, 2023 and 2026, and the flagship (本店) of four LE PINEAU shops, all in Osaka. Regulars come back for fair prices and generous sizes: a Mont Blanc dense with chopped chestnut, the layered classic chocolat, Gâteau Fraise, a strawberry tart on pie crust, cream puffs with milky cream, and mini soufflé cakes (fromage, and a chocolate one almost like nama chocolate). Cookies are sold singly, including a bitter 60%-cacao chocolate cookie (¥270). The small café next to the shop serves morning sets of avocado or tuna-and-cheese toast and asks for one drink each; payment can be combined with shop purchases. Expect lines at Halloween and Christmas. A regular noted the shop's 32nd anniversary in April 2023.

chef_bio.background: Patisserie that calls itself Osaka-born; four shops (Kita-Horie flagship, Tamatsukuri, Umeda Hanshin, Umekita Green Place) per the official site; Tabelog Sweets WEST Top 100 in 2020, 2022, 2023 and 2026 (Tabelog). A regular marked its 32nd anniversary in April 2023 (Tabelog review).
chef_bio.specialty: Mont Blanc; classic chocolat; soufflé cakes; cream puffs.

anecdotes.text: "The Mont Blanc features a strong flavor of chestnut cream complemented by finely chopped chestnuts, while the lightness of the whipped cream and sponge cake creates a perfectly balanced taste." — October 2026.
"The soufflé chocolate has a slightly gooey texture reminiscent of fresh chocolate, and it's incredibly rich." — October 2026.

places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: the courses are mostly meat and seafood skewers (wagyu, pork tenderloin, shrimp, pike conger, Spanish mackerel); one skewer is dipped in broth.
places.hours_raw: Mon, Tue, Thu–Sun 17:00–23:00 (last order 22:30); closed Wednesday (Tabelog). Reservations and same-day walk-ins both welcome (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners), e-money and QR (Tabelog). 13 seats: 7 at the counter, tables for 4 and 2; heated tobacco only in a designated area; school-age children welcome (Tabelog). places.cuisine: Creative kushikatsu courses at a counter (13 seats) · 8-, 10/12- and 15-skewer courses, or omakase until you say stop · ¥3,980 12-skewer course with a glass of wine: shrimp in shiso, wagyu, squid with okra and sea-urchin sauce, taro in rice-cracker crumbs, pike conger with plum sauce, Manganji pepper stuffed with meat, octopus and cheese wrapped in yuba (dipped in broth), asparagus, pork tenderloin with mustard sauce, broad-bean tofu, angel shrimp, Spanish mackerel · seasonal ingredients · Kirin Ichiban Shibori draft ¥620 · sake, shochu, wine
places.notes: [Kushikatsu · Minami-Senba, creative skewer courses] A calm, tucked-away counter near Shinsaibashi where the menu is essentially three skewer courses (8, 12 or 15 pieces) or an omakase that runs until you call a stop. The ¥3,980 course of 12 skewers comes with a glass of wine and moves through shrimp wrapped in shiso, wagyu, squid with okra and sea-urchin sauce, taro coated in rice crackers, pike conger with plum sauce, octopus and cheese wrapped in yuba and dipped in broth, and pork tenderloin with mustard sauce. Skewers are fried two at a time and handed over hot. Diners like the seasonal ingredients; one found it closer to standard kushikatsu than the 'creative' name suggests. Walk-ins are welcome; closed Wednesdays.

chef_bio.background: Kushikatsu restaurant that opened on 22 March 2023 (Tabelog).
chef_bio.philosophy: Sauces made from vegetable trimmings to cut food waste (Tabelog, shop-provided).
chef_bio.specialty: Octopus and cheese in yuba; pork tenderloin with mustard sauce.

anecdotes.text: "My favorites are the pork tenderloin with mustard sauce and the octopus and cheese wrapped in yuba, which you dip in broth." — October 2026.
"They offered a lot of seasonal ingredients, which were fresh and delightful. The service was quick, and everything was delicious." — October 2026.

places.name: ANNIE's Diner
places.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information; burgers, flour tortillas (burritos, quesadillas, tacos) and sauces point to wheat. Taco rice and the hamburg-steak plates are the dishes to ask about.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: hamburg steaks, burgers, chicken wings, chili con carne, cheese and egg throughout; no vegan statement.

Cards, e-money and QR accepted (Tabelog). 12 seats: 8 at the counter, one table of 4; smoking allowed except at lunch (Tabelog; a February 2026 diner went early for that reason). On the 2nd floor; look for the menu board on the street and on the stair landing (Tabelog reviews). Weekday lunch fills and lines form by noon (October 2026 review). Opened 7 February 2024 (Tabelog).

places.cuisine: Retro American diner with Mexican dishes (12 seats) · lunch: hamburg steak with a choice of weight and sauce, rice, soup, salad and potatoes (about ¥1,000), taco rice, a monthly special (chashu and fried egg set, eel torotama hamburg, arrabbiata cheese hamburg) · dinner: 200 g hamburg steak ¥1,400, Mexican potato salad ¥500, chicken, beef or pork tacos, beef burrito, chili con carne cheese quesadilla with guacamole and salsa, Buffalo wings with blue-cheese yogurt dip, melt garlic rice, "Maximum The Burg" on a teppan with hot cheese poured over, chocolate banana split · Corona
places.notes: [American diner · Minami-Senba, hamburg-steak lunches and Tex-Mex nights] A second-floor diner done up in retro Americana (dolls, colorful stickers) with a counter and one window table. Lunch is the draw: a hamburg steak where you choose the weight, the sauce and how much rice, with soup, salad and potatoes for about ¥1,000, plus taco rice and a monthly special that one regular (14 visits) comes back for every time — a chashu-and-fried-egg set in October 2026, an eel torotama hamburg in July. Expect a line by noon. Evenings turn Tex-Mex: tacos you squeeze lime over, two-piece beef burritos, a chili-con-carne quesadilla with guacamole and salsa, Buffalo wings with a blue-cheese yogurt dip, and the 'Maximum The Burg', finished at the table with hot cheese. Smoking is allowed at night but not at lunch.

chef_bio.background: American diner with Mexican influences that opened on 7 February 2024 (Tabelog).
chef_bio.specialty: Hamburg steak; monthly lunch special; tacos and burritos.

anecdotes.text: "This month's limited-time offering is the Unagi Torotama Hamburg, likely due to the Day of the Eel… the hamburger sauce was a sweet soy-based blend that complemented the eel perfectly." — July 2026, 13th visit.
"I was able to choose the weight of the steak and the sauce, and they also asked how much rice I wanted. With rice, soup, salad, and potatoes included, it was around JPY 1000." — December 2025.

places.name: おにぎり三昧 ちゅん太郎 (Onigiri Zanmai Chuntaro)
places.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information; the onigiri rice is plain, but fillings (mentaiko butter, egg-yolk miso, cream-cheese miso, tenmusu), miso soups, fried chicken and agedashi tofu may involve soy sauce, miso or batter.
places.vegan_detail: Ask. No vegan statement; ume onigiri and vegetable sides (spinach ohitashi, okara) exist, but okaka is bonito and the soups and ohitashi likely use fish dashi.

Cards accepted; no e-money or QR (Tabelog). 15 seats: 7 at the counter, 8 at tables; non-smoking, ashtray outside; children and strollers welcome (Tabelog). At the back of the building, easy to miss (Tabelog shop text). An April 2025 review describes a limited onigiri lunch 13:00–15:00 (one plate ¥1,500 or a pork kakuni set); not on the current listing. Opened 11 February 2021 (Tabelog).

places.cuisine: Onigiri izakaya with seasonal fish, meat and vegetable dishes (15 seats) · onigiri of organic Koshihikari from Okayama: egg-yolk miso, mentaiko butter, house tuna mayo, cream-cheese miso, okaka, ume, tenmusu · miso soups including a "nebaneba" soup of sticky ingredients, clam soup and Senba soup · firefly squid, dashimaki, fried chicken, mackerel grilled with miso, white miso with dried persimmon, agedashi tofu, oden in winter, sashimi platter · "one plate" of three small onigiri with sides · sake and shochu
places.notes: [Onigiri izakaya · Minami-Senba, a one-person counter at the back of a building] A small izakaya hidden at the back of the Nippo Eco Building, run by one young owner, where the onigiri are the point: soft, gently shaped rice (organic Koshihikari from Okayama) with crisp nori and fillings like egg-yolk miso, mentaiko butter, house tuna mayo, cream-cheese miso and tenmusu. Around them come careful home-style dishes — firefly squid, dashimaki, mackerel grilled with miso, agedashi tofu, and a white miso with dried persimmon one regular calls exceptional — and a list of miso soups, from a sticky 'nebaneba' soup to clam soup with huge clams. Diners mention organic, pesticide-free ingredients and say non-drinkers are just as welcome. The 'one plate' of three small onigiri can only be ordered when the owner isn't busy.

roles: Owner (runs the shop alone, per an October 2025 review)
chef_bio.background: Onigiri izakaya that opened on 11 February 2021 (Tabelog); "run by a young man on his own" (October 2025 review).
chef_bio.philosophy: Seasonal fish, meat and vegetables, finished with onigiri; organic rice and vegetables (Tabelog shop text; 2025 reviews).
chef_bio.specialty: Onigiri; miso soups; white miso with dried persimmon.

anecdotes.text: "The onigiri were fluffy and tender, pairing wonderfully with the crispy nori… watching the preparation process gave me the impression that they were handled gently to preserve the rice's deliciousness." — April 2025, One Plate ¥1,500.
"Everything was delicious, but the white miso with dried persimmons was truly exceptional." — March 2026, fifth visit.

places.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information; mapo tofu, the house chili oil and the four-hour meat sauce are seasoned sauces, and the menu also has xiao long bao, shumai and gyoza in wheat wrappers.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: the mapo tofu is built on a minced-meat sauce, and the rest of the menu is chicken, shrimp and pork; no vegan statement.
places.hours_raw: Mon–Sat 11:30–15:00 (last order 14:30) and 18:30–22:00 (last order 21:15); closed Sunday; closed 31 December–3 January (Tabelog). Reservations accepted (Tabelog). Lunch is cash or PayPay only; cards accepted at dinner; no e-money; PayPay and au PAY (Tabelog). 18 seats, counter seating; non-smoking; children and strollers welcome (Tabelog). Lines form at lunch (October 2026 review). Opened 2 November 2022 (Tabelog).
places.neighborhood: Shinmachi 1-25-3, 8R Bld.5 1F — 3 min from Yotsubashi Stn, 4 min from Nishi-Ohashi Stn
places.cuisine: Mapo tofu specialist and Chinese bistro with wine (18 seats) · Shin-chan's Mapo Tofu (sweet and spicy) ¥1,400 at lunch with rice (free refills), soup and pickled mustard greens · First Love Mapo Tofu (hot and numbing) · mapo curry · house chili oil and a meat sauce cooked for four hours · at dinner mapo with an egg yolk to stir in · ebi mayo with nuts · yodare chicken · spicy chicken · xiao long bao · shrimp shumai · Kurobuta gyoza · sesame dumplings
places.notes: [Mapo tofu · Shinmachi, a café-looking Sichuan bistro with lunch lines] A stylish, café-like front in the Shinmachi office district hides a mapo tofu specialist; at lunch the line tells you you've found it. The house chili oil and a chunky meat sauce simmered for four hours carry two versions: Shin-chan's Mapo Tofu, sweet-spicy with a hint of cinnamon and a numbness that builds slowly (¥1,400 with rice refills, soup and pickled mustard greens), and the hot First Love Mapo Tofu, named for the jolt it gives. There's also a mapo curry. Some diners find the standard heat mild and suggest asking for it spicier. At dinner the mapo comes with an egg yolk to stir in, alongside ebi mayo under crunchy nuts, yodare chicken, xiao long bao and Kurobuta gyoza. Lunch is cash or PayPay only; closed Sundays.

chef_bio.background: Mapo tofu specialist that opened on 2 November 2022 (Tabelog).
chef_bio.specialty: Mapo tofu with house chili oil and a four-hour meat sauce; ebi mayo; yodare chicken.

anecdotes.text: "The first bite left a lasting impression with a subtle sweetness from the cinnamon aroma. At first, I thought it wasn't too spicy, but as I continued eating, the numbing sensation from the Sichuan peppercorns gradually kicked in." — October 2026, Shin-chan's Mapo Tofu (Sweet and Spicy) ¥1,400.
"The signature dish, Mapo Tofu, is served in a unique style where you mix in the egg yolk placed in the center." — September 2026, dinner.

places.name: だし処 船場山本 (Dashi Dokoro Semba Yamamoto)
places.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information; the kombu-cured sashimi, dashimaki and dashi chazuke are dashi-based, but soy sauce, miso soup and the chicken tempura set are likely wheat sources.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: the house dashi is kombu with honkarebushi bonito (official site), and the sets center on fish, egg and chicken.
places.hours_raw: Mon–Sat 11:00–14:00 (last order 13:30) and 17:00–22:00; closed Sundays, holidays and the 2nd and 4th Wednesday (Tabelog). No lunch reservations, and lunch ends when sold out (official site; Tabelog). Dinner reservations accepted; dinner is generally limited to 2 hours (Tabelog). Cards, e-money and QR accepted (Tabelog). 11 seats: 5 at the counter, 6 at tables; non-smoking (Tabelog). Lines form before opening at lunch (2026 reviews). Google Maps leads to 小倉屋山本's main store instead; follow the directions on the official site (official site). Opened 13 December 2021 (Tabelog).
places.neighborhood: Minami-Senba 4-10-22, in a back alley near Shinmachibashi — 5 min from Shinsaibashi Stn Exit 3 or Yotsubashi Stn Exit 1-A
places.cuisine: Dashi-centered Japanese cooking in a renovated old house (11 seats) · dashi of ma-kombu from southern Hokkaido and Makurazaki honkarebushi · lunch: kombu-cured gozen ¥1,600 (three kombu-cured sashimi such as sea bream, salmon, kinmedai, skipjack or butterfish; dashimaki; kinpira gobo; tsukudani; miso soup; finished as dashi chazuke with salted kombu), chicken tempura gozen, a daily gozen (simmered sea bream) · dinner: à la carte and courses, autumn 2026: Kagoshima Black Wagyu yaki-shabu with Izumo eggs, autumn salmon dashi chazuke, lotus root fried in rice-cracker crumbs, hojicha pudding and fig brûlée · seasonal sake and shochu
places.notes: [Dashi cooking · Minami-Senba, a hidden old house run by a 170-year-old Osaka company] A small, modern-feeling Japanese restaurant in a renovated old house down a narrow Senba back alley, run by 小倉屋山本, a company with 170 years of history, on the street where it was founded (official site). Everything turns on the dashi: ma-kombu from southern Hokkaido and honkarebushi from Makurazaki. Lunch is the famous part, with a line before opening and no reservations: the kombu-cured gozen (¥1,600) brings three sashimi cured in kombu, a dashimaki diners call the best, kinpira gobo and miso soup, then hot dashi poured over rice and salted kombu for dashi chazuke. A regular on a 14th visit was still seen off by the familiar staff. Dinner is courses and à la carte with seasonal sake. Google Maps points to the company's main store; use the site's directions.

chef_bio.background: Japanese restaurant run by 小倉屋山本, a company with 170 years of history, in a renovated old house on the Senba back alley where the company was founded (official site). Opened 13 December 2021 (Tabelog).
chef_bio.philosophy: "The essence of dashi cooking rooted in Osaka tradition" — dashi from southern-Hokkaido ma-kombu and Makurazaki honkarebushi (official site).
chef_bio.specialty: Kombu-cured gozen with dashi chazuke; dashimaki.

anecdotes.text: "I poured the dashi over the rice, topped it with salted kombu, and made the ultimate dashi chazuke… the best way to experience the umami of the dashi." — October 2026, Kombu-zime Gozen ¥1,600.
"As always, I was seen off by the familiar staff. Thank you for a wonderful meal! I will definitely come back." — October 2026, 14th visit.

places.name: 片岡篤司 (Kataoka Atsushi)
places.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information; omakase sushi with soy-marinated tuna, simmered eel, miso soup and an ebi-mayo roll add-on, so ask about soy sauce and glazes when booking.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: an omakase sushi course of fish and shellfish.
places.hours_raw: Mon, Tue, Thu–Sun 18:00–23:00; closed Wednesday (Tabelog). Reservation only (Tabelog); bookings through the OMAKASE site or by Instagram DM @atushi.sushi, and diners report waits of about six months (September 2026 reviews). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners), Rakuten Edy, iD, QUICPay, PayPay, Rakuten Pay (Tabelog). 9 seats, 8 at the counter; non-smoking (Tabelog). Inside the Quinto Shinsaibashi Bldg, at the back on the left; nothing outside signals a sushi bar (September 2026 reviews). Opened 17 November 2024 per Tabelog; a review says October 2024.
places.neighborhood: Higashi-Shinsaibashi 1-13-11, Quinto Shinsaibashi Bldg 1F (at the back) — about 5 min from Shinsaibashi Stn, 229 m from Nagahoribashi Stn
places.cuisine: Omakase sushi counter (9 seats) · sushi course ¥25,000 (October 2026), mostly nigiri after one or two small dishes · several kinds of shari matched to the toppings, red-vinegar seasoned and firm · examples (September 2026): Akashi sea bream, Awaji squid, Nemuro ikura with kombu dashi, charcoal-grilled Chiba hairtail, Kesennuma bonito, Lake Biwa trout, Otaru saury with matsutake rice, marinated tuna, chu-toro, Kishiwada kintaro sardine, Hokkaido botan shrimp with shrimp miso, simmered anago · add-ons: toro-taku roll, "adult" ebi-mayo roll · sake, wine, highballs
places.notes: [Sushi · Higashi-Shinsaibashi, the hard-to-book counter of a young former Shizuku head chef] An unmarked counter at the back of an office building, behind a grey Italian-plaster wall with the name in vertical stainless-steel letters. Kataoka Atsushi led the popular Sushi Shizuku Nagahori branch before opening here in late 2024; bookings filled months ahead before the doors opened, and regulars now wait about six months. Diners describe a dedicated perfectionist who keeps experimenting, notably with several kinds of rice matched to different toppings (red vinegar, firm, on the larger side). The course is almost all nigiri — Akashi sea bream, Nemuro ikura, Otaru saury over matsutake rice, a surprisingly rich Kishiwada sardine — and regulars add the toro-taku roll and the 'adult' ebi-mayo. An apprentice, Kanta, works alongside. One first-timer found the rice too salty; most come back.

chef_bio.background: Previously led the Nagahori branch of Sushi Shizuku in Osaka; went independent in late 2024 (September 2026 review; Tabelog opening date 17 November 2024). Reviewers call the chef young. Works with an apprentice named Kanta (October 2026 review).
chef_bio.philosophy: Several kinds of shari matched to different toppings, changed and refined from visit to visit (October 2026 review).
chef_bio.specialty: Omakase nigiri; ebi-mayo and toro-taku rolls.

anecdotes.text: "The use of several types of rice for different toppings is one of the charms of this restaurant. It felt like a new type of rice was served this time that wasn't present during my last visit." — October 2026, sushi course ¥25,000, fifth visit.
"Opened in October 2024, this sushi restaurant 'Kataoka Atsushi' has gained immense popularity, with reservations fully booked for over three months before its opening." — September 2026.

places.name: 料理店オクノ (Ryori Ten Okuno)
places.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information; handmade pasta, fried fish and cream sauces are on the courses, but dishes change daily, so ask when booking.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: prosciutto, foie gras, beef, lamb, wild boar, fish and cheese run through the courses.
places.hours_raw: Daily 12:00–14:30 and 17:00–23:30; closing days not fixed (Tabelog). Lunch by reservation only: chef's omakase of 5 dishes ¥3,500 or 8 dishes ¥5,000 (Tabelog). Dinner courses and à la carte; reservations recommended (Tabelog reviews). Cards and PayPay; no e-money (Tabelog). 17 seats: 5 at the counter, three tables of 4; non-smoking; children and strollers welcome; sommelier on staff (Tabelog). One October 2026 diner reports 20–30 minutes between courses with a single chef cooking. Opened 13 September 2023 (Tabelog); a regular has come since the previous ownership.
places.neighborhood: Nambanaka 1-16-4 — 3 min from Nankai Namba Stn
places.cuisine: Playful Italian from an open kitchen, mixing Italian regional cooking with Japanese, Chinese and ethnic ideas (17 seats) · omakase courses (5, 7 or 8 dishes; lunch 5 dishes ¥3,500, 8 dishes ¥5,000) or à la carte · handmade pasta with seasonal sauces (Ezo deer, porcini, ragù, truffle and pork, fish and pesto) · foie gras omelet · carpaccio · crisp-skinned Spanish mackerel · lamb hamburg · red-wine-braised beef cheek · baked cheese stuffed with mushrooms and wild boar · homemade ricotta with prosciutto · natural wines chosen by sommelier staff, by the decanter
places.notes: [Italian · Nambanaka, playful omakase and natural wine] A tucked-away open-kitchen Italian a few minutes from Nankai Namba that blends regional Italian cooking with Japanese, Chinese and ethnic ideas, and changes the menu daily. Choose an omakase (5, 7 or 8 dishes) or go à la carte: regulars return for the foie gras omelet, a lamb hamburg, handmade pasta with seasonal sauces (Ezo deer, porcini, truffle and pork), red-wine-braised beef cheek, and a baked cheese stuffed with mushrooms and wild boar. The staff sommeliers pour natural wine, red and white by the decanter. One chef cooks, so a full course can take close to three hours. Lunch is omakase only and must be reserved (¥3,500 or ¥5,000).

chef_bio.background: Italian restaurant that opened on 13 September 2023 (Tabelog); a regular has visited since the previous ownership (June 2025 review). Dishes cooked by one chef (October 2026 review).
chef_bio.philosophy: Italian regional cooking combined with Japanese, Chinese and ethnic ideas; a playful, daily-changing menu (Tabelog, shop-provided).
chef_bio.specialty: Handmade pasta with seasonal sauces; foie gras omelet; natural wine.

anecdotes.text: "I was really happy to see the return of the foie gras omelet, and I enjoyed it again today… I also tried the lamb hamburger for the first time, and it was delightful." — October 2026, fourth visit.
"The highlight was the baked cheese stuffed with mushrooms and wild boar—it was the most impressive dish!" — October 2026, omakase course.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: 料理店オクノ、大阪市浪速区難波中1-16-4、南海なんば駅から徒歩3分、毎日12:00〜14:30・17:00〜23:30、不定休、ランチは予約のみでおまかせ5品3500円か8品5000円、カード・PayPay可、電子マネー不可、17席 (カウンター5、テーブル4×3)、禁煙、子供・ベビーカー可、ソムリエあり、オープン日2023年9月13日。店の紹介: オープンキッチンの遊び心あるイタリアン、イタリアの郷土料理に和・中・エスニックの発想、季節で変わるソースの手打ちパスタ (Ezo の鹿、ポルチーニ)、ソムリエのスタッフが選ぶ自然派ワイン、日替わり、おまかせコース。口コミ(2025年6月〜2026年10月): フォアグラのオムレツ、カルパッチョ、皮のパリッとした鰆、羊のハンバーグ、牛ほほ肉の赤ワイン煮、きのこと猪を詰めた焼きチーズ、魚とジェノベーゼのパスタ、トリュフと豚のパスタ、自家製リコッタと生ハム、デキャンタのワイン、シェフ一人で料理して皿の間が20〜30分、前のオーナーのころから通う常連。

places.name: 酒肴哲 (Sakana Tetsu)
places.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information; oden broth and doteyaki are usually soy- and miso-seasoned, and the finish is udon.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: the oden broth is dashi, and the sakana are fish, offal and meat.
places.hours_raw: Mon–Sat 17:00–23:00 (last order 22:30, last seating 22:00); closed Sunday, and Sunday–Monday when Monday is a holiday; other irregular closures announced on Instagram (Tabelog). Reservations accepted; stays may be limited to 2 hours when busy; walk-ins possible right at 17:00 on weekdays, reservations essential later (Tabelog; September 2026 review). Cards accepted; no e-money or QR (Tabelog). 15 seats: an L-shaped counter of 10 and one table of 5 (tables for groups of three or more); non-smoking, smoking area outside; wheelchair accessible (Tabelog). Tabelog Izakaya WEST Top 100 in 2024, 2025 and 2026. Opened 27 February 2010 (Tabelog).
places.neighborhood: Nipponbashi 2-7-27, in a narrow back alley — about 8 min from Nipponbashi Stn (Kintetsu, Sakaisuji Line)
places.cuisine: Oden and sakana (small dishes for drinking) counter (15 seats) · oden served piece by piece, each heated in a small pot of the broth: daikon, potato, egg · doteyaki · potato salad · roast beef with onion and a mild spiced sauce · thick-cut Spanish mackerel sashimi with salt and vinegar · sea bream, pike conger, squid, chicken liver, soft roe, tofu, yuba, octopus, tomato with cheese · udon in the oden broth to finish · beer in thin glasses, sake, shochu, wine
places.notes: [Oden izakaya · Nipponbashi, a back-alley counter and a three-time Tabelog Top 100] An inconspicuous counter in a narrow alley behind Nipponbashi Station, filled with the smell of oden, that has made Tabelog's Izakaya WEST Top 100 in 2024, 2025 and 2026. The oden comes almost kaiseki-style: each piece is warmed to order in a little pot of the deep, rich broth and the broth goes back to the main pot, and the meal ends with udon in that broth. Around it, small carefully made plates — the doteyaki one diner calls the best anywhere, potato salad, lightly dressed roast beef, thick slices of salt-and-vinegar Spanish mackerel. The à la carte board carries no prices, so it's easy to run up a bill. One regular noticed the staff pacing each dish to a slow eater without being asked. Walk in right at 5 pm on a weekday; book for later.

chef_bio.background: Oden and sakana izakaya that opened on 27 February 2010; Tabelog Izakaya WEST Top 100 in 2024, 2025 and 2026 (Tabelog).
chef_bio.philosophy: Dishes that put the ingredients and their match with drink ahead of show (July 2026 review).
chef_bio.specialty: Oden warmed piece by piece; doteyaki; udon in oden broth.

anecdotes.text: "The broth was transferred to a small pot for heating, ensuring no waste as it was returned to the main pot after heating." — September 2026, oden.

"The person I visited with had a very slow eating pace. The staff noticed this without us saying anything and timed the serving of the next dish perfectly to match our eating speed." — October 2026, second visit.

places.name: だいちゃん (Daichan)
places.gf_detail: Ask. Handmade soba from Nagano buckwheat, and a reviewer had juwari (100% buckwheat) soba, but the tsuyu is soy-based and there is tempura; ask which soba is juwari that day.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: the soba broth is dashi, and the side dishes include beef, squid, clams and shrimp tempura.
places.hours_raw: Mon and Wed 17:00–23:00; Thu–Sun 11:45–14:00 and 17:00–23:00; closed Tuesday and the fourth Monday (Tabelog). Reservations accepted; call ahead if bringing children (Tabelog). Cards and PayPay per Tabelog; a June 2026 diner says lunch is cash only. 9 counter seats; non-smoking (Tabelog). Opened 1 March 2014 (Tabelog).
places.neighborhood: Nipponbashi 2-7-20, near NGK — about 5 min from Kintetsu Nipponbashi and Nankai Namba Stns
places.cuisine: Handmade soba and Japanese dishes at a 9-seat counter, one chef · thin, white soba from Nagano buckwheat; juwari soba; zaru with wasabi, oroshi hiyakake, curry soba, soba with eggplant and myoga · shrimp tempura, chicken tempura, seasoned egg · night: omakase small dishes and a Japanese course: beef and komatsuna, marinated firefly squid, fried ginkgo, grilled sesame tofu, clams with vinegar miso, salt-grilled mackerel, lotus-root dumplings, chestnut rice, saikyo-yaki, beef shigureni · sake and shochu with sobayu
places.notes: [Soba · Nipponbashi near NGK, a one-chef counter for lunch soba and evening sake] A clean, calm counter of nine seats where one chef makes the soba in the shop from Nagano buckwheat — thin, pale and springy, with juwari on offer. Lunch (Thursday to Sunday) is zaru with fresh wasabi, oroshi hiyakake or curry soba, with hot, thin-battered shrimp tempura one diner calls perfect; one diner found portions small. Evenings turn into a sake stop: omakase small plates such as marinated firefly squid, grilled sesame tofu in dashi and clams with vinegar miso, a Japanese course with salt-grilled mackerel and chestnut rice, and soba to finish, with shochu cut with sobayu. Lunch is cash only, per a June 2026 diner.

roles: Chef (runs the counter alone, per January and June 2026 reviews)
chef_bio.background: Soba and Japanese restaurant that opened on 1 March 2014 (Tabelog); soba made in-house from Nagano buckwheat (February 2026 review).
chef_bio.specialty: Handmade thin soba; juwari soba; shrimp tempura.

anecdotes.text: "The handmade soba was thin, had a great texture, and was truly delicious with just the right amount of chewiness… the shrimp tempura was amazing! It was freshly fried, hot, with a thin, crispy batter." — June 2026, Zaru (with wasabi) and Oroshi Hiyakake, large size.
"The Ju-wari soba was simple yet delightful. I tried two types: the plain soba and the one with eggplant and myoga." — September 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: だいちゃん、大阪市中央区日本橋2-7-20、近鉄日本橋駅・南海なんば駅から徒歩5分ほど、月・水17:00〜23:00、木〜日11:45〜14:00・17:00〜23:00、火曜と第4月曜休み、予約可、子連れは電話で確認、カード・PayPay可、9席 (カウンターのみ)、禁煙、オープン日2014年3月1日。口コミ(2026年1月〜9月): 長野県産のそば粉の手打ちそば、細くて白い、十割そば、ざる (わさび)、おろし冷かけ、カレーそば、茄子と茗荷のそば、海老天、とり天、味玉、夜はおまかせの酒肴と和食のコース (牛肉と小松菜、ホタルイカの沖漬け、銀杏の素揚げ、焼き胡麻豆腐、あさりのぬた、塩鯖、蓮根まんじゅう、栗ご飯、西京焼き、牛のしぐれ煮)、そば湯割りの焼酎、料理人ひとりで営業、量は少なめという声、昼は現金のみという声、NGKの前。

cultural_comfort.note: Counter only; bring cash for lunch (2026).

places.name: 酒と肴 よしまさ (Sake to Sakana Yoshimasa)
places.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information; sashimi and salt-grilled fish are the core, but the sets also carry tempura, fried fish, cutlets and simmered fish, so ask about soy sauce and batter.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a fish izakaya; sets come with fish and miso soup.
places.hours_raw: Mon–Fri 11:30–13:30 (last order 13:30) and 17:30–22:30 (food last order 21:30, drinks 22:00); Sat and holidays 17:30–22:00 (last order 21:30); closed Sunday, and at year-end, New Year and Obon (Tabelog). Dinner ends when ingredients run out; a 2-hour limit may apply when busy; on 30 December courses only (Tabelog). Reservations accepted; the owner prefers phone bookings to online ones, and online bookings get a confirmation call (Tabelog). Cash only: no cards, e-money or QR (Tabelog; May 2026 review). 19 seats: 6 at the counter, 12 at tables; smoking allowed (Tabelog). At lunch, popular items sell out around 12:30, and the grilled fish takes 15 minutes or more (March and August 2026 reviews).
places.neighborhood: Nipponbashi 2-8-16, Nipponbashi Residence 1F, set back from Sakaisuji near Kuromon Market — 5 min from Nipponbashi Stn, about 10 min from Nankai Namba
places.cuisine: Fish izakaya, fish delivered direct from the source and sake chosen by the chef (19 seats) · lunch sets: grilled fish set ¥1,200 (a different seasonal fish each day, served with the head), daily special ¥1,000 (a main plus sashimi or grilled fish), special ¥1,300 (sashimi, grilled fish and a fried dish), Irodori gozen ¥1,600 (sashimi, grilled or simmered fish, rolled omelet, small sides), rice refill ¥200 (2026) · grilled fish seen in 2026: kanpachi, renko-dai, flatfish, yume-kasago, akamuromaji, mako-garei · evening: sashimi platter, simmered whole fish, grilled abalone, oden, fried horse mackerel, anago zosui; fish sukiyaki hot pot in the cold months (2+ people) · courses: omakase four dishes ¥3,300 / ¥3,850 / ¥4,400, fish sukiyaki course ¥4,400 or ¥5,500 · sake, shochu
places.notes: [Fish izakaya · Nipponbashi near Kuromon Market, the grilled-fish lunch counter] A slightly hidden ground-floor izakaya set back from Sakaisuji, where the fish comes direct from the source and the sake is the chef's choice. At lunch, people working nearby come for set meals that read like a seasonal fish chart: the ¥1,200 grilled fish set brings a different whole-headed fish each day — kanpachi, renko-dai, yume-kasago, akamuromaji, mako-garei — and one five-time diner keeps coming back just to see which. The ¥1,300 special adds thick-cut sashimi and a fried dish; portions are generous. Grilling is slow (15 minutes or more) and one person cooks, so come at 11:30; popular items sell out by about 12:30. Evenings are for sashimi platters, simmered fish and, in winter, a fish sukiyaki hot pot. Cash only; the owner, whom one diner found a little shy, prefers bookings by phone.

roles: Owner-chef (one person in the kitchen, March 2026 review)
chef_bio.background: Fish izakaya that buys fish direct from the source; the chef chooses the sake (Tabelog, shop-provided). The owner prefers analog ways and asks for reservations by phone (Tabelog). One person works the kitchen (March 2026 review).
chef_bio.philosophy: Fresh fish from the source; at lunch a different seasonal fish grilled each day instead of the usual mackerel (June–July 2026 reviews).
chef_bio.specialty: Daily grilled-fish set with the head; sashimi platter; fish sukiyaki hot pot.

anecdotes.text: "This was my fourth time enjoying grilled fish, and each time it has been a different seasonal catch, complete with the head! … This time, it was 'Yume Kasago'!!!" — July 2026, grilled fish set meal ¥1,200.
"I decided on the Special Colorful Gozen for JPY 1600… The grilled fish was explained to be Renko Tai… The sashimi was thickly cut and looked fantastic." — May 2026, lunch.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: 酒と肴 よしまさ、大阪市中央区日本橋2-8-16 日本橋レジデンス 1F、日本橋駅から徒歩5分、南海なんば駅から徒歩8分、月〜金11:30〜13:30・17:30〜22:30 (フードL.O. 21:30、ドリンクL.O. 22:00)、土・祝17:30〜22:00、日曜休み、年末年始・お盆休み、夜は食材がなくなり次第終了、混雑時は2時間制、予約可 (店主はアナログ派で電話予約を希望、ネット予約には店から確認の電話)、カード・電子マネー・QR不可、19席 (カウンター6、テーブル12)、喫煙可。店の紹介: 産地直送の魚と店主が選ぶ日本酒、刺身の盛り合わせ、寒い時期は魚すき鍋 (2名から)、おまかせ4品3300円・3850円・4400円、魚すき鍋コース4400円・5500円。口コミ(2025年3月〜2026年8月): 堺筋沿いのビルの奥、黒門市場の近く、焼魚定食1200円 (毎日ちがう旬の魚、頭つき)、日替わり定食1000円、日替わりスペシャル1300円 (刺身・焼魚・揚げ物)、彩り御膳1600円、ご飯おかわり200円、カンパチ、Renko Tai、カレイ、Yume Kasago、Akamuromaji、Mako-Garei、焼くのに15分以上、厨房はひとり、12時半ごろには売り切れも、夜は刺身の盛り合わせ、魚の煮付け、アワビ焼き、おでん、アジフライ、穴子雑炊、飲み放題、天ぷらが生焼け気味だったという声、少し人見知りの店主、常連と地元の客、現金のみ。

cultural_comfort.note: Cash only; the owner prefers phone bookings (Tabelog).

places.name: 堀江串揚げ 勝新 (KATSUSHIN)
places.gf_detail: The shop says its kushiage can be made gluten-free and that it caters for wheat allergy on request (「小麦アレルギー、グルテンフリーご対応致します。ご希望の方はお声をお掛け下さい。」, shop site). Reviewers (October 2025–September 2026) describe a rice-flour batter fried in rice oil. But a February 2026 diner mentions breadcrumbs, a May 2026 course included a wheat-gluten (nama-fu) skewer, the fryer is not described as separate, and the dips include soy sauce and sauce. Say so when booking and ask how the gluten-free skewers are fried.
places.vegan_detail: Ask. The shop says its kushiage can be made vegetarian (shop site), but vegan is not mentioned; the course mixes seafood and meat, and the dips and the closing chazuke use dashi.
places.hours_raw: Mon–Sat 18:00–01:00; closed Sunday (Tabelog; hours may change). The shop site gives 18:00–24:00, last entry 23:00, closed Sunday, and closes early when the day's ingredients run out. Reservations accepted, and diners say they are a must: one person runs the shop and it is usually full (July and August 2026 reviews). Cards (JCB, AMEX) and QUICPay; QR payments accepted (Tabelog). 10 seats, about six at the counter and one table for four (August 2026 review); non-smoking (Tabelog). Open about ten years: a regular since the opening mentions a 10th-anniversary chateaubriand skewer (July 2026 review).
places.neighborhood: Kitahorie 1-10-2, 1F — 113 m from Yotsubashi Stn (about 5 min)
places.cuisine: Creative kushiage, between kushikatsu and tempura, from the day's market produce (10 seats) · omakase skewers until you say stop, or fixed courses of 10, 12, 13, 15 or 20 skewers; a May 2026 diner put it at about ¥300 a skewer · rice-flour batter, 100% Tsuno rice oil from Wakayama (shop site) · salad with fried zucchini to start · skewers seen in 2025–26: angel shrimp, wagyu tenderloin, kisu with crab and mitsuba, lotus root with shiso and minced pork, potato with truffle butter, octopus with Brussels sprouts, Kawachi duck with porcini, whelk with maitake, firefly squid with bamboo shoot, abalone with canola blossoms, roast beef wrapped around foie gras, eel chazuke, dessert skewers · dips: sesame salt, dashi soy sauce, sauce, lemon · aosa dashi chazuke · highballs, wine by the bottle
places.notes: [Kushiage · Kitahorie, a one-person counter of creative skewers in rice flour and rice oil] A ten-seat Horie counter that has turned out creative kushiage for about ten years, with one person doing everything. The shop calls its style halfway between kushikatsu and tempura: market produce in a light rice-flour batter, fried in Wakayama rice oil and finished with a torch, so diners keep eating without feeling heavy. Skewers arrive one by one until you say stop, or in courses of 10 to 20: angel shrimp, wagyu, kisu with crab and mitsuba, Kawachi duck with porcini, a roast-beef-and-foie-gras finale, even an eel chazuke skewer and dessert. A tomato-and-mozzarella salad with hot fried zucchini opens, and the aosa dashi chazuke is a favourite way to finish. Unusually for kushiage, the shop says it can make the skewers gluten-free or vegetarian on request — say so when you book. One November 2025 diner found the batter hard and gritty; a September 2026 diner ranks it No. 1 for skewers.

roles: Owner (runs the shop alone, per July and August 2026 reviews)
chef_bio.background: Creative kushiage counter in Kitahorie, open about ten years (July 2026 review, from a regular since the opening). One person cooks and serves (July and August 2026 reviews); a diner describes the master as having a strong personality (August 2026 review).
chef_bio.philosophy: Kushiage halfway between kushikatsu and tempura, from seasonal market produce; 100% rice oil, and gluten-free, wheat-allergy, vegetarian and children's skewers on request (shop site).
chef_bio.specialty: Omakase creative kushiage; aosa dashi chazuke.

anecdotes.text: "Creative skewers made with rice flour and rice oil. They are simply the best… crispy, light, delicious, and won't leave you feeling heavy." — September 2026.
"I've been coming to this place since it opened 10 years ago. The quality at this price is unbeatable." — July 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 店のサイト: 大阪堀江 創作串揚げ 勝新、大阪市西区北堀江1-10-2 都市開発ビル 101、18:00〜23:00最終入店・24時閉店、日曜定休、ネタが売り切れ次第終了。串揚げは「串カツ」と「天ぷら」の中間の料理、ベジタリアン・グルテンフリーにも対応、子供用の串揚げあり、その日に市場で仕入れた旬のものの串揚げ、おまかせ串揚げコース (よいところで声をかける、目安10本・15本・20本)、和歌山県の築野 (つの) 米油100%使用、小麦アレルギー・グルテンフリー対応 (希望の人は声をかける)。食べログ: 堀江串揚げ 勝新、四ツ橋駅から113m、月〜土18:00〜翌1:00、日曜休み、予約可、カード (JCB、AMEX)・QUICPay・QR可、10席、禁煙。口コミ(2025年10月〜2026年9月): 米粉の衣と米油、軽くてもたれない、最後にバーナーで仕上げ、おまかせで好きなところで止める、10・12・13・15・20本のコース、1本300円ほど、最初のサラダと揚げたズッキーニ、天使の海老、和牛ヒレ、キス・カニ・三つ葉、蓮根と大葉の挽肉、トリュフバターのじゃがいも、タコと芽キャベツ、Kawachi の鴨とポルチーニ、つぶ貝と舞茸、ホタルイカと筍、生麩の酢味噌といくら、アワビと菜の花、ローストビーフのフォアグラ巻き、鰻の茶漬け、デザートの串、ごま塩・だし醤油・ソース・レモン、あおさのだし茶漬け、ひとりで営業していていつも満席なので予約は必須、開店から10年の常連、10周年のシャトーブリアンの串、衣が固くてざらついたという声も。

cultural_comfort.note: Book ahead (one-person counter, usually full); mention gluten-free or vegetarian when booking (2026).

gf_cross_contamination.text: A May 2026 omakase included a wheat-gluten (nama-fu) skewer, and a February 2026 diner mentions the shop's care over "flour and breadcrumbs"; no separate fryer is described.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Dips offered: sesame salt, dashi soy sauce, sauce and lemon (February 2026 review); ask which are wheat-free.

staff_allergy_handling.text: Shop: 「小麦アレルギー、グルテンフリーご対応致します。ご希望の方はお声をお掛け下さい。」 (wheat allergy and gluten-free catered for; ask).

positives.text: Shop: kushiage can be made vegetarian or gluten-free (「串揚げはベジタリアン・グルテンフリーにも対応しており」); frying oil is 100% Tsuno rice oil.
Reviewers describe a rice-flour batter fried in rice oil (October 2025–September 2026).

places.name: まぐろひろし (Maguro Hiroshi)
places.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information; the bowls come with wasabi soy sauce and red miso soup, and the evening course includes a tuna burger on a brioche bun and sesame-miso dishes. The shop accepted a no-mayonnaise request made at booking (April 2026), so ask when you reserve.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a tuna specialist; every bowl and course is built on tuna.
places.hours_raw: Mon–Sat and public holidays 11:00–14:00 (last order 14:00) and 17:30–22:30 (last order 22:00); closed Sunday, plus irregular days (Tabelog). Lunch bowls without reservation; a June 2026 diner found a queue before 11:00. Evening omakase by reservation, now bookable for one person (April 2026 review). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners), e-money (Rakuten Edy, nanaco, WAON, iD, QUICPay) and PayPay (Tabelog). 10 counter seats; private hire possible; non-smoking, smoking area outside; children of school age welcome; take-out (Tabelog). English, Chinese and Korean menus and English-speaking staff (Tabelog). Opened here on 20 January 2026 per Tabelog; reviewers date the opening to February 2026.

places.cuisine: Tuna specialist counter, every part of the fish (10 seats) · lunch bowls with red miso soup and pickles: B negitoro bowl ¥2,050 (February 2026; Yamato yam topping +¥100), C half-and-half of lean tuna and negitoro ¥1,980 (June–July 2026), H marinated tuna mix bowl; deep bowls with about 250 g of rice · evening omakase ¥9,900 (April 2026): two of four obanzai (shirasu with sansho oil ¥500, simmered tuna cheek ¥800), a tuna burger on brioche, three nigiri (lean, kama-toro, marinated chu-toro), hand rolls (negitoro, yam and tuna, menegi with sudachi, avocado with nametake, tuna mayo) and a citrus dessert · à la carte: tuna behind the eye with sesame miso ¥800, tuna sashimi with garlic, tuna fish balls, squid and tuna maki on some days · tuna seen in 2026: a 260 kg Nachi-Katsuura fish aged a week, Oma, Canadian · wide sake list, shochu, wine; draft beer ¥800
places.notes: [Tuna · Minamisenba, a tuna-only counter from bowls at lunch to omakase at night] A modern Japanese counter three minutes from Nagahoribashi with a whole tuna head in the cold case by the door. It grew out of a members-only tuna club and a borrowed-space lunch counter in Tenjinbashisuji 6-chome that sold out its 30 bowls a day, and moved here in early 2026. Lunch is bowls: negitoro with egg yolk and yam, or the popular half-and-half of marinated lean tuna and creamy negitoro over a deep bowl of rice. Evenings are a ¥9,900 tuna omakase — simmered tuna cheek that falls apart, a tuna burger on brioche, nigiri of lean, kama-toro and marinated chu-toro, then hand rolls — with sake matched to each cut. Diners keep mentioning the owner behind the counter: friendly, funny and full of stories about the fish. One August 2026 diner found the hand rolls too alike.

chef_bio.background: Started as a members-only tuna club, "Maguro Kai" (June 2026 review), then ran lunch in a shared (borrowed) space in Tenjinbashisuji 6-chome, limited to 30 servings, with omakase by referral only; opened its own shop in Minamisenba in early 2026 (February and April 2026 reviews; Tabelog opening date 20 January 2026).
chef_bio.philosophy: Every morning fresh tuna chosen at the market, rare cuts and aged tuna, rice blended to suit the fish, and sake matched to each part (Tabelog, shop-provided).
chef_bio.specialty: Tuna bowls; tuna omakase with rare cuts and hand rolls.

anecdotes.text: "The tuna served is aged from a 260kg catch in Kii Katsura… The simmered tuna cheek came with two large chunks… It was tender enough to fall apart with chopsticks." — April 2026, omakase course ¥9,900.
"The owner, who provides interesting descriptions of the flavors, is very friendly! Oh, and by the way, the owner is really entertaining!" — June 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: まぐろひろし、大阪市中央区南船場2-11-9 チサンマンション心斎橋 104、長堀橋駅から徒歩3分、心斎橋駅から徒歩5分、月〜土・祝11:00〜14:00・17:30〜22:30 (L.O. 22:00)、日曜休み、不定休あり、予約可、カード・電子マネー・PayPay可、10席 (カウンター)、貸切可、禁煙 (外に喫煙所)、子供可 (小学生から)、テイクアウト、英語・中国語・韓国語のメニュー、英語を話すスタッフ、オープン日2026年1月20日。店の紹介: 和モダンの空間でまぐろを丸ごと、毎朝市場で選ぶ鮮魚、希少部位や熟成まぐろ、ネタに合わせたブレンドのシャリ、部位に合わせる日本酒。口コミ(2026年2月〜10月): Tenjinbashisuji 6-chome の間借り営業から南船場に移転、間借りのころは30食限定、おまかせは紹介制だった、会員制の「Maguro Kai」から始まった、昼はB定食ネギトロ丼2050円 (Yamato (Nebaristar) のトッピング100円)、C定食ハーフ&ハーフ (赤身とネギトロ) 1980円、H定食、赤だし、ご飯は250gほど、11時前から行列、夜はおまかせコース9900円 (おばんざい2品、まぐろバーガー、握り3貫、手巻き、デザート)、しらすの山椒オイル500円、まぐろのほほ肉の煮付け800円、目の裏の身の胡麻味噌和え800円、まぐろのにんにく刺し、つみれ、Nachi-Katsuura の260kgのまぐろを1週間熟成、Oma のまぐろ、カナダのまぐろ、Tanaka Rokujugo などの日本酒、楽しくて話のおもしろい店主、手巻きの味が似ていたという声も。

cultural_comfort.note: English menu and English-speaking staff (Tabelog).
