places.neighborhood: Umeda 3-1-3, B2F of Lucua Osaka (ルクア大阪), in the Barchika food floor — 1 min from JR Osaka Stn
places.cuisine: Creative Chinese and Taiwanese dishes with wine (official site; prices tax included, read November 2026, and they vary by shop) · Rantei special sweet-and-sour pork, fried Kagoshima mochi-buta with the sauce poured on afterwards and a heap of green onion, 8 pieces ¥1,870 · Taiwan ramen, the house signature since the first shop, a soup of minced pork cooked with garlic and doubanjiang ¥1,320 (¥1,430 at this shop in October 2026) · large shrimp in mayonnaise sauce ¥1,870 · crab fried rice with lettuce ¥1,650 · black-vinegar sweet-and-sour pork ¥1,650 · three-cold-dish starter of steamed chicken, century egg and jellyfish ¥1,980 · hot-and-sour soup ¥1,100 · almond tofu ¥605 · lunch set meals with rice, pickles, soup and salad, rice and soup refilled free: the sweet-and-sour pork set, the Rantei set of sweet-and-sour pork, Taiwan ramen and fried rice, mapo tofu, Taiwan ramen, mapo noodles (¥1,580, October 2026) · this shop only: black-vinegar braised-pork sweet-and-sour set, a five-starter platter, and an afternoon tea of six Chinese sweets with jasmine, pu-erh or oolong tea ¥1,980 (Tabelog) · courses of 8 dishes ¥4,000, or ¥5,500 with 120 minutes of drinks; a dinner set ¥2,750 (Tabelog)
places.notes: [Chinese · Umeda, creative Chinese under Osaka Station] A branch of Rantei, an Osaka group of seven Chinese restaurants whose first shop is on Tabelog's Top 100 list (Tabelog), opened in April 2026 on the Barchika food floor two levels under Lucua, a minute from the JR gates. The group builds its menu on creative Chinese cooking matched with wine. Most people come for the sweet-and-sour pork, fried Kagoshima pork with the sauce poured on afterwards and buried in green onion, which more than half of lunch customers order (official site), or for the Taiwan ramen, the group's signature since its first shop: thin noodles in a chilli-laden soup of minced pork with garlic and doubanjiang. Lunch sets come with refills of rice and soup, and you can pick the heat and the numbing of the mapo noodles. Diners found the mapo tofu good, the shrimp in mayonnaise bouncy, and one sweet-and-sour pork over-fried (September–October 2026). Only this shop serves an afternoon tea of six Chinese sweets, panda buns among them, with a pot of tea for ¥1,980.

roles: Kitchen of the Rantei group (head cooks and sommeliers unnamed)
chef_bio.background: Per the official site (chinese-bistro-rantei.com, copyright THREE-M; read 2026-11-01): the concept is "creative Chinese × wines of the world", with each shop's head cook and a sommelier testing new dishes together; the special sweet-and-sour pork is made to suit red or white wine, not the usual sharp sweet-and-sour; seasonal ingredients and ingredients rare in Japan, cooked by methods learned at the source. The group lists seven shops in Osaka. Per the shop-maintained Tabelog listing: the main shop is on Tabelog's Top 100 list; this shop opened 23 April 2026. The Tabelog invoice number T4120001023884 is registered to 株式会社スリーエム (NTA invoice register).
chef_bio.philosophy: "A dish to go with wine" (葡萄酒に合う、一皿を; official site).
chef_bio.specialty: Rantei special sweet-and-sour pork; Taiwan ramen; mapo tofu.

anecdotes.text: "The dish was loaded with chili and featured thin Hong Kong-style noodles, topped with minced pork reminiscent of dan dan noodles." — October 2026, Taiwan ramen for JPY 1,430.
"The adorable panda buns are so cute that it feels almost wasteful to eat them." — October 2026, the afternoon tea set.
"I appreciated that I could choose the level of spiciness and numbness to my liking." — October 2026, mapo noodle set meal JPY 1,580.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト: 蘭亭、【創作中華×世界のワイン】がコンセプト、各店の料理長とソムリエが試作を重ねる、蘭亭特製酢豚は赤ワインにも白ワインにも合う、旬の食材、日本では珍しい現地の食材、本場の調理法、QSCH。店舗は谷九本店、本町店、茶屋町店、上一店、南本町店、ルクアバルチカ店、近鉄上本町店。ルクアバルチカ店: 大阪市北区梅田3-1-3 ルクア大阪 バルチカ B2F、全日11:00〜23:00 (L.O.22:30)、不定休、テーブル34席、カウンター14席、限定メニュー (黒酢角煮酢豚定食、前菜5種盛り合わせ、アフタヌーンティーセット)。一品料理 (税込、店舗により異なる): 蘭亭特製酢豚 (8個) 1,870円 (鹿児島産もち豚の唐揚げ、タレは後がけ、青ネギ)、台湾ラーメン1,320円 (創業当初からの看板、豚挽き肉をにんにくと豆板醤で炒めて煮立てたスープ)、前菜3種盛り1,980円、大エビのマヨネーズソース1,870円、レタス入りカニチャーハン1,650円、黒酢酢豚1,650円、酸辣湯1,100円、杏仁豆腐605円。お昼の定食: 白ごはん・お漬物・スープ・サラダつき、ごはんとスープはおかわり自由、特製酢豚定食はダントツの1番人気、蘭亭定食 (酢豚、台湾ラーメン、五目チャーハン)。食べログ (店舗会員): 中華・居酒屋・ラーメン、JR 大阪駅から徒歩1分、本店は食べログ百名店、カード・電子マネー・PayPay 可、48席、禁煙、2026年4月23日オープン、8品のコース4,000円、飲み放題つき5,500円、アフタヌーンティー1,980円。口コミ(2026年9月〜10月): 台湾ラーメン1,430円、細い香港麺、唐辛子たっぷり、鶏皮の揚げ物のお通し、麻婆麺定食1,580円は辛さとしびれを選べる、麻婆豆腐定食、焼いた gyoza と takana の漬物、エビマヨ、特製チャーハン、パンダまんじゅうのアフタヌーンティー。

places.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information. Paella is rice, but the menu also has fideuà made with short pasta, the "Airbag" crispy bread, baguette, cannelloni and cakes; nothing is described as gluten-free.
places.vegan_detail: Ask. Tabelog's feature list ticks "vegetarian options", but no vegetarian or vegan dish is named; the signature paellas are seafood or chicken, and the mushroom salad comes with cheese.
places.hours_raw: Mon–Fri 11:00–15:30 (last order food 14:30, drinks 15:00) and 17:00–23:00 (last order food 22:00, drinks 22:30); Sat, Sun and holidays 11:00–23:00 (Tabelog). places.neighborhood: Umeda 3-2-123, 3F of Innogate Osaka (イノゲート大阪), Barchika 03 — directly connected to the west exit of JR Osaka Stn
places.cuisine: Barcelona seafood restaurant and paella house (official site) · about five paellas plus a daily one (October 2026), cooked 17 minutes over a direct flame (Tabelog): the Escribà paella of shrimp, mussels, clams and white fish, eaten with wooden spoons; squid-ink fideuà of short pasta with aioli; seasonal paella; chicken; small sizes for sharing (October 2026) · tapas: the "Airbag", crispy bread under sliced prosciutto, broken with a hammer at the table; patatas bravas; potatoes with dill sauce; garlic shrimp; meatball stew; shaved raw mushroom salad with cheese · sangria of cava, white or red wine; wines matched to the paellas · desserts: a limited fruit roll cake (fig in October 2026, +¥300 on a course), Basque cheesecake · XIRINGUITO course of seven dishes, lunch or dinner ¥4,800; Mon–Thu dinner courses with two hours of drinks: six dishes ¥7,000, eight dishes ¥8,500 (Tabelog, tax included) · about ¥7,900 a head for the course with drinks (October 2026)
places.notes: [Spanish · Umeda, Barcelona paella at Osaka Station] The Japanese outpost of a Barcelona beach restaurant, opened on the Olympic year of 1992 by Joan Escribà and known locally for the city's best paella, came to Kansai in July 2024 on the third floor of Innogate Osaka, straight off the west exit of the station. A bright, beach-house room of 82 seats serves about five paellas, cooked 17 minutes over a direct flame: the house Escribà paella of shrimp, mussels and clams, with crisp rice at the bottom of the pan, and a squid-ink fideuà made with short pasta, both favourites in 2026 reviews. Start with the "Airbag", crisp bread under prosciutto that you smash with a hammer, and garlic shrimp. The seven-dish XIRINGUITO course is ¥4,800 at lunch or dinner; finish with the fruit roll cake. One October 2026 diner found the portions small. Book ahead: one diner found it full and booked a week out the next time (October 2026).

chef_bio.chef_name: Joan Escribà (ジョアン エスクリバ)
roles: Owner and executive chef of XIRINGUITO Escribà, Barcelona (official site)
chef_bio.background: Per the official site (xiringuitoescriba.jp, read 2026-11-01): XIRINGUITO Escribà opened by the Mediterranean in Barcelona in 1992, the year of the Barcelona Olympics, and has been loved by locals and visitors for over 25 years as the seafood restaurant serving Barcelona's best paella. Joan Escribà also owns the beach club Guingueta Escribà and the modern Spanish restaurant La Picanteria, and is owner-chef and chocolatier of Escribà. The Osaka shop opened 31 July 2024 as the first in Kansai; the site's copyright is TRANSIT GENERAL OFFICE INC.
chef_bio.specialty: Escribà paella; squid-ink fideuà; "Airbag" prosciutto bread.

anecdotes.text: "What stood out was the perfect cooking of the rice and the fragrant crispy bits at the bottom of the pan." — October 2026, seafood paella with mushroom salad, meatball stew and garlic shrimp.
"It was fun to break it apart with a hammer, and the combination of the crispy bread and prosciutto was delicious." — October 2026, of the "Airbag".
"I thought the portion size was quite small; is that typical here?" — October 2026, a lunch meeting.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト: XIRINGUITO Escribà (チリンギート エスクリバ)、バルセロナで一番おいしいパエリアを提供、7月31日に関西初出店、1992年にスペイン・バルセロナにオープン、25年以上地元の人に愛されるシーフードレストラン、オーナー兼エグゼクティブシェフのジョアン エスクリバはバルセロナ生まれ、オリンピックの1992年に地中海沿いに開店、ビーチクラブ Guingueta Escribà とモダンスペイン料理店 La Picanteria のオーナー、エスクリバのオーナーシェフでショコラティエ。メニュー: エスクリバパエリア (エビ、ムール貝、アサリ、白身魚、木のスプーンで)、イカスミのフィデウア (パスタで作るパエリア、アリオリソース)、"エアバッグ" 生ハムスライスとクリスピーブレッド、カヴァ・白ワイン・赤ワインのサングリア。食べログ (店舗会員): スペイン料理・海鮮、大阪市北区梅田3-2-123 イノゲート大阪 バルチカ03エキウエ 3F、大阪駅西口直結、月〜金11:00〜15:30、17:00〜23:00、土・日・祝11:00〜23:00、カード・電子マネー・PayPay 可、82席、禁煙、子ども可、2024年7月31日オープン、直火で17分のパエリア、海の家のような内装、数量限定のフルーツロールケーキ、XIRINGUITO コース7品4,800円、月〜木の2時間飲み放題つきコース6品7,000円・8品8,500円。口コミ(2026年10月): パエリアは約5種と日替わり、イカスミがおすすめ、底のおこげ、キノコのサラダとチーズ、ミートボールの煮込み、ガーリックシュリンプ、エアバッグはハンマーで割る、小さいサイズのパエリア、イチジクのロールケーキ、バスクチーズケーキ、イカスミのショートパスタ、飲み放題つきで1人約7,900円、量が少ないという声も、ベビーカーで来店、ポテトにディルソース。

cultural_comfort.note: The official site and menu are in Japanese and English (read November 2026); dishes are shared tapas and paella.

places.cuisine: Edo-mae sushi, tempura and Japanese courses in the XEX WEST floor (Tabelog) · lunch: tempura set with salad, starters and rice plus a seasonal dessert buffet ¥5,000 (Shine Muscat in autumn 2026; melon in July 2026); seasonal starters and 8 omakase nigiri with a toasting sake ¥4,800 (Tabelog, tax included) · counter sushi à la carte; the squid and the horse mackerel singled out (May 2026) · a September 2026 Japanese course: taro, edamame and pumpkin tofu, sea bream and bonito sashimi, winter melon and sea bream soup, autumn tempura with matsutake, charcoal-grilled wagyu, matsutake rice, just under ¥20,000 with drinks · a tempura course with all-you-can-drink: starters, two sashimi including bonito tataki, hamo soup, soba (August 2026) · monaka with whipped cream and red bean (May 2026) · sake, shochu and wine (Tabelog)
places.notes: [Sushi · Nishi-Umeda, the Japanese room of XEX WEST] The Japanese room of XEX WEST, a floor at the top of Herbis PLAZA ENT that puts an Italian restaurant, a bar and this sushi and tempura counter side by side (Tabelog). At lunch most people book a plan: a tempura set followed by a seasonal fruit dessert buffet, or eight nigiri with seasonal starters; at night it is counter sushi à la carte or a Japanese course with wagyu and matsutake in autumn. Diners in 2026 praised the service more than anything: the chef asks about likes and dislikes, talks with the counter and places each piece on the side of the hand you eat with. The squid and horse mackerel stand out (May 2026). One August 2026 diner was splashed by water from the fish sink and found the apology curt. Dinner adds a ¥580 seat charge and 10% service; dinner is for school-age children and up.

chef_bio.background: Per the shop-maintained Tabelog listing: XEX WEST is "a fusion restaurant" with Italian cuisine, Japanese cuisine and a bar on one floor (The BAR and Salvatore Cuomo Bros. are the sister rooms); An serves Japanese cuisine and Edo-mae sushi from seasonal ingredients and fish from nearby waters. A June 2026 diner calls it "a valuable establishment since the opening of Herbis ENT"; a May 2026 diner had eaten at an XEX location in Tokyo. The Tabelog invoice number T6010401054605 is registered to 株式会社ワイズテーブルコーポレーション, Akasaka, Tokyo (NTA invoice register, read 2026-11-01).
chef_bio.specialty: Edo-mae sushi; tempura set with dessert buffet.

anecdotes.text: "They carefully observe which hand the customer uses and place the sushi in a way that makes it easy to pick up, which is truly impressive." — April 2026.
"I was pleasantly surprised by how tasty the squid was, and before I knew it, I had ordered about five pieces!" — May 2026.
"The chef was very attentive, picking up on my likes and dislikes, and providing wonderful service by engaging in conversation." — September 2026.

places.name: うめだ一丁目スカイビア (Umeda Icchome Sky Beer)
places.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information. BBQ courses of meat, seafood and vegetables grilled at the table with two sauces and salt and pepper (October 2026); sausages, tandoori chicken and a finishing dish are part of the courses, and nothing is described as gluten-free.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: set BBQ courses built on pork, beef, lamb, chicken and seafood, with a vegetable platter as one part.
places.hours_raw: Daily 15:00–22:30 (last order food 21:30, drinks 22:00) (Tabelog). April to December open every day, with a tent for rain; January to March closed Mondays; closed 1–3 January with the building; may close for typhoons or heavy rain (Tabelog). Reservations accepted; around 19:00 in beer-garden season is crowded, so book before 18:45 or after 19:15; 10% off courses starting before 17:00 (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners, UnionPay), IC cards and other e-money, PayPay, Alipay and WeChat Pay (Tabelog). 220 table seats; up to 440 for private hire (220 in winter) (Tabelog; official site); no smoking at the tables, smoking area (Tabelog). Children welcome, kids' menu; menu in English, Chinese and Korean (Tabelog). Access: in Osaka Ekimae Dai-1 Building take the lift on the Nishi-Umeda Station side (right) of the central lift hall to R (13F); the left lifts stop at 12F (Tabelog). Opened 17 June 2025 (Tabelog).
places.neighborhood: Umeda 1-3-1, rooftop (13F) of 大阪駅前第1ビル — 1 min from Nishi-Umeda Stn (Yotsubashi Line), 3 min from Kitashinchi Stn
places.cuisine: Rooftop BBQ and hot-pot beer garden with all-you-can-drink courses (Tabelog, tax included, 10% off before 17:00): Standard BBQ ¥5,800 (three starters, Satsuma Chami pork chuck eye roll, domestic pork belly, homemade tandoori chicken of Bichu Kogen chicken, sausages, two seafood, eight seasonal vegetables, a finishing dish); Deluxe ¥7,300 (adds thick beef tongue, Saroma wagyu sirloin, shrimp, squid and scallops); Premium ¥10,000 (Japanese Black wagyu strip loin, Saroma wagyu round, four wagyu compared, dessert) · a lamb course ¥5,800 (September 2026) · beef motsunabe in December 2025 · drinks: eight draft beers from four brewers, among them Asahi Super Dry, Sapporo Black Label, Kirin Ichiban Shibori, Yebisu, Premium Malt's and Heartland (October 2026), self-poured from a button tap; 20-plus highballs on a choice of whiskies; 47 prefectural shochu from November to March
places.notes: [BBQ beer garden · Umeda, on the roof of the station buildings] A beer garden on the roof of Osaka Ekimae Dai-1 Building, opened in June 2025 and built as a Showa-retro street of stalls: lanterns light up at dusk, the official site likens the mood to Taiwan's Jiufen, and an Inari shrine sits on the roof. Under an all-weather tent, groups grill set courses of pork, wagyu, lamb, seafood and vegetables on gas grills, with two hours of all-you-can-drink from eight draft beers you pour yourself at the push of a button, highballs made on the whisky you pick, and in winter 47 shochu from every prefecture. Diners liked the drinks and the city view at dusk; several found the meat portions on the cheaper courses small (September and October 2026), and on a rainy night one corner got wet. Courses run ¥5,800–10,000, 10% off before 17:00. Take the right-hand lifts to the roof.

chef_bio.background: Per the official site (umedaskybeer.com, read 2026-11-01): a Showa-retro rooftop of stalls on 大阪駅前第1ビル, lanterns at dusk "like Taiwan's Jiufen", a 正一位稲荷神社 shrine on the roof, private hire up to 440 seats (220 in winter), eight draft beers from the four big brewers, 20-plus highballs and, from November to March, shochu from all 47 prefectures. The Tabelog invoice number T4120001274503 is registered to ジョナサン・フーズ株式会社 at 梅田1-3-1 (NTA invoice register). Opened 17 June 2025 (Tabelog).
chef_bio.specialty: BBQ courses with all-you-can-drink draft beer.

anecdotes.text: "When refilling, you return the empty glass to a tray and pour a new one yourself. Although it was self-service, the beer poured automatically with the push of a button." — September 2026, the lamb course for JPY 5,800.
"Since it was also a birthday celebration, I opted for the Matsu Premium Course." The staff explained each kind of meat at the table. — September 2026, 3 pm in Silver Week.
"Enjoying drinks while gazing at the beautiful city was a blissful experience, but I think it could be improved by lowering the price by another JPY 1,000." — October 2026, the standard course.

places.cuisine: Seafood izakaya run directly by a central-market wholesaler, with fish delivered every morning (Tabelog) · lunch bowls with a fish-broth miso soup: seafood yukke bowl ¥900 (August and October 2026), Okapi's tuna bowl ¥900 (July 2026, limited), seafood bowl ¥1,000 with salmon, ikura and shirasu, miso soup, salad and pickles (July–October 2026) · evenings: sashimi platters (three kinds: salmon, sea bream, yellowtail; five kinds with seared pieces), large creamy oysters, horse-mackerel namerou, hamo and anago tempura, shirayaki eel (August–September 2026), grilled sanma and a seafood potato salad (September 2026), seared bonito (October 2026) · seasonal fish from across Japan, e.g. grilled turban shell from Mie and raw Hokkaido oysters (Tabelog) · shochu such as "Ikino Tsuyu" and "Tokuchu Amakusa", sake, Asahi Maru F draft beer
places.notes: [Seafood izakaya · Umeda, Osaka Station Building No. 4 B2F] A small seafood bar in the basement of Osaka Station Building No. 4, a minute from Higashi-Umeda, run directly by a fish wholesaler from the central market, with fish delivered each morning. At lunch it sells seafood bowls for ¥900–1,000 with a fish-broth miso soup that diners single out; one regular on a ninth visit still calls the price remarkable (October 2026), and the limited tuna bowl goes early. From mid-afternoon at weekends and in the evening it is a drinking spot: thick-cut sashimi platters, palm-sized oysters, namerou, hamo and anago tempura and grilled eel, with shochu and a Maru F draft. Twelve counter seats suit solo diners; smoking is allowed. One August 2026 diner found the food slow to come, and one September 2026 diner found the seats cramped and the service cool.

Reservations accepted; give a phone number that answers or an online booking is cancelled (Tabelog). Lunch is cash only (Tabelog; October 2026); cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners) at dinner; no e-money or QR (Tabelog). One drink per person; no bringing your own alcohol; children order a course too (Tabelog). 15 seats, about seven at the counter plus tables (September 2026); groups of 12–15 or private hire up to 20; non-smoking (Tabelog). Opened 14 April 2014 (Tabelog).

places.cuisine: Tempura counter: seasonal vegetables chosen with a vegetable sommelier, some of them rare, two frying oils, live shrimp from a tank fried two ways, and a rice blend chosen by a rice master for the tendon, tencha and tempura rolls (Tabelog) · dinner courses (Tabelog, tax included): 13 tempura in 18 dishes ¥8,800; 14 tempura ¥11,000; 15 tempura with abalone ¥14,300 · lunch: custom tendon ¥1,200 (choose four from shrimp, hamo, kisu, squid and four vegetables; miso soup, pickles, iced coffee or tea; September 2026); premium tendon with two shrimp and abalone ¥3,500 (October 2026); a 9-item tempura course with sesame tofu and ikura, salad and sparkling wine, ending in a kakiage rice bowl and an orange served in its peel (October 2026); the abalone course at lunch (August 2026) · pieces named in 2026 reviews: shrimp, kisu, hamo, anago, sea bass, sawara or amadai with caviar, fugu shirako, abalone, Beni Haruka and Anno sweet potato, fig, lotus root, makomotake, maitake · finish with a tempura rice bowl or tempura chazuke · sake to match
places.notes: [Tempura · Kitashinchi, a seventh-floor counter] A tempura counter on the seventh floor of a building at the west entrance of Kitashinchi's main street, near the Sakurabashi crossing. The shop chooses seasonal vegetables with a vegetable sommelier, fries in two oils, and keeps shrimp alive in a tank; the chef dusts each piece with a brush. Courses run ¥8,800–14,300 at dinner, through shrimp, kisu, hamo and abalone to sweet potato and figs, and end with a tempura rice bowl or tempura chazuke whose dashi a third-time diner calls exquisite (October 2026). Lunch is the bargain: a ¥1,200 tendon built from eight pieces you choose, or an abalone tendon for ¥3,500, cash only. With a small kitchen team, food can take a while; allow time. One September 2026 diner noticed a cloth smell on the rice bowl. Staff walked one diner to the lift (October 2026).

roles: Chef (unnamed), who fries at the counter
Owner (unnamed; "friendly and easy to talk to", September 2026 review)
chef_bio.background: Shop text (Tabelog): seasonal ingredients and carefully selected tempura; seasonal vegetables sourced in consultation with a vegetable sommelier, including rare ones; two frying oils; live shrimp; a rice blend chosen by a rice master for tendon, tencha and tempura rolls. Opened 14 April 2014. In 2026 reviews: the chef "seemed very sincere" and the owner "friendly and easy to talk to" (September); "a skilled team of two chefs and one part-timer" (October); a September diner describes it as a one-person operation at the fryer.
chef_bio.philosophy: Seasonal ingredients fried to bring out their own flavour (Tabelog).
chef_bio.specialty: Seasonal tempura course; custom tendon at lunch.

anecdotes.text: "The dashi for the tempura rice at the end was exquisite, making the meal enjoyable until the very last bite." — October 2026, a third visit.

"You can customize your tempura rice bowl with 4 items from a selection of shrimp, conger eel, whiting, and squid. Choose 4 more items from onions, lotus root, broccoli, maitake mushrooms, sweet potatoes, pumpkin, and eggplant." — September 2026, the ¥1,200 lunch.
"The chef skillfully dusts the tempura with flour using a brush." — October 2026, the ¥3,500 premium tendon.

cultural_comfort.note: Set tempura courses at the counter; lunch is cash only (2026). No English evidence found.

places.name: 北新地 鮨 なか川 (Kitashinchi Sushi Nakagawa)
places.gf_detail: Ask when booking. No gluten information. One set course of seasonal vegetables, sashimi, a grilled dish (sawara saikyo-yaki in November 2025), 7–8 nigiri and red miso soup; sushi and sashimi are usually served with soy sauce, which normally contains wheat.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: one set course of seafood and sushi, with a shrimp-flavoured red miso soup.
places.hours_raw: Mon–Sat 18:00–23:00, last order 21:00; may close early when ingredients run out, so phone ahead (Tabelog). Sundays and holidays: private bookings only, for four or more, booked a day ahead (Tabelog). One course only, ¥22,000 tax included, plus a service fee; seat reservations for guests 10 and over (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners); no e-money or QR (Tabelog). 14 seats: 8 at the counter and a table for 6; private rooms for 4 and 6; private hire up to 20; non-smoking; takeout; catering from ¥18,000 a person for 8 or more (Tabelog). Opened 14 July 2014 (Tabelog).
places.neighborhood: Kitashinchi, GOTS北新地ビル一号館 3F — 3 min from JR Kitashinchi Stn
places.cuisine: One kaiseki-style course, ¥22,000 tax included: seasonal vegetable appetizer, sashimi in the shop's own presentation, a grilled speciality, 7–8 pieces of Edomae sushi, a red miso soup made to bring out shrimp (Tabelog) · fish from ports across Japan; rice from Yae Hara, Nagano, "Sun and Earth Rice" with no added sugar; tableware chosen with care (Tabelog) · a November 2025 course: persimmon shiraae, sawara, kue, young kanpachi, aji, sawara saikyo-yaki, ishidai, aori squid, marinated tuna, tachiuo, akagai, shirako, a bowl of raw sakura shrimp and sea urchin, red miso soup, toro · charcoal-grilled fish skin, sweet shrimp (April 2026); toro-taku, anago (January 2026) · Daishinshu sake, a favourite of the chef (January and April 2026); the chef visits sake breweries and wine producers to build pairings (Tabelog) · about ¥20,000–26,000 a person with drinks (August and September 2026)
places.notes: [Sushi · Kitashinchi, a sake-loving sushi counter] An eight-seat sushi counter with private rooms, three floors up in Kitashinchi, serving one course of fish from ports across Japan: seasonal vegetables, thick-cut sashimi, a grilled dish, Edomae nigiri and a shrimp-rich red miso soup, on rice from Yae Hara in Nagano seasoned without sugar. Diners remember the sashimi above all, and a November 2025 course ended with a bowl of raw sakura shrimp and sea urchin. The chef seeks out sake breweries and wine makers for pairings and is fond of Daishinshu sake. Diners describe a warm, entertaining chef, who per an August 2026 diner has ties to surfers and joins beach clean-ups; tell the staff your budget and dishes and drinks are suggested to fit it (January 2025). The course is ¥22,000; with drinks expect ¥20,000–26,000. Book ahead: a September 2026 weekday was full. Private rooms suit business dinners.

chef_bio.background: Shop text (Tabelog): seafood from ports across Japan; the chef personally visits sake breweries and wine producers to make pairings and pursues harmony with the rice; tableware that reflects the spirit of Nakagawa; events, private parties and catering. Opened 14 July 2014. Reviews: the chef is warm and entertaining (November 2025, September 2026); "may not have the typical sushi chef appearance, but … has connections with surfers and participates in beach clean-up activities" (August 2026); holds Daishinshu sake dear (April 2026).
chef_bio.philosophy: The deliciousness of Japan's seafood, in harmony with rice, sake and tableware (Tabelog).
chef_bio.specialty: Sashimi; sake pairing; raw sakura shrimp and sea urchin bowl.

anecdotes.text: "As soon as we entered, the enticing aroma of delicious food lifted our spirits. (I later realized it was the smell of the skin being grilled over charcoal.)" — April 2026, a birthday dinner.
"The raw sakura ebi and uni rice bowl was the highlight of the day!" — November 2025, a first visit.
"Just share your budget, and the staff will recommend dishes and drinks accordingly." — January 2025, a business dinner.

cultural_comfort.note: One set course, with drinks suggested by the chef; book ahead (2025–2026). No English evidence found.

places.name: Sushi Tiger OSAKA
places.gf_detail: Ask when booking: the shop asks for allergies in advance and may not manage requests on the day (Tabelog). No gluten information; courses include anago tempura sushi and sauces from around the world, and cha soba (buckwheat-tea noodles, usually with wheat) at lunch (October 2026).
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: sushi courses of fish, shellfish, wagyu and egg.
places.hours_raw: Lunch 11:30–14:30 (last order 14:00) every day except Friday; dinner 18:00–22:30 (last order 22:00) every day, in two seatings starting at 18:00 or 20:30 (Tabelog). Opened 21 September 2026 (Tabelog shop text, "Opening on 9/21"; an October 2026 review says it opened the month before); the Tabelog opening-date field reads 19 January 2024. Tell the shop about dislikes and allergies in advance (Tabelog). No cover charge; cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners); no e-money or QR (Tabelog). 20 seats: 10 at the counter and private rooms for 4 and 6 (groups of 3 or 4 and more, courses from ¥5,500); non-smoking (Tabelog).
places.neighborhood: Kitashinchi, キチリンビル 1F — 3 min from JR Kitashinchi Stn, 4 min from Nishi-Umeda Stn
places.cuisine: Modern sushi from Vietnam: Edomae technique (preparation, rice, hand-shaping) with ingredients, methods and sauces from around the world (Tabelog) · dinner omakase until 6 December 2026: 8 pieces with seasonal appetizers ¥4,950; 10 pieces with chutoro cheese and anago tempura sushi ¥6,050; 12 pieces with black wagyu and oyster ¥7,150 (tax included); a sake pairing with all-you-can-drink from 20+ kinds for ¥3,300 more (Tabelog) · lunch course ¥5,000, rice bowls from ¥1,000 (Tabelog); a Sushi Gozen of 9 kinds (October 2026); seafood yukke bowl with tuna, salmon and yellowtail under a quail yolk ¥1,000, cha soba ¥330 (October 2026) · an October 2026 course: sea bream, amberjack, marinated red fish, chawanmushi, squid, young horse mackerel, hot-spring yuba, sardine, bluefin chutoro, black wagyu, anago tempura, sea urchin and ikura, oyster · bluefin tuna with truffle cheese (October 2026) · red-vinegar rice mixed live at the counter (October 2026)
places.notes: [Sushi · Kitashinchi, a Vietnamese sushi brand comes to Japan] The first Japanese branch of Sushi Tiger, a sushi brand from Vietnam, opened in Kitashinchi on 21 September 2026. It keeps Edomae technique and red-vinegar rice, mixed live at the counter, but tops the nigiri with ideas from abroad: chutoro with truffle cheese, black wagyu, oyster, anago tempura. Dinner courses run ¥4,950–7,150 for 8–12 pieces, with sushi-bar showmanship; a ¥3,300 add-on brings a sake pairing and free-flowing drinks. Lunch brings a ¥1,000 seafood yukke bowl or a sushi set. In its first month the room was mostly overseas guests, with staff interpreting (October 2026). Most diners loved the fun; a traditionalist missed plain fish with soy sauce, and another was not keen on the rice. No lunch on Fridays.

roles: Sushi chefs (unnamed in the sources read)
chef_bio.origin: Sushi Tiger began in Vietnam; this is its first shop in Japan (Tabelog). Viet Nam News (26 July 2026) reports the brand built its name in Ho Chi Minh City before opening in Hanoi.
chef_bio.background: Shop text (Tabelog): "Sushi Tiger," a beloved sushi brand from Vietnam, values Edo-style techniques of preparation, rice and hand-shaping while combining ingredients, cooking methods, materials and sauces from around the world, to "reconstruct the deliciousness of the world into modern sushi that breaks the mold". An October 2026 diner calls it a concept planned overseas and brought back to Japan.
chef_bio.philosophy: Preserve Edomae tradition while rebuilding sushi with flavours from around the world (Tabelog).
chef_bio.specialty: Creative nigiri courses; chutoro with truffle cheese.

anecdotes.text: "The live sushi rice cutting right in front of me, along with the chef's bold yet delicate performance, kept my senses engaged" — October 2026.
"Most of the customers were from overseas, but the staff provided attentive service while acting as interpreters." — October 2026, after bluefin tuna with truffle cheese.
"Instead of just eating normally, it feels like you're constantly being thrown curveballs or sliders, haha." — October 2026.

cultural_comfort.note: Mostly overseas guests in October 2026, with staff interpreting; set courses booked ahead. No English menu listed.

staff_allergy_handling.text: Tabelog: "Please inform us in advance about any dislikes or allergy information. We may not be able to accommodate requests on the day of your visit."

places.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information. Yakitori come from the charcoal grill, and the rice bowls are topped with a sweet-savoury yakitori sauce (June and September 2026); marinated kara-age, chicken katsu and pasta are on the menu. Nothing is described as gluten-free.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a chicken grill; the house tofu and salads come alongside chicken, and the course ends with chicken-broth chazuke.
places.hours_raw: Mon–Fri 11:30–13:30 and 17:30–23:00 (last orders: food 22:15, drinks 22:30); Sat 17:30–22:30 (last orders: food 21:45, drinks 22:00); closed Sun and holidays (Tabelog). Reservations accepted; the private room can be used by groups of three or more (Tabelog). Appetiser charge ¥500 a head (Tabelog's original text: お通し代としておひとり様あたり５００円（税込）). places.cuisine: Charcoal-grilled yakitori of chicken from Fukuchiyama, ground fresh each morning, with marinated kara-age, chicken tataki and house tofu made from soy milk; pasta to finish (Tabelog) · "Horo-yoi Set" of a starter, five omakase skewers and a drink ¥1,490 (Tabelog, tax included; ¥1,200 in December 2025 and March 2026, ¥1,300 in January 2026) · "Furafura" course of eight dishes with a drink ¥2,980 (Tabelog; ¥2,490 in February 2026, ¥2,980 in September 2026): starter, three omakase skewers, salad, homemade zaru tofu, marinated kara-age, grilled chicken thigh with tomato, chicken-broth chazuke (February 2026) · skewers named in reviews: liver, segimo, gizzard, cartilage, heart, seseri, skin, an overfilled negima, tsukune, tender breast (2025–2026) · lunch: yakitori rice bowl with an onsen egg ¥600 (December 2025), ¥700 (June 2026); chicken steak gozen on a hot iron plate ¥850 (December 2025, May 2026), with a free rice refill (December 2025); kara-age rice bowl ¥800 (September 2026); chicken katsu gozen ¥990, the same as the kara-age gozen (July 2026) · sake from around Japan poured into masu, and shochu (Tabelog)
places.notes: [Yakitori · Nishinakajima, a charcoal counter since 2003] A small yakitori izakaya a few minutes from Nishinakajima-Minamigata Station, open since 2003, with a ten-seat counter and a tatami room at the back. The shop says its chef cooks with skills from the hotel trade, and one diner heard the chef was once an Italian cook (March 2026), which may explain the mustard and mayonnaise on the skewer plate. The chicken comes from Fukuchiyama, ground the same morning. The usual order is the "Horo-yoi Set" (two diners order it every visit): a starter that changes daily (cold shabu with ume dressing in March 2026, a mochi gratin in January), five omakase skewers and a drink for about ¥1,200–1,500, with a negima so packed there is no place left to hold the skewer. The homemade tofu is a specialty. At lunch, charcoal smoke out front draws office workers in for a yakitori rice bowl (¥700 in June 2026) or a chicken steak set (¥850), and the counter fills by noon. Smoking is allowed. Closed Sundays.

roles: Chef (unnamed) with one or two floor staff
chef_bio.background: Per the Tabelog listing: "Utilizing skills honed in the hotel industry, our chef personally prepares a variety of dishes with great care"; the chicken comes from Fukuchiyama and the tofu is handmade from soy milk; pasta was added at customers' request. A March 2026 diner heard the chef "used to be an Italian chef". December 2025: the owner and one young staff member ran lunch; March 2026: the chef and two staff. Opened 1 September 2003 (Tabelog).
chef_bio.specialty: Horo-yoi Set (starter, five skewers and a drink); marinated kara-age; homemade tofu; yakitori rice bowl at lunch.

anecdotes.text: "The skewers are packed from tip to tail, leaving almost no place to hold them!" — March 2026, on the negima.
"That's when I noticed some suspicious smoke… could it be? Yakitori grilled over charcoal during lunch? I was drawn in like a magnet." — December 2025, a ¥600 yakitori rice bowl.
"What really impressed me was the homemade tofu. I knew it was a specialty, but this was my first time ordering it." — June 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: こだわり炭火焼鳥 ふらふら、焼鳥・居酒屋、大阪市淀川区西中島4-5-22 第３新大阪ビル 1F、Midosuji 線 西中島南方駅1番出口から徒歩3分、阪急京都線 南方駅から徒歩4分、月〜金11:30〜13:30、17:30〜23:00、土17:30〜22:30、日・祝休み、予約可、お通し代500円、カードと PayPay 可、電子マネー不可、18席 (カウンター10、座敷8)、貸切20名まで、喫煙可、英語・中国語・韓国語のメニュー、2003年9月1日オープン。店の紹介: ホテルで磨いた腕で料理長がていねいに作る、Fukuchiyama の朝びきの鶏の焼鳥、漬け込みの kara-age、鶏のタタキ、豆乳から作る手作り豆腐、締めのパスタ、日本酒を升で。セット: 「Horo-yoi Set」お通し、おまかせ串5本、ドリンク1杯1,490円、8品の「ふらふら」コース2,980円。口コミ(2025年12月〜2026年9月): Horo-yoi Set は1,200〜1,300円、日替わりのお通し、ねぎまは串いっぱい、レバー、せぎも、砂ずり、ハツ、せせり、皮、つくね、むね、昼は焼鳥丼600〜700円、チキンステーキ御膳850円、kara-age 丼800円、チキンカツ御膳990円、昼すぎにはカウンターがほぼ満席、手作り豆腐が名物、料理長はもとイタリアンの料理人と聞いたという声。

cultural_comfort.note: Tabelog lists a menu in English, Chinese and Korean with photos; no evidence of English-speaking staff. Lunch is a short menu of sets.

places.name: ゑにしな (Enishina)
places.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information. Chicken cuts are grilled with salt or with the homemade miso sauce (miso sauces often contain wheat or barley); fried chicken wings and cold noodles are on the course.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a chicken grill. Vegetables such as shiitake, white leek, onion and cabbage are side orders to chicken, and nothing is described as vegan.
places.hours_raw: Mon, Tue, Thu, Sun and holidays 17:00–01:00; Fri, Sat and the day before a holiday 17:00–03:00; closed Wednesday; other closing days not fixed (Tabelog). Reservations accepted (Tabelog). Cover charge ¥290 (Tabelog's original text: チャージ料290円（税込）). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners), e-money and QR payments (Tabelog). 16 seats: 8 at the counter (up to 10) and terrace seats; whole-shop hire up to 20; smoking allowed (Tabelog), at your seat too (July 2026); English menu (Tabelog). Opened in September 2021 as a counter yakiniku restaurant (a November 2021 review) and later turned to chicken (2024–2025 reviews).
places.neighborhood: 西中島3-21-18, ground floor — 2 min from Nishinakajima-Minamigata Stn (Midosuji Line), 5 min from Hankyu Minamikata Stn (Tabelog); just east of the Shin-Mido expressway, on the south side of the street next to a red pachinko parlour (March 2026)
places.cuisine: Chicken yakiniku grilled at the counter, with salt or a homemade miso sauce modelled on the chicken-and-miso grill of Matsusaka in Mie (Tabelog; August 2024) · all-you-can-drink course with draft beer: grilled-chicken platter, chicken sashimi, fried chicken wings, cold noodles and dessert ¥3,780 (Tabelog, tax included; ¥3,480 in August 2024, ¥3,980 in March 2025); in July 2026 the course was chicken tataki, five kinds of grilled chicken, wings and cold noodles · every cut ¥550 (March 2026), portions large · cuts named in reviews: young chicken, old hen, thigh, sasami, heart, liver, gizzard, bonjiri, yagen cartilage, harami, seseri, chicken belly (2024–2026) · sausages, shiitake, white leek, onion, kimchi, unlimited cabbage for the miso sauce (2024–2026) · Korean-style cold noodles or seaweed soup to finish, sorbet (2024–2026) · PSB on draft (March 2026); Akaboshi beer (July 2025)
places.notes: [Chicken yakiniku · Nishinakajima, a late-night counter] An eight-seat counter in a drinking street near Nishinakajima-Minamigata, with Showa-retro tiles and a few terrace seats, where you grill chicken yourself and dip it in a homemade miso sauce worked out from the chicken-and-miso grills of Matsusaka in Mie (Tabelog; August 2024). It opened in September 2021 as a counter beef yakiniku (November 2021) and had turned to chicken by July 2024. Order cuts at ¥550 each (March 2026), from tender young chicken to chewy old hen, a whole heart and a liver seared rare; the portions are big. The all-you-can-drink course, with chicken sashimi, a grilled platter, wings and cold noodles, is ¥3,780 on Tabelog. Open till 1 am, and till 3 am on Friday and Saturday; one diner came in at midnight for a solo grill and seaweed soup (June 2026). One diner found the owner a little curt at first (March 2025); another found owner and staff very friendly (June 2026). Smoking is allowed. Closed Wednesday.

chef_bio.background: Per the Tabelog listing: a chicken grill in a "nostalgic Showa retro atmosphere" with eight counter seats, recommending its homemade miso sauce "inspired by the famous chicken miso grill from Mie Prefecture". A November 2021 diner described it as the counter yakiniku "Enishina", opened in September 2021 on the former site of the counter sukiyaki restaurant "Mitsumaru", lunch only at first and dinner from October 2021. An August 2024 diner wrote that the miso sauce "was crafted by researching flavors from a Matsusaka restaurant" and that the shop had shifted from a yakiniku format; a March 2025 diner, that it "used to be a beef-centric yakiniku restaurant".
chef_bio.specialty: Chicken yakiniku with homemade miso sauce; all-you-can-drink chicken course.

anecdotes.text: "The miso sauce was so good that I couldn't resist dipping the unlimited cabbage into it, making my drinks keep flowing." — August 2024.
"I stumbled into a chicken yakiniku restaurant, drawn in by the shimmering red lanterns at midnight." — June 2026, a solo late-night grill finished with seaweed soup.
"I tried to order everything listed on the menu, but was advised that the portions are quite generous." — March 2026.

places.notes: [Yakitori · Higashimikuni, a charcoal grill behind glass] A roomy yakitori restaurant near Higashimikuni Station, seven minutes' walk from JR Shin-Osaka, opened in June 2023, with counter seats facing a charcoal grill behind glass, sofas and a tatami room, so it works for families as well as after-work drinks. The shop grills fresh domestic chicken with a homemade sweet-savoury sauce, and the tsukune is the house favourite: fluffy and as big as a rice ball, with a truffle version too. Chicken sashimi comes as a five-kind platter with sweet Kyushu soy sauce. Diners praise the sake list and draft Sapporo Black Label, and one regular keeps the bill under ¥4,000 a head even after eating and drinking a lot (October 2026). Weekday lunch is back since March 2026 with ¥1,000 rice bowls, but one person was running it alone in March and May 2026, and a May 2026 diner waited 39 minutes; go early if you are short of time.

chef_bio.background: Per the Tabelog listing: "Our restaurant carefully grills selected ingredients over charcoal. We use freshly sourced domestic chicken", with a homemade sweet and savoury sauce and fresh sashimi; counter and sofa seats "for family meals or important business meetings". Opened 30 June 2023 (Tabelog). A March 2026 lunch was "a complete one-person operation", served in 18 minutes; in May 2026 the staff was again working solo and gave a free kara-age for the wait.
chef_bio.specialty: Tsukune; five-kind chicken sashimi platter; charcoal yakitori.

places.notes: [Yakitori · Nishinakajima, a binchotan counter among offices] A 20-seat yakitori shop behind wooden doors in the office blocks between Shin-Osaka and Nishinakajima-Minamigata, open since about 2018 and full most weeknights, often with office parties. The chicken is Daisen jidori over Kishu binchotan, with jazz playing because the owner thought it "fits the ambiance" (September 2026). Skewers come one at a time, in order: sasami with wasabi or plum, neck, heart, gizzard, thigh, tsukune, about ¥260–290 each (2026). Around them, more than a yakitori shop needs: chicken sashimi and namero, a fish of the day, broccoli and maitake tempura, sasami cheese nanban, and a kamameshi cooked in chicken soup to finish (it takes 20 minutes, so order it first). A weekday visit means booking ahead; a Saturday is calmer. Every seat is smoking.

places.notes: [Chinese · Nishinakajima, a local Chinese canteen] A 48-seat Chinese restaurant on a side street between Shin-Osaka and Nishinakajima-Minamigata, open since 2019, with an eye-catching front and a staff from China, quick and friendly (2025). At lunch it fills up for set meals around ¥800, a mapo hot pot set or shark-fin-sauce fried rice, with fried rice or a mini ramen for ¥100 more; dishes come in about four minutes (March 2025). In the evening it turns into a banquet hall: a two-hour all-you-can-order buffet of 50 dishes with drinks for ¥3,800, booked out on Fridays (October 2026), or small plates like Cantonese steamed chicken (¥450) and Peking duck (¥1,980). Flavours run mild to fiery; one diner found the spicy beef stir-fry hot even for a chilli lover (September 2026). Smoking is allowed at the tables; one diner who dislikes smoke booked 17:30 on a Sunday (October 2026).

places.notes: [Mexican · Nishinakajima, a late-night taco and tequila bar] A second-floor bar off Shin-Midosuji, north of Nishinakajima-Minamigata, serving tacos and Mexican spirits since 2011; the owner is a certified Tequila Maestro and Mezcalero who explains the bottles well, and the back bar holds over 600 Mexican spirits (Tabelog; July 2026). An August 2025 diner wrote that it is known as the best tequila bar in western Japan. The food holds its own: "premium tacos" on a fried, slightly sweet tortilla, a taco set on yellow or blue masa, mozzarella quesadillas and taco rice, in portions people call large (March 2026), with mild spice you adjust with hot sauce. It stays open until 5 a.m. on weekdays, so it doubles as a last stop, and runs a weekday lunch Tuesday to Thursday. English menu; ¥500 table charge; smoking allowed.

places.cuisine: Hotel Italian, with lunch buffets and afternoon tea (Tabelog) · half-buffet lunch: a main of your choice with all-you-can-eat vegetables and pizza and a drink bar ¥2,000 (Tabelog); mains in 2026 included pasta, a weekly special, pork and beef sirloin (June) and homemade sausage and burdock tagliatelle in cream sauce or salmon, mushroom and shiso spaghetti (October); the buffet: a salad bar of many leaves and roots with homemade dressings, potato dauphinoise, garlic mushrooms, chili con carne with soy meat, two soups, bagels, croissants, cinnamon rolls, focaccia (October 2026) · autumn afternoon teas ¥5,500 with free-flow coffee and tea: grape (muscat and Kyoho parfait, mousse, tart, prosciutto pinchos, quiche, scones) and chestnut, 18 October–30 November (Mont Blanc, pear, apple, pumpkin quiche, bruschetta); the signature is a "melty tiramisu" that spreads when the tube is lifted (October 2026) · cake set from the showcase with baked goods, ice cream and a drink ¥1,300 (October 2026) · dinner: "Hearty Italian Course" with two hours of drinks ¥6,000: prosciutto with buffalo mozzarella, bagna cauda, fresh pasta with shrimp cream, T-bone steak, cake (August 2026) · Christmas buffets 21–26 December 2026: lunch with desserts ¥3,000, dinner with roast beef and sweets ¥5,500 (Tabelog, tax included) · baked goods to take away (Tabelog)
places.notes: [Italian · Shin-Osaka, a hotel restaurant with afternoon tea] The ground-floor restaurant of the Holiday Inn & Suites Shin-Osaka, opened in December 2025 in a bright, high-ceilinged room ten minutes' walk from the station, with a free shuttle bus. Three things draw people: a ¥2,000 half-buffet lunch, a main pasta or meat with a big salad bar, pizza and breads (featured on a TV show in October 2026); seasonal afternoon teas at ¥5,500, grape then chestnut in autumn 2026, built around a "melty tiramisu" and made from scratch in the hotel kitchen, with sweetness kept low; and a ¥1,300 cake set from the showcase. Dinner is Italian courses with free-flow drinks and a T-bone steak. Most diners loved it; one family found an empty room, small portions and a single server at dinner (October 2026). English menu and English-speaking staff.

roles: Hotel kitchen: a chef (a woman, per an October 2026 review) and a pastry chef (unnamed)
chef_bio.background: Per the Tabelog listing: the Italian restaurant of the Holiday Inn & Suites Shin-Osaka, opened 22 December 2025, serving a vegetable lunch buffet, seasonal afternoon tea, cakes and baked goods to take away, and Italian dinners. Per reviews: "Everything is homemade in the hotel kitchen" with no preservatives (October 2026); "the female chef makes everything from scratch without relying on pre-made products", and the sweetness is kept in check so the whole tea can be finished (October 2026); cakes "made by the hotel's pastry chef" (August 2026); the lunch was featured by the food blogger M Saburo on a TV show (October 2026).
chef_bio.specialty: Half-buffet lunch; seasonal afternoon tea with melty tiramisu.

anecdotes.text: "When the tube is removed, the cream spreads beautifully, allowing you to enjoy the rich chestnut flavor." — October 2026, the chestnut afternoon tea.
"The female chef makes everything from scratch without relying on pre-made products." — October 2026, the grape afternoon tea.
"The staff member was managing the floor alone and seemed overwhelmed, but [was] very pleasant." — October 2026, a family steak dinner.

places.cuisine: Omakase sushi: omakase ¥10,000 and ¥15,000; lunch Tuesday–Saturday ¥5,000 with 10 nigiri, two seasonal dishes and dessert (Tabelog, tax included); dinner from ¥8,000 (July 2026 review) · July 2026 ¥10,000 course: chilled chawanmushi with corn and aosa, tuna from Shiogama (Miyagi), simmered summer vegetables, sawara grilled with tamamiso, then sea bream, kisu, squid with sea urchin, marinated tuna, simmered clam, eel roll, sweet shrimp, kinmedai, chutoro, simmered anago and a toro-taku hand roll, with hojicha ice cream · September 2026: charcoal-grilled eel, raw and grilled sanma, simmered octopus with matsutake, akagai with liver sauce, sweet-shrimp mixed rice, aosa red miso soup · red-vinegar rice, small and firm (July 2026) · desserts made by the chef (September 2026) · medium bottles of beer, sake (choose your own cup), wine, cocktails
places.notes: [Sushi · Kitashinchi, a ten-seat omakase] A small sushi bar up the stairs of an unassuming Kitashinchi building, with six counter seats and a private room for four, run by the group behind the 心屋 seafood restaurants. The draw is price: a ¥10,000 omakase in Kitashinchi that diners call remarkable value, mixing seasonal side dishes (a chilled corn chawanmushi in July, raw and grilled sanma in September) with about a dozen nigiri on firm red-vinegar rice, from squid with sea urchin to a toro-taku hand roll, and the chef's own hojicha ice cream. A ¥5,000 lunch with ten nigiri runs Tuesday to Saturday by reservation. A July 2026 diner found the staff young and friendly, September diners a warm chef; one noted in September 2026 that the chef had changed to a younger one. Extra orders are limited to what the course used (July 2026).

roles: Sushi chef (unnamed; changed by September 2026, per a review)

chef_bio.background: Shop text (Tabelog): skilled chefs, the finest ingredients and carefully prepared rice; a counter to watch the chef and private rooms. Opened 3 March 2025. The sushi chef is also young but very skilled" (July 2026); "The chef who specializes in aged sushi had changed, and now there's a younger chef" (September 2026); "the chef's warm personality" (September 2026); desserts "handmade by the chef" (September 2026), though a July 2026 diner was served "a pre-packaged item".
chef_bio.philosophy: Seasonal ingredients and carefully prepared rice (Tabelog).

"While you can place additional orders after finishing the course, the options are limited to what was served in the course" — July 2026.

places.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information. The signature dishes are sandwiches (mackerel, and a wagyu katsu sandwich with demi-glace); Inaniwa udon appears in autumn (October 2025); grilled fish and sashimi are usually served with soy-based seasoning.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a fish-and-sake restaurant (sashimi, charcoal-grilled fish, clams, crab, wagyu); vegetable dishes such as water eggplant also appear (June 2026).
places.hours_raw: Mon–Sat 17:30–23:00, last order 22:00; closed Sundays and holidays (Tabelog). Same-day cancellation fee: 100% of the course, or ¥5,500 a person for à la carte bookings; tables for two may be moved to the counter (Tabelog). places.cuisine: Japanese cooking for sake: seasonal fish and vegetables, as sashimi or grilled over charcoal (nodoguro and kinki are popular); the mackerel sandwich and black-wagyu katsu sandwich to finish or take home; rare sake and selected wine, with sake ware to choose (Tabelog) · courses or à la carte: an omakase course ¥19,800 with the katsu sandwich of Kumamoto black wagyu "Wao" tenderloin and demi-glace (July 2025) · dishes in reviews: assorted sashimi, grilled natural kue, matsutake Inaniwa udon, filet sandwich (October 2025); bonito with sudachi, sake-steamed clams (July 2025); kazunoko potato salad, sea-bream miso grilled rice balls (July 2025); matsutake and sanma rolls (October 2025); seiko crab (December 2025); surf clam with shiso, grilled swordfish, water eggplant (June 2026) · a separate sake menu (July 2025)
places.notes: [Japanese · Kitashinchi, fish and sake on the third floor] A fifteen-seat restaurant for seasonal fish and rare sake on Eirakucho Street in Kitashinchi, with a seven-seat counter and sofa tables. Order a course or à la carte: sashimi platters, fish grilled over charcoal (nodoguro, kinki, natural kue), seasonal dishes like matsutake and sanma rolls or seiko crab in winter, and the house signatures, a mackerel sandwich and a black-wagyu katsu sandwich cooked rare with demi-glace, which you can take home if you cannot finish. There is a menu just for sake, served in handsome sake ware. It is expensive (¥20,000–30,000 a head is common) and popular for business dinners; book ahead. Japanese menu only, no children, and go easy on perfume in the small room.

chef_bio.background: Shop text (Tabelog): high-class Japanese cuisine; seasonal fish as sashimi or grilled over charcoal; the mackerel sandwich and the cutlet sandwich as signature dishes "known for their beautiful cross-sections"; rare Japanese sake and selected wines; eye-catching tableware. Opened 27 October 2016.
chef_bio.philosophy: Seasonal fish and vegetables in refined dishes, with carefully chosen sake (Tabelog).
chef_bio.specialty: Black-wagyu katsu sandwich; mackerel sandwich; charcoal-grilled fish.

anecdotes.text: "The perfect rare doneness and the juicy, luxurious meat paired with the demi-glace sauce were simply amazing!!" — July 2025, the katsu sandwich in a ¥19,800 omakase.
"I was intrigued by a unique dish, the Kazunoko Potato Salad, which had a rich dashi flavor, making it a wonderfully Japanese-style potato salad" — July 2025, a third visit.
"The appetizer of surf clam was incredibly delicious and left a strong impression. It was refreshing with a nice hint of shiso." — June 2026.

cultural_comfort.note: Tabelog: "Sorry, we only have a Japanese menu." Staff recommend sake on request (July 2025).

places.notes: [Italian · Chayamachi, a cheese-and-honey café] A bright café-style Italian restaurant on the ninth floor of NU Chayamachi, by the Hankyu station, built around more than twenty cheeses and a range of raw honeys: drizzle the honey over the Chicago pizza, whose cheese floods out when cut, or over cheesecake. Cheese fondue for dipping vegetables and baguette, Camembert ajillo and burrata fill out the menu, and at lunch an add-on brings unlimited tastings of eight cheeses and three honeys. Prices are moderate: lunch sets from about ¥1,850, dinner courses from ¥3,500. Popular for girls' nights and birthdays, with semi-private rooms; one October 2026 weekday a queue formed minutes after opening. Some diners found the Chicago pizza hard to cut or the cheese cooled, and dessert slow to come.

roles: Kitchen and staff (unnamed in the sources read)
chef_bio.background: Shop text (Tabelog; official site): a cheese-specialist Italian with over 20 cheeses, fresh and aged, mostly Japanese and European, and raw honey; Chicago pizza and cheese fondue are the popular dishes; many drinks made with raw honey. Opened 20 June 2012.
chef_bio.philosophy: The salt of cheese with the sweetness of raw honey (official site).
chef_bio.specialty: Chicago pizza with raw honey; cheese fondue.

places.gf_detail: Ask when booking. No gluten information. Horse sashimi comes with a sweet soy sauce, the Harihari hot pot ends with soba, and courses include Saikyo-grilled fish and nigiri, which are usually seasoned with soy sauce containing wheat.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: courses of sushi and horse meat; the hot pot broth is made from bonito and horse bones (June 2026).
places.hours_raw: Mon–Sat and the day before or after a holiday 18:00–22:30, last order food 22:00, drinks 22:15; closed Sundays and holidays (Tabelog). Two seatings, 18:00 and 20:30, in December 2026; menus can be tailored to a budget (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners); no e-money or QR (Tabelog). 17 seats: 7 at the counter and sunken-kotatsu tables for 4 and 6 in a tatami room, which can be booked whole; non-smoking; children welcome; English, Simplified Chinese and Korean menus; digital menu (Tabelog). Opened 1 September 2025 (Tabelog).
places.neighborhood: Kitashinchi, 谷安セドナビル 3F — 3 min from JR Kitashinchi Stn
places.cuisine: Sushi with fresh horse meat sent from Kumamoto (Tabelog) · courses: "Kiwami" Sushi Bakou course with horse meat and seafood ¥16,500; Sushi Bakou course of the day's fish ¥10,890; Sakura hot pot course of horse sashimi and Harihari hot pot ¥10,500 (Tabelog, tax included); a sushi-only course for diners who skip horse meat (June 2026) · June 2026 Kiwami course: natural bluefin and sea bream sashimi, ume suisho, strained ankimo, sea bream wrapped in kombu with horse meat, shiso and green onion, carbonara-style chawanmushi, abalone with liver sauce and grated cheese, marinated bluefin with yuzu pepper, striped jack, young kohada, three cuts of horse sashimi, the Harihari hot pot of horse meat and watercress in a bonito and horse-bone broth ending in soba, and hojicha pudding · Densuke anago, uni piled over the rice, toro-taku, sablefish Saikyo-yaki, ice cream with honey poured at the table (June–July 2026) · horse liver sashimi, lava-grilled horse tongue (July 2026) · sake chosen for the season's fish; koto music in the room (June 2026)
places.notes: [Sushi · Kitashinchi, sushi and Kumamoto horse meat] A Kitashinchi restaurant that began as a horse-meat specialist and reopened as a sushi bar in September 2025, keeping horse meat sent from Kumamoto alongside the fish. The top course pairs the two: sea bream wrapped in kombu with horse meat and shiso, three cuts of horse sashimi with a sweet soy sauce, and a Harihari hot pot of horse meat and watercress in a bonito and horse-bone broth, between nigiri of marinated bluefin with a hidden dab of yuzu pepper, uni piled over the rice and abalone in liver sauce. Courses run ¥10,500–16,500; a sushi-only course suits diners who skip horse meat. Diners praise a friendly head chef and staff who pace dishes to the table; one family asked the chef for a sushi cake for a child's birthday (July 2026). Counter seats and sunken-kotatsu rooms; English, Chinese and Korean menus.

roles: Head chef (unnamed; "very friendly and approachable", June 2026 review)
chef_bio.origin: The shop was a horse-meat specialty restaurant before it reopened as a sushi bar (September and October 2026 reviews); Tabelog opening date 1 September 2025.
chef_bio.background: Shop text (Tabelog): authentic sushi made with seasonal fresh fish and fresh horse meat directly from Kumamoto; four courses featuring sushi and horse meat; sake to match seasonal fish; counter and tatami seating. Reviews: a long-time regular from the horse-meat days (September 2026); "Bakou, which originally specialized in horse meat" now offering sushi courses (October 2025).
chef_bio.philosophy: The sea and the land in one course (Tabelog).
chef_bio.specialty: "Kiwami" course of sushi and horse meat; Harihari hot pot.

anecdotes.text: "My family tends to eat at a slower pace, but the staff adjusted the timing of the dishes accordingly, allowing us to savor each plate without feeling rushed." — June 2026, the ¥16,500 Kiwami course.
"I requested the chef to create a sushi cake in advance" — July 2026, a child's birthday on a fourth visit.
"The horse sashimi and liver sashimi were both exquisite, and the combination of horse meat and the crisp watercress in the hot pot was simply outstanding." — September 2026.

cultural_comfort.note: English, Simplified Chinese and Korean menus (Tabelog); set courses explained by a friendly chef (2026).

places.name: 炭火焼肉 大歓 (Sumibi Yakiniku Daikan)
places.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information. Meat comes salted (tongue with green-onion salt) or marinated, and the menu has cold noodles, namul with gochujang and Korean dishes; nothing is described as gluten-free.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a charcoal yakiniku menu of beef, horumon and chicken; namul, kimchi and perilla leaves are the plant dishes mentioned.
places.hours_raw: Tue–Sun 17:00–24:00; closed every Monday, holidays included (Tabelog). For later hours the shop points to its second branch near Mikyu-bashi, open 17:00–03:00 (Tabelog). Reservations accepted, and needed: full and turning walk-ins away at 20:00 on a weekday (August 2026); no seat choice, though requests for non-smoking, counter or table can be noted; please do not cancel on the day (Tabelog). Courses have a two-hour limit from September 2026 (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners), iD, QUICPay and PayPay (Tabelog). 50 seats: a counter of 6 on 1F (non-smoking) and tables on 2F and 3F (smoking) (Tabelog; August 2026 review). Opened 5 October 2017 (Tabelog).
places.neighborhood: Higashi-Shinsaibashi 1-9-12, a house on three floors — 2 min from Nagahoribashi Stn, 5 min from Shinsaibashi Stn
places.cuisine: Charcoal-grilled yakiniku of Japanese black wagyu with homemade side dishes, in a house (Tabelog) · courses with 120 minutes of free drinks, ¥6,800 and ¥8,800 for higher-grade wagyu, for 4–20 people (Tabelog) · à la carte, many cuts in half portions (August 2026): premium salted tongue and thick-cut tongue, tongue with green-onion salt, outside skirt, premium mino, ribeye, cheek, short ribs, shabu-grilled premium loin, premium liver grilled or as sashimi, omasum sashimi, yukke, chicken thigh (2026) · tataki-style salad, namul and kimchi platter just under ¥1,000 (August 2026), perilla leaves · cold noodles, oxtail soup, egg soup, rice · beer, wine by the half bottle
places.notes: [Yakiniku · Higashi-Shinsaibashi near Nagahoribashi] A charcoal yakiniku restaurant filling a house on three floors near Nagahoribashi, the counter downstairs and smoking tables above, that describes itself as run by a "meat professional". The tongue is the order that diners repeat: salted, thick-cut, or with green-onion salt, then outside skirt, mino and the premium liver, many cuts in half portions so two people can try more. Finish with oxtail soup or cold noodles. It is often full, even on weekdays, so book; diners spent about ¥5,000–10,000 a head in 2026, and the all-you-can-drink courses for groups are ¥6,800 or ¥8,800. Closed Mondays.

roles: Owner described by the shop as a "meat professional"; unnamed (Tabelog)
chef_bio.background: Per the Tabelog shop text: an authentic charcoal yakiniku restaurant in a private house, focused on homemade dishes and premium Japanese black wagyu, "owned by a meat professional"; opened 5 October 2017; a second branch near Mikyu-bashi serves until 03:00.
chef_bio.specialty: Salted tongue; premium liver; outside skirt.

anecdotes.text: "It was so full that walk-ins without a reservation were turned away, so be sure to make a reservation!" — August 2026, 8 PM on a weekday.
"Looking at the menu, I noticed that many meats can be ordered in half portions, making it easy to sample various cuts in smaller amounts." — August 2026.
"Since the beef tongue is a specialty here, we ordered thick slices along with two types of green onion salt" — September 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ (店舗会員): 炭火焼肉 大歓 (Sumibi Yakiniku Daikan)、焼肉・ホルモン・韓国料理、大阪市中央区東心斎橋1-9-12、長堀橋駅から2分、心斎橋駅から5分、火〜日17:00〜24:00、月曜休み (祝日でも)、深夜は近くの2号店 (Mikyu-bashi 店、17:00〜3:00) へ、予約可、席の指定は不可 (1階禁煙、2階と3階は喫煙)、当日のキャンセルは控えて、2026年9月からコースは2時間制、120分飲み放題付きのコース6,800円と8,800円 (4〜20名)、カード・iD・QUICPay・PayPay 可、50席 (カウンター6、テーブル44)、一軒家、手作りにこだわる本格炭火焼肉、「肉のプロ」が営む店、2017年10月5日オープン。口コミ(2026年8月〜10月): 上塩タン、厚切りタン、ねぎ塩タン、ハラミ、上ミノ、リブロース、上レバー、ユッケ、ハーフサイズが多い、ナムルとキムチの盛り合わせ1,000円弱、テールスープ、冷麺、平日20時でも満席で予約なしは断られていた、ワインはハーフボトルのみ、ひとり5,000〜10,000円ほど。

cultural_comfort.note: À la carte yakiniku grilled at the table over charcoal; book ahead (2026). No English evidence found.

places.cuisine: Yakiniku of meat from a long-established butcher, with raw-meat dishes (Tabelog; 2025–2026 reviews) · assorted tongue: special tongue, green-onion salt tongue, salted tongue, tongue geta, ¥2,728 for two (July 2026) · raw harami yukke with egg yolk ¥1,628 (July 2026) · wagyu yukke · yamakake heart sashimi with grated yam and egg yolk · raw tsurami, tongue sashimi · harami, premium harami, loin, kainomi, premium mino, white omasum, liver, red meat, sirloin cap (2026) · yaki-suki (grilled sukiyaki) · omakase of five cuts (July 2026) · napa-cabbage kimchi, bean-sprout namul · chige ramen, half-size cold noodles · bottled beer, sake and wine
places.notes: [Yakiniku · Higashi-Shinsaibashi, until 3 a.m.] A 22-seat yakiniku room on Kasayacho Street among the bars between Namba and Shinsaibashi, buying from a long-established butcher and open until 3 a.m. six nights a week. It is known for raw-meat dishes: harami yukke stirred with egg yolk, raw tsurami, tongue sashimi and a heart sashimi under grated yam. Then the tongue platter of four kinds (¥2,728 for two in July 2026), harami, liver and white omasum on a flat roaster, and chige ramen to finish. Expect ¥6,000–8,000 a head. Smoking is allowed, so no one under 20; book early, and not for 19:00.

roles: Unnamed; a yakiniku restaurant "run by a butcher" (April 2025 review)
chef_bio.background: Per the Tabelog shop text: "Enjoy the finest meat directly from a long-established butcher shop to your heart's content." An April 2025 diner calls it a yakiniku restaurant run by a butcher. Opened 10 September 2019.
chef_bio.specialty: Raw harami yukke; assorted tongue; yamakake heart sashimi.

anecdotes.text: "First and foremost, you absolutely must order the Assorted Tongue (JPY 2,728 for two servings). This time, I ordered five servings, and I appreciate that they adjust the quantity based on the number of people." — July 2026.
"I was pleasantly surprised that they remembered my face even though it had been quite a while since my last visit." — October 2026, a favourite heart sashimi with grated yam and egg yolk.
"The roaster was of the teppan-yaki type, so rather than grilling a lot at once, it felt like a place where you can slowly enjoy each piece of meat." — June 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ (店舗会員): 焼肉 無双武蔵、焼肉・ホルモン、大阪市中央区東心斎橋2-6-19 三ツ寺ギャラクシービル5号館 1F、日本橋駅から徒歩7分、なんば駅から徒歩9分、月〜土・祝前・祝後17:30〜翌3:00 (L.O. 2:30)、日曜・祝日休み、23時閉店の日は Instagram のストーリーハイライトで、予約は早めにネットで、19時スタートの予約は不可、連絡なしで15分遅れると取り消し、前日キャンセルは1名3,000円、チャージ1名330円 (税込)、カード・PayPay 可、22席 (カウンター2×3、テーブル4×4)、喫煙可のため20歳未満は入店不可、老舗の精肉店直送の肉、2019年9月10日オープン。口コミ(2025年4月〜2026年10月): 精肉店が営む焼肉店、タン盛り合わせ2人前2,728円、生ハラミユッケ1,628円、とろろのハツ刺し、タン刺し、白センマイ、レバー、チゲラーメン、ハーフの冷麺、平らなロースター、ひとり6,000〜8,000円ほど、周りはガールズバーやホストクラブ。

places.name: 大阪うどん いなの路 (Osaka Udon Inanoji)
places.gf_detail: Not gluten-free in practice: wheat udon (and soba) in dashi, tempura bits and tempura on the menu; no gluten-free option described.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: every bowl is served in the house dashi (official site), and the menu is built on beef, chicken and egg.
places.hours_raw: Mon, Tue, Wed and Sun 11:00–20:00; Fri and Sat 11:00–22:00; closed Thursday; closes early when the noodles sell out; check social media for extra closures (official site; Tabelog). No reservations (Tabelog). Queues at opening: 5–13 people waiting and 20–30 minutes in October 2026. Order by QR code on your phone (October 2026). Water is self-service (October 2026). Cards: AMEX only; no e-money or QR payments (Tabelog). About 5 counter seats on 1F and more seats up a steep stair on 2F (official site; 2026 reviews); non-smoking (Tabelog). Opened 3 September 2022 (Tabelog).
places.neighborhood: Sennichimae 1-8-2, on the street a reviewer calls Aiai Bridge Street — 3 min from Nippombashi Stn exit B26
places.cuisine: Osaka udon in a slightly sweet house dashi, the recipe recreated from memory of the closed 信濃そば (official site) · meat udon, the signature, ¥1,100 (Tabelog; October 2026) · special curry udon, curry soba with extra meat · kizami udon, kitsune udon, tori-namba udon, oyako-namba udon · niku-sui with egg, the meat broth without noodles · haikara udon with tempura bits · meat soba · dashimaki, onigiri, takikomi gohan, limited chestnut rice (October 2026) · shrimp tempura topping · sake and shochu (official site; 2026 reviews)
places.notes: [Udon · Sennichimae, the taste of a lost noodle shop] A small udon shop a few minutes from Nippombashi Station, that recreated the dashi of the closed noodle shop 信濃そば without a written recipe, working from the memory of its taste (official site); the shop says well-known customers came back for it, and reviewers mention the comedians Downtown and the TV show Gobugobu. Order the meat udon (¥1,100 in October 2026): soft Osaka noodles, sweetish broth, tender meat and green onion; or the niku-sui with onigiri, the curry udon, or a kitsune udon. Expect a queue at 11:00 and on weekend lunches; order by QR code; about five counter seats downstairs and more up a steep stair. Closed Thursdays, and earlier when the noodles run out.

roles: Owner of 大阪うどん いなの路 (official site)
chef_bio.background: Per the official site: 大阪うどん いなの路 wanted to keep the taste of the earlier 信濃そば, whose detailed recipe did not survive, and recreated it over a long time from the memory of its flavour; news of the revival brought many famous people and customers back for the taste they knew. The dried-fish supplier and noodle maker have changed since then, but the taste is carried on, refined, with new small dishes to go with drinks. The owner 山根 正也 writes that the aim is for people across Japan to taste it. Branches: 桜井店 in 箕面市 (opened 27 June 2023) and 西宮えびす店 in 西宮市 (opened 5 December 2025). A regular of seven visits writes in October 2026 that the soup "took years to perfect" and is even better than the previous generation's.
chef_bio.philosophy: "Carry on the traditional taste while seeking development and improvement every day" (official site, translated).

anecdotes.text: "I arrived around 11:40 AM, and it was fully packed with about 12-13 people waiting outside." — October 2026, meat udon after a 30-minute wait.
"There was no recipe, so it took years to perfect this soup. I believe the result is even better than the previous generation's soup." — October 2026, a seventh visit, curry soba with extra meat.
"To finish, I saved half of the seasoned rice and poured the meat and broth over it" — October 2026, meat soba and takikomi gohan.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト: 大阪うどん いなの路、山根 正也、伝統的な味の継承と「発展」「改良」、全国の方にこの味を、厳選素材の「こだわりの出汁」、名物の肉うどん、丼物、だし巻や天ぷらなどの一品でお酒、シメにうどんや肉吸い、細かいレシピが残っていなかった先代「信濃そば」の味を、味の記憶を頼りに長い時間をかけて再現、多くの著名人やお客様が思い出の味を求めて来店、節屋も製麺所も当時とは変わったが味を受け継ぐ、1階はカウンター席、2階も、お品書き: 名物 肉うどん、特製カレーうどん、きざみうどん、とりなんばうどん、きつねうどん、親子なんばうどん、肉吸い (玉子入り)、だし巻、おにぎり、本店 大阪市中央区千日前1-8-2、11:00〜20:00 (金・土は22:00まで)、木曜休み、麺売り切れ次第終了、桜井店 (箕面市、2023年6月27日)、西宮えびす店 (西宮市、2025年12月5日)。食べログ: 予約不可、カードは AMEX のみ、禁煙、2022年9月3日オープン、肉うどん1,100円。口コミ(2026年5月〜10月): 少し甘い出汁、やわらかい麺、開店時から行列、QR コードで注文、1階のカウンターは5席ほど、急な階段で2階へ、肉吸い、haikara うどん、カレーそば、栗ご飯 (期間限定)。

cultural_comfort.note: Order by QR code on your phone; a short menu led by meat udon (October 2026). No English evidence found.

places.gf_detail: Ask when booking. No gluten information. The omakase course runs from tempura and kimchi through seasoned and marinated cuts, a sukiyaki-style thigh dipped in egg and sauce, seared meat sushi and soup; nothing is described as gluten-free.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a Kobe-beef yakiniku course with seafood starters; salad, kimchi and vegetable tempura are its only plant dishes.
places.hours_raw: Daily 17:00–23:00 (Tabelog). Reservations by phone (official site) or online (Tabelog). Service charge 10% (Tabelog). Cards, iD, PayPay and Alipay (Tabelog). 38 seats, semi-private rooms for 2 and 4 with open ceilings, so neighbouring voices carry (Tabelog; August 2026 reviews); non-smoking; children welcome (Tabelog). Menu in English, Simplified Chinese and Korean, and English-speaking staff (Tabelog). The shop text states it has Muslim-friendly certification (Tabelog). Opened 1 July 2022 (Tabelog).

places.cuisine: Yakiniku of Kobe beef and rare and aged cuts with kappo-style dishes (official site; Tabelog) · OMAKASE course (Wabi) ¥16,500, 12 items (Tabelog): starters that change daily, e.g. vegetable and octopus tempura, kombu-cured sea bream, pork belly wrapped round okra (2026); salad and three kimchi; seared salted yukke with wasabi and garlic chips; aged tongue with sudachi; Kobe beef steak, chateaubriand and strip loin; three omakase lean cuts; wagyu outside skirt; thigh sukiyaki dipped in egg; seared meat nigiri; soup of the day; vanilla ice cream or fresh chocolate with coffee or green tea (August–October 2026) · à la carte also available · wines and sake
places.notes: [Yakiniku · Hozenji Yokocho, Kobe-beef omakase] A Kobe-beef yakiniku restaurant inside the stone-paved Hozenji Yokocho, where an owner trained in kappo cooking adds Japanese touches to grilled meat (official site). The 12-dish omakase (¥16,500) is the way in: tempura or kombu-cured sea bream to start, seared salted yukke, aged tongue with sudachi, a Kobe chateaubriand or strip-loin steak, three lean cuts, sukiyaki-style thigh in egg, then seared meat sushi and dessert. The rooms are semi-private, with open ceilings. Many diners in 2026 were visitors from overseas; there is an English menu and English-speaking staff. Add 10% service; expect about ¥15,000–20,000 a head.

roles: Owner trained in kappo cooking, unnamed (official site)
chef_bio.background: Per the official site: yakiniku that is "not just grilled meat" but carries a sense of Japan, with the skills of an owner from a kappo background and a wide wine list, set in Hozenji Yokocho. An August 2026 diner credits the kombu-cured sea bream, vegetable tempura and okra-wrapped pork belly starters to the chef's kaiseki background. Opened 1 July 2022.
chef_bio.philosophy: "Enjoy yakiniku that is not just grilled meat, with a sense of Japan" (official site, translated).

places.cuisine: Yakiniku of aged wagyu, mainly Matsusaka beef and Miyazaki's Kirishima beef bought from the producers, with aged meat and aged tongue (Tabelog) · Hozenji course ¥11,550 (October 2026): seasonal kimchi (lotus root, napa cabbage, cucumber), choregi salad, wagyu sashimi of the day (sirloin-cap salt yukhoe, wagyu and takuan roll, sirloin-cap sashimi), aged salted tongue and tongue kalbi with grilled vegetables, aged cuts in sauce (top sirloin, spencer roll, sirloin cap), rice, fresh offal, sudachi cold noodles, a dessert chosen from seven · Kitan lunch course ¥6,000 (September 2026) · aged-tongue bento ¥1,650 (regular; a premium version has the tongue root) with a raw egg yolk and salted green onion (September 2026) · other dishes in 2026 reviews: thick-cut aged tongue, aged wagyu outside skirt, chateaubriand with wasabi soy sauce, ribeye with sukiyaki sauce and yolk · birthday plate on request
places.notes: [Yakiniku · Hozenji Yokocho, aged wagyu in private rooms] A yakiniku house in a 120-year-old Japanese restaurant building in Hozenji Yokocho, made over so that every seat is a private room, many of them tatami rooms with sunken seating where you take your shoes off. It belongs to the small Kitan group (its Minami-Senba shop is the original) and serves aged meat and aged tongue, mainly Matsusaka and Miyazaki's Kirishima beef bought from the producers. The ¥11,550 Hozenji course runs from three wagyu sashimi through aged salted tongue and tongue kalbi to aged cuts in sauce, fresh offal and sudachi cold noodles, with a dessert chosen from seven; lunch brings a ¥6,000 course or a queue for the ¥1,650 aged-tongue bento. Birthday diners in 2026 praised the staff, who kept one party's cake in the fridge and set out the party's shoes on leaving. Book courses by the day before; dinner adds 5% service. English menu.

chef_bio.background: Per the shop-maintained Tabelog listing: renovated from a 120-year-old Japanese restaurant building in Hozenji Yokocho, an alley kept since the Edo period; concept "enjoying meat from various angles", with aged meat, aged tongue and creative dishes; beef bought directly from producers, mainly Matsusaka beef and Kirishima beef from Miyazaki. Two Kitan yakiniku shops: the Minami-Senba main shop (osaka_yakiniku_kitan_minamisenba in data, whose record cites an official site listing 南船場, 法善寺 and 韻) and this one. Opened 3 April 2022.

chef_bio.specialty: Aged tongue; aged wagyu courses; aged-tongue bento.

anecdotes.text: "I brought a paper bag with a cake to enjoy at home, and the staff kindly offered to keep it in the refrigerator for us. When we left, they had neatly arranged our shoes" — October 2026, the Hozenji course for a birthday.
"The 'Premium' option includes the tongue root, while the 'Regular' features the middle or tip parts of the tongue." — September 2026, aged-tongue bento ¥1,650.

"The gentle texture of the earthen walls, along with the decorative alcove featuring pebbles, hanging scrolls, and a single flower vase, created a luxurious atmosphere" — October 2026, the Hozenji course ¥11,550.

places.notes: [Café · Shinsaibashi, Louis Vuitton's café floor] The café on the seventh floor of the Louis Vuitton building on Midosuji, reached by its own lift away from the crowded store and sharing the floor with SUGALABO V. Expect the monogram everywhere: on the latte art of the ¥2,000 V Café latte, on the chocolate tart, on the waffle under a tuna tartare. The thing to order is the mille-feuille assembled to order with Madagascar vanilla cream (¥3,500, August 2026), or one of the gateaux, which run large, or a Yame matcha tiramisu. At lunch there is pasta and a seafood gratin, and a ¥20,000 seasonal course with a ¥14,000 pairing for a splurge. Diners in 2026 found the staff warm and the prices high but the setting worth it. Walk-in only; 10% service.

places.cuisine: Charcoal yakitori of Omi duck from Takashima, Shiga, and Yamato chicken raised for the group by 雅chickfarm in Nara, plus fermented dishes (Tabelog) · duck tataki of breast and thigh, duck sashimi with grilled skin, chicken sashimi platters (breast, gizzard, neck; five kinds of Yamato chicken), with house condiments such as garlic koji, yuzu, miso, wasabi and salt (September–October 2026) · duck skewers: neck, heart, gizzard, heart with green onion · quail eggs on chicken sashimi, charcoal-grilled edamame, caciocavallo cheese four ways, "adult" potato salad with three cheeses, duck kara-age, thick rolls, grilled rice balls, soba to finish, sweet-potato butter (2026 reviews) · craft beer, sake, a Kamojin sour and many non-alcoholic drinks (2026 reviews) · table charge ¥385
places.notes: [Yakitori · Sennichimae, duck until 2 a.m.] A three-storey yakitori house near Nankai Namba built around duck: Omi duck from Takashima in Shiga, and Yamato chicken raised for the group by a Nara farm, grilled over charcoal or served raw. Start with duck tataki of breast and thigh or a platter of chicken sashimi, eaten with house condiments such as garlic koji, yuzu and miso, then skewers of duck neck, heart and gizzard; fermentation runs through the menu, developed with a well-known fermentation specialist. There are oddities to try (caciocavallo grilled four ways, a three-cheese potato salad, duck kara-age) and soba with duck to finish. Open until 2 a.m. daily, so it works as a second stop; a counter suits solo diners. Diners in 2026 found it delicious if a little pricey for the portions, and one busy night slow. Raw chicken is served here.
