places.name: 手打ち麺 やす田 (Teuchi Men Yasuda)
places.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: thick handmade wheat noodles with kansui (October 2026), in a shio or shoyu broth.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: iriko (dried sardine) and bonito broths with pork chashu.
places.hours_raw: Tue–Sun 11:30–14:30, until sold out; closed Monday, plus irregular days and frequent temporary closures (Tabelog). One November 2026 diner had found it closed several times; another found it open at 14:00 (October 2026), and one Saturday it opened at 11:19 with five already seated (October 2026). Expect a short wait at noon: 10–20 minutes in October 2026. Order by telling the owner and pay after (October 2026). Cash only (Tabelog). 7 counter seats; table seats closed since March 2019, when the owner began running the shop alone (Tabelog). Non-smoking, ashtray at the door (Tabelog). English menu (Tabelog). No large size; no tsukemen (October 2026; Tabelog). Opened 13 September 2011 (Tabelog).
places.neighborhood: 東中島1-21-2, 新大阪ハイツ 106 — 4 min from the east exit of Shin-Osaka Stn: left out of the exit, right at the FamilyMart on the corner, right at the next crossing, on the right (Tabelog)
places.cuisine: Tabelog Ramen 100 every year 2017–2025 (WEST to 2022, OSAKA from 2023) · handmade-noodle ramen (Tabelog) · shio ramen with iriko ¥900, the order most people make; shoyu ramen with katsuobushi (reviews) · extra chashu: shio with extra chashu ¥1,200 (October 2026) · rice on the side: katsuo rice ¥200 heaped with bonito flakes (October 2026), kombu rice, and a small chashu rice bowl with a sweet sauce (October 2026) · toppings: green onion, white onion, menma and two slices of pork-belly chashu (2025–2026)
places.notes: [Ramen · Shin-Osaka east side, one man and seven seats] A seven-seat counter four minutes from the Shin-Osaka east exit, open since 2011 and in Tabelog's Ramen 100 every year from 2017 to 2025. Since 2019 the owner has run it alone, making the noodles by hand, cooking, serving and taking cash; one October 2026 diner wrote of "respect" for the solo operation. The noodles are the point: thick, curly and chewy, "about the thickness of a disposable chopstick" and close to udon (October 2026), in a clear, gentle shio broth of iriko, with green and white onion, menma and pork-belly chashu, ¥900. Add katsuo rice for ¥200. Lunch only, until the noodles run out, and it often closes without notice, so have a backup. Cash only; no large size.

roles: Owner (unnamed), runs the shop alone since March 2019 (Tabelog)
chef_bio.background: Per the Tabelog listing (remarks): "Due to focusing on ramen, we are not serving tsukemen. We often have temporary closures. As of March 2019, the owner is handling everything alone, so we have closed the table seating and are only offering counter seating." Opened 13 September 2011; Tabelog Ramen 100 (WEST 2017–2022, OSAKA 2023–2025). Per reviews: "The owner operates the restaurant solo, skillfully handling the noodle draining, bowls, and toppings" (June 2025); "The owner was running the place solo" (October 2026).
chef_bio.specialty: Handmade thick curly noodles; iriko shio ramen.

anecdotes.text: "They are about the thickness of a disposable chopstick, making me wonder if they were udon … However, they seem to have kansui added, giving them a slight yellow tint." — October 2026, shio ramen ¥900 and katsuo rice ¥200.
"I've tried to come a few times before, but it was always closed for temporary reasons." — November 2026.
"Although the opening time is supposed to be 11:30, [the shop] opened at 11:19, and there were already five customers seated at the counter." — October 2026, a Saturday.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: 手打ち麺 やす田、ラーメン、大阪市東淀川区東中島1-21-2 新大阪ハイツ106号、JR 新大阪駅東口から徒歩4分、火〜日11:30〜14:30 (売り切れまで)、月曜休み、不定休あり、臨時休業が多い、現金のみ、カウンター7席、禁煙 (入口に灰皿)、英語メニュー、2011年9月13日オープン、つけ麺はなし、2019年3月から店主ひとりで営業しテーブル席は休止、食べログ ラーメン百名店 (WEST 2017〜2022、OSAKA 2023〜2025)。口コミ(2025年6月〜2026年11月): 塩らあめん900円、塩らあめんのスープは魚の出汁が効いた透明タイプ、麺は極太の縮れ麺、カツオ飯200円は鰹節のはるか下にご飯、昆布飯、チャーシュー丼、醤油ラーメン、チャーシュー増し1,200円、口頭で注文してあと払い、大盛りなし、店主ひとりで手際よく、店内は暑い、何度か臨時休業で入れなかった。

cultural_comfort.note: English menu (Tabelog); order by telling the owner, pay after.

noodles.notes: Handmade thick curly noodles with kansui, chewy and close to udon (October 2026); "a good bite due to the higher water content" (October 2026).

ramen.signature_bowl: Shio ramen with iriko (塩らあめん), ¥900 (October 2026).
ramen.chashu: Two slices of pork-belly chashu, tender with sweet fat (2025–2026); extra chashu available.

vegan.note: Iriko and bonito broth; pork chashu.

ramen.pantheon: Shin-Osaka's one-man handmade-noodle counter: udon-thick curly noodles in a clear iriko shio.

oiliness: "The strength of the medium-thick hand-pulled noodles in this light broth" — placed low.
clarity: "The broth had a high level of clarity"; a second diner's caption: 透明タイプ (B537733055).
aroma_punch: "A strong iriko flavor without any bitterness", against "a subtle aroma of iriko" (B322292983) — mid-scale between the two.

places.name: vegecafe＋α (Vege Cafe + α)
places.gf_detail: Ask. A December 2025 review shows a vegan soup-curry plate captioned as free of the 28 specified allergens and gluten-free (アレルギー特定原材料28品目不使用。グルテンフリー。), served with rice-flour bread, and the cafe serves rice-flour cookies (June 2026). But the shop's own text promises allergy-friendly gelato, not gluten-free food, and the cafe bakes wheat bread on site (whole-grain rolls, natural-yeast breads), so ask what is gluten-free today and how it is kept apart.
places.vegan_detail: The shop says its gelato "caters to vegans and those with allergies" (Tabelog). A December 2025 review shows a vegan soup-curry plate with rice-flour bread. Lunch (fried fish, scrambled egg) and the breakfast sandwiches are not vegan; ask which gelato flavours are vegan that day.
places.hours_raw: Tue–Sat 09:00–17:00 (food last order 16:00, drinks 16:30); lunch 11:00–14:00 until sold out; closed Sunday, Monday and holidays (Tabelog). The limited "Vege Cafe Kago Gozen" lunch is best booked; at busy times a 90-minute limit (Tabelog). Walk-ins at 11:00 on a Saturday got in (May 2026). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX) and e-money; no service charge (Tabelog). 49 seats: 6 at the counter, 43 at tables, a semi-private room for up to 15, whole hire for 20–50; non-smoking indoors, smoking only on the terrace (Tabelog). Pets on the open terrace only, not when it rains; children welcome, child-friendly dishes, no high chairs; free Wi-Fi; wheelchair accessible; English menu (Tabelog). A takeaway gelato and coffee window faces the street (May 2026).
places.neighborhood: 西中島6-9-20, ground floor of 新大阪GHビル, with a courtyard terrace across from a tableware shop (December 2025) — 7 min from Nishinakajima-Minamigata Stn, also reachable from Hankyu Minamikata and Shin-Osaka (Tabelog)
places.cuisine: Vegetable-led cafe with its own gelato; organic vegetables grown on the rooftop (Tabelog) · "Vege Cafe Kago Gozen" lunch basket ¥1,350, limited: a main of the day (fried horse mackerel with mustard tartar and rosemary in May 2026), three small sides, salad and vegetable soup, with a drink (May 2026; ¥1,790 with iced coffee) · vegan soup-curry plate with rice-flour bread (December 2025) · breakfast: prosciutto, lettuce and cheese sandwich on a Kiryu-yeast whole-grain roll ¥900, three natural-yeast breads of your choice ¥640, coffee set +¥400 (October 2026); a glass of red wine with breakfast +¥500 (December 2025) · Basque cheesecake (December 2025); rice-flour cookie with coffee (June 2026) · gelato made in house since July 2020, prized three years running at an Italian gelato competition (Tabelog; October 2026), e.g. organic apple balsamic and mascarpone (October 2026); a coffee float with gelato to take away (May 2026)
places.notes: [Cafe · Nishinakajima, vegetables, bread and gelato] A roomy 49-seat cafe in the Nishinakajima office district, a seven-minute walk from Nishinakajima-Minamigata, that grows organic vegetables on its rooftop and makes its own gelato, prized three years running at an Italian competition (Tabelog). Mornings bring natural-yeast breads and sandwiches on whole-grain rolls; at lunch the limited "Kago Gozen" basket (¥1,350) sets a main of the day beside small vegetable sides, salad and soup, so book. The shop says its gelato suits vegans and people with allergies, and a December 2025 diner had a vegan soup-curry plate with rice-flour bread. Seasonal decorations, a mix of tables and chairs, a courtyard terrace where dogs are welcome. Closed Sundays, Mondays and holidays.

chef_bio.background: Per the shop-maintained Tabelog listing: a cafe focused on "food", "vegetables" and "space", with organic vegetables grown on the rooftop and a healthy, vegetable-rich menu; a gelato shop added in July 2020, whose gelato "caters to vegans and those with allergies" and "has won awards for three consecutive years at the world's most prestigious gelato competition". Per reviews: bread baked on site (October 2026); the staff speak "in a soothing manner" (October 2026); "the staff had a warm atmosphere" (July 2026).
chef_bio.philosophy: "Everyone leaves with a smile" (Tabelog, of the gelato).
chef_bio.specialty: Kago Gozen vegetable lunch; house gelato.

anecdotes.text: "Free of the 28 specified allergens. Gluten-free." — a December 2025 diner's caption for the vegan soup-curry plate (アレルギー特定原材料28品目不使用。グルテンフリー。).
"When I asked if I could change it, [the staff] kindly accommodated my request." — May 2026, swapping the gelato in a takeaway coffee float.
"This gelato is an award-winning flavor from the world's toughest gelato competition in Italy." — October 2026, organic apple balsamic and mascarpone.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ (店舗会員): vegecafe＋α、カフェ・野菜料理・ジェラート、大阪市淀川区西中島6-9-20 新大阪GHビル 1F、西中島南方駅から徒歩7分、火〜土9:00〜17:00、ランチ11:00〜14:00 (売り切れまで)、日・月・祝休み、予約可、混雑時は1.5時間制、カード・電子マネー可、サービス料なし、49席、テラスのみ喫煙可、ペットはテラス席のみ、子ども可、Wi-Fi、英語メニュー。店の紹介: 屋上で無農薬の野菜を育てる、2020年7月からジェラートの店、ジェラートはヴィーガンやアレルギーの人にも、世界的なジェラートの大会で3年連続入賞。口コミ(2025年12月〜2026年10月): 桐生酵母全粒粉ロール使用 生ハムレタスチーズサンド900円、珈琲セット (+400円)、天然酵母パン3種640円、veganスープカレープレート (アレルギー特定原材料28品目不使用、グルテンフリー) と米粉パン、Kago Gozen 1,350円、アジフライとからしのタルタル、バスクチーズケーキ、米粉のクッキー、テイクアウトの窓口でコーヒーフロート、りんごのバルサミコとマスカルポーネのジェラート。

places.name: 粉もん處 光圀 裏なんば店 (Konamon Dokoro Mitsukuni Ura Namba)
places.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: the okonomiyaki batter is 100% Japanese wheat (official site), the yakisoba and modern-yaki use wheat noodles, and the monjayaki is a flour batter. The menu marks allergens with pictograms, so ask staff about any side dish.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: the okonomiyaki batter is made with a Kyoto-style bonito dashi (official site), and the fillings are pork, seafood, egg and cheese.
places.hours_raw: Daily 11:00–15:00 (last order 14:00) and 17:00–23:00 (last order 22:00); no closing day (official site; Tabelog). Lunch is limited to 90 minutes and takes no courses; when busy, dinner seats are limited to two hours (official site). Reservations online or by phone; on-the-day booking worked on a weekday (2026 reviews); in September 2026 two walk-in groups were turned away. Each guest orders at least one drink and one dish; no outside drinks (official site). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners, Discover), IC cards, e-money and QR (official site; Tabelog). 40 seats, all at sunken horigotatsu tables (September 2026 review); a heated-tobacco-only smoking area; private hire possible (Tabelog). Upstairs on 2F, up stairs that one diner found steep (Google review quoted on the official site). Children welcome (Tabelog).
places.neighborhood: Namba Sennichimae 3-18, 中村ビル 2F, in Ura Namba — 4 min from Kintetsu Nippombashi, Nihonbashi or Nankai Namba Stn
places.cuisine: An "upmarket" okonomiyaki house with creative monjayaki and wine (official site; prices from the official menu) · okonomiyaki on a batter of 100% Japanese wheat with Kyoto-style bonito dashi: pork ¥1,300, squid ¥1,500, shrimp ¥1,800, scallop ¥2,000, natto ¥1,200, mozzarella ¥1,900, seafood special ¥2,700; miso-shibire and salted-shrimp "shizuku" versions · modern-yaki with fresh noodles straight from the parent company's noodle works, pork ¥1,600 to seafood special ¥3,000 · about ten creative monjayaki ¥2,600–¥2,800: basil Genovese with Parmigiano, white-miso with melting mochi (the house speciality), Sichuan mapo, prawn and scallop ebi-chili, beef-jaw curry, gratin, bibimbap · yakisoba on chewy fresh noodles boiled to order; beef-jaw (agosuji) yakisoba (September 2026) · side dishes for drinking: poached-egg avocado and shrimp tartare, seared cured-mackerel carpaccio, dashimaki, salmon potato salad with tenkasu, smoked daikon with cream cheese, octopus and zucchini with anchovy (2026 reviews); grilled apple with ice cream to finish · courses with all-you-can-drink (2026 reviews) · every KENZO ESTATE wine plus about 20 others; Japanese whiskies such as 響, 山崎 and 白州
places.notes: [Okonomiyaki · Ura Namba, okonomiyaki and creative monja with wine] Up a flight of stairs in Ura Namba, a calm Japanese room of sunken horigotatsu tables that bills itself as an "upmarket" okonomiyaki house and, as one diner found, is one of the few that take bookings. The head chef's okonomiyaki uses 100% Japanese wheat and a Kyoto-style bonito dashi and comes fluffy, loaded with shrimp and scallops; the yakisoba and modern-yaki use fresh noodles from the noodle works behind the shop, which several diners rate as the real star. The monjayaki go far from the classic, cooked for you at the table: basil Genovese, white miso with mochi, mapo, ebi-chili, bibimbap. Plenty of side dishes for drinking, all of the KENZO ESTATE wines and Japanese whisky. Tabelog Okonomiyaki 100 in 2025. Book ahead (walk-ins were turned away on a September 2026 night); open daily for lunch and dinner to 23:00.

roles: Head chef (unnamed; 料理長 on the official site)
chef_bio.background: Per the official site: the head chef spent years eating around restaurants before deciding to cook, and worked out the batter and the cooking through trial and error; the yakisoba noodles come from the noodle works that is the shop's parent company. The site stocks every KENZO ESTATE wine. Tabelog Okonomiyaki 100, 2025. No opening date or owner is given.
chef_bio.philosophy: A "one rank above" okonomiyaki house: ingredients, technique and taste pursued to their limit (official site).
chef_bio.specialty: Seafood okonomiyaki; creative monjayaki; fresh-noodle yakisoba.

anecdotes.text: "On this day alone, two groups were turned away." — September 2026, mozzarella okonomiyaki.
"The okonomiyaki was incredibly fluffy and delicious, but the yakisoba was the real star—thick noodles with a chewy texture" — October 2026, a weekday walk-in.
"It felt like there were many international customers." — October 2026.

places.notes: [Yakiniku · Namba, private-room wagyu above the station] On the 10th floor of Namba HIPS, reached from Namba station without going outside, 25 private rooms of two to sixteen seats, many with a night view. The pitch is A5 kuroge wagyu and Kobe beef at low prices (cuts from ¥680), and a raw-meat licence for its signature wagyu mille-feuille yukhoe, layered with green onion and mixed with egg yolk. Rice is cooked to order pot by pot, best with wagyu and ikura on top. Weeknight courses start at ¥5,000 for ten dishes (Tuesday to Thursday), with all-you-can-drink for ¥2,000 more. Diners in 2026 praise the value and the privacy for dates and celebrations; one found the grilled cuts only average and the room dark. Renewed in June 2025. Tabelog Yakiniku WEST 100 in 2022.

chef_bio.background: Per the official site: aims to be the best-value yakiniku in Japan for A5 kuroge wagyu and Kobe beef; licensed to serve raw meat; rice cooked to order in individual pots; renewed and reopened on 10 June 2025. Opened 15 April 2015 (Tabelog). Tabelog Yakiniku WEST 100, 2022. No owner or chef is named.
chef_bio.specialty: Wagyu mille-feuille yukhoe; thick-cut tongue; pot-cooked rice with wagyu and ikura.

anecdotes.text: "An unusual combination was the ikura (salmon roe) with wagyu rice, which surprisingly worked well together." — October 2026, a first visit.

places.name: 作一 本店 (Sakuichi Honten)
places.gf_detail: Ask when booking. No gluten information. A kappo built around fish: sashimi, grilled fish and plain-cooked seasonal produce are on the long à la carte menu, but tempura, fried fugu and katsu are wheat, and soy sauce and dashi-based seasonings are used throughout.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a fish-led Japanese kitchen with dashi-based dishes; vegetables appear mainly as seasonal sides.
places.hours_raw: Mon–Sat from 17:00; the official site gives 17:00–22:00 with last orders (drinks included) at 21:30 since March 2022, while Tabelog lists 17:00–24:00. Closed Sunday and the third Monday of each month (official notice, from February 2024). Reservations; walk-ins possible (April 2026). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners) and e-money; no QR; no service charge (Tabelog). 40 seats on the 3rd and 4th floors: an 8-seat counter, private rooms for 2 to 8 including horigotatsu rooms; smoking allowed on the 3rd floor and in a two-person room on the 4th (Tabelog). The entrance is on the 4th floor (September 2025). The sister counter 弘作一 is on the ground floor of the same building (official site).
places.neighborhood: Nishi-Shinsaibashi 1-10-3, エースビル 3F・4F, behind the Nikko Hotel Osaka (September 2025 review) — 1 min from Shinsaibashi Stn exit 8
places.cuisine: Osaka kappo where you choose from a handwritten menu of the day's produce, over a metre long (March 2026; "about 1.8 metres", September 2025), and ask for it cooked as you like; a course from ¥15,000 (8–9 dishes: starter, sashimi, simmered, vinegared, grilled or fried, dressed, hassun, seasonal rice or kamameshi, dessert) (official site) · spring 2026: Yura purple sea urchin, conger eel and octopus from Himeji, bamboo shoots, green peas, sea-bream roe, young ayu from Lake Biwa, negi-maguro, firefly-squid risotto (March 2026) · autumn 2025: sashimi platters of about ten fish, matsutake from a basket to choose, grilled sea bream, dobin-mushi, Iwaya kisu tempura, akagai nuta, funazushi, mackerel bōzushi, fried fugu, sea-bream rice, beef fillet as steak or katsu · in season on the site (November 2026): roe-filled shishamo dried overnight, autumn mackerel bōzushi · diners report ¥10,000–¥49,999 a head
places.notes: [Kappo · Shinsaibashi, a long-running Osaka kappo with a metre-long menu] On the upper floors of a building behind the Nikko Hotel Osaka, a quiet kappo that has cooked in Minami for more than 40 years and moved here from 三津寺筋 in October 2002. The rooms, designed by 喜多俊之 of IDKデザイン on a theme of medieval Naniwa, run from an eight-seat counter where the owner cooks to private rooms for two to eight. The joy is the handwritten menu of the day, over a metre of washi listing seasonal fish and vegetables, from which you choose and say how you would like it cooked: Yura sea urchin, Biwa ayu, firefly-squid risotto in spring; matsutake picked from a basket, dobin-mushi, mackerel bōzushi in autumn. A course runs from ¥15,000. Long a favourite for business dinners; expect ¥20,000–¥30,000 a head. Closed Sundays.

chef_bio.chef_name: 奥長弘一 (as written; no romaji given)
roles: 主人 (owner) of 作一 (official notices, signed 主人 奥長弘一)
The owner cooks at the counter (official site: カウンターでは店主みずからが…腕を振るいます)
Sister counter 弘作一 managed by 河村幸貴 (official site)
chef_bio.background: Per the official site: Sakuichi has traded for more than 40 years and now has two shops in one building, 作一本店 on the 3rd and 4th floors and 弘作一 on the ground floor (renewed on 12 June 2020); the main shop moved from 三津寺筋 in October 2002, with interiors by 喜多俊之 of IDKデザイン on the theme of "medieval Naniwa"; the owner cooks at the counter with the season's produce. A March 2026 diner on a fifth visit, and others since 2022, describe choosing dishes and cooking styles with the chef across the counter.
chef_bio.philosophy: "作一に行けば、本物が食べられる" — go to Sakuichi and you eat the real thing (official site tagline); a quiet place to ease the day's fatigue (official site).
chef_bio.specialty: Seasonal fish chosen from the daily menu; sashimi platters; mackerel bōzushi.

anecdotes.text: "The menu, written on a washi paper over a meter long, lists seasonal ingredients alongside classic dishes, making it a joy to discuss and decide what to eat today." — March 2026, a fifth visit.
"I have fond memories of this place from my days working at a major securities firm, where I visited many times for business dinners." — August 2026.
"I was allowed to choose from a basket of Iwate matsutake mushrooms" — October 2025.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト (sakuichi.com): 作一、日本料理、作一に行けば、本物が食べられる、40年以上営業、同じビルに2つの店、作一本店 (3・4階、完全個室、4階2名・4名、3階6名・8名)、弘作一 (1階、2020年6月12日新装開店、店長 河村幸貴、主人 奥長弘一)、2002年10月に三津寺筋より移店、IDKデザインの喜多俊之さんのコンセプトは「日本、浪速の中世」、カウンターでは店主みずからが四季折々の旬の素材で腕を振るう、西心斎橋1-10-3 エースビル3・4階、2022年3月22日から17時〜22時 (L.O.21時30分)、2024年2月から定休日は日曜日と第三月曜日、コース15,000円〜 (前菜、お造り、煮物、酢の物、焼き物又は揚げ物、和え物、八寸盛り、季節のごはん・釜飯、デザート)、季節のおすすめ (2026年11月): 子持ち本ししゃも一夜干し、秋サバの棒ずし。食べログ (店舗会員): 日本料理、40席 (カウンター8、個室)、3階と4階の2名個室は喫煙可、カード・電子マネー可、サービス料なし。口コミ(2025年9月〜2026年8月): 1メートル以上の和紙のお品書き、好きな素材と調理法を選べる、お造りの盛り合わせ、松茸を籠から選ぶ、土瓶蒸し、鯖の棒ずし、ふぐの唐揚げ、接待に、Nikko Hotel Osaka の裏、入口は4階。

cultural_comfort.note: A long handwritten Japanese menu; order by talking with the chef or staff. No English evidence found.

places.gf_detail: Ask when booking. The listing asks guests to state allergies and dislikes in advance and says same-day requests may not be possible. Courses include homemade bread, granita, and a dessert tree; nothing is described as gluten-free.

Up to three hours in the ABC Motor Pool across from the entrance, north of Minami Elementary School (Tabelog). Non-smoking (Tabelog).

places.cuisine: French courses with a dessert tree (prices include tax and service; official site, read November 2026) · lunch: Menu Avantarge, 8 dishes ¥5,900; Menu Luxueux, 11 dishes ¥7,800; Menu Prestige, 11 dishes with lobster and beef fillet ¥13,600 · dinner: Menu Saison, 12 dishes ¥9,200; Menu Gastoronomie ¥12,800; Menu Dégustation, all left to the chef ¥16,500; Menu Spécialité de Chef ¥22,000 (book two days ahead) · an August 2026 Avantarge: salmon tartare with summer vegetables, corn parfait, Spanish mackerel with crisp skin, granita, a choice of two mains, corn rice, house-baked breads, the dessert tree (any of eight desserts), coffee or tea, petits fours; beef cheek (October 2026), lamb carved at the table (September 2026), sanma mixed rice (October 2026) · a sommelier and wine pairings · birthday plates; a ¥2,800 children's meal (shrimp tempura or pasta)
places.notes: [French · Higashi-Shinsaibashi, courses in a former securities office] Through a heavy door, past the old vault door kept from the building's days as a securities company, a high-ceilinged room with a single tree reaching up from a stone floor laid like a river, and private rooms on a mezzanine. The courses change with the season, from an eight-dish lunch at ¥5,900 to a chef's surprise menu at ¥16,500, all with tax and service included, and end at the dessert tree, where you pick from about eight desserts, as many as you like (one diner who was full got tiny portions of each). Service is warm and funny: diners in 2026 describe staff and a sommelier who joke, remember returning guests, cut the lamb at the table and explain each dish. A favourite for birthdays and family celebrations; children are welcome in private rooms. Closed Mondays and the third Monday to Wednesday.

chef_bio.background: Per the official site, run under the name Cabinet2'H (copyright 2005–2009); courses only, prices including service and tax; staff recruitment notice and an Instagram account (site news, March 2026). An October 2026 diner says the building was formerly a securities company, its vault door still at the entrance. The listing is shop-maintained (corporate member) and says the kitchen is particular about vegetables and fish.
chef_bio.specialty: Seasonal French courses; the dessert tree.

anecdotes.text: "I was greeted by the imposing vault door, a remnant of its former life as a securities company." — October 2026.
"I wanted to try them all, but when I mentioned I was full, [the staff] kindly served me very small portions!" — September 2026, weekday lunch, on the dessert selection.
"I was informed that my sister isn't very fond of meat, so [the kitchen] prepared a low-temperature cooked chicken dish [instead]." — August 2026, a ¥5,900 lunch for a birthday.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト (french-2h.jp): ドゥアッシュ、東心斎橋1-7-18、地下鉄御堂筋線心斎橋駅5・6出口から徒歩7分、提携駐車場あり、ランチ11:30〜15:00 (L.O.13:30)、ディナー17:30〜22:30 (L.O.21:00)、定休日は月曜日と第3月曜日〜水曜日。ランチ: Menu Avantarge 8皿5,900円、Menu Luxueux 11皿7,800円、Menu Prestige 11皿13,600円 (魚料理はオマール海老、肉料理は牛フィレ肉)、料理とデザート、食後のお飲物と小菓子。ディナー: Menu Saison 12皿9,200円、Menu Gastoronomie 12皿12,800円、Menu Dégustation 16,500円 (料理長に全ておまかせ)、Menu Spécialité de Chef 22,000円 (前々日までに予約)、価格はすべてサービス料、消費税込み。デザートツリーからお好みのデザートを。2026年3月にお休みのお知らせ、Instagram開始。食べログ (店舗会員): フレンチ・洋食、アレルギーや苦手な食材 (牡蠣、生魚、貝、フォアグラ) は事前に、36席、個室 (4〜20名)、子どもは個室のみ、お子様料理2,800円、1人1ドリンク、サービス料10%込み、禁煙、ベジタリアンメニューあり、ソムリエ。口コミ(2026年8月〜10月): 証券会社だった建物の金庫の扉、天井まで伸びる木、川のような石の床、中二階の個室、デザートを好きなだけ、肉が苦手な人に低温調理の鶏、ラムをテーブルで切り分ける、楽しいスタッフ、誕生日のプレート。

places.cuisine: Tempura counter and standing bar using seafood bought daily at Osaka Kizu Market, fried in small batches in front of you (Tabelog; Gourmet Kineya press release) · weekday lunch sets with rice, red miso soup and free refills of boiled whitebait (press release; September 2026): the recommended set of seven tempura (shrimp, cod, scallop, eggplant, green pepper, daikon, pickled ginger) ¥770 (August and October 2026), chicken tempura set ¥880 (August 2026), the 幸おとこ set ("Sachi Otoko", four seafood and seven vegetable tempura; September 2026); large rice ¥50 more (August 2026) · at night: seven-piece bite-size tempura platter ¥500, large shrimp ¥320, soft-boiled egg tempura ¥120, rice ¥150, red miso soup ¥120 (September 2026); conger eel, mentaiko-and-nori roll, tofu tempura, sesame tofu, tomato, ginkgo nuts; tempura rice bowl at night too; ochazuke · salt and curry salt to dip · fried-tofu dishes and house-made tofu (Tabelog) · Maru F draft beer ¥480 (August 2026), Osaka local sake, happy-hour highballs: four highballs, seven tempura, ginkgo nuts and ochazuke for ¥2,000 (October 2026)
places.notes: [Tempura · Umeda underground, a tempura counter in Whity] A small U-shaped counter in the Whity Umeda underground mall where tempura is fried a few pieces at a time in front of you, from seafood bought each morning at Osaka Kizu Market. Gourmet Kineya opened it in February 2025 as a tempura izakaya named after the market. At lunch, a set of seven pieces (shrimp, cod, scallop, eggplant, pepper, daikon and red pickled ginger) with rice and red miso soup is ¥770, and the boiled whitebait is free to refill. After 15:00 it becomes a standing bar: a ¥500 plate of seven bite-size tempura, a ¥320 large shrimp, beer and Osaka sake, salt or curry salt to dip. A September 2026 diner found the pieces small but cheap; an October 2026 diner ate and drank four highballs for ¥2,000. One older regular says the same owner ran a tempura-bowl shop here twenty years ago (October 2026). No bookings.

roles: Counter staff of 株式会社グルメ杵屋レストラン (unnamed)
chef_bio.background: Per the Gourmet Kineya Restaurant press release (PR TIMES, 21 January 2025): a new izakaya format built on freshly fried tempura, opened at Whity Umeda on 20 February 2025, its main ingredients bought daily at Osaka Kizu Market; lunch sets of daily tempura named 「幸おとこ」 and 「幸むすめ」, free refills of boiled whitebait from the market, and bite-size tempura (豆天) at night. Per an October 2026 review: a regular of a cheap tempura-bowl shop here twenty years ago was told by staff that "the owner hasn't changed".
chef_bio.specialty: Tempura fried to order; lunch set with free whitebait.

places.notes: [Chinese · Umeda, tofu-and-yuba Chinese in Jizo Yokocho] The second shop of 梅香, a Chinese restaurant produced by the tofu-and-yuba chain Ume no Hana, opened in June 2025 in the Jizo Yokocho lane of Hankyu Sanbangai, a few steps from the Hankyu gates. Sets follow a one-soup, three-dish pattern and lean on the group's tofu and yuba: mapo tofu with a tofu salad, a soy-milk shrimp mayonnaise lighter than most, tofu shumai, yuba tempura. The favourite is yurinchi, fried chicken in a sweet-sour chilli sauce, alone or paired with mapo tofu in the ¥1,960 double-main set. Diners were mixed: good mapo and yurinchi, but a soggy fried rice, dishes that felt reheated and a cramped room (2026). Happy hour pours beer at ¥308. The shop cannot handle allergy requests.

places.cuisine: Wine bar and restaurant with wines by the glass chosen by a senior sommelier, served from a dispenser that keeps them fresh, and world draft beer (Tabelog) · weekday lunch buffet ¥2,200: salad bar, cold and hot starters, pizza, paella, curry, desserts and drinks, with a main chosen from Italian, French, German, American or Spanish dishes (Tabelog); cordon bleu and cowboy steak among the mains (October 2026); a steak lunch with fries about ¥2,150, no rice (August 2026); Belgian fries, pizza and pasta (August 2026) · courses with two hours of drinks: September–November course of charcuterie, Caesar salad, Italian fried chicken, roast pork and basil Genovese pasta with one craft beer and three wines ¥4,500 (listed down from ¥5,500); year-end course with two draft beers and a self-service wine buffet ¥5,000 (from ¥6,000) (Tabelog) · by the glass: Riesling, Napa Chardonnay (October 2026); a sparkling wine with cherry-blossom petals, ajillo and cheese (October 2026) · the fried chicken in the course singled out (July 2026)
places.notes: [Wine bar · Umekita, a big wine hall under Grand Front] A large, chandelier-lit wine restaurant in the basement of Grand Front Osaka's North Building, with sofa seats, private rooms and 120 seats, run by the ZATO group. Glasses come from a dispenser that keeps open bottles fresh, picked by a senior sommelier: Riesling, Napa Chardonnay, a sparkling wine with cherry-blossom petals (October 2026). Weekday lunch is a world buffet for ¥2,200, salad bar, pizza, paella and curry, plus a main from five countries such as cordon bleu or a cowboy steak. At night it fills with company parties on two-hour drink courses of charcuterie, Caesar salad, Italian fried chicken and roast pork from ¥4,500, the same courses as the neighbouring Sekai no Beer Hakubutsukan (August 2026). Book for evenings; a 10% service charge applies.

chef_bio.background: Per the shop-maintained Tabelog listing: a spacious floor with private and semi-private rooms, microphones and projectors for parties; world beers and wines; a dispenser that limits wine deterioration; glass wines chosen by a senior sommelier; chandeliers; opened 26 April 2013. The operator's page (zato.co.jp, ZATO group) lists the Grand Front Osaka shop as its only 世界のワイン博物館. An August 2026 diner notes the courses match those of the nearby Sekai no Beer Hakubutsukan.

places.cuisine: Seasonal Japanese by a chef with fifteen years of training, the menu rewritten every day (official site; Tabelog) · lunch (official site, ¥1,000 each with a small side dish, salad, soup and pickles): 牛黄味丼 of Saga black wagyu, 手つなぎ丼 (oyako-don of Ise red chicken), seafood bowl of three marinated fish; daily set ¥1,500 with two small dishes · dinner courses (Tabelog, tax included): 6 dishes ¥4,400, 8 dishes ¥5,500 (sashimi, braised beef tendon, Saikyo-miso grilled yellowtail, lotus root with mentaiko, umeboshi rice porridge, dessert), 9 dishes ¥6,600 (sashimi, lotus-root dumpling, shishamo, fried catfish from Shimonoseki, wagyu skirt with onion, umeboshi porridge, dessert) · à la carte from a scroll-like menu: three-kind sashimi, beef-tendon stew, octopus, cream croquettes, dobin-mushi even in summer (July 2026); dobin-mushi, sashimi and crab with lettuce in autumn (September 2025) · about seven beers including Sapporo Lager, Kaku highball, sake and shochu (July 2026; Tabelog)
places.notes: [Japanese · Umeda, a seasonal counter under the station buildings] A quiet Japanese restaurant at the far western end of the Osaka Ekimae Dai-1 Building basement, where "Ofukuro no Aji Imai", which fed office workers here for over forty years, merged with "Shiki no Aji Kishou" of the Tenjinbashi-suji arcade, whose chef Sato had cooked Japanese food for fifteen years (Tabelog). The site says the menu has changed every single day since opening. Lunch is a bargain: ¥1,000 for a Saga wagyu beef bowl, an oyako-don or a marinated seafood bowl, each with a small seasonal side dish, salad and soup. At night sit at the counter for sashimi, beef-tendon stew, cream croquettes or dobin-mushi, or book a course from ¥4,400. Diners call the chef imposing at first and chatty once the food comes out (July 2026); one found it pricey (March 2026). Smoking is allowed; weekends only by reservation, if at all.

chef_bio.chef_name: Sato (chef; romaji from Tabelog, kanji not given)
roles: Chef, formerly of "Shiki no Aji Kishou" just off the Tenjinbashi-suji shopping street (Tabelog)
chef_bio.background: Per the shop-maintained Tabelog listing: "Ofukuro no Aji Imai" served salarymen after work at the Osaka Ekimae building for over forty years from the Showa era and became "Imai Kishou" by merging with "Shiki no Aji Kishou", led by Chef Sato, who has mastered Japanese cuisine for fifteen years, just off the Tenjinbashi-suji shopping street; opened 19 September 2012. Per the official site (copyright SANAE.inc): no day since opening without a change to the menu. A July 2025 diner saw the owner handling lunch alone; a March 2026 diner praises the woman serving.
chef_bio.philosophy: "今井きしょうの料理は大人に残された清淡な遊びです" (Imai Kishou's cooking is a pure, light pleasure left for grown-ups; official site).
chef_bio.specialty: Saga wagyu beef bowl at lunch; seasonal sashimi; dobin-mushi.

anecdotes.text: "The Gyukoumi Don comes with a small side dish, salad, miso soup, and pickles for JPY 1000. … For this quality, JPY 1000 is an unbeatable value." — April 2026, a fifth visit.

places.notes: [Italian · Umeda, an osteria under the station buildings since 1998] A long-running Italian osteria in the basement of Osaka Ekimae Dai-4 Building, one of three Gaudente shops in Osaka and Kobe and a Tabelog Italian WEST 100 pick in 2021. The idea is an Italian izakaya: friendly staff, regional dishes "in true Italian portions" and wine from all over Italy (official site). Weekday lunch starts with pasta sets from ¥1,500, generous on seafood; since EXPO 2025 there is also a Serbian lunch of cheese or meat pies and cevapi from the Serbian Pavilion's restaurant. Dinner is a ¥4,880 prix-fixe or à la carte, and each autumn fresh porcini arrive from Italy for linguine, risotto or fritto (¥4,000, October 2026). It fills on Sundays, so book; diners praise the staff's memory and the handling of birthday-cake requests (October 2026).

Lunch is the easy way in: ten pieces of sushi with miso soup for ¥1,680 (October 2026), seafood bowls, or sets with a mini udon or chawanmushi. Reviews call the fish fresh and the room calm, but one July 2026 diner found the rice firm and the chawanmushi bland. It is one of the 魚萬 group's restaurants.

places.cuisine: Dim sum and small plates of Chinese, Hong Kong and Taiwanese food, with Thai, Vietnamese and Korean dishes and natural wine (official site; Tabelog) · lunch: Chinese congee with three dim sum ¥1,430 (September 2026), e.g. shrimp dumplings, xiao long bao and fish-roe shumai with pickled mustard greens in the congee (October 2026); seasonal mushroom congee (September 2026); Hainan chicken rice with two dim sum ¥1,600, coriander optional (June 2026); daily plate such as yurinchi (October 2026); a limited sweet-and-sour pork lunch with soup, dessert and free large jasmine rice (October 2026) · dim sum named in reviews: tobiko shumai, seafood dumplings, shark-fin dumplings · dinner courses with two hours of drinks (Tabelog, tax included): Taiwanese casual course of dim sum, spring rolls, Taiwanese fried chicken and fried rice ¥5,500; Chinese course with black-vinegar sweet-and-sour pork, steamed buns and sesame balls ¥6,600; Hong Kong omakase course ¥7,700 · natural wines and original drinks (Tabelog)
places.notes: [Dim sum · Umekita Park, a park café of dim sum] A bright café-restaurant in a pavilion of Umekita Park at Grand Green Osaka, next to the Waldorf Astoria, opened in September 2024; the other SIK eatery is by Utsubo Park. The concept is a Chinese restaurant a woman can walk into alone (official site): dim sum by a chef from well-known restaurants, Chinese, Hong Kong and Taiwanese small plates, and natural wine. Lunch is the favourite: a bowl of gentle congee with three steaming dim sum for ¥1,430, or Hainan chicken rice, ordered by QR code. Dogs are welcome on the terrace and, at set hours, inside; at weekends it opens at 8:00. You can borrow a picnic set and take a bottle of wine into the park. Book for lunch; the room is small and popular.

roles: Dim sum chef with experience at well-known restaurants (unnamed; Tabelog)
chef_bio.background: Per the official site (sik-eatery.com, read 2026-11-01): a café and restaurant based on Chinese, Hong Kong and Taiwanese food, also Thai, Vietnamese and Korean; the concept is a Chinese restaurant a woman can enter alone; renamed from "CAFE" to "eatery" in April 2024; two shops, うつぼ公園店 and グラングリーン大阪店 (opened September 2024); the Grand Green shop is a small-plate Chinese bar in Umekita Park with takeaway, opened-bottle wine sales and free picnic-set loans; featured in SAVVY (October and November 2026 issues), Meets Regional (April 2026) and まっぷる 大阪'27. Per Tabelog: a variety of dim sum "crafted by a chef with extensive experience at renowned restaurants".
chef_bio.philosophy: "日常の中にある“非日常”な「食」の体験" (an out-of-the-ordinary food experience within everyday life; official site).

anecdotes.text: "The shumai has a chunky meat texture, and when you bite into it, the rich flavor bursts out." — October 2026, Hainan chicken rice with tobiko shumai and seafood dumplings.

places.cuisine: Busan-style nakkopse: a red hot pot of octopus, offal and shrimp, in four levels of spice, eaten with free refills of bean-sprout namul, seaweed and kimchi (Tabelog; 2026 reviews) · naksamse with pork belly (August–September 2026) · add more offal, shrimp, octopus or ramen noodles; finish with bokkeumbap, rice fried in the leftover broth, with cheese and flying-fish roe (Tabelog; September 2026) · minari or celery chijimi (July–September 2026) · kongguksu in summer (July 2026) · many makgeolli, alcoholic and non-alcoholic, and Korean drinks (Tabelog)
places.notes: [Korean · Kitahorie, Busan-style nakkopse] A small Kitahorie shop, three minutes from Yotsubashi, devoted to nakkopse, the Busan hot pot of octopus, offal and shrimp in a bright red broth. Pick one of four spice levels (one diner found mild barely spicy, another regretted the hot one), eat it over rice with free refills of bean-sprout namul, seaweed and kimchi, and finish by frying rice in what is left, with cheese and flying-fish roe on top. Diners in 2026 singled out the sweet, tender offal and the crisp minari chijimi; there are plenty of makgeolli to drink. Orders go through your phone; the menu and some staff are in Korean. The room is small and seating is 90 minutes, so book. Closed Mondays.

chef_bio.background: Shop-maintained Tabelog listing: authentic nakkopse from Korea with plump octopus, juicy offal and shrimp; bokkeumbap fried until crisp to finish; a wide range of makgeolli and Korean drinks; Hangul name 정낙지 on the listing. Opened 26 September 2023.
chef_bio.specialty: Nakkopse; bokkeumbap with cheese; minari chijimi.

anecdotes.text: "Nakkopuse has four levels of spiciness, and I chose medium, which wasn't too spicy for me—it was just right." — July 2026.
"I've tried Nakkopuse at various places, but I think the horumon here is the sweetest and the most delicious." — October 2026, a repeat visit.
"For the finale, I had Bokkeumbap with cheese topping, which was filled with tobiko and tasted amazing!" — September 2026, a first nakkopse.

places.notes: [Kaiseki · Nishi-Shinsaibashi, a hidden flat on the 9th floor] A reservation-only Japanese restaurant hidden in a flat on the ninth floor of an apartment building behind the Hotel Nikko, made over into tatami and table rooms for two up to 28, quiet enough that, the listing says, celebrities come incognito. The house dish is a Kyoto duck hot pot of duck raised in Kyotanba, finished with handmade soba (¥7,700 with all-you-can-drink in November 2025); otherwise take the ten-dish seasonal kaiseki, with thick-cut sashimi and steamed kinmedai. Diners praise the value and the staff, who dimmed the lights for elderly guests at one party (August 2026); one found the walls between rooms thin. Bookings are getting harder (April 2026); cancellations the day before are charged in full. Closed Sundays and holidays.

chef_bio.background: Shop-maintained Tabelog listing: a reservation-only restaurant in a converted flat behind the Nikko Hotel, with tatami rooms and tables, kaiseki and Kyoto duck hot pot; ducks raised from chicks in Kyotanba's clean water and air and shipped direct from a Kyoto duck farm; "even celebrities visit incognito"; sister shop Rilegalo. Neighbours in the same building: LiLo Coffee Roasters on 1F (osaka_lilo_coffee_roasters_shinsaibashi) and Pesca on 10F (osaka_pesca_shinsaibashi), per their address_ja in data.
chef_bio.specialty: Kyoto duck hot pot; seasonal kaiseki.

anecdotes.text: "The staff was incredibly attentive, adjusting the lighting for the elderly guests and showing great care throughout our visit." — August 2026, a private dinner for twelve.
"The soba noodles served at the end were handmade, and the broth was so delicious that I drank every last drop." — January 2026, the duck hot pot.
"I've noticed that for about a month now, it's become difficult to make a reservation without booking in advance." — April 2026, a regular.

places.notes: [Taiwanese · Higashi-Shinsaibashi, the stone-pot hot pot] A long-running Taiwanese restaurant on a Higashi-Shinsaibashi corner, its walls lined with celebrity autographs, where regulars of ten and even thirty years come back for the stone-pot hot pot: pork, seafood, squid balls and vegetables stir-fried in sesame oil in front of you, then simmered in a gentle chicken-bone broth that diners drink by the bowl, with noodles to finish (¥4,730 a person with three starters). Do not skip the homemade oyster spring rolls, crisp outside and soft inside, the dried-radish omelette, or the shijimi clams steeped a week in house soy sauce. The chef trained at Tsuji Culinary Institute and in Taipei and Kaohsiung, and diners call the owner-chef friendly. Chinese spoken. Closed Sundays except in December.

The site describes a long-established shop (老舗) with many regulars and celebrity autographs on the walls, featured in the media, including the TV programme どやメシ紀行. Tabelog adds that the chef travels to Taiwan regularly. Reviews: regulars of more than 10 years (April 2025) and 30 years (October 2025); "the owner-chef is very friendly" (August 2026).
chef_bio.specialty: Stone-pot hot pot; oyster spring rolls; soy-marinated shijimi.

places.notes: [French · Higashi-Shinsaibashi, a 30-year bistro] A small French restaurant up a flight of stairs east of the クリスタ長堀 underground mall, open for about 30 years by the staff's count and still cooking one omakase course of the season, booked two days ahead. In August 2026 that meant bright seasonal-vegetable appetizers, a cold soup in a big bowl, crisp-skinned fish and a tender steak; the 2024 menus ran to wild-boar gratin, stone bass with firefly squid and a sirloin-cap tartare. It is a place people return to for decades: one couple came back on the anniversary of a first date there 23 years before (2023), and business diners call it consistent. Lunch ran about ¥3,000–4,000 and dinner ¥10,000–15,000 with wine in 2026. Counter seats are comfortable for one. Closed Mondays.

chef_bio.background: The official site (© 2012) states that the restaurant works by reservation with an omakase course, booked two days ahead. An August 2026 diner was told by the staff that it opened about 30 years ago; a 2023 diner had a first date there 23 years earlier.

places.notes: [Italian · Nishi-Shinsaibashi, fresh-pasta lunch and afternoon tea in a hotel] The second-floor restaurant of the Tokyu Stay Mercure Osaka Namba, a calm room above a lobby busy with overseas travellers (October 2026), open from lunch through afternoon tea to dinner. The weekday lunch is the draw: pick one of a dozen fresh pastas, the noodles sent from Awaji Island each morning, and help yourself to the baker's breads, croissants of fermented butter, and six deli salads, soft drinks included, from ¥2,900. Afternoons are for seasonal afternoon tea (¥6,000 in autumn 2026, Shine Muscat and chestnut) and large fruit parfaits; evenings for set courses from ¥5,500, with a whole cake on the anniversary course. Diners praise the bread, the smiling staff and the value; the buffet can queue at busy times (June 2026).

places.notes: [Yakiniku · Nipponbashi, whole-cattle A5 wagyu on a thick teppan, noon to midnight] The Nipponbashi branch of Manryo, a yakiniku name diners know from its other Osaka shops (reviewers mention Minami-Morimachi and Tenma), on Sakaisuji near Kuromon Market and open straight from noon to midnight. The beef is A5 black wagyu bought whole, so the menu reaches into rare cuts, and it cooks on a thick iron plate that you rub with beef fat as you go, with a printed guide to grilling times. Order the Nipponbashi-only negi shio tan, thick tongue under green-onion salt, then the phantom kalbi if it isn't sold out and the 20-second shabu-yaki loin dipped in egg; finish with stone-grilled bibimbap and the big clam-and-seaweed soup. A regular on an eighth visit (September 2026) calls the tongue a favourite. Lunch is quiet but at evening prices. One August 2026 diner missed an explanation of the grill and found the service mechanical; another was puzzled at first at cleaning the plate during the meal.

roles: Branch manager and staff unnamed in every source read
chef_bio.background: Opened 11 January 2023 (Tabelog). Reviewers know Manryo from other Osaka branches, including Minami-Morimachi, and note that closing days differ by location (2026). A December 2025 reviewer says the shop buys whole A5 black-wagyu cattle; a September 2026 reviewer names Kyushu and Hyogo wagyu. Diners describe staff who take orders in person rather than by tablet and a manager overseeing the room well (August 2026).
chef_bio.specialty: Nipponbashi-only negi shio tan; phantom kalbi; 20-second shabu-yaki loin.

places.notes: [Yakiniku · Higashi-Shinsaibashi, a 1964 Shizuoka yakiniku's Osaka shop] The Osaka outpost, opened in 2019, of a Shizuoka yakiniku founded in 1964 and, per its Tabelog text, popular with baseball and soccer players. A lively, old-style room near Nagahoribashi with a counter, tables and a shoes-off tatami area, where you grill domestic black wagyu chosen by the owner over charcoal shichirin in rising smoke. The thick-cut tongue steak is limited to ten a day; diners in 2026 also praise the thick, tender negi tan shio, the premium outside skirt, the toro yukhoe and the choice of kimchi, and finish with the house cold noodles and makgeolli. Portions are generous and drinks are on the dear side (August 2026); one September 2026 diner found the cuts too fatty. Smoking is allowed, and booking is wise.

chef_bio.background: Per the Tabelog shop text: founded in 1964, a popular Shizuoka restaurant frequented by many gourmet celebrities, including baseball and soccer players, where booking is a must; it opened in Shinsaibashi on 14 September 2019, focusing on high-quality domestic black wagyu chosen by the owner. A September 2026 reviewer has been to other Nandaimon branches. Diners describe a cheerful welcome and friendly staff (2026).
chef_bio.specialty: Thick-cut tongue steak (10 a day); premium salted tongue; cold noodles.

anecdotes.text: "I've seen many yakiniku restaurants with the name \"Nandaimon,\" but this one is a long-established popular spot from Shizuoka that has made its way to Osaka, and you can really taste the quality." — August 2026.

"It was great that we could choose from different types of kimchi, and the meat was incredibly delicious!" — September 2026.

places.cuisine: Vietnamese home and street cooking by a Vietnamese chef, Tam, with Vietnamese fermented seasonings, in a room styled on Mekong garden restaurants with decor brought from Vietnam (Tabelog) · lunch sets: pho with rice ¥1,300, nine pho and noodle choices, two rice choices, with pickles and a sweet (September 2026); braised pork (kakuni) set ¥1,300 (October 2026); healthy lunch set ¥1,950 with fresh and fried spring rolls, chicken pho, green-papaya salad on shrimp chips and coconut chè (September 2026) · pho of boiled beef shank or braised tendon, chicken pho, bún bò Huế, mixed noodles, shrimp-salt rice; coriander refilled free on request (2026) · fresh spring rolls of shrimp and pork with two sauces, stir-fried pork tongue, duck hot pot with taro and pork belly, goat dishes (2026) · courses, tax included: Vietnam course ¥3,500 (11 items), Anngon course ¥5,000 (13 items), all-you-can-drink to add (Tabelog) · lotus tea, lychee-yogurt drink, draft beer ¥620
places.notes: [Vietnamese · Minami-Semba, pho and spring rolls since 1998] A Vietnamese restaurant up a narrow stair near Shinsaibashi, open since 1998 and cooked by a Vietnamese chef, Tam, in a room dressed with things brought from Vietnam to evoke the Mekong's garden restaurants. Lunch fills fast: choose one of nine pho or noodle bowls with a rice dish (¥1,300), or the ¥1,950 healthy set of fresh and fried spring rolls, chicken pho, green-papaya salad and chè, and ask for more coriander, which is free. The fresh spring rolls of shrimp and pork are the house signature, one October 2026 diner's best in Osaka; at night come in a group for duck hot pot, goat or stir-fried pork tongue. Some find it tuned to Japanese tastes; one September 2026 diner lost a bowl of broth cleared too fast.

roles: Vietnamese chef "Tam" (Tabelog; no full name or kanji given)
chef_bio.background: Opened 12 April 1998 (Tabelog); a September 2026 reviewer counts 28 years. Per the Tabelog shop text, authentic Vietnamese dishes by Chef Tam, made with Vietnamese fermented seasonings and local ingredients by traditional methods, in a space inspired by the garden restaurants of the Mekong with every decorative item chosen in Vietnam.
chef_bio.philosophy: "A mini trip to Vietnam" (Tabelog shop text).
chef_bio.specialty: Fresh spring rolls; pho; bún bò Huế; duck hot pot.

anecdotes.text: "The signature fresh spring rolls are packed with shrimp and vegetables, offering a variety of flavors with fish sauce and sesame. Personally, I think they are the best in Osaka." — October 2026.
"Additionally, when I asked the staff, I was delighted to find out that cilantro is available for free refills! It was a cilantro festival, indeed!" — September 2026, healthy lunch set ¥1,950.
"The Bun Bo Hue was a Vietnamese dish I had been wanting to try for a long time; it was slightly spicy with chewy noodles, and it tasted fantastic!" — September 2026.

Happy hour beer and highball ¥200 (September 2026). places.cuisine: Skewers grilled on a teppan and finished with a splash of dashi, eaten with the house sauces (Tabelog) · sauces: plum soy, the original sauce, sesame miso, salt (October 2026) · courses: 8-skewer course with salad, small dish and rice ¥2,800 (listed from ¥3,850; ochazuke or egg on rice +¥200); skewer bar set of three skewers and a drink ¥1,500 (listed from ¥2,250); 10 skewers and 15 dishes with 90-minute all-you-can-drink ¥5,000 (listed from ¥7,200; booking only) (Tabelog, tax included) · ¥2,000 course of six skewers with salad, a small dish, white or 15-grain rice and miso soup, refills free (September–October 2026) · skewers named in 2026 reviews: shrimp, shrimp mayo, lotus root, quail egg in bacon, burdock in bacon, chicken wings, yam chicken roll, pork-wrapped maitake, celery-wrapped pork, salmon and beef, squid, shiso chicken, eel, ginkgo, zucchini, asparagus · sorbet to finish · non-alcoholic drinks ¥490 (October 2026)
places.notes: [Teppan skewers · Umeda, Hankyu Sanbangai B2F] A cosy counter-and-tables shop in the Hankyu Sanbangai basement, from Unzen, a Kitashinchi skewer house that diners date to 1950. Skewers of meat, seafood and vegetables are cooked on a teppan rather than over charcoal, splashed with dashi, and set down two at a time beside the sauce that suits each one: plum soy, the house sauce, sesame miso or salt. It runs all day with one menu, so a ¥2,000 course of six skewers with salad, rice and miso soup works as a late lunch, and a ¥1,500 set of three skewers and a drink as a quick stop. Booking ahead earns small extras like a sorbet or an extra skewer. Several 2026 reviews mention attentive staff from overseas who explain each skewer. Quiet on some weekend afternoons.

roles: Staff and manager (unnamed in the sources read)
chef_bio.origin: A branch of Unzen, whose main shop is in Kitashinchi (May 2026 review); the business dates from 1950 (August 2026 review: "Established in 1950"; October 2026 review: "over 50 years of history").
chef_bio.background: Shop text (Tabelog): each skewer carefully grilled on an iron plate and finished with a splash of dashi, "fluffy and piping hot"; an original sauce; open continuously with a full menu; a sister restaurant, Kushiage Mono Shun, in LUCUA. A June 2026 diner who knew the Kitashinchi counter writes that the owner there "cooks everything with great care".
chef_bio.philosophy: Light skewers, fluffy and hot from the teppan (Tabelog).
chef_bio.specialty: Teppan skewers with dashi; sauce pairings.

"First, they served edamame and fresh raw vegetables including cabbage, daikon radish, carrot, and green onion." — August 2026, the ¥1,500 skewer bar set.

places.cuisine: Standing bar for domestic tiger fugu: only Japanese fish of 1.2 kg or more, prepared in the shop (official site); fish from the central market (Tabelog), mainly from Kumamoto and Nagasaki (October 2026) · official menu: tessa from ¥528, tecchiri ¥968, fugu zosui ¥748; no courses · tessa ¥480 (September and October 2026); small tecchiri pot; fugu skin; kara-age, tempura and fugu nigiri; grilled matsutake; oden (2026 reviews) · homemade ponzu (Tabelog) · about 30 sakes (Tabelog) or over 40 brands (October 2026); all-you-can-drink sake ¥1,408 Monday–Wednesday, ¥550 more at weekends (October 2026); chilled hirezake (fin sake) · a long fugu evening came to ¥8,998, a lighter one about ¥3,000 (September–October 2026)
places.notes: [Fugu · Umeda, a standing fugu bar] A second-floor standing bar a minute from Hankyu Umeda that sells domestic tiger fugu at drinking-bar prices: tessa sashimi from about ¥500, a hot pot just under ¥1,000 and a rice-porridge finish, plus fugu skin, kara-age, tempura and nigiri. The owner, 島本 一樹, opened it in September 2025 at 39 after appearing on the TV pitch show Reiwa no Tora, wanting fugu to be an everyday dish rather than a special-occasion one (official site). Sake runs to 30–40 kinds with a cheap all-you-can-drink, and the chilled fin sake is a favourite. Diners found the fugu as good as at a regular fugu restaurant (October 2026) and the owner friendly. No seats, no courses; an hour after work is the idea. Closed Thursdays.

chef_bio.background: Official site (read 2026-11-01), the owner's timeline: 2004, part-time at a seafood restaurant; 2006, full-time there, later running it; from 2009, experience at several mostly Japanese restaurants; 2014, part-time at a fugu and crab specialist, then its manager; 2015, went independent with an izakaya that later failed; 2016, opened a fugu specialist; 2018, a bento shop and a standing bar, then a move to Nishiyodogawa; February 2025, appeared on "令和の虎" and won full backing ("完全ALL"); September 2025, opened 大阪ふぐ太郎, aged 39. The site: "ふぐ料理は高級で格式高い。そんなイメージを変えたくて、この店を始めました。" Reviews: "The owner has a friendly demeanor" (October 2026); "the trendy spot that appeared on 'Reiwa no Tora'" (October 2026).
chef_bio.philosophy: "ふぐを特別な日だけの料理にしない" — fugu should not be only for special days (official site).

anecdotes.text: "The cheapest sashimi (tessa) in Osaka is an astonishing JPY 480. All-you-can-drink Japanese sake is JPY 1408 on Mondays, Tuesdays, and Wednesdays." — October 2026.
"Including the Hirezake, the quality was on par with any regular fugu restaurant." — October 2026, a ¥8,998 evening of sashimi, skin, hot pot, sushi and tempura.
"The owner has a friendly demeanor, and the chilled Hirezake is easy to drink and incredibly delicious!" — October 2026.

places.cuisine: Japanese food and sake: a chef with 30 years' experience, sake chosen by a sake-diploma holder (Tabelog) · the Fusae Set, a little of everything seasonal (meat, sashimi, simmered and fried dishes), with sea urchin and salmon roe for ¥500 more (Tabelog; October 2026) · a 6-dish course with 90-minute all-you-can-drink ¥4,000 (Tabelog; August 2026); a sake all-you-can-drink course (August 2026) · dishes in 2026 reviews: four kinds of sashimi, kisu tempura, chilled pork shabu, fried sardine cake, dote-yaki, Osaka-age (August); shumai, chicken skirt, smoked cheese (July); kakiage (June); obanzai; oden, dashimaki, roast beef, toro-taku, chashu, eggplant and okra simmered (October) · sake list changing with the season
places.notes: [Izakaya · Umeda, Osaka Station Front Building No. 2 B1F] A small sake-and-Japanese-food bar in the basement of Osaka Station Front Building No. 2, the main shop of a three-shop group in the station-front buildings (Tabelog). The cooking comes from a chef with thirty years behind the stove, the sake from a holder of a sake diploma, and the signature Fusae Set puts a little of everything on one tray, sashimi, tempura, meat and simmered dishes, with sea urchin and salmon roe as a ¥500 extra. Obanzai, oden, shumai and fried sardine cakes fill the board, and a ¥4,000 course with 90 minutes of drinks makes it an easy office party. Diners praise friendly, energetic staff; one July 2026 group was asked for last orders 90 minutes after sitting down. Cash only; book same-day by phone.

The room is large and calm with sofas and Osaka-themed art. A July 2026 diner noted that most staff come from overseas and speak good Japanese; a September 2026 diner saw many European hotel guests. No lunch on Wednesdays.

places.gf_detail: Ask when booking. No gluten information. A fish-led Japanese kitchen: sashimi, grilled eel and dobin-mushi sit beside tempura and dishes in dashi and soy-based sauces; nothing is described as gluten-free.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: seasonal fish, eel, crab and beef, with dashi-based dishes throughout.

places.cuisine: Seasonal Japanese cooking, à la carte or as a course (2026 reviews) · seasonal course ¥12,000 (September 2026); a sake-pairing course (October 2026) · autumn 2026: assorted sashimi, dobin-mushi of matsutake and conger eel, crab with sweet potato in a thick sauce, scallop and sea-urchin tempura, crab miso, grilled eel both shirayaki and with sauce, Chateaubriand, grilled rice balls, wasanbon ice cream (September–October 2026) · summer 2026: hamo with fine bone-cutting, ayu, wild eel, a lotus-root dumpling, sweet grilled asparagus (June 2026) · sake from around Japan, e.g. Nabeshima and Kuro Ryu (June 2026); a five-sake selection on staff advice (September 2026) · diners report ¥6,000–¥19,999 a head (2026)
places.notes: [Japanese · Shinsaibashi, a 1987 counter for seasonal à la carte] On the fifth floor of a building near Daimaru, a calm Japanese room with a fifteen-seat counter and two semi-private tatami rooms, open since 1987. One diner says the way to eat here is à la carte from a long seasonal list with no prices shown: in autumn 2026 dobin-mushi of matsutake and conger eel, crab with sweet potato, scallop and sea-urchin tempura, eel grilled two ways and Chateaubriand, finished with grilled rice balls and wasanbon ice cream; in summer, finely bone-cut hamo, ayu and wild eel. There is also a ¥12,000 seasonal course and a sake pairing, and staff explain each dish and suggest sake from around Japan. Old Western classics play in a Japanese room (June 2026). Used for business dinners and for entertaining overseas guests (October 2026). Closed Sundays.

chef_bio.background: Shop-maintained (corporate-member) Tabelog listing; opened 2 March 1987; the listing says the kitchen is particular about fish and about sake and shochu. No owner or chef is named in the sources read, and no official site was found.
chef_bio.specialty: Seasonal à la carte; eel; dobin-mushi.

places.gf_detail: Ask when booking. The site says courses are built around each guest's preferences and allergies, but nothing is called gluten-free; courses include bread, and the fish course at dinner comes in a donabe with a sauce meant for bread.
places.vegan_detail: Ask when booking. Vegetables from contract farms open every course and the site promises courses adjusted to preferences, but the courses are built on fish and meat (wagyu, venison, Iberico pork) and no vegan menu is listed.

Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners, UnionPay) and QR (PayPay, d Barai, Rakuten Pay, au PAY); no e-money (Tabelog). 26 seats (Tabelog; 28 on the official site), tables set apart, semi-private curtained spaces for 2 to 8; non-smoking, smoking on the terrace; wheelchair accessible; children welcome, children's plate ¥2,800 booked ahead, no high chairs or changing tables (Tabelog). On the 6th floor; the lift is at the back of the building (September 2026).

places.cuisine: French courses built on vegetables from contract farms, fish sent straight from the market and wagyu, venison and Iberico pork (official site; prices include tax and service, read November 2026) · lunch: full-course lunch ¥5,000 online (normally ¥6,000), the lighter Déjeuner ¥4,000 (limited days), chef's courses A ¥9,500, B ¥12,500, C ¥16,500 · dinner: Petit Bonheur ¥6,000, Menu Bonheur ¥7,500, Gourmand ¥8,000 online, chef's courses A ¥9,500, B ¥12,500, C ¥16,500 with luxury ingredients; anniversary courses with a message on the dessert plate · wine pairings of three or four glasses chosen by the chef and sommelier · 2026 dishes: an opening plate of rare, colourful vegetables each explained, sea urchin and tomato jelly, onion potage, chestnut soup, fish in a donabe at dinner, aged venison, beef with optional foie gras, matcha desserts (June–October 2026)
places.notes: [French · Shinsaibashi, a 1980 hideaway above the arcade] A minute from Daimaru, up a lift at the back of a building to the sixth floor, a French restaurant founded in 1980 that calls itself a hideaway for 45 years. The site's promise is a relaxed room rather than hotel formality, and the second-generation owner 下村 runs it with chef 中川. Courses open with a plate of rare vegetables from contract farms, each explained at the table, then fish sent straight from the market (cooked in a donabe at dinner) and meat such as wagyu or venison, with foie gras as an extra; repeat guests are promised different dishes. Lunch from ¥4,000, dinner from ¥6,000, tax and service included. Popular for birthdays and anniversaries: diners in 2026 describe messages written on dessert plates, photos taken at the table and a celebration plate for a wedding. Closed Mondays and one other day a month.

chef_bio.chef_name: 中川 (chef; surname only, as written)
roles: Owner: 下村, second generation (official site: 店主 下村, 2代目店主)
chef_bio.background: Per the official site: the founder joined 志摩観光ホテル at 賢島 in Mie, gained service experience at a French restaurant in Osaka, and founded Amitie in 1980 with a dozen-odd seats, moving into this building's 6th floor when it was completed in 1988. The second-generation owner keeps the founder's idea of a relaxed place for real French food, alongside a chef "who loves food and wine too much". Vegetables come from contract farms that build the soil to grow Italian vegetables; wagyu and venison are carefully handled to remove gaminess; fish arrives straight from the market. The site aims to build each course around the guest's tastes and allergies and to serve repeat guests different dishes.
chef_bio.philosophy: Not hotel-style formality but a relaxed room, kind-to-the-body ingredients and real French food; forget about manners, wine orders and dress codes (official site).
chef_bio.specialty: Vegetable starter plates; fish in a donabe; anniversary courses.

anecdotes.text: "The owner's thoughtful hospitality makes me feel as if I've returned home" — August 2026, a second visit.
"I visited this restaurant for a memorable anniversary dinner on the day we registered our marriage." — August 2026, aged venison main.
"Be careful, as the elevator is located at the back." — September 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト (ami-gr1980.com): 1980年創業 フランス料理のお店、心斎橋 大丸より徒歩1分、ビル6階の隠れ家、隠れ続けて45年、店主 下村 シェフ 中川。どんなお店: 三重県賢島の志摩観光ホテルに入社後、大阪のフランス料理店でサービスの経験を積み、1980年に「アミチェ」を創業、当初は10数席、1988年に今のビルができて移転、先代の気持ちを大切に2代目店主として、料理とワインが好きすぎるシェフと共に、契約農家の自然野菜、黒毛和牛や鹿肉、イベリコ豚、市場直送の魚、ディナーの魚料理は土鍋仕立て、記念日コースはデザートの皿にメッセージ、好みやアレルギーを考慮してコースを作る、2回目以降は違った料理を。ランチ: フルコースランチ5,000円 (通常6,000円、ネット予約)、シェフおまかせコース A 9,500円・B 12,500円・C 16,500円、デジュネ4,000円 (数量・曜日限定)。ディナー: シェフおまかせコース A 9,500円・B 12,500円・C 16,500円、グルマンコース8,000円 (ネット限定)、ムニュ・ボヌール7,500円、プチ・ボヌール6,000円。店舗情報: ラ・シーンビル6F、ランチ L.O. 13時30分、ディナー L.O. 19時30分、21時30分閉店、月曜定休 (祝日の場合は翌日) と不定休月1回、28席、カーテンスペース2〜8名、各種カードと QR 決済。クリスマス (12月19日〜26日) は限定コースのみ。食べログ (店舗会員): フレンチ、税・サービス料10%込み、26席、半個室、禁煙 (テラスで喫煙可)、車椅子可、お子様プレート2,800円、ソムリエ。口コミ(2026年6月〜10月): 珍しい野菜の前菜を一つずつ説明、ウニとトマトのジュレ、玉ねぎのポタージュ、栗のスープ、熟成した鹿肉、フォアグラの追加、デザートにお祝いのメッセージ、写真を撮ってくれる、エレベーターは奥。

cultural_comfort.note: Set courses explained dish by dish; book online through the official site. No English evidence found.

Reservations only for the 18:00 opening (Tabelog). The Sunday lunch draws a queue: 5 to 10 or more people before 11:30, and an hour's wait for later arrivals (May–June 2026); evenings can be quiet (June 2026). Cards and QR accepted; no e-money; no service charge (Tabelog). Seating: 3–4 at the counter, two tables for four and a raised table for five or six (2026 reviews). Non-smoking; no small children (Tabelog). No rice dishes, as a sign at the door says (August 2026).

places.cuisine: Hand-cut soba with sake and small dishes (2026 reviews) · five kinds of soba, chosen per serving (about 130 g): seiro, coarse-ground seiro, coarse-ground inaka, sarashina and grilled buckwheat; 十割 and 二八 at the same price; the day's choice varies (October 2026) · もり蕎麦 ¥950 (April and June 2026), two servings ¥1,900; duck soba ¥1,700 (May 2026); 100%-buckwheat duck dipping soba ¥1,900 (January 2026); grated-yam bukkake; spicy grated-daikon soba; matcha soba (May 2026) · small dishes: 板わさ with wasabi and sea-urchin miso ¥480, 辛味大根じゃこおろし ¥480, ホタルイカ沖漬け ¥480 (June 2026), soba-yaki-miso ¥550, dashimaki ¥750, sobagaki ¥1,150 (2026), Kyoto sawara ¥1,800, Toyama firefly squid with vinegar miso ¥900 (April 2026) · sake by the 180 ml from ¥1,600; Yebisu bottles ¥700; umeshu ¥700
places.notes: [Soba · Shinmachi, a couple's soba bar for sake and noodles] A calm, clean Japanese-modern room on a Shinmachi street, run by a couple (as diners in 2022 and June 2026 describe it), with a few counter seats, tables and a small raised area, and jazz playing. The soba is the point: up to five kinds a day, from white, delicate sarashina to dark coarse-ground inaka, with 100% buckwheat (十割) costing the same as the 80/20 blend (二八), and a sign at the door saying there are no rice dishes. Evenings are for sake and small plates first (itawasa with sea-urchin miso, fiery karami daikon, firefly squid, sobagaki, dashimaki), then a plate of cold soba from ¥950. Lunch is Sundays only, with a queue before 11:30. Open Thursday to Sunday evenings; book for the 18:00 start.

roles: Run by a couple (unnamed): "the couple who runs the restaurant" (December 2022 review), "The restaurant is run by a couple" (June 2026 review)
chef_bio.background: No official site found and the Tabelog listing is not shop-maintained; the facts come from the listing and 2026 reviews. A December 2022 diner and a June 2026 diner both describe a couple running the shop. The soba line-up changes with the seasons (January 2026 review).
chef_bio.specialty: Mori soba in five grinds; duck dipping soba; sobagaki.

anecdotes.text: "The restaurant is run by a couple, creating a warm and inviting atmosphere." — June 2026, first in line for Sunday lunch.

"十割も二八も値段が同じなのが凄い" (that 十割 and 二八 cost the same is amazing) — June 2026, もり蕎麦 950円 each.

places.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information. Sashimi and the saba sushi (made to be eaten without soy sauce, August 2026) are the plainest; tempura, simmered fish and miso soup use wheat batter or soy-based seasonings.

Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners); no e-money or QR; no table charge (Tabelog). 40 seats over three floors (August 2026), with a counter on the 1F and tatami private rooms for 8, 12 and 20; non-smoking (Tabelog). places.cuisine: Osaka sushi and fish izakaya, known for its saba sushi (battera) (2026 reviews) · saba sushi topped with a leaf (a "mint-like" leaf, July 2026) and a hint of sansho (August 2026), made to be eaten without soy sauce; a half order is ten pieces (July–August 2026); to take away · a ¥4,400 course: appetizers, four kinds of sashimi, chawanmushi, simmered fish (sea bream with burdock), three tempura with vegetables, saba sushi; all-you-can-drink can be added (July–August 2026) · à la carte: tuna, salmon and scallop sashimi; tekka maki and toro-taku maki; dobin-mushi of matsutake (October 2026); hamo and corn tempura, eggplant dengaku, dashimaki, steamed sea-bream bones, grilled sea-bream head, red miso soup (2026) · imo shochu and sake · two people with two drinks each spent just over ¥8,000 (July 2026)
places.notes: [Sushi · Ura Namba, an old sushi house famous for battera] Tucked into a back alley behind Namba Grand Kagetsu, a three-storey sushi house with a genuine retro feel, a counter downstairs and tatami rooms above, which an August 2026 diner dates to 1955. It is known above all for saba sushi: a battera with a leaf on top and a hint of sansho, eaten without soy sauce, ten pieces even as a half order, and sold to take away. The ¥4,400 course runs from sashimi and chawanmushi through simmered sea bream and tempura to the saba sushi; à la carte there are tuna and salmon sashimi, tekka maki, dobin-mushi in autumn and steamed sea-bream bones. One regular was on a 45th visit in October 2026; another found the place empty on a Saturday night and called it too well hidden. Prices are modest. Closed Sundays and holidays.

roles: Owner and chef (unnamed; "the hospitality from the owner was warm and kind", August 2026)
chef_bio.background: Shop-maintained (corporate-member) Tabelog listing; no opening date is given there. An August 2026 diner says the restaurant has been around since 1955, and calls the retro feel genuine, not manufactured. The listing says the kitchen is particular about fish, sake and shochu.
chef_bio.specialty: Saba sushi (battera); simmered sea bream; the ¥4,400 course.

anecdotes.text: "Just a 5-minute walk from Nihonbashi and Namba, this long-established sushi restaurant has been around since 1955." — August 2026, the course at the 1F counter.
"Several customers came in just to grab this battera without dining in. It seems to be well-loved by the locals." — August 2026.
"To my surprise, it was completely empty! Seriously, it was too hidden!" — August 2026, a Saturday night.

places.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: wheat udon, with tempura toppings (chikuwa, soft-boiled egg, chicken, maitake) and a bonito dashi or bukkake sauce.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a bonito dashi (October 2026) and toppings of chikuwa, egg, chicken and beef.
places.hours_raw: Daily except Tuesday 11:00–15:00 (last order 14:30), holidays included (Tabelog; reopened 2 September 2025 after a break). The listing notes also say "closed on Wednesdays", which contradicts its own table; check before going. Buy a ticket at the machine outside first; cash, or PayPay if you call the staff out to the machine (September and October 2026). 9 counter seats; non-smoking (Tabelog). Lunch lines of five to ten are usual on weekdays, with waits of 5–10 minutes; one person cooks and serves, so the next group goes in only when seats are cleared (September–October 2026).
places.neighborhood: 西中島5-16-1, 味の小路 ("Flavor Alley") on the ground floor of JR Shin-Osaka Stn, outside the ticket gates and under the tracks, at the end of the alley (Tabelog; September–October 2026)
places.cuisine: Sanuki udon with a Kansai-style dashi, cut and boiled to order (October 2026) · the signature chiku-tama tempura bukkake, chikuwa and soft-boiled egg tempura with ginger, green onion and lemon, hot or cold, ¥880; the regular size is about two portions (September–October 2026) · chicken and egg tempura bukkake (September 2026) · meat bukkake with domestic wagyu and maitake tempura ¥1,350 (October 2026) · kasu udon ¥930 (October 2026) · kake udon with chikuwa and egg tempura ¥880 (October 2026)
places.notes: [Udon · Shin-Osaka Station, a one-person Sanuki counter] A nine-seat udon counter at the end of the 味の小路 food alley under the Shin-Osaka tracks, outside the ticket gates, from the Kamatake udon shops that a July 2026 diner calls famous in Minami. One person makes, boils and serves every bowl (2026). The order is the chiku-tama tempura bukkake (¥880): glossy, neatly folded noodles, chewy but smooth, under a big crisp chikuwa tempura and a runny soft-boiled egg tempura, with ginger, green onion and lemon, cold or hot. Meat bukkake with wagyu and maitake tempura (¥1,350) and kasu udon (¥930) are the richer choices. Buy your ticket at the machine before joining the line; lunchtime waits are short but steady. Lunch only, closed Tuesdays. A good stop between trains.

roles: Owner (unnamed), runs the counter alone (October 2026 review)
chef_bio.background: Per the Tabelog listing: reopened 2 September 2025, with Tuesday as the regular day off. Per reviews: "The owner was running the place by himself" (October 2026); "The restaurant operates with just one staff member, who seemed quite busy" (September 2026); "Even with just one staff member, the service felt efficient without any unnecessary movements" (October 2026); "Kamatake Udon is a famous spot in Minami" (July 2026).

anecdotes.text: "The presentation of the udon is beautiful, neatly folded, and it shines with a wonderful gloss … [The shop serves] it freshly cut and boiled." — October 2026, chiku-tama tempura bukkake ¥880.
"I thought katsu udon referred to tenkasu (tempura scraps), but it actually had pieces of beef in it." — October 2026; the diner's photo caption reads かすうどん 930円.
"The regular size comes with about two servings, making it quite filling." — September 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: 釜たけうどん 新大阪店、うどん、大阪市淀川区西中島5-16-1 JR新大阪駅 味の小路 1F、11:00〜15:00 (L.O.14:30)、火曜休み (祝日は営業)、2025年9月2日に営業再開、カード・電子マネー不可、PayPay 可、カウンター9席、禁煙。口コミ(2026年7月〜10月): 店の外の券売機、PayPay は店員さんを呼ぶ、ちくわ天と半熟卵天のぶっかけ880円 (生姜、ねぎ、レモン)、普通盛りで約2玉、かけうどんにちくわ天と半熟卵天880円、肉ぶっかけ1,350円 (国産和牛、舞茸天)、かすうどん930円、鶏天ぶっかけ、讃岐うどんに関西のだし、切りたてゆでたて、店主ひとりで営業、昼は行列。
