places.cuisine: Chicken paitan ramen with snacks and drinks (reviews) · chicken bone ramen, a frothy, creamy chicken paitan with simmered chicken-breast chashu ¥1,000 (2025–2026); a milder version (August 2025) · chicken shoyu ramen ¥950, medium-thick wavy noodles, served with pepper (August 2025) · chicken paitan curry ramen ¥1,050 (April 2026) · extra noodles ¥230, chicken rice ¥450 (September 2025) · snacks: kara-age ¥150 a piece, chicken-skin gyoza ¥150, croquette ¥250 (2025–2026), minced cutlet, chicken tataki, chicken ham with yuzu pepper (2025–2026) · cold chuka noodles in summer (August 2025) · bottled beer ¥650 (2025–2026) · pickled ginger, yuzu pepper and black pepper on the counter (April 2026)
places.notes: [Ramen · Nishinakajima-Minamigata, a chicken paitan bar for the evening] A small, wood-lined ramen counter a little down an alley near Nishinakajima-Minamigata, open since 2023, evenings only, with a sign calling it a ramen shop where you can drink. Start with kara-age or chicken-skin gyoza at ¥150 a piece and a beer, then the chicken bone ramen (¥1,000): a frothy, creamy white chicken paitan, rich but easy to finish, with simmered chicken-breast chashu and medium-thin noodles. The chicken shoyu (¥950) and a chicken curry ramen are the other bowls, and extra noodles are ¥230. The owner and one part-time staff member run it (August 2025), and foreign travellers turn up too (June 2025). Pay after; closed Sundays.

roles: Owner (unnamed) and a part-time staff member (August 2025 review)
chef_bio.background: Per the Tabelog listing: Chicken Ramen Niwatori, ramen, opened 8 June 2023. Per reviews: "There are two staff members: the owner and a part-time female employee" and "The sign at the entrance claims it's a ramen shop where you can drink" (August 2025); "The staff were very friendly, and the interior felt new and comfortable" (May 2026); a "ramen bar" with a wooden theme (April 2026).
chef_bio.specialty: Creamy chicken paitan ramen; snacks by the piece.

anecdotes.text: "Both of the appetizers I ordered were crispy and juicy … The soup had a rich and creamy flavor, spreading the essence of chicken throughout my mouth." — April 2026, chicken bone ramen ¥1,000, kara-age and chicken-skin gyoza ¥150 each.
"Next to me, there were a couple of foreign travelers quietly enjoying [the ramen]. I can see why: [the bowls are] easy to finish in one go." — June 2025.
"It was quite a rich chicken paitan, but surprisingly easy to finish even after a night out." — December 2025.

places.name: Imakoko Kitchen Merrymomo
places.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten statement from the shop. Brown rice is the base of every set, and a March 2025 diner mentions cakes "free from wheat and eggs" and rice-flour cakes, but the menu also has wheat noodles (tantanmen, lemon ramen), fried dishes and canned wheat-gluten meat, and the miso soup relies on a dashi of unstated make (May 2026).
places.vegan_detail: Every day there is a plant-based set: set A has a plant-based main with five sides, brown rice and miso soup, and set C is brown-rice onigiri with miso soup and pickles; a June 2026 diner calls A and C vegan (¥1,300 and ¥1,100). The vegetable curry is "made entirely vegan, without any animal products" (June 2026), and there are veggie mapo tofu, a veggie hamburger and veggie taco rice (Tabelog; 2025). Set B and some noodles use meat or fish. Ask what goes into the miso-soup dashi (May 2026).
places.hours_raw: Mon–Fri 07:30–22:00; Sat 11:00–22:00 (last order 21:00); closed Sundays, holidays and some days at New Year and Obon (Tabelog). Lunch sets until 14:00, an "After Lunch" menu after that (January and May 2025), set meals from 17:00 (October 2025). Dinner courses need a booking for two or more by the business day before (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners) and PayPay, d Barai, au PAY; no e-money (Tabelog). 30 seats at tables, sofas and a counter; a private room for four; smoking allowed per Tabelog. A shelf of organic condiments, brown rice and drinks for sale (October 2024; May 2026). Full at a May 2026 weekday lunch, with a short wait. Opened 1 April 2014 (Tabelog).
places.neighborhood: 西中島6-8-8, ground floor of 花原第8ビル — 5 min from Nishinakajima-Minamigata Stn, 7 min from Hankyu Minamikata, 10 min from JR Shin-Osaka (Tabelog)
places.cuisine: Macrobiotic and organic set meals around brown rice, vegetables, grains and seaweed (reviews; Tabelog: organic, vegetable dishes, vegetarian options) · weekday lunch: set A, plant-based main with five daily sides, brown rice with red quinoa and miso soup ¥1,300; set B, the same with a meat or fish main (chicken katsu, sautéed horse mackerel, tara fritto) ¥1,300; set C, brown-rice onigiri with miso soup and pickles ¥1,100 (June 2026) · vegetable curry of lentils with fresh and grilled vegetables, fully vegan (June 2026) · soupless sesame tantanmen with minced meat, white or black sesame (May 2026) · veggie mapo tofu (January 2025), veggie hamburger and shungiku tempura (March 2025) · summer menu: lemon ramen, veggie taco rice, soupless dandan noodles, chilled chuka noodles, ¥1,280 or ¥1,080 at lunch; lunch set with three sides, miso soup and salad +¥200, drink +¥100, dessert +¥220 (Tabelog) · dandelion coffee; soy-yogurt and rice-flour cheesecake (June 2026); cakes free from wheat and eggs (March 2025) · wine, cocktails and smoothies (Tabelog; 2023)
places.notes: [Macrobiotic · Nishinakajima, brown-rice set meals from 7:30] A roomy 30-seat organic kitchen in the Nishinakajima office blocks, open since 2014 and from 7:30 on weekdays, where macrobiotic cooking means a tray of brown rice with red quinoa, miso soup and five small vegetable dishes around a main. Choose set A with a plant-based main, set B with meat or fish, or a ¥1,100 brown-rice onigiri set; a June 2026 diner counts A and C as vegan. There is also a lentil vegetable curry made without animal products, veggie mapo tofu, and summer noodles. Desserts lean on soy yogurt and rice flour, with dandelion coffee. Diners praise the kind staff and a knowledgeable owner (2024), and visitors come from other prefectures and abroad (2024–2025). Book dinner courses a day ahead.

chef_bio.background: Per the shop-maintained Tabelog listing: Imakoko Kitchen Merrymomo, organic and vegetable dishes with vegetarian options, opened 1 April 2014. Per reviews: "a kitchen diner that offers traditional Japanese meals centered around brown rice, vegetables, grains, and seaweed" with ideas like "non-separation of spirit and matter" and "yin-yang balance" (October 2024); "Having chats with the incredibly interesting and knowledgeable owner is priceless" (November 2024); "All the staff members are lovely and kind" (May 2024); "attracts many international visitors" (July 2025).
chef_bio.specialty: Brown-rice set meals with a plant-based main; vegan curry.

anecdotes.text: "Sets A and C are vegan options." — June 2026, weekday lunch (A ¥1,300, C ¥1,100).
"It's made entirely vegan, without any animal products. The rice is brown rice, and the curry is a special healthy blend based on lentils." — June 2026, vegetable curry.
"They also offer cakes that are free from wheat and eggs, and you can enjoy dandelion coffee here. This place is suitable for vegetarians and even has canned gluten meat available." — March 2025.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ (店舗会員): Imakoko Kitchen Merrymomo、オーガニック・野菜料理・居酒屋、大阪市淀川区西中島6-8-8 花原第8ビル 1F、西中島南方駅から徒歩5分、月〜金7:30〜22:00、土11:00〜22:00 (L.O.21:00)、日・祝休み、ディナーのコースは2名から前営業日までに予約、カード・PayPay・d払い・au PAY 可、電子マネー不可、30席、4名の個室、喫煙可、2014年4月1日オープン、ベジタリアン対応、夏のメニュー (レモンラーメン、ベジタコライス、汁なし担々麺、冷やし中華、1,280円、ランチ1,080円)。口コミ(2020年5月〜2026年6月): マクロビオティック、玄米と赤キヌア、みそ汁、日替わりの小鉢5品、A セットは植物性のメイン1,300円、B セットは肉か魚のメイン1,300円、C セットは玄米おにぎり1,100円、A と C はヴィーガン、レンズ豆のベジカレーは動物性なし、汁なしごま担々麺、ベジ麻婆豆腐、ベジハンバーグ、たんぽぽコーヒー、豆乳ヨーグルトと米粉のチーズケーキ、小麦と卵を使わないケーキ、グルテンミートの缶詰も販売、みそ汁はだしの味、物知りな店主、他府県や海外からの客も。

cultural_comfort.note: Popular with visitors from abroad (July 2025). No English menu evidence found.

places.name: 鰻家 (Unagiya)
places.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: Kansai-style kabayaki glazed with a sweet tare (the usual unagi tare is soy-based), and more sauce on the table; ask if you want to try it plain.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: eel, eel liver soup and rolled omelette with eel.
places.hours_raw: Tue–Fri 11:00–17:00; Sat 11:00–19:00; closed Sunday, Monday and holidays; until sold out (Tabelog). No phone bookings: a sign-up board goes out at the shop at 9:30 for the 11:00, 12:00, 13:00 and 14:00 seatings, ten seats each, and people start queuing before 9:30 (2026 reviews); Saturday-evening seatings (16:00 and 18:00) can be booked (Tabelog; July and October 2026). The 14:00 slot sometimes has room; one diner phoned around 13:00 to check (October 2026). Cards accepted (Tabelog; September 2026). 10 counter seats; non-smoking; no photos of the cooking or kitchen (Tabelog; September 2026). Eel is prepared after you order, so allow 20–25 minutes (September–October 2026).
places.neighborhood: 西中島4-5-22, ground floor of 第3新大阪ビル, the same building as the yakitori shop osaka_furafura_nishinakajima — 3 min from Nishinakajima-Minamigata Stn (Tabelog)
places.cuisine: Kansai-style eel: live eel taken from the tank, split, skewered and grilled over charcoal in front of the counter, without steaming, crisp outside and soft inside (2023–2026) · Tabelog Unagi 100 (2018, 2019, 2022, 2024, 2026) · unaju regular ¥5,000 (July and September 2026) · unaju "jo" ¥6,200 with eel omelette, liver soup and pickles (2026) · unaju "tokujo" ¥8,000, adding uzaku and eel rolled round burdock (July and October 2026) · unadon (August 2026) · grilled liver ¥550 (July 2026) · extra rice free (July 2026) · the unaju comes with sauce and sansho on the table to add (September and October 2026) · eel from Aichi (January 2023) or Tokushima (July 2026) · Yebisu medium bottle ¥680, non-alcoholic beer ¥450 (2026)
places.notes: [Unagi · Nishinakajima-Minamigata, Kansai eel grilled to order] A ten-seat counter three minutes from Nishinakajima-Minamigata, in Tabelog's Unagi 100 five times since 2018, where every eel comes live from the tank and is split, skewered and grilled over charcoal in front of you, Kansai style, without steaming: crisp, fragrant skin and soft, fatty flesh. The unaju runs ¥5,000, ¥6,200 with an eel omelette, liver soup and pickles, or ¥8,000 with uzaku and eel-wrapped burdock as well; it arrives lightly glazed, with a sweetish sauce and sansho on the counter to add. There is no phone booking: write your name on the board outside at 9:30 for a seating between 11:00 and 14:00 (queues start earlier), or try the 14:00 slot later. No photos of the kitchen. Allow 20–25 minutes.

chef_bio.background: Per the Tabelog listing: unagi, ten counter seats, reservations only for Saturday evenings, open until sold out, no photos for posting; Tabelog Unagi 100 in 2018, 2019, 2022, 2024 and 2026. Per reviews: the chef "takes live eels from the fish tank, prepares them, skewers them, and grills them over charcoal right in front of you" (October 2026); "[It is said that] it takes three years to master skewering, eight years to learn filleting, and a lifetime to perfect grilling, and I truly appreciate the skill of the master chef" (October 2026); a nine-time visitor describes the same ritual from 2023 to 2026 (August 2026).
chef_bio.specialty: Kansai-style unaju grilled over charcoal from live eel.

anecdotes.text: "When I drove by the restaurant just after 9:10 AM, there were three people waiting … I returned to the restaurant at 9:20 AM to find about 15 people already waiting." — July 2026, the special unaju ¥8,000 and regular ¥5,000.
"It arrives without sauce, just the rice bowl itself. You can add as much sauce as you like from the table, and this sauce is incredibly delicious!" — September 2026, unaju ¥5,000.
"Unlike the Kanto style, there's no steaming involved, resulting in a crispy texture while the eel remains tender." — October 2026.

places.cuisine: Hakata-style vegetable skewers wrapped in pork, yakitori and Hakata dishes in private rooms (Tabelog) · assorted vegetable rolls: six for ¥2,100 (September 2026), ten also served (August 2026); rolls named in 2026: lettuce and pork (the most popular), Hakata green onion, okra with grated yam, daikon oden, mini tomato with bacon and basil, potato, avocado and cheese, enoki, yakisoba, eggplant, pork and shiso · Makinshai potato salad with a soft egg and tobiko ¥680, salt-seared bonito ¥1,100, "gourmet potatoes" under prosciutto and cheese sauce, salmon and ikura kamameshi ¥1,580 (September 2026); soy-marinated quail eggs; goma-kanpachi; mentaiko · sudachi sour ¥700; fruit sours (Tabelog) · courses with two hours of drinks: weekday Meguri course ¥4,000, Maki course ¥5,000 (duck with plum, sashimi, grilled shrimp, two vegetable rolls, rare salmon cutlet, August 2026), Kiwami course ¥5,500 (coupon prices on Tabelog, tax included)
places.notes: [Izakaya · Chayamachi, Hakata vegetable skewers in private rooms] A large izakaya on the fifth floor of a Chayamachi building near Hankyu Umeda, built around Hakata's vegetable-wrapped skewers: lettuce, green onion, okra with yam, mini tomato with basil or even yakisoba, rolled in thin pork and grilled over charcoal. Most guests take one of the many private rooms, from rooms for two with a farmhouse look to rooms for thirty-six, and order by QR code. Beyond the skewers, diners liked the potato salad under a soft egg and fish roe, the thick salt-seared bonito, potatoes buried in prosciutto and a salmon and ikura kamameshi (September 2026). Courses with two hours of drinks run ¥4,000–5,500. Reviews note noisy neighbours through the partitions and one billing mix-up that was put right.

chef_bio.background: Per the shop-maintained Tabelog listing: vegetable skewers and Hakata dishes, designer private rooms for 2 to 36, irori menu items; opened 10 March 2018. The Tabelog invoice number T5120001190055 is registered to 株式会社炉暖, Nishinari-ku (NTA invoice register, read 2026-11-01).

anecdotes.text: "My favorite was the most popular, the Lettuce-wrapped Pork. The moment I took a bite, the crispness of the lettuce combined perfectly with the juiciness of the meat!" — September 2026.
"The room has a unique design, reminiscent of a traditional Japanese dwelling, which adds a charming and fun touch." — August 2026, a private room for two.
"The partitions created a private room-like atmosphere where we could relax, but unfortunately, the noise from the neighboring table was quite bothersome..." — October 2026.

places.cuisine: Omakase of small nigiri on rice seasoned with a blend of three red vinegars, Hokkaido sea urchin and tuna from around Japan, with junmai sake and wine (Tabelog) · seasonal omakase, 12 nigiri with starters, ¥25,000 tax included (Tabelog) · an autumn 2026 course: sanma and eel to start, kinmedai with a shiso sauce and sea grapes, seared kinki with purple sea urchin, a lotus-root dumpling in crab sauce or a chilled soup of horse mackerel and cucumber, then shinko, new squid, kohada, kombu-cured sweet shrimp, clams from Mie, anago, tuna cuts, homemade ikura, a sea-urchin rice bowl, toro-taku with Ariake nori, an egg made with shrimp over two hours, and koji-pickled bettara-zuke (September–October 2026) · spring 2026: bamboo shoot, bonito with mustard, nodoguro with sea urchin
places.notes: [Sushi · Kitashinchi, an eight-seat red-vinegar counter] A quiet eight-seat sushi counter one minute from Kitashinchi Station, opened in 2023, whose logo was brushed by the calligrapher who wrote the label of the whisky Hibiki (Tabelog). One omakase at ¥25,000: a few seasonal starters such as kinmedai in a shiso sauce or seared kinki under purple sea urchin, then twelve small nigiri on firm rice seasoned only with salt and a blend of three red vinegars, one of them made for over 200 years, and a bowl of rice heaped with Hokkaido sea urchin. Diners mention the shinko in its short season, the shrimp-filled tamago cooked for two hours, and a reserved but kind chef (2026). Baseball players and sumo wrestlers are among the regulars, per two September 2026 reviews. Two seatings a night.

chef_bio.background: Per the shop-maintained Tabelog listing: only an omakase course, small sushi on rice made with a blend of three types of red vinegar, Hokkaido sea urchin and tuna from across Japan, junmai sake and wine; the logo by a calligrapher who also wrote the name of the whisky "Hibiki"; opened 30 September 2023. A September 2026 review adds that the traditional red vinegar has been made for over 200 years and the rice is seasoned only with salt and vinegar; reviews note Hanshin Tigers players, sumo wrestlers and other athletes among the guests (September and October 2026).
chef_bio.philosophy: Bringing people together over delicious sushi (Tabelog).

anecdotes.text: "The head chef, though somewhat reserved, was incredibly gentle and kind, a remarkable person full of knowledge." — October 2026.
"The shrimp-filled egg was made over two hours✨ When I took a bite, it had a gentle sweetness reminiscent of dessert" — September 2026.
"This restaurant is frequented by players from the Hanshin Tigers and sumo wrestlers, and I enjoyed the seasonal omakase course priced at JPY 25,000." — September 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ (店舗会員): 鮨 邂逅、寿司、大阪市北区曽根崎新地1-5-8 ピアースエイトビル 2F、北新地駅から徒歩約1分、月〜土 18:00〜と20:30〜の2部制、日・祝休み、完全予約制、カード可、電子マネー・QR 不可、カウンター8席、貸切可、禁煙 (廊下に灰皿)、2023年9月30日オープン、おまかせのみ、3種の赤酢を合わせた小ぶりのシャリ、Hokkaido のウニと各地のマグロ、純米酒とワイン、ロゴは「響」の題字を書いた書家、季節のおまかせコース (握り12貫と前菜など) 25,000円 (税込)。口コミ(2026年4月〜10月): サンマとうなぎ、金目鯛としそのソースと海ぶどう、あぶったキンキと紫ウニ、レンコンのまんじゅうとカニのあん、アジときゅうりの冷たいお椀、新イカ、新子、コハダ、昆布じめの甘エビ、Mie のハマグリ、アナゴ、マグロ、自家製いくら、ウニ丼、Ariake の海苔のトロたく、2時間かけたエビ入りの玉子、べったら漬け、春のたけのことカツオ、のどぐろとウニ、200年以上続く赤酢、塩と酢だけのシャリ、阪神タイガースの選手や力士も来る、物静かでやさしい大将。

cultural_comfort.note: One omakase at an eight-seat counter, reservation only (Tabelog). No English evidence found.

places.cuisine: Daily obanzai of seasonal ingredients, light courses and à la carte, with sake, domestic and overseas whisky and wine (Tabelog) · KURUMI course of grilled fish, six obanzai and a choice of meat dish ¥6,050 (Tabelog, tax included) · recommended: potato salad, soy-marinated red shrimp (Tabelog) · dishes in 2026 reviews: young sweetfish nanban, "adult" potato salad, small wagyu hamburg, yodare chicken, spicy glass noodles, homemade beef jerky (February); fried young burdock, mozzarella ravioli (March); curry to finish (May); conger-eel nanban (July); braised beef tendon, goya champuru, tsukune simmered with winter melon, saikyo-grilled black cod (July); homemade shumai, seafood gratin (August–October); simmered quail eggs, marinated conger eel (October) · about seven or eight sakes, e.g. Handorikawa, Toyo Bijin, Momo no Shizuku (August and October 2026) · obanzai bento of five kinds ¥1,300 (Tabelog)
places.notes: [Obanzai · Kitashinchi, a counter of small seasonal dishes] A warm, wood-lined counter on the third floor of a Kitashinchi building, open on weekday nights since 2022, where more than twenty obanzai a day sit on the counter and come out in small bowls, so you can try many. Expect Japanese and Western small plates side by side: young sweetfish nanban, potato salad, simmered quail eggs, homemade shumai, a small wagyu hamburg, mozzarella ravioli, seafood gratin and a curry to finish, with a short list of good sakes. A young owner and a small team run it, and the owner's hospitality is why one regular has been 36 times (October 2026). It is full from 18:00 to 20:00, so book or come late; one October 2026 diner found the bill about 20% higher than expected. Smoking is allowed; closed weekends.

chef_bio.background: Per the shop-maintained Tabelog listing: daily seasonal obanzai, light courses and à la carte, recommended potato salad and soy-marinated red shrimp, a range of whiskies and wines, a cozy wooden hideaway; opened 24 March 2022. A July 2026 diner saw "the young owner and a young female assistant" running it; an October 2026 diner, two women; a regular praises the owner's hospitality (October 2026, a 36th visit).
chef_bio.specialty: Daily obanzai; homemade shumai; potato salad.

anecdotes.text: "When you go, it's always packed, especially from 6 PM to 8 PM. However, the later hours are a good time to aim for" — October 2026, a 36th visit.
"With over 20 types of obanzai available, we decided to try different dishes from last time. The homemade beef jerky was so delicious that we ordered it again." — February 2026, a business trip.
"These hot, juicy dumplings had a great texture!" — October 2026, the homemade shumai.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ (店舗会員): おばんざい KURUMI、居酒屋・日本料理、大阪市北区曽根崎新地1-5-8 ピアースエイトビル 3F、北新地駅から徒歩5分、月〜金17:30〜24:00 (L.O.料理23:00、ドリンク23:30)、土・日・祝休み、予約可、カード可、電子マネー・QR 不可、15席 (カウンター9、半個室6)、喫煙可、テイクアウト、2022年3月24日オープン、季節の食材の日替わりおばんざい、軽めのコースとアラカルト、ポテトサラダと赤エビの醤油漬け、国内外のウイスキーとワイン、木のぬくもりの隠れ家、焼き魚と6種のおばんざいと選べる肉料理の KURUMI コース6,050円、おばんざい5種の弁当1,300円 (当日注文・配達)。口コミ(2026年2月〜10月): 20種以上のおばんざい、小鮎の南蛮漬け、大人のポテトサラダ、和牛の小さなハンバーグ、よだれ鶏、ピリ辛春雨、自家製ビーフジャーキー、新ごぼうの素揚げ、モッツァレラのラビオリ、締めのカレー、ハモの南蛮、牛すじ煮込み、ゴーヤチャンプルー、冬瓜とつくねの煮物、銀ダラの Saikyo 焼き、自家製シュウマイ、シーフードグラタン、うずらの煮卵、ハモのマリネ、日本酒7〜8種、18時〜20時は満席、遅い時間はねらい目、若い店主と女性のスタッフ、36回通う常連、思ったより2割ほど高いという声。

cultural_comfort.note: Small counter with the day's obanzai on display; book ahead for 18:00–20:00 (2026). No English evidence found.

places.notes: [Izakaya · Kitashinchi, seafood and a noodle to finish] A calm fifth-floor izakaya in the Kitashinchi Building, a few steps from an underground-mall exit, named for the shime, the noodle that ends a night: soba or a rich clam ramen. Before that come generous sashimi platters served one per person (Nagasaki sea snail, Kagoshima tuna and amberjack, a seared Kagawa scallop), big Goto Islands oysters, firefly squid, homemade tofu and dashimaki, at prices diners call fair for Kitashinchi (2025–26). There is also a kue hotpot course with fish from the Goto Islands. Private rooms suit business dinners, and e-cigarettes are allowed there. Open until 1:00 on weekdays; Saturday by booking only.

chef_bio.background: Per the shop-maintained Tabelog listing: seasonal seafood and selected sake, finishing with soba or ramen, "the chef's special dishes"; courses include Nagasaki kue hotpot with fish from the Goto Islands "delivered directly from our sister restaurant in Fukuoka"; opened 1 July 2023. A July 2026 diner mentions the shop's duck mascot.
chef_bio.specialty: Sashimi platter; clam ramen or soba to finish.

anecdotes.text: "The assorted sashimi platter (JPY 1,800, tax included) was served individually, making it easy to eat, which was a thoughtful touch." — July 2026.
"Although Kitashinchi has a reputation for being upscale, I was pleasantly surprised by how affordable this place was." — December 2025.
"The soba served at the end was also very tasty, further enhancing my satisfaction with the meal." — March 2026.

places.name: ちゃぶ台バル 8※ (Chabudai Bar 8※)
places.gf_detail: Ask when booking; the shop asks for allergies with course bookings (Tabelog). No gluten information. Tacos come in tortillas, and the jerk chicken and other dishes use house spice blends whose ingredients are not listed.
places.vegan_detail: Shop statement (Tabelog): "Vegetarian and vegan options are available as well"; Tabelog lists vegan and vegetarian options. Reviews describe vegetable-rich lunch plates and roasted vegetables with balsamic sauce (2025), but most named dishes (taco rice with ground beef, jerk chicken, garlic shrimp) are meat or seafood, so ask which dishes can be made vegan.
places.hours_raw: Tue–Sat 11:45–14:00 (last order 13:30) and 18:00–23:00 (last order 22:00); closed Sunday and Monday, but groups can book on closed days by phone (Tabelog). Lunch was taco rice only on a June 2026 visit. Dinner cover (otoshi) ¥350 (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX), IC cards and other e-money, PayPay, d Barai, Rakuten Pay, au PAY, Alipay, WeChat Pay (Tabelog). 35 seats at low chabudai tables, shoes off, plus a half-floor nook; private hire 20–50; non-smoking; English menu and digital menu; children welcome; takeout, bento and hors-d'oeuvre catering (Tabelog; 2026 reviews). Opened 12 May 2008 (Tabelog).
places.neighborhood: A back street two minutes from Umeda Sky Building, in a renovated old house — 505 m from JR Osaka Stn (Tabelog)
places.cuisine: Creative dishes of many genres with house-made spices and fish and vegetables from the market each day (Tabelog) · lunch: taco rice ¥900, +¥300 for jerk chicken (May 2025); large taco rice ¥1,100 (July 2026), three rice sizes and a Gorgonzola sauce to change the flavour (June 2026); a daily plate of grilled pork loin with salad, potage and rice ¥1,200 (May 2025) · evening: jerk chicken, tacos, roasted vegetables with balsamic, garlic shrimp, carpaccio (2025–2026) · courses with 120-minute all-you-can-drink: standard ¥5,000 (6 dishes, carpaccio, special of the day, jerk chicken), slightly luxurious ¥6,000 (8 dishes) (Tabelog); the listing also mentions ¥4,400 and ¥5,500 courses, and diners paid ¥4,400 (May 2026) and about ¥4,600 (January 2026)
places.notes: [World dishes · by Umeda Sky Building, low tables in an old house] A renovated old house on a back street two minutes from the Umeda Sky Building, where you take off your shoes and sit at low chabudai tables (there is also a half-floor nook). The kitchen cooks across cuisines with its own spice blends; diners keep coming back for the jerk chicken and the taco rice, which is the whole lunch menu some days, in three sizes with a Gorgonzola sauce on the side. Dinner is all-you-can-drink courses from about ¥4,400 for groups and office parties. The shop says it has vegetarian and vegan options. Diners describe a friendly owner and a cosy, slightly cramped room; one found the spicy seasoning repetitive, and the low tables are hard on the legs over a long evening. Closed Sundays and Mondays.

chef_bio.background: Shop text (Tabelog): a cozy 35-seat restaurant in a renovated traditional house two minutes from Umeda Sky Building; fresh ingredients from the market each day, house-made spices, creative dishes across genres; lunch and dinner, plus bento and hors-d'oeuvre catering; vegetarian and vegan options. Opened 12 May 2008.
chef_bio.philosophy: Deliciousness across genres, from the day's market (Tabelog).

anecdotes.text: "As always, I enjoyed pleasant conversations with the friendly owner and had a great time with the delicious dishes." — May 2026, a workplace gathering.
"For lunch, they only offered Taco Rice at 8*. I ordered it with all the toppings, but unfortunately, they were out of avocado." — June 2026.
"The chabudai, which the restaurant is named after, creates a nice ambiance, but sitting for a long time can be uncomfortable for your legs." — August 2026.

cultural_comfort.note: English menu and digital menu (Tabelog); some overseas visitors (May 2025). Shoes off, low tables.

staff_allergy_handling.text: Tabelog course notes: "If you have any allergies, dislikes, or specific dish requests, please let us know when making your reservation."

positives.text: Shop statement (Tabelog): "Vegetarian and vegan options are available as well"; Tabelog lists vegan and vegetarian options.

places.gf_detail: Ask when booking. No gluten information. Courses include foie gras with bread, a sukiyaki-style course (sukiyaki sauce is usually soy-based with wheat), garlic rice and sauces; a diner who skipped foie gras was given another dish (July 2026).
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: teppan courses of wagyu, abalone, foie gras and seafood.
places.hours_raw: Daily 12:00–22:00 per Tabelog; on weekends and holidays dinner runs in two seatings at 18:00 and 20:30 (Tabelog), and a March 2026 diner describes the same two seatings for dinner generally. Reservation only; special prices for bookings through the shop's Instagram (Tabelog). Closed the third Sunday of each month and 2–3 other days a month (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners, UnionPay), IC cards and other e-money, PayPay, d Barai, Rakuten Pay, au PAY, Alipay (Tabelog). 7 counter seats; private hire by phone; non-smoking; bring-your-own drinks (Tabelog).
places.neighborhood: Kitashinchi, JMビル B1F — 3 min from JR Kitashinchi Stn
places.cuisine: Teppanyaki of A5 wagyu fillet and live domestic black abalone, finished with an abalone-liver sauce (Tabelog) · courses (Tabelog, tax included): recommended course with abalone, fillet and strip loin ¥11,500 (10 dishes), with an anniversary cake ¥13,000; simple course without abalone and double fillet ¥11,500; a VIP course (December 2025) · a March 2026 course: sea bream with fresh-grated wasabi, oyster and wakame soup, foie gras on dashi-simmered daikon with balsamic, live Nagasaki abalone in a truffle-scented liver sauce turned into risotto with rice, tenderloin, ribeye sukiyaki-style with an onsen egg, garlic rice · seasonal starters: tuna and bonito sashimi with daikon in place of rice (November 2025), firefly squid and clam soup (March 2026); shirako (November 2025) · foie gras rice (July 2026) · sake and wine; mini bottles of sparkling; non-alcoholic wine (2025–2026)
places.notes: [Teppanyaki · Kitashinchi, seven seats around one griddle] A seven-seat basement teppan counter in Kitashinchi, run by owner-chef Ryuichi Yasekawa (Tabelog), that diners call remarkable value for the area. Courses at ¥11,500 run from sashimi or a seasonal soup through foie gras on dashi-soaked daikon to live abalone in a truffle-scented liver sauce, which the chef turns into a small risotto with rice, then wagyu fillet and a sukiyaki-style ribeye with an onsen egg and garlic rice. A November 2025 diner found the owner-chef working alone and very friendly; another regular comes four or five times a year. Dishes can be swapped (one diner skipped foie gras), and the anniversary cake is ¥1,500 more. Reservation only; bring your own wine if you like.

chef_bio.background: Shop text (Tabelog): high-quality teppanyaki at a counter only; ingredients from trusted suppliers, the pride being A5 wagyu fillet and live domestic black abalone, finished with a rich abalone-liver sauce; an open kitchen; local sake and wine. Reviews: on a November 2025 visit "the owner-chef was running the place" alone and was very friendly; "The chef's kindness truly enhances the deliciousness of the dishes" (July 2026).
chef_bio.philosophy: Ingredients delicious to look at and to eat (Tabelog).
chef_bio.specialty: Live abalone with liver sauce; foie gras on daikon; wagyu fillet.

anecdotes.text: "The liver sauce was simply outstanding, and the addition of truffle aroma made it elegant without being too heavy. I also appreciated the touch of adding a bit of rice at the end" — March 2026, a birthday course.
"The highlight of the day was the foie gras with radish." — November 2025.
"I visit this place about 4 to 5 times a year." — July 2026; the shop swapped the foie gras for another dish on request.

cultural_comfort.note: Set teppan courses at a seven-seat counter, booked ahead (Tabelog). No English evidence found.

places.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information. The menu centres on fresh pasta, baguette, quiche and tapas (2026 reviews).
places.vegan_detail: Ask. No vegan information. Dishes in reviews are mostly meat, cheese and seafood (tripe, Bolognese, Comté, squid-ink penne); a lotus-root quiche came with vegetables (August 2026).
places.hours_raw: Mon–Sat 18:00–23:00; closed Sundays and holidays, though it may open on some holidays (check the website) (Tabelog). Happy hour on champagne from opening until 18:59 (Tabelog). Lunch: Tabelog lists dinner only, but reviewers ate pasta lunches and a booked wagyu lunch course in January and February 2026. Service charge 10% (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners), e-money, PayPay (Tabelog). 18 seats: 10 at the counter, two tables for 4, semi-private seating; non-smoking all day (Tabelog).
places.neighborhood: Kitashinchi, 中山ビル 1F — a few minutes from Kitashinchi Stn exit 11-21, 4 min from Nishi-Umeda Stn
places.cuisine: French tapas, pasta and mains with seasonal ingredients, and champagne and wine at a counter (Tabelog) · evening: trippa (honeycomb tripe in tomato with beans) (October 2026); squid-ink and tomato penne (October 2026); lotus-root quiche (August 2026); 24-month Comté (July 2026); portions adjusted for a group of four (October 2026) · champagnes by the glass, e.g. "Réserve de la Terre", Pommery, a changing "Kimagure" champagne; Bourgogne Chardonnay (July–August 2026) · lunch (January–February 2026): fresh pasta (Bolognese, tomato-cheese); a set of baguette, appetizers, pumpkin soup, Satsuma Chami pork and Kyoto leek Bolognese, Basque cheesecake and café au lait; a booked black-wagyu lunch course · a new chef and new dishes (August 2026)
places.notes: [French · Kitashinchi, champagne and tapas at a counter] A ten-seat counter (plus two tables) from the Champagne Shokudo group, for French tapas, fresh pasta and a long list of champagne by the glass, cheapest in the happy hour before 19:00. Regulars order trippa in tomato, a lotus-root quiche or squid-ink penne alongside a glass of Pommery or the changing house champagne; a new chef arrived in summer 2026 and added dishes, which one regular called more refined (August 2026). Lunch was served early in 2026 (pasta lunches at about ¥1,000–3,000), though the listing gives dinner hours only. Expect ¥5,000–10,000 at dinner, plus 10% service. Non-smoking.

roles: Chef (unnamed; new by August 2026, per a review)
chef_bio.origin: Part of the シャンパン食堂 group: シャンパン食堂 北新地本店, this shop, and Stand Champagne Shoku in Kitashinchi, Akasaka Mitsuke and Ebisu (Tabelog remarks).
chef_bio.background: Shop text (Tabelog): French tapas, pasta and main dishes with seasonal ingredients, and champagne and wine at the counter; "It's all about the season!" The listing notes it is not the champagne-and-gyoza bar of the same group.
chef_bio.philosophy: Seasonal food with champagne (Tabelog).
chef_bio.specialty: Champagne by the glass; trippa; fresh pasta.

anecdotes.text: "Recently, the chef has changed, and the dishes have become even more refined, with many new menu items added!" — August 2026, a third visit.
"The lotus root on top of the quiche is nicely roasted, providing a great crunch and is incredibly tasty." — August 2026, with Pommery.
"The portion sizes were explained to us", and portions were adjusted for the group — October 2026, four people à la carte.

cultural_comfort.note: Counter ordering of tapas and wine by the glass (2026). No English evidence found.

Opened 28 June 2021 (Tabelog).
places.neighborhood: Kitashinchi main street, 谷安セッティモビル 3F — 3 min from JR Kitashinchi Stn and Nishi-Umeda Stn
places.cuisine: Japanese omakase of 7–8 dishes, with salt-grilled tuna and Miyazaki beef among the highlights, and wine pairings from a sommelier (Tabelog) · dinner course ¥14,300 (¥13,000 before tax); course with a guaranteed private room for two ¥16,500 (Tabelog) · a July 2025 course: scallops and summer vegetables in jelly, amadai and winter melon soup, tuna, sea bream and squid sashimi, fried eel with beef and myoga sauce, chawanmushi with shark fin and shrimp · earlier dishes: abalone, soft-shelled turtle, oysters, shirako chawanmushi and oyster rice (February 2025); firefly-squid rice with sansho and bamboo shoot, chicken paitan with thin noodles (April 2024); wild boar, a bite-sized tenderloin katsu (December 2024); tuna and sea-urchin sushi (April 2025) · seiko crab and, unexpectedly, burgers (December 2025) · leftover rice packed to take home (April 2026)
places.notes: [Japanese · Kitashinchi main street, a small omakase counter] A small Japanese restaurant on Kitashinchi's main street with a six-seat counter cut from a single slab and a private room, serving an omakase of seven or eight dishes built on the season (salt-grilled tuna, Miyazaki beef, shark fin and shrimp chawanmushi, a seasonal rice pot) with wine chosen by a sommelier. The course is ¥14,300, or ¥16,500 with a private room for two. Reviews describe one chef cooking for the room, chatty and attentive, with a member of staff serving; it stays open late and allows smoking, e-cigarettes included. Few reviews but loyal ones: one guest is on a tenth visit (January 2026). Leftover rice comes home with you in a box.

roles: Chef (unnamed), cooking alone (December 2024 and April 2025 reviews)
chef_bio.background: Shop text (Tabelog): authentic Japanese cuisine by skilled artisans; an omakase course of carefully selected ingredients such as salt-grilled tuna and Miyazaki beef; wine pairings by a sommelier; private rooms and a single-slab counter. Opened 28 June 2021. Reviews: "Yasaka is a Japanese restaurant run by a single chef" (April 2025); "the chef was working solo during a busy time" (December 2024); "run by a tanned chef and a female staff member" (July 2025); "The chef is incredibly entertaining and a great conversationalist" (July 2025).
chef_bio.philosophy: Seasonal Japanese cooking paired with wine (Tabelog).

anecdotes.text: "The shirako chawanmushi (savory egg custard) and the oyster takikomi gohan (seasoned rice) were particularly outstanding." — February 2025, a seventh visit.
"The absolute highlight was the hotaru ika (firefly squid) rice as the closing dish." — April 2024.
"I even received some leftover rice as a takeaway." — April 2026.

cultural_comfort.note: One omakase course at a small counter or private room (Tabelog). No English evidence found.

places.name: ステーキハウス ウイスキーノヴァ (Steak House Whisky Nova)
places.gf_detail: Ask when booking. No gluten information. Steaks and fish are charcoal-grilled and the sides include potatoes, mushrooms and salads, but courses come with focaccia or brioche and sauces are not described; nothing is called gluten-free.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a steakhouse; courses are built around dry-aged beef, pork or fish.
places.hours_raw: Daily 11:30–14:30 (last order 14:00) and 17:30–22:30 (last order 21:30) (hotel site; Tabelog). Reservations online or by phone; same-day walk-ins found a table (September 2026). Service charge 15% (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners); no e-money or QR (Tabelog). 58 seats (hotel site; 56 on Tabelog), private rooms for 4–8, a counter, window seats over the city; non-smoking; smart casual (hotel site; Tabelog). Birthday plates and cakes; a kids' plate (hotel site; September 2026). Corkage was ¥10,000 for wine (June 2026). On the 32nd floor of the hotel, linked to Namba Station (May 2026). Opened 1 July 2023 (Tabelog).
places.neighborhood: Nambanaka 2-11-50, Centara Grand Hotel Osaka 32F — 4 min from Namba Stn (Osaka Metro)
places.cuisine: Dry-aged steaks over charcoal with produce from around Osaka (hotel site) · beef aged 2–4 weeks in a dedicated dry-ageing room and seared in a charcoal oven at about 500°C (hotel site) · signature cuts: T-bone, L-bone, sirloin (hotel site); strip loin and fillet (March 2026) · also caviar with house brioche, grilled seasonal fish, charcoal-grilled Caesar salad, an aged-beef burger, a lunch charcoal-grilled sirloin (hotel site) · lunch courses: ¥7,700 a person (October 2026); a September 2026 course of seasonal-leaf salad, Bocchan pumpkin soup, a choice of wood-fired fish (120 g) or domestic sirloin (90 g), two-year-aged potato fries, aged maitake and sorbet; dry-aged pork as a main (September 2026); corn ice cream and a cow-shaped cinnamon cookie · a two-person ¥8,000 course with dining-club perks (June 2026) · a Japanese-whisky-led collection with bottle keep (hotel site); Nova Highball Citrus (May 2026); premium wines · steak knives made by 實光 of Sakai, with a choice of handle (hotel site) · on the 29th of each month some courses are 29% off (hotel site)
places.notes: [Steak · Namba, dry-aged beef on the 32nd floor] On the 32nd floor of Centara Grand Hotel Osaka, linked to Namba station, a calm steakhouse with big windows over the city. The beef is dry-aged two to four weeks in its own ageing room and seared in a charcoal oven at around 500°C (hotel site); T-bone, L-bone and sirloin are the signatures, cut with knives made for the restaurant by the Sakai knifesmith 實光. Lunch courses (about ¥7,700 in October 2026) bring salad, soup, a choice of fish or steak and sides that diners rate as highly as the meat, above all the sweet two-year-aged potato fries. The whisky list leans Japanese, with bottle keep. Diners in 2026 praise the view and the birthday touches; one found the steak ordinary for the price and the ¥10,000 corkage steep. 15% service. Open daily for lunch and dinner.

roles: Hotel restaurant team of Centara Grand Hotel Osaka (unnamed)
chef_bio.background: Per the hotel site: a steakhouse of aged beef and produce from around Osaka, with premium wines, on the 32nd floor overlooking the city; beef dry-aged 2–4 weeks and cooked in a charcoal oven at about 500°C; steak knives specially made by 實光, a Sakai knife maker of more than 110 years, with a choice of persimmon, laurel, oak or cherry handles; a collection centred on Japanese whisky with a bottle-keep service. Opened 1 July 2023 (Tabelog). The Tabelog listing is shop-maintained; the service charge rose from 13% to 15% on 1 January 2024.
chef_bio.specialty: Dry-aged T-bone and sirloin; two-year-aged potato fries.

anecdotes.text: "Two-year aged meikuin potato fries were sweet and delicious." — September 2026, a same-day birthday lunch.
"We chose both the strip loin and filet, and [the staff] kindly served them on separate plates." — March 2026, a weekend lunch.
"The corkage fee for wine was JPY 10,000!" — June 2026, a diner who found the steak inferior to other steak restaurants.

Book on the official site, which takes priority over other booking sites; late arrivals keep the two-hour slot from the booked time (official site; Tabelog). At dinner one drink per person (soft drinks fine) and a ¥330 appetizer charge with alcohol; no appetizer at lunch (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners, UnionPay) and QR (PayPay, Alipay, WeChat Pay) (Tabelog). 22 seats: an 8-seat counter, tables and a tatami room for 4–6 without a sunken floor; non-smoking; children welcome; takeaway and delivery; English, Chinese and Korean menus (Tabelog). One chef cooks, so food can take time (October 2026). Opened 3 April 2023 (Tabelog).

places.cuisine: Tonkatsu and pork shabu-shabu of brand pork: TOKYO X and Kagoshima kurobuta (official site) · the signature is a TOKYO X top-loin katsudon (official site) · tonkatsu of TOKYO X loin and fillet, Kagoshima kurobuta (150 g, September 2026), fried in a revised double-fry style since a summer 2026 relaunch as "Shin Hizono" (September 2026) · new weekday lunch from September 2026: loin tonkatsu set (120 g) ¥1,500 with free rice refills, chicken katsu, curry, katsudon, a mini katsudon (September–October 2026); pork miso soup with plenty of burdock · dinner: TOKYO X shabu-shabu course ¥4,950 (appetizer, shabu-shabu in a clay pot, house tsukune, vegetables, green-tea soba or zosui, yuzu sorbet; October 2026); courses comparing three brand pork (official site); a tonkatsu course of chicken, salmon, vegetables, fillet, loin and a spencer roll, finishing with katsudon or katsu curry (September 2026) · shabu-shabu dipped in a house soba dashi (no buckwheat flour) and ponzu, with yuzu kosho (official site) · à la carte: sliced chicken sashimi, kurobuta gyoza, seasonal specials such as autumn salmon in saikyo miso (September 2026) · characterful shochu, e.g. 夢幻 (imo), chosen by a chef from Kagoshima (official site)
places.notes: [Tonkatsu · Shinmachi, TOKYO X and kurobuta by a pork-loving owner] A clean, calm counter-and-table room on a Shinmachi back street, opened in 2023 by an owner the site calls a pork lover, with a chef from Kagoshima. The pork is TOKYO X and Kagoshima kurobuta: crisp, light tonkatsu that one diner says is best with just salt, a TOKYO X top-loin katsudon as the signature, and at night shabu-shabu of the same pork in a clay pot with a house soba dashi and ponzu, finished with green-tea soba. The kitchen relaunched as "Shin Hizono" in summer 2026 with a new frying method and, from September, a ¥1,500 weekday lunch set. With one chef at the stove, food takes a little time; dinner is by course or à la carte with one drink each. Regulars come from as far as France (September 2026). Book on the official site; closed Sundays and holidays.

roles: Owner (unnamed; "豚好きな店主", a pork-loving owner, per the official site)
Chef from Kagoshima (official site: 当店の料理人は…鹿児島県の出身)
chef_bio.origin: Kagoshima (the chef, per the official site)
chef_bio.background: Per the official site: tonkatsu and shabu-shabu by a pork-loving owner, using the "phantom pork" TOKYO X and Kagoshima kurobuta; the signature is a TOKYO X top-loin katsudon; shabu-shabu dipped in an original soba dashi made without buckwheat flour; the chef comes from Kagoshima, the home of shochu, and picks shochu for taste, not fame. Opened 3 April 2023 (Tabelog). A September 2026 regular describes a "Shin Hizono" relaunch with a new frying technique that summer and a new lunch menu from September, and a night when, with a staff member ill, two people ran the room.
chef_bio.philosophy: Shochu chosen for being truly delicious regardless of fame (official site).
chef_bio.specialty: TOKYO X tonkatsu and katsudon; TOKYO X shabu-shabu.

anecdotes.text: "Guests from Kanto, repeat visitors from France, and regulars gathered to enjoy tonkatsu and shabu-shabu" — September 2026, an 11th visit, the Shin Hizono banquet course.
"Tokyo X has an incredible sweetness, so I recommend enjoying it with salt. It feels like a waste to use sauce." — May 2026, lunch.
"Since the cooking is done by a single chef, it takes a little time to prepare." — October 2026, the ¥1,500 lunch loin set.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト (tonkatsu-butashabu-hizono.com): とんかつ 豚しゃぶ 樋ぞの、四ツ橋駅3分、豚好きな店主が創るとんかつや豚しゃぶ、このサイトからのネット予約が最優先、幻の豚 TOKYO X や鹿児島黒豚、名物は TOKYO X を使用した上ロースかつ丼、TOKYO X のしゃぶしゃぶ鍋、銘柄豚それぞれの鍋コース、焼酎は「夢幻 (芋)」をはじめ、当店の料理人は焼酎の本場・鹿児島県の出身、しゃぶしゃぶはオリジナルのそば出汁 (そば粉不使用) とポン酢、柚子胡椒、締めの茶そば (雑炊に変更可能)、3種食べ比べのコース、西区新町1-22-19 桑名ビル 1F、四ツ橋駅2番出口徒歩3分、西大橋駅2番出口徒歩2分、心斎橋駅徒歩8分、月〜金 11:30-14:00・18:00-22:30、土 18:00-22:30、日曜・祝日休み (祝日はまれに営業)。食べログ (店舗会員): とんかつ・豚しゃぶ・かつ丼、22席 (カウンター8)、座敷の個室 (掘りごたつなし)、夜は1人1ドリンク、お酒を頼むと付き出し330円、禁煙、子ども可、テイクアウト・デリバリー、英語・中国語・韓国語のメニュー、2023年4月3日オープン。口コミ(2026年5月〜10月): TOKYO X は塩で、2026年夏に揚げ方を変えて「Shin Hizono」に、9月から新しいランチ (ロースかつ定食1,500円、ご飯おかわり無料)、TOKYO X しゃぶしゃぶコース4,950円、とんかつのコース、ごぼうたっぷりの豚汁、Kanto や France からの客、料理人ひとりなので少し時間がかかる。

cultural_comfort.note: English, Chinese and Korean menus (Tabelog); book on the official site; regulars from abroad (September 2026).

places.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: a wheat bakery (focaccia, mochi bread, campagne, baguettes, buns, scones); the group says it uses domestic wheat where it can (official site).
places.vegan_detail: Ask. The salt focaccia (olive oil, salt) and plain hard breads may suit, but many breads use cream, butter, cheese, mentaiko or bacon; nothing is labelled vegan.

places.cuisine: The breads of Pane Porcini, the Fukushima bakery (2026 reviews; official group site) · salt focaccia ¥269 (June 2026) or ¥290 (August 2026); mochi bread ¥269; salt roll with truffle butter ¥231; peach bressane ¥220; mentaiko campagne on a whole-wheat dough; the chewy "mochiri" baguette; cream bread; bacon épi; a creamy Margherita focaccia pizza; Earl Grey scone; Florentine; corn dog; chocolate breads (2026 reviews) · the group's bakery is known for salt focaccia, mochi bread and cream bread and uses domestic wheat as far as possible (official site)
places.notes: [Bakery · Shinmachi, the Fukushima favourite without the queue] A small bakery near Nishi-Ohashi that sells the breads of Pane Porcini, the popular Fukushima bakery whose group also runs an Italian taverna, bar, latteria and salumeria there. Diners come for the same signatures without the Fukushima line: a big, salty, olive-oil salt focaccia, chewy mochi bread, a soft custard cream bread, mentaiko campagne and a chewy baguette, mostly ¥220–¥300. On the last Saturday of the month it turns into a night bar (19:00–22:00). Reviews are mixed: most 2026 diners were happy, but a long-time Fukushima customer felt the quality had dropped after a change of staff (October 2026). Closed Sundays.

chef_bio.background: Per the Porcini group site (porcini.jp): the group's bakery Pane Porcini in Fukushima, a small back-street bakery open late, is known for salt focaccia, mochi bread and cream bread and uses domestic wheat where it can; the group also runs Taverna Porcini, Bar Porcini, a latteria and a salumeria in Fukushima. Diners describe this Shinmachi shop as Pane Porcini's sister store (2026). Opened 10 May 2023 (Tabelog).
chef_bio.specialty: Salt focaccia; mochi bread; cream bread.

anecdotes.text: "This is a sister restaurant of the extremely popular bakery 'Pane Porcini,' known for its long lines in the gourmet hotspot of Fukushima." — June 2026.
"The Mentaiko Campagne immediately caught my eye. The flavor of the whole wheat dough combined with the mentaiko paste creates a unique deliciousness!" — August 2026.
"Since the time the shop in Fukushima opened, I've bought around 200 items, but this might be the end for me." — October 2026.

places.notes: [Sweets · Minami-Horie, a neighbourhood patisserie since 2013] A small, stylish patisserie in the sweets-crowded streets of Horie, open since 2013 and praised by one local family as the best cake shop around. The case runs from a rich Mont Blanc on a tart base and a pistachio Mont Blanc to strawberry shortcake, Shine Muscat tart and raspberry mousse, with the TV-famous Horie pudding and a shelf of baked goods (moelleux chocolat and tigre at ¥410 in March 2026, before an April price rise). Diners call the cream light and not too sweet; one found a mille-feuille ordinary. Takeaway, with one table outside. Cash only. Closed Tuesdays and Wednesdays.

chef_bio.background: Shop-maintained (corporate-member) Tabelog listing; opened 4 January 2013. A March 2026 reviewer describes high-quality fresh and baked sweets based on classic French pastry, well regarded among Kansai patisserie fans. No owner or official site was found.

places.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: wheat ramen noodles; sets add fried rice or kara-age.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: tonkotsu-based broths with minced meat and chashu.
places.hours_raw: Daily 11:00–15:00 and 18:00–24:00; hours may change (Tabelog); a June 2026 diner says it is open until 1 am. No reservations; no cards or e-money; QR payments accepted (Tabelog). Counter seating and big tables, including an octagonal one (June 2026); smoking allowed (Tabelog). Reviews go back to 2007 on a ramen database, per a June 2026 diner.

places.cuisine: Ramen in tonkotsu, dandan, shio and shoyu, plus the house "Jinanbo" bowl (June 2026) · Jinanbo ramen: a tonkotsu base with spicy miso and sautéed minced meat, served in a cast-iron pot (May and June 2026); "Jinanbo All Toppings" with chashu, minced meat, seasoned egg, wood ear, menma and green onion ¥1,350 (June 2026); the large size comes in a mortar-like bowl (September 2026) · tonkotsu ramen, mild for the style (July and September 2026) · tantanmen, creamy (May 2026); tantan mazesoba with medium-thick wavy noodles, minced meat, nori and chashu (May 2026) · sets with fried rice made with minced meat, ¥1,300 (May 2026), or kara-age (September 2026); Tianjin rice set (April 2026)
places.notes: [Ramen · Higashinakajima, tonkotsu in an iron pot] A long-running ramen shop on the main road south-east of Shin-Osaka Station, with reviews going back to 2007 (June 2026), open till midnight or later. The house "Jinanbo" ramen is a tonkotsu base with spicy miso and minced meat, brought bubbling in a cast-iron pot, "neither a true pork bone ramen nor a dan dan noodle" to one doubter (September 2026). There is also a mild tonkotsu, a creamy tantanmen, a tantan mazesoba with chewy wavy noodles, and shio and shoyu, usually ordered with fried rice made with minced meat; the half portion is close to a full one (May 2026). Portions are big; lunch fills it to 80% (May 2026). Smoking is allowed.

chef_bio.background: No shop description on Tabelog. A June 2026 diner notes reviews on a ramen database dating back to 2007, "so it seems this place has been in business for nearly 20 years"; staff explained that the minced meat in the Jinanbo is milder than in the dandan (June 2026).
chef_bio.specialty: Jinanbo ramen in a cast-iron pot; tantan mazesoba.

anecdotes.text: "It's also unique that it's served in a cast iron pot instead of a regular bowl." — June 2026, the Jinanbo All Toppings for JPY 1,350.
"The half rice … was actually double what I imagined! It was practically a full portion of fried rice." — May 2026, with the tantan mazesoba.

places.cuisine: Iekei-style tonkotsu shoyu ramen and tsukemen (2025–2026) · tonkotsu shoyu ramen: thick or thin noodles, firmness, strength and chicken oil to order, with a free bowl of rice (2025–2026); a layer of oil, chashu and quail eggs on the house tonkotsu (July 2026); tonkotsu shio with seasoned egg ¥980 (June 2026); nori tonkotsu shoyu (September 2025) · tsukemen in a seafood and pork-bone dip with thick noodles, regular 350 g and large 550 g free (October 2026), up to 750 g free (June 2026); Super Rich Seafood Tsukemen SP ¥1,180 (May 2026); tsukemen special with chashu (July 2026) · sets with half fried rice, or rice, gyoza and kara-age (July and September 2026) · pickled ginger on the table (2025)
places.notes: [Ramen · Nishinakajima, iekei bowls and free big tsukemen till midnight] A 26-seat ramen counter two minutes from Nishinakajima-Minamigata, open 11:00 to midnight every day since 2013. The ramen is in the iekei mould, a rich tonkotsu shoyu where you choose thick or thin noodles, firmness, strength and oil, with a free bowl of rice, "more like Hakata Tonkotsu Ramen than Yokohama Iekei" to one diner (September 2025). Many come for the tsukemen: thick noodles in a seafood and pork-bone dip, with the large 550 g portion free and up to 750 g on request (2026), though the dip can run short. Fast, filling and cash only; smoking is allowed in the afternoon on weekdays and all day at weekends.

chef_bio.background: No shop description on Tabelog; opened 3 December 2013 (Tabelog). The listing links menyasubaru.com, which no longer resolved on 2026-11-01. Reviewers describe the style as "Yokohama-style" or iekei (2025–2026) and guess at a chain or franchise (June and August 2026); no other branch is named in any source read.
chef_bio.specialty: Iekei-style tonkotsu shoyu; tsukemen with free large portions.

anecdotes.text: "As always, I ordered the extra-large serving of 750 grams. One of the great things about this place is that you can choose your portion size for free." — June 2026, the tsukemen.
"The broth was rich with soy sauce flavor and very delicious. It felt more like Hakata Tonkotsu Ramen than Yokohama Iekei." — September 2025.
"After drinking at two places, I visited this restaurant for a late-night ramen fix for the first time." — June 2026, tonkotsu shoyu with thick noodles.

places.notes: [Tsukemen · Nishinakajima, rich pork tsukemen since 2009] A 15-seat tsukemen shop between Nishinakajima-Minamigata and Shin-Osaka, open since 2009 and a Tabelog Ramen 100 pick every year from 2019 to 2025, with a line most lunchtimes and many evenings. The pork tsukemen is the reason: a very rich dip of pork bone and seafood with braised pork in it, so the shop's own instructions tell you to dip the smooth medium-thick noodles only lightly (October 2026); a lighter, slightly tangy chicken tsukemen is the alternative. Every bowl ends with a bite of rice to pour the last of the dip over. Buy your ticket before you queue; the line moves fast. Cash only. Open till 22:20, all day at weekends.

chef_bio.background: Per the Tabelog listing: opened 10 March 2009; social media posts on Facebook and Instagram "tend to be written for the entire group"; Tabelog Ramen WEST 100 2019–2022 and Ramen OSAKA 100 2023–2025. An October 2026 diner regrets that "the Tenma location closed down". Reviewers note a detailed written guide to the menu and to how lightly to dip (October 2026).
chef_bio.specialty: Pork tsukemen; chicken tsukemen; rice for the leftover dip.

anecdotes.text: "What stood out to me was the detailed explanation of the menu and how to enjoy the tsukemen." — October 2026, the Toki Ya Special Pork Tsukemen for JPY 1,550.
"There was a line of seven people waiting at that hour, which shows how popular this place is." — October 2026, just before 21:00, seated in about ten minutes.
"The final broth rice was creamy and surprisingly good." — October 2026, the pork spicy tsukemen for JPY 1,150.

places.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: wheat noodles from Menya Teigaku in Kyoto (October 2026); the chashu bowl is topped with mayonnaise.

places.cuisine: Whole-chicken shoyu chuka soba and monthly specials · marudori (whole-chicken) shoyu: Hinai chicken broth ¥1,100 (October 2026); with flavoured egg ¥1,250, large noodles +¥150, Kujo green onion +¥200 (October 2026); special with two slices of rare chashu, egg, meat wontons, menma and green onion (September 2026) · a clear broth of Hinai and Men-suke chicken, glossy with chicken oil (2026); on a September 2026 "Chicken Day", Hinai and Men-suke chicken with a dashi of Rishiri kombu and shiitake · medium-thin straight noodles from Menya Teigaku (October 2026) · rare pork-shoulder chashu (October 2026); chicken chashu (September 2026) · special salt seafood ramen, oil soba (October 2026); squid-and-niboshi ramen and a limited cold dried-squid ramen (October 2026) · morning ramen, sanma and Hinai chicken ¥1,400 (October 2026) · chashu rice bowl with mayonnaise and shichimi ¥480 (October 2026) · Sapporo Lager, with a small plate of menma (October 2026)
places.notes: [Ramen · Nishimiyahara, whole-chicken shoyu from a Mutahiro alumnus] A bright, spotless chuka soba shop a ten-minute walk west of Shin-Osaka Station, opened in 2018 by a former manager of Chuka Soba Mutahiro (October 2026) and on Tabelog's Ramen 100 list from 2023 to 2025. The bowl to order is the marudori shoyu: a clear, chicken-oil-glossy broth of Hinai and Men-suke chicken, Kyoto noodles from Menya Teigaku, rare pork-shoulder chashu and Kujo green onion, ¥1,100–1,250 (October 2026). Specials change often (squid and niboshi, salt seafood, oil soba), and once a month on the second Sunday there is a lottery morning ramen, sanma in October 2026. One devotee has logged 155 visits (October 2026). The owner cooks each bowl; when it's busy, write your name and wander. Cash only; closed Monday and Tuesday.

chef_bio.background: Per an October 2026 review: "opened in 2018 by the former manager of the renowned 'Chuka Soba Mutahiro' in Osaka"; "The owner was in the kitchen skillfully preparing each bowl with great care"; noodles from Menya Teigaku in Kyoto. Opened 9 June 2018; Tabelog Ramen OSAKA 100 2023–2025 (Tabelog).
chef_bio.specialty: Marudori (whole-chicken) shoyu ramen; monthly morning ramen.

anecdotes.text: "Wow, the broth, concentrated with the flavors of Hinai chicken and Men-suke chicken, is incredibly delicious!" — October 2026, a diner on visit 155, the marudori shoyu with flavoured egg for JPY 1,250.
"You can taste the essence of sanma even without its physical form." — October 2026, the monthly morning ramen, sanma and Hinai chicken for JPY 1,400.
"I found the noodles to be somewhat lacking. They just couldn't compete with the broth." — October 2026, the large marudori ramen.

places.name: しゃにむに 心斎橋本店 (SHANIMUNI Shinsaibashi)
places.gf_detail: Ask when booking (the listing asks guests to state allergies). No gluten information. Binchotan-grilled skewers and eel come with tare, and the courses run through tempura, sushi and pudding; nothing is described as gluten-free.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: courses of fish, chicken skewers, eel and wagyu; the lunch is grilled meat on rice.
places.hours_raw: Mon–Fri lunch 11:30–14:00; Mon–Sat and holidays dinner 17:30–22:00 (last order food 21:00, drinks 21:30); closed Sunday and some irregular days (Tabelog). Reservations accepted, same-day too; say whether you want the counter or a private room; tell the shop about allergies and dislikes; two-hour limit at busy times; no children below elementary-school age; cancel at least two days ahead (Tabelog). Appetiser ¥770 and 10% service at dinner (Tabelog). Cards, e-money and PayPay (Tabelog). 30 seats: a counter of 9 and four private rooms, sunken seating, for 2 up to 20; smoking only in the private rooms, and not at lunch (Tabelog).

places.cuisine: Japanese robata of seasonal ingredients from around Japan grilled slowly over chosen binchotan (Tabelog shop text) · courses: basic ¥9,900, special kaiseki "Kotobuki" ¥12,100, seasonal "Roku" kaiseki (Tabelog) · à la carte: sashimi, charcoal-grilled chicken skewers, harami skewers, grilled eel, sirloin cap, octopus simmered with daikon, potato salad, soft-roe tempura, temari sushi, oyakodon (2025–2026 reviews) · wasanbon pudding, also to take away, sometimes sold out (July 2026) · lunch on weekdays: grilled-meat set ¥1,800 (May 2026), a box of harami and rib over rice with rice in sizes (February 2026), served with rooibos tea instead of water (October 2026) · a long list of sake and shochu, e.g. coarse peach liqueur
places.notes: [Robata · Higashi-Shinsaibashi, private rooms by the charcoal] A stylish, unmarked-looking robata restaurant on a quiet back street near Nagahoribashi: a counter in front of the binchotan where the chef grills, and four sunken private rooms behind it for two to twenty. Dinner is courses (¥9,900–12,100) or à la carte sashimi, skewers, grilled eel and seasonal small plates with a long sake list; finish with the wasanbon pudding. Weekday lunch is a grilled-meat box over rice for about ¥1,800. Diners describe a calm room, attentive staff and a gracious owner (2026). No young children; closed Sundays; add a ¥770 appetiser and 10% service at dinner.

roles: Owner and chef, unnamed in the sources read
chef_bio.background: Per the Tabelog shop text: charcoal grilling over binchotan, a traditional Japanese method, with seasonal food gathered from around Japan and private rooms for up to 20. An October 2026 diner describes a thoughtful, beautiful owner and the chef working behind the counter; a January 2026 diner praised the women on the floor staff and a staff member who ran after the diner to return a forgotten item.
chef_bio.philosophy: "Enjoy the quality of the ingredients, the heart of the griller and the grilled food while it is still hot" (Tabelog shop text, translated).
chef_bio.specialty: Binchotan-grilled skewers and eel; seasonal kaiseki courses; wasanbon pudding.

anecdotes.text: "I also appreciate the staff member who ran after me to return my forgotten item." — January 2026, a sake and sushi course with extra skewers.
"Instead of plain water, they offer delicious rooibos tea!" — October 2026, a third lunch visit.
"The only downside was that the Wasanbon Pudding for takeout was sold out" — July 2026, a colleague's wedding celebration.

places.cuisine: Kyoto duck shipped direct from Kyoto and handmade soba (Tabelog shop text) · Kyoto duck hot pot course of six dishes ¥6,710; duck hot pot course with free drinks ¥7,500; grilled-shabu course with free drinks ¥7,500 (Tabelog; September 2026) · Kyoto duck and Kujo green-onion grilled shabu-shabu with ponzu or house sesame sauce · duck sukiyaki · finish with soba, zosui or thick somen · duck tataki, duck prosciutto, duck chawanmushi, all-parts duck skewers (thigh, negi, heart, gizzard, breast, liver, skin), tsukune · lunch: oyakodon, Kyoto duck bukkake soba set, Kyoto duck roast box with a mini soba, sudachi soba · sake chosen by the owner (July 2026)
places.notes: [Duck and soba · Hozenji Yokocho] A duck house in the north alley of Hozenji Yokocho serving Kyoto duck sent from Kyoto, with private rooms upstairs. At dinner the order is a duck course: tataki and duck ham, then grilled shabu-shabu of duck and Kujo green onion on a teppan (staff show you how), or the duck hot pot, finished with the handmade soba. Lunch is calmer and cheaper: oyakodon, a roast-duck box with a mini soba, or duck bukkake soba. Book for the private rooms; Monday nights are courses by reservation only. Expect ¥6,000–8,000 a head at dinner.

places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: courses of foie gras, fish, wagyu, lamb or pork with butter and cream sauces.
places.hours_raw: Open only on Friday, Saturday, Sunday and holidays: lunch 11:30–14:30; dinner 17:30–21:00 (last order 20:30), on Saturday and the day before a holiday until 21:30 (last order 21:00); closed Monday to Thursday except holidays (Tabelog). places.cuisine: Classic French in a hotel dining room (2025–2026 reviews) · courses at ¥7,500, ¥10,000 and ¥13,000 (August 2025); a Friday dinner course ¥10,000 (February 2026); an executive course ¥32,000 with caviar, abalone, lobster and A5 wagyu (March 2025) · e.g. pâté en croûte of Daichi pork, lobster bisque, wagyu fillet Rossini with Périgueux sauce, bouillabaisse, turbot gratin (winter 2024); a spring menu with tuna tartare and hachis Parmentier (March 2026); foie gras and steak (June 2026); a choice of main such as lamb or pork (July 2026); a September 2026 lunch with bell-pepper soup and meat with foie gras and truffle sauce · two breads and two butters, incl. smoked butter · several dessert plates and a trolley of petits fours to choose from (2024–2026) · wine
places.notes: [French · Shinsaibashi, a weekend hotel classic] The French restaurant of Hotel Nikko Osaka, three floors above Shinsaibashi Station, now open only Friday to Sunday and on holidays. The cooking is classic: pâté en croûte, bisque, Rossini-style wagyu with foie gras and truffle sauce, and a run of desserts ending with a trolley of petits fours you pick from. Courses ran ¥7,500–13,000 in 2025–2026 (¥10,000 on a February 2026 Friday), with a ¥32,000 luxury course, plus 15% service. Reviews in 2026 are mostly warm, though a July 2026 diner found the lamb and pork mains tough. Good for anniversaries; wheelchair accessible.

roles: Hotel Nikko Osaka; chef unnamed in the sources read
chef_bio.background: Reviewers call it a long-established French restaurant of Hotel Nikko Osaka; a March 2025 diner who had found the cooking had slipped noticed it improved and wondered whether the chef had changed. Open only on weekends and holidays (Tabelog).
chef_bio.specialty: Classic French courses; dessert trolley of petits fours.

anecdotes.text: "For this quantity and quality, the Friday price is JPY 10,000!" — February 2026.
"We could choose as many tea sweets as we liked from a wide selection!" — August 2026, a celebration on the middle course.
"The atmosphere is relatively casual for a hotel French restaurant. … However, the meat in the main course was tough" — July 2026, a lamb main.

places.neighborhood: Namba 5-1-60, なんばスカイオ 6F, above Nankai Namba Stn — 1 min walk
places.cuisine: Rice restaurant of the rice-cooker maker Zojirushi: rice blended by a five-star rice master and cooked in its top "Enbutaiki" cooker, with seasonal side dishes (Tabelog shop text) · set meals from ¥2,300 at lunch (October 2026), e.g. salmon and chunky vegetables in black-vinegar sauce ¥2,300, roast pork with grated-onion sauce, teriyaki chicken, salmon rare cutlet · three rices to compare (a soft and a firm cooking, multigrain or brown) with free refills from the counter, small sides such as sea bream, umeboshi and nori tsukudani, and a sea-bream chazuke to finish (2026) · egg ¥300 (October 2026) · rice ice cream for dessert · dinner kaiseki "Aki Hime" with free drinks ¥8,900 (Tabelog) · Zojirushi craft beer "Zou no Mai" · bento and a roast beef set to take away
places.notes: [Set meals · Namba, a rice-cooker maker's dining room] The restaurant of the rice-cooker maker Zojirushi on the sixth floor of Namba Skyo, above Nankai Namba Station, where rice is the main course: two or three rices cooked in the company's top cooker, soft, firm and multigrain, to compare and refill as often as you like, with a fish or meat main and small sides. Finish with sea-bream chazuke and rice ice cream. Lunch sets start at ¥2,300 (October 2026); take a numbered ticket from about 10:30, as queues of 30 minutes are usual, and there is a 60-minute limit. The restaurant does not accommodate food allergies.

roles: Restaurant of Zojirushi Mahobin (Tabelog shop text); the listing links dynac-japan.com
chef_bio.background: Per the Tabelog shop text: a rice restaurant by Zojirushi Mahobin, with rice blended by a five-star rice master and cooked in the "Enbutaiki" cooker that reproduces a traditional kamado; seasonal set meals at lunch and kaiseki at dinner; bento to take home. Opened 17 October 2018; a sister shop opened in Umeda (Tabelog 27152910 in the crawl). An October 2026 diner recalls long queues on the news at the opening.
chef_bio.specialty: Three rices with free refills; sea-bream chazuke; rice ice cream.

anecdotes.text: "I started checking in around 10:30. I was the 7th in line" — September 2026, a second visit, all three types of rice.
"However, the real reason I keep coming back to this place is for the dessert—rice ice cream." — October 2026.
"The only thing I would mention is that paying JPY 300 for one egg seems a bit pricey" — October 2026, seated at noon after a numbered ticket.

cultural_comfort.note: Numbered tickets and a QR code for the queue; staff explain the rices (September 2026). No English evidence found.

places.name: トッサ・ジ・クラッサン (Tossa Ji Croissant)
places.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information. The straw-grilled bonito is served with salt, garlic and other condiments, but set meals include obanzai in dashi and soy, and dinner courses run to pasta.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: Kochi seafood, bonito and yellowtail, with side dishes in dashi.

Reservations accepted; lunch bookings until 13:45; table requests are not guaranteed, parties of two may be put at the counter; private rooms only by phone, with a course, for 5 or more (Tabelog). No cover charge (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners) and PayPay; no e-money (Tabelog). 62 seats: 8 at the 1F counter, 22 at 1F tables, 32 on 2F, with private rooms for 5–32; some days only 1F is open; non-smoking; families with children often at weekends (Tabelog). Opened 6 January 2017 (Tabelog).
places.neighborhood: Kitahorie 1-6-19, one street west of Yotsubashi-suji — 1 min from Yotsubashi Stn exit 4
places.cuisine: Kochi (Tosa) ingredients worked into a Japanese-French menu, with Tosa sake (Tabelog) · the signature: bonito caught that day in Tosa, straw-grilled to order in the Tosa "warayaki" style and served with salt (Tabelog; 2026 reviews) · lunch obanzai set of straw-grilled bonito and Tosa yellowtail with several small dishes, rice and a raw egg ¥1,980 (September–October 2026); a Tosa yellowtail seafood bowl set; a set with bonito, yellowtail and namero (October 2026) · lunch bottle of beer ¥800 (October 2026) · dinner à la carte and courses with all-you-can-drink, from straw-grilled bonito to sukiyaki and pasta (September 2026) · more than 20 sakes direct from Kochi (Tabelog)
places.notes: [Kochi cooking · Kitahorie, straw-grilled bonito] A two-floor Kochi restaurant a minute from Yotsubashi Station where the bonito arrives from Tosa the same day and is seared to order over burning straw in the Tosa way, and from the counter you can watch the flames. Lunch is the draw: the obanzai set of straw-grilled bonito and fat Tosa yellowtail side by side, eaten with salt, garlic and green onion, with a run of dashi-rich small dishes and a raw egg for your rice (¥1,980 in October 2026). In the evening the menu turns Japanese-French around the same fish, with more than 20 sakes from Kochi and courses for groups. Diners find it pricey for lunch but worth it; book, especially Fridays. Closed most Sundays.

chef_bio.background: Shop-maintained Tabelog listing: a creative restaurant using seasonal ingredients from Kochi (Tosa), cooked with French technique into a fusion of Japanese and Western flavours; bonito delivered the same day and straw-grilled to order; over 20 Kochi sakes, recommended by the staff; families with small children and parents' groups on Sundays. Opened 6 January 2017.

anecdotes.text: "After placing my order, I was able to watch the straw grilling right in front of me, and it was quite impressive!!" — October 2026, the obanzai set.
"I had the Set Meal featuring a comparison of smoked bonito and Tosa yellowtail for JPY 1,980. It's highly recommended to eat it with salt" — September 2026.
"The grilled bonito is delicious, but the sashimi of yellowtail was truly amazing." — October 2026, lunch.

places.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information. Shirasu bowls and sashimi come with soy-based sauces, and sets include tempura, croquettes and fried oysters.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a seafood izakaya of shirasu, sashimi and fried fish.
places.hours_raw: Daily 11:00–15:00; dinner 17:00–22:00 except Wednesday, when it closes after lunch (Tabelog). Reservations accepted; the Shirasu Gozen set is limited (five a day in September 2026) and bookable (2026 reviews). Starter ¥380 at dinner (Tabelog). Cards, IC cards and other e-money, and QR payments including PayPay, Alipay and WeChat Pay (Tabelog). 33 seats at the counter, tables and outdoor tables; smoking only outside; private hire up to 40 (Tabelog). QR ordering (October 2026). In Namba CITY's Komejirushi food alley under the tracks, across from the South Building exit; directly connected from Nankai Namba Station south exit (Tabelog). Opened 6 April 2024 (Tabelog).
places.neighborhood: Nambanaka 2-10-25, なんばこめじるし under the Nankai tracks, Namba CITY — 3 min from Nankai Namba Stn
places.cuisine: Port seafood izakaya, the Namba sister of a Kishiwada shop (Tabelog; ikari-f.co.jp) · shirasu straight from Kishiwada fishing port, raw (nama) or boiled (kamaage) (Tabelog) · original raw-shirasu bowl ¥1,000, large +¥110–120 (January and October 2026); shirasu bowl lunch of boiled shirasu ¥990 (September 2026) · Shirasu Gozen of raw and boiled shirasu with fried fish, a raw egg and miso soup ¥1,600, limited (September–October 2026) · Kinchaku Ya set of sashimi, shirasu, squid shiokara, sweet-simmered small fish, croquette and fried oyster ¥1,600 (October 2026) · "masu-mori" chef's assortments of 3, 5 or 10 items (Tabelog) · senbero set of a draft beer and three daily small dishes (October 2026); quick-drink set ¥1,100 (September 2026) · nine one-cup sakes, frozen fruit sours, Kishiwada beer (Tabelog; September 2026) · seafood hot pot in winter (Tabelog)
places.notes: [Seafood izakaya · Namba CITY, Kishiwada shirasu] A lively little seafood izakaya in the Komejirushi alley under the Nankai tracks, the Namba branch of a Kishiwada fishing-port shop, with counter, tables and seats outside and festival music on the speakers. Shirasu comes straight from Kishiwada port, and the thing to order is the raw-shirasu bowl, ¥1,000 at lunch in October 2026, or the limited Shirasu Gozen with both raw and fluffy boiled shirasu, fried fish and a raw egg (¥1,600). At night there are assortments of the day's fish served in a masu, a 'senbero' set of beer and three small dishes, one-cup sakes and Kishiwada beer. Regulars come back several times a month; one found the portions small for men. Closed Wednesday evenings.

chef_bio.background: Per the operator's site (ikari-f.co.jp): two directly run shops, きんちゃく家 岸和田店 and きんちゃく家 なんば店, serving fresh fish at low prices, including Osaka shirasu sent direct from Kishiwada fishing port. Tabelog: opened 6 April 2024; a sister of a famous shop in Kishiwada.

anecdotes.text: "I've become hooked on fresh shirasu and this is my third visit this month." — September 2026, the raw-shirasu bowl.
"I arrived just as they opened, and the staff said, 'You made it just in time for our special limited offer of 5 servings!'" — September 2026, the Shirasu Gozen.
"The Senbero Set includes a draft beer and three daily specials. Today, it featured shirasu (young sardines) tsukudani, octopus wasabi, and tempura of kiss fish." — October 2026.

places.cuisine: Izakaya of genuine ingredients: vegetables from the company's own farm in Yao, freshly shaved katsuobushi, Hokkaido free-range pork, a pot sauce of three-year-aged mirin, and junmai sake (Tabelog) · the social-media "Jewel Box" lunch in a wooden treasure chest of sashimi, roast beef, kara-age, dashimaki, potato salad and obanzai, with katsuobushi from Ibusuki shaved without limit ¥2,590 (October 2026; rice refills extra) · a meat-wrapped lunch (October 2026) · dinner course ¥3,800: appetizer, fried simmered daikon with fried-leek sauce, a seasonal dish, dashi shabu-shabu in a small pot, soba to finish, a choice of salmon-and-tuna rice bowl (October 2026) · house tofu with katsuobushi shaved at the table as the starter; jasmine-tea pudding (October 2026)
places.notes: [Izakaya · Ura-Namba, freshly shaved katsuobushi] A second-floor izakaya in the Ura-Namba back streets, up a steep staircase behind a plain door, built on vegetables from the company's own farm in Yao and katsuobushi shaved so thin it flies off the plate. At lunch it is famous on social media for the 'Jewel Box', a wooden treasure chest of sashimi, roast beef, kara-age, dashimaki and small dishes, with bonito flakes from Ibusuki for the rice without limit (¥2,590 in October 2026; book the day before). In the evening, try the deep-fried simmered daikon and the ¥3,800 course of dashi shabu-shabu with soba, ideally in the gold private room. One diner found the box pretty but unremarkable and the rice refills extra (October 2026). There is a sister restaurant, BELLA BOCCA, downstairs.

chef_bio.background: Shop-maintained Tabelog listing: a hideaway izakaya for adults focused on genuine ingredients (vegetables from its own farm in Yao, where guests can join farm days; freshly shaved katsuobushi; Hokkaido free-range pork; a pot sauce made with three-year-aged mirin) and junmai sake; opened 10 May 2023. Operator kimiyu.co.jp. Reviews in October 2026 mention a sister on 1F, BELLA BOCCA, and an Umeda location.
chef_bio.philosophy: "The truly delicious meal is eating with a gentle mother and family" (company site).
chef_bio.specialty: Jewel Box lunch; freshly shaved katsuobushi; fried simmered daikon.

anecdotes.text: "Be careful, as the katsuobushi is very thin and fluffy, so it might fly away! Haha." — October 2026, the house-tofu starter.
"I had the Gem Box Lunch for JPY 2,590, which was a hearty meal. The bonito flakes were all-you-can-eat" — October 2026.
"Although bonito flakes were available for unlimited refills, there was an extra charge for rice refills" — October 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ (店舗会員): 達屋 なんば店 (TAZ-YA)、居酒屋・しゃぶしゃぶ、大阪市中央区難波千日前1-8 2F、月〜金11:30〜14:30・17:00〜23:00、土・日11:00〜15:00・17:00〜23:00、予約可、限定の Jewel Box のランチは平日は前日までに予約、週末は数量限定、混雑時はディナー2時間・ランチ1時間、お通し代500円・個室料1人500円 (ディナーのみ)、カード・PayPay 可、34席、2階、24席のホールと4・6・8名の個室 (VIP 個室)、貸切24〜30名、禁煙、2023年5月10日オープン。店の紹介 (英訳): 自社の農園の野菜、削りたてのかつお節、Hokkaido の放牧の豚、3年熟成の本みりんの鍋のたれ、純米酒、大人の隠れ家の居酒屋、Yao の自社農園の農業体験。会社のサイト (kimiyu.co.jp): 「優しいお母さんと家族と食べる食事」が一番おいしいもの。口コミ(2026年10月): Jewel Box のランチ2,590円 (刺身、ローストビーフ、唐揚げ、だし巻き、ポテサラ、おばんざい、Ibusuki のかつお節はおかわり自由、ご飯のおかわりは有料)、肉巻きのランチ、3,800円のコース (大根の揚げ煮、だしのしゃぶしゃぶ、締めのそば、サーモンとマグロの丼)、自家製の豆腐に目の前でかつお節、ジャスミンティーのプリン、金色の個室、急な階段、1階の姉妹店 BELLA BOCCA、Umeda にも店。
