places.cuisine: Charcoal grill and yakitori, with rare Kawachi duck from a supplier of 150 years, thick-cut beef tongue and wagyu (Tabelog) · napa-cabbage kimchi ¥350, beef-tongue tsukimi hamburg ¥800, beef-tongue roast beef ¥850, black-wagyu katsu sandwich ¥2,200, assorted meat sushi of three kinds ¥1,750, chicken thigh with sauce ¥650 (October 2026) · wagyu hiuchi stir-fried with peppers ¥1,200 (August 2026) · thick-cut toro beef tongue, Kawachi duck sashimi and roast, a rare cutlet, kamo shabu-shabu in ichiban dashi (Tabelog; 2026 reviews) · charcoal potato salad, chicken-dashi rolled omelette with shirasu, beef-tongue yukhoe kimbap, toro-taku kimbap, beef-tongue bolognese spring rolls (2026 reviews) · braised beef tongue or pork as the starter (2026 reviews) · table charge ¥500
places.notes: [Charcoal grill · Higashi-Shinsaibashi, beef tongue and Kawachi duck] A two-floor charcoal grill in the Galaxy building lanes of Higashi-Shinsaibashi, open straight from noon to 11 p.m., with a bar-like counter downstairs and tables and sofas upstairs. Despite the yakitori name the stars are beef tongue (a thick-cut 'toro' tongue skewer, a tongue tsukimi hamburg, tongue roast beef) and rare Kawachi duck, served as sashimi, roast or shabu-shabu in ichiban dashi, with creative plates like a black-wagyu katsu sandwich (¥2,200) and an assortment of meat sushi (¥1,750) in October 2026. It belongs with the Ura-Namba grill Black. Diners found it generous and stylish if a bit pricey and cramped; no cards, but PayPay works. Weekends book out.

chef_bio.background: Shop-maintained Tabelog listing: rare Kawachi duck through a unique route from a supplier with 150 years of history; thick-cut toro beef tongue; Kawachi duck roast and rare cutlet; kamo shabu-shabu in ichiban dashi; private rooms. Opened 2 February 2023. An August 2026 diner was told it is a sister of the charcoal-grill Italian Black in Ura-Namba.
chef_bio.specialty: Thick-cut toro beef tongue; Kawachi duck; meat sushi.

places.name: ステーキ・デボン (Steak Devon)
places.gf_detail: Ask when booking. No gluten information. Teppanyaki steak with several sauces, butter-grilled seafood with tartar, garlic rice seasoned with garlic soy sauce, crab fried rice or curry to finish; the staff checked each course dish for a pregnant diner (November 2025).
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: Kobe-beef and wagyu teppanyaki courses with seafood and butter.

Founded 1970 (official site).

places.cuisine: Teppanyaki of Kobe beef and Kyushu A5 black wagyu, grilled by a chef at each table (Tabelog; official site) · courses (Tabelog, tax included): C course of Kyushu A5 wagyu steak 100 g, nine dishes from a roast-beef starter to garlic rice and dessert ¥14,850; teppan feast with live Ezo abalone, Akashi octopus and black-wagyu steak ¥18,150; year-end course for four or more ¥17,600 (7 September 2026 – 30 January 2027) · the Devon course ¥17,930 (December 2024) and a chef's course of Kobe strip loin, wagyu fillet and seafood ¥22,000 (September 2025) · in reviews: roast beef, butter-grilled seafood with homemade tartar, oysters, Ise lobster, abalone, a whole baked potato with butter, grilled vegetables, roasted Aomori garlic, then garlic rice, crab omelette fried rice, beef pilaf or curry, dessert, and coffee with cookies (2024–26) · beef fillet cutlet sandwich; dozens of wines (Tabelog)
places.notes: [Steak · Kitashinchi, Kobe-beef teppanyaki since 1970] A Kitashinchi steakhouse founded in 1970, on the fifth floor of a building where staff wait at the ground-floor lift and a cow greets you when the doors open (2024–25 reviews). Besides an eight-seat counter there are four sofa booths, each for up to seven around its own large teppan, screened from the next so it feels private, which makes it a choice for families and business dinners. A chef at each table grills Kobe beef and A5 Kyushu wagyu with seafood such as abalone, oysters or Ise lobster, alongside a sweet buttered whole potato and roasted garlic diners rave about, before garlic rice or crab fried rice. Courses run ¥14,850–22,000 plus 10% service; one diner felt the courses lacked seasonal touches for the price (March 2026).

chef_bio.background: Per the official site (devon1970.com, read 2026-11-02): founded in Kitashinchi in 1970, "a steakhouse that history speaks for", Kobe beef bought on the strength of long trading, a counter and sofa booths for up to seven around large teppan, partitioned so neighbours cannot see each other. Per Tabelog: a dedicated chef grills in front of you; Kyushu A5 wagyu and Kobe beef; dozens of wines.
chef_bio.philosophy: "Gratitude to our guests", handed down since 1970 (official site).
chef_bio.specialty: Kobe-beef teppanyaki; baked potato with butter; garlic rice.

anecdotes.text: "On the 5th floor of the Kitashinchi Building, you are greeted by a cow as the elevator doors open." — September 2025, the chef's recommended course for JPY 22,000.

places.cuisine: Vietnamese food cooked by a chef from Vietnam, with Vietnamese beer, wine, spirits and cocktails (Tabelog) · lunch: beef-tendon pho with a mini rice bowl for ¥100 more (October 2026); bun cha, bun bo hue (October 2026); a banh mi and che buffet (October 2026); an all-you-can-eat che lunch (Tabelog) · à la carte: fresh and fried spring rolls, stir-fried water spinach with garlic, tom yum goong with shrimp, octopus and clams, shrimp and lettuce fried rice with lemongrass, green papaya salad with shrimp crackers, banh xeo, whole stuffed squid, wild boar in fermented shrimp sauce, frog, lime-leaf fries, che with coconut milk (hot or cold) (October 2026) · coriander refilled free (October 2026) · courses: Ho Chi Minh course without drinks ¥3,500; Vietnam course with 90 minutes of drinks ¥4,800; Bia Hoi course ¥5,800 (Tabelog, tax included)
places.notes: [Vietnamese · Umeda, a Vietnamese beer hall since 2001] A big, cheerful Vietnamese restaurant in a basement off Shin-Midosuji east of Umeda, open since 2001 and cooked by a chef from Vietnam, where one regular has eaten for over twenty years (October 2026). Weekday lunch is busy enough to queue: pho with beef tendon, bun cha with grilled meatballs, or a banh-mi-and-che buffet. In the evening come for Vietnamese beer with fresh and fried spring rolls, water spinach in garlic, banh xeo, lemongrass fried rice with shrimp and lettuce, stuffed squid or frog, all with as much free coriander as you like. Portions are large, so share. Ordering is by smartphone; drinks courses start at ¥4,800. An October 2026 diner noticed customers who seemed to be Vietnamese.

chef_bio.background: Per the shop-maintained Tabelog listing: authentic Vietnamese dishes by a Vietnamese chef, fresh spring rolls and pho, Vietnamese beer, wine, spirits and cocktails; opened 17 July 2001. places.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information. You choose the noodles (vermicelli, thick vermicelli, corn noodles, spinach noodles or Chinese wheat noodles) and toppings such as fish balls, dumplings and cheese tteokbokki, in one of three broths whose ingredients are not described.

places.cuisine: Mala tang, built ingredient by ingredient (Tabelog: tantanmen genre) · three broths: traditional mala, a milder "golden" broth, and a thick, numbing sesame "sticky" broth; spice levels you choose (2026) · ingredients from ¥100 a tag: vegetables, mushrooms, tofu skin, fish and shrimp balls, dumplings, cheese tteokbokki, seasoned egg, baby corn, white fungus and more (2026) · noodles: vermicelli, thick vermicelli, corn noodles, spinach noodles, Chinese noodles (2026) · a nine-ingredient bowl with spinach noodles came to ¥2,010, tax included (October 2026); another to ¥1,345 (September 2026) · sides and sweets: sweet potato sticks in rice paper, a panda "Nomi Chi" mochi with red bean ¥150, panda-pattern buns (2026)
places.notes: [Mala tang · Nishinakajima, a pick-your-own spicy soup shop with pandas] A 16-seat mala tang shop near Nishinakajima-Minamigata, opened in February 2026 and already lined up at lunch. Instead of weighing a self-served bowl, you pick bamboo tags from a display of samples, each tag a fixed portion from ¥100, and the kitchen cooks it: vegetables, mushrooms, tofu skin, fish balls, dumplings and a choice of five noodles. Then choose the broth, a classic spicy mala, a milder golden one, or a thick sesame "sticky" broth, and a spice level; level 2 is properly hot (2026). A full bowl runs about ¥1,300–2,000. Panda decor, panda mochi for dessert. One regular found the spice and the order inconsistent once (September 2026).

chef_bio.background: Per the Tabelog listing: mala tang (listed as tantanmen), opened 22 February 2026. Per reviews: "Instead of the typical weight-based selling style, [the shop uses] a method where you select bamboo tags while looking at food samples" (October 2026); "The staff are incredibly kind" (October 2026); "The staff provided a thorough explanation" (May 2026); the shop is themed around pandas, with panda aprons and panda sweets (2026).

places.notes: [Set meals · Higashi-Mikuni, chicken nanban for office lunches] A 16-seat chicken nanban specialist two minutes from Higashi-Mikuni Station, open since 2009, full before noon on weekdays with office workers and tradesmen (June 2026). You order on your phone by QR code, even while in line. The chicken nanban comes as breast, juicy and tender, or thigh, fried, dipped in sweet vinegar and covered in homemade tartar; the mix adds kara-age (¥1,650), and plain sets are ¥1,300. Large rice is free and there is stir-fried takana on the table to stretch it, plus a jar of "Maximum" seasoning. Keema curry with a chicken nanban on top is the other draw. One diner credits Miyazaki chicken for the flavour (December 2025). Closed Sundays.

chef_bio.background: Per the shop-maintained Tabelog listing: cafeteria and curry, opened 1 September 2009. Per reviews: "a Chicken Nanban specialty set meal restaurant" with "an atmosphere reminiscent of an old-fashioned set meal restaurant" (June 2026); "As expected, it's chicken from Miyazaki!" (December 2025); "Maximum seasoning, which is popular among camping enthusiasts and locals from Miyazaki" (May 2026); the order system moved from a ticket machine to phone ordering in 2024 (June 2024 review).
chef_bio.specialty: Chicken nanban with homemade tartar; keema curry.

anecdotes.text: "Orders are placed via QR code. It seems you can order on your smartphone while waiting in line." — June 2026.
"It's a popular place with a wait of 7 people. After about 15 minutes, I was seated … my food arrived in just 2 minutes after sitting down." — December 2025, chicken nanban mix.
"I decided to try the curry for the first time, and it was packed with more meat than I expected! Mixing in a bit of tartar sauce made it incredibly delicious!" — August 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ (店舗会員): 南蛮食堂 東三国店、食堂・カレー、大阪市淀川区東三国4丁目16-16、東三国駅から徒歩2分、JR 新大阪駅から10分、月〜土11:00〜22:00 (L.O.21:40)、日曜休み、カード・電子マネー・QR (Alipay、WeChat Pay も) 可、16席 (カウンター4、テーブル12)、禁煙、子ども可、テイクアウト、2009年9月1日オープン。口コミ(2023年5月〜2026年8月): チキン南蛮の定食の専門店、むねかももを選ぶ、甘酢と自家製タルタル、チキン南蛮定食1,300円、むね・もも・kara-age のミックス1,650円、kara-age 定食5個1,300円、チキンカツ定食、キーマカレー、チキン南蛮のせカレー、ごはん大盛り無料、卓上の高菜炒め食べ放題、玉ねぎとごまのドレッシング、卓上の Maximum (店でも880円で販売)、スマホの QR コードで注文、昼前から行列、生ビール550円、Miyazaki の鶏という声。

cultural_comfort.note: Order on your phone by QR code; Alipay and WeChat Pay accepted (Tabelog). No English menu evidence found.

places.name: バラの木 (Bara no Ki)
places.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: fried shrimp, tonkatsu, cutlets and croquettes in breadcrumbs, demi-glace sauce, and Neapolitan pasta.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: hamburg steak, fried shrimp, pork cutlets, sausages.
places.hours_raw: Mon–Sat 11:00–14:00 and 17:30–22:00; closed Sunday; hours may change (Tabelog). Cash only at lunch; at dinner cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners) and e-money (Tabelog). 20 seats, about five tables for four (February 2025); non-smoking (Tabelog). Lunch is served quickly; self-service miso soup with refills (2024–2026). Reopened in July 2024 after a closure and renovation (October 2024 review).
places.neighborhood: 東三国4-16-15, クイーンハイツ, 2 min from Higashi-Mikuni Stn (Tabelog; March 2025); next door to Namban Shokudo (東三国4-16-16)
places.cuisine: Yoshoku (Tabelog) · lunch: the "Bara no Ki Lunch" of a small hamburg steak and butterflied fried shrimp with salad and potatoes ¥1,000 (2024–2025); tonkatsu lunch with demi-glace, ginger pork lunch, katsu curry (September 2026); fillet cutlet lunch ¥1,000, Neapolitan large ¥1,200 (August 2024); large rice free, miso soup self-service with refills (2024) · evening: pork fillet cutlet and Kagoshima-chicken kara-age rice set ¥1,200 (March–April 2025); appetizer trio ¥800, fries ¥500, Sanriku fried oysters with homemade tartar ¥1,000, shrimp and shirasu ajillo with baguette ¥900 (February 2025); Iwate pork sausages, garlic toast, prosciutto (October 2024) · Peroni draft ¥800, Kaku highball ¥550 (February 2025)
places.notes: [Yoshoku · Higashi-Mikuni, a neighbourhood western-food house] A small yoshoku restaurant two minutes from Higashi-Mikuni Station that closed for a while and reopened in July 2024 after a renovation, now clean and calm with soft music. Lunch is the reason to come: the house "Bara no Ki Lunch" of a small hamburg steak and crisp butterflied fried shrimp for about ¥1,000, or tonkatsu with demi-glace, ginger pork and katsu curry, with self-service miso soup that one diner rated the best part (October 2024). In the evening it becomes a small bistro-izakaya with Sanriku fried oysters, ajillo, sausages and Peroni. Portions are on the modest side (2024). Cash only at lunch; closed Sundays.

roles: Kitchen and floor staff (unnamed); two staff per reviews
chef_bio.background: Per the Tabelog listing: yoshoku, 20 seats, lunch cash only. Per reviews: before the closure, "the owner manages everything alone" (October 2023); after reopening, "The master and a lady in the hall were managing the place" (September 2024) and "The staff consists of two men responsible for both service and cooking … The service was attentive, giving off a feeling of experience and professionalism" (October 2024); "I heard that [the restaurant] had been closed for a while, but [it] reopened in July of this year" (October 2024); the menu was narrowed to four lunches by September 2026.
chef_bio.specialty: Hamburg steak and fried shrimp lunch.

anecdotes.text: "Overall, the plate was well-balanced, but the standout was the miso soup. It had a perfect saltiness and temperature … of course, I went for a refill." — October 2024.
"I tried the fried oysters from Sanriku (JPY 1000). They were freshly fried and bursting with the rich flavor of the oysters. The homemade tartar sauce was a nice touch." — February 2025.
"The menu features only the Bara no Ki Lunch, Tonkatsu Lunch, Katsu Curry, and Ginger Pork Lunch." — September 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: バラの木、洋食、大阪市淀川区東三国4-16-15 クイーンハイツ、東三国駅から130m、月〜土11:00〜14:00、17:30〜22:00、日曜休み、昼は現金のみ、カード・電子マネー可、20席、禁煙。口コミ(2023年10月〜2026年9月): 休業のあと2024年7月に改装して再開、小さなハンバーグとエビフライのバラの木ランチ1,000円、デミグラスのとんかつランチ、生姜焼き、カツカレー、ヒレカツランチ、ナポリタン、ごはん大盛り無料、みそ汁はセルフでおかわり自由、夜は前菜3種800円、フライドポテト、Sanriku のカキフライ1,000円、エビとしらすのアヒージョ900円、Iwate の豚のソーセージ、ガーリックトースト、生ハム、Kagoshima の鶏の kara-age のライスセット1,200円、Peroni、角ハイボール、量はひかえめ、静かな BGM。

cultural_comfort.note: Order at the table; cash only at lunch. No English evidence found.

places.name: マレーシア ボレ (Malaysia Boleh)
places.gf_detail: Ask; the shop takes allergy requests for courses (official site). No gluten information. Noodle dishes (mee goreng, curry noodles with wheat noodles, spicy seafood thick noodles) contain wheat; fried rice, curries and satay use sauces whose ingredients are not listed.
places.vegan_detail: Ask. Tabelog lists vegetarian options, and the menu has vegetable dishes such as stir-fried water spinach and spicy eggplant salad, but the water spinach is cooked with belacan (shrimp paste) per the official site, and curries and noodles often use shrimp or fish seasonings.
places.hours_raw: Wed–Mon 11:30–14:30 (last order 14:00) and 17:30–23:00 (last order 22:00); closed Tuesday (official site; Tabelog). Two-hour limit at busy times (Tabelog). Lunch queues around 12:30–13:00 (September 2026). Course bookings from two people, in advance (official site). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners), IC cards, PayPay, d Barai, au PAY (official site; Tabelog). 26 seats (tables and a small counter); private hire for about 30; non-smoking; children and strollers welcome (Tabelog). The official site announces a price revision from 1 December (year not given).
places.neighborhood: Facing Umeda Sky Building, 大淀南1-4-20 — 7 min from JR Osaka Stn, 10 min from JR Fukushima Stn
places.cuisine: Malaysian cooking based on Nyonya (Chinese-Malay) dishes, with seasonings bought in Malaysia every year and halal-marked seasonings and ingredients, plenty of halal dishes (official site; Tabelog) · coconut keeps the spice mild (Tabelog) · courses (official site; Tabelog, tax included): Penang course ¥4,200 (prawn crackers, tofu and egg roll salad, satay, tom yum goong, stir-fried water spinach, chicken curry and rice, spicy seafood thick noodles, dessert), Malacca course ¥4,700, Makan course with 90-minute all-you-can-drink ¥5,000 · lunch sets about ¥1,000 with soup, salad and dessert (tapioca): nasi goreng, mee goreng, fried rice, curry noodles with coconut broth, kapao rice, yellow and green curries (August–October 2026) · evening: nasi lemak, stir-fried frog with vegetables, spicy eggplant salad, seafood pineapple fried rice (September 2026)
places.notes: [Malaysian · by Umeda Sky Building, Nyonya cooking] A small Malaysian restaurant facing the Umeda Sky Building, which calls itself Osaka's only Malaysian restaurant and has been open about twenty years, per a September 2026 diner. The cooking is based on Nyonya (Chinese-Malay) dishes, made with seasonings the shop brings back from Malaysia each year; the official site says it uses halal-marked seasonings and ingredients so Muslim guests can eat with peace of mind, and Tabelog lists many halal dishes, though it is not described as certified and alcohol is served. Lunch is the bargain, about ¥1,000 for nasi goreng, mee goreng or curry noodles with soup, salad and tapioca, and a queue forms around 12:30. Evening courses start at ¥4,200 (satay, tom yum goong, water spinach with belacan, chicken curry, spicy seafood noodles). Friendly staff who remember regulars. Closed Tuesdays.

roles: Owner (unnamed; signs a notice on the official site)
chef_bio.background: Official site (read 2026-11-02): "大阪唯一のマレーシア料理店" (Osaka's only Malaysian restaurant); Nyonya cooking, a fusion of Chinese and Malay food, with many halal dishes; seasonings bought in Malaysia every year to reproduce the authentic taste; "ハラールマーク付きの調味料や食材を使用しておりますので、イスラム教徒のお客様にも安心して" (halal-marked seasonings and ingredients, so Muslim guests can eat with peace of mind); a room decorated with Malaysian goods. A September 2026 diner writes it seems to have been in business for about 20 years.
chef_bio.philosophy: Authentic Malaysian taste, made so that every guest can eat with peace of mind (official site).
chef_bio.specialty: Nasi goreng and mee goreng lunches; satay; Penang course.

anecdotes.text: "The staff remembered me, and it felt just like old times." — September 2026, the kapao rice.
"I arrived at 12:30, but there was a line, so I wandered around for a bit... Even after returning around 1 PM, the line was still there." — 17 September 2026.
"The meal came with a salad and dessert, tapioca, all for JPY 1000." — September 2026, the curry noodles.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト: マレーシア ボレ、大阪唯一のマレーシア料理店、スカイビルとうめきたの近く、中華とマレーの料理が融合したニョニャ料理がベース、ハラール対応メニューも豊富、毎年マレーシアで調味料を仕入れ、ハラールマーク付きの調味料や食材を使用、サテー、空芯菜のブラチャン炒め、えびの入ったピリ辛の太麺、ペナンコース4,200円 (クルポ、豆腐卵巻きサラダ、サテー、トムヤムクン、空芯菜、チキンカレー＆ライス、海鮮ピリ辛太麺、本日のデザート、2名から事前予約、アレルギーは相談を)、大阪市北区大淀南1-4-20、11:30〜14:30 (L.O.14:00)、17:30〜23:00 (L.O.22:00)、火曜定休、カード・交通系電子マネー・PayPay・d払い・au PAY 可、12月1日から価格改定のお知らせ。食べログ (店舗会員): マラッカコース4,700円、飲み放題つきのマカンコース5,000円、26席、禁煙、子ども歓迎、混雑時は2時間制、ハラールとベジタリアンのオプション。

cultural_comfort.note: Order from a menu of Malaysian dishes; staff explain the menu (September 2026). A September 2026 diner found few tourists. No English menu listed.

staff_allergy_handling.text: Official site (Penang course): "アレルギーや食べられないものがありましたらご相談下さい" (consult the shop about allergies and foods you cannot eat).

positives.text: Official site: halal-marked seasonings and ingredients are used so that Muslim guests can eat with peace of mind; Tabelog lists halal and vegetarian options. Not described as halal-certified; alcohol is served.

places.name: pesce&carne MIMOZA ～ミモザ～ (pesce & carne MIMOZA ~ Mimoza ~)
places.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information. Courses centre on pasta, gnocchi, pizza and baguette with the ajillo (2026 reviews).
places.vegan_detail: Ask. No vegan information. Courses are built on fish from the market, beef and pork, with cheese sauces and parfaits.
places.hours_raw: Mon–Fri 11:30–14:30 (last order food 13:30) and 17:00–22:30 (last order food 21:30, drinks 22:00); Sat, Sun and holidays 11:30–15:00 and 17:00–22:30 (Tabelog). Bookings lapse 15 minutes after the reserved time without contact; same-day bookings within an hour by phone (Tabelog). A 90-minute limit was given on one October 2026 booking. Cover (otoshi) ¥380; a 10% year-end surcharge from early December to 5 January (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB) and PayPay; no e-money (Tabelog). 20 seats (30 standing); non-smoking (Tabelog). Opened 2 September 2025 (Tabelog).
places.neighborhood: お初天神東門ビル 2F, a minute from Ohatsu Tenjin — 3 min from Higashi-Umeda Stn exit 7
places.cuisine: Italian of seasonal ingredients by a young chef from a well-known restaurant; everything homemade, from appetizers to desserts; wines and cocktails chosen by the chef (Tabelog) · lunch: pasta or pizza with salad, soup and a drink ¥2,200, three appetizers +¥500, steak +¥1,500 (October 2026); Awaji beef steak lunch course ¥3,500 and French pork steak ("Marietta") course ¥3,000, one drink minimum (Tabelog) · evening: Mimoza course of fish and meat, 11 dishes, food only ¥6,500 (Tabelog); girls'-night course with all-you-can-drink (sparkling and wine, no beer) ¥6,000 for women, ¥6,500 for men: three appetizers, seasonal ajillo, the house pasta, pork chuck-eye steak, gnocchi in cheese sauce, a parfait (September–October 2026) · mackerel with ume and gochujang cream pasta (September 2026)
places.notes: [Italian · Ohatsu Tenjin, a young chef's homemade Italian] A twenty-seat second-floor Italian a minute from the Ohatsu Tenjin shrine, opened in September 2025, where a young chef from a well-known restaurant makes everything in house. Most 2026 diners came for the girls'-night course (¥6,000, ¥6,500 for men) with all-you-can-drink sparkling and wine: three appetizers, an ajillo good enough to mop up with baguette, the house pasta, a pork steak and gnocchi in cheese sauce, then a parfait. Lunch is a ¥2,200 pasta or pizza set, with appetizers or a steak as add-ons. Birthdays get the lights dimmed and music for the plate. Complaints: a lunch price rise and thin pasta (October 2026), and a 90-minute booking that ended before the main was finished.

roles: Chef (unnamed), young, trained at a well-known restaurant (Tabelog)
chef_bio.background: Shop text (Tabelog): stylish Italian a minute from Ohatsu Tenjin; authentic Italian with seasonal ingredients; everything homemade from appetizers to desserts; "Passionate Italian Cuisine by a Young Chef from a Renowned Restaurant"; wines and cocktails selected by the chef. Opened 2 September 2025. An October 2026 diner booked here was moved by phone to the restaurant's "second location nearby".
chef_bio.philosophy: Seasonal produce, everything homemade (Tabelog).
chef_bio.specialty: Girls'-night course; gnocchi with cheese sauce.

anecdotes.text: "Suddenly, the lights went out, and Disney-like music started playing" as a birthday plate came out — September 2026.
"The ajillo was so delicious that I could almost drink the oil, and I wanted to ask for more baguette." — October 2026, the girls'-night course.
"The main dish arrived just 15 minutes before I was supposed to leave" — October 2026, a booking with a 90-minute limit.

cultural_comfort.note: Set courses or lunch sets (2026). No English evidence found.

places.name: 地酒だいにんぐやす (Jizake Dining Yasu)
places.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information. The menu includes fresh pasta, maitake tempura and spiced fried eggplant; sashimi, sushi rolls and shirako ponzu are usually eaten with soy-based sauces containing wheat.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a seafood and sake izakaya (sashimi, sushi rolls, shirako, clams, yukke).
places.hours_raw: From 18:00 until closing, no fixed end; closing days not fixed; bookings outside these hours by arrangement, including lunch, late-night and early-morning private hire (Tabelog). Reservations recommended; often fully booked (2026 reviews). Prices shown before tax; no service charge (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners), e-money and QR (Tabelog). 14 seats: 7 at the counter, 8 at tables (tables by reservation; parties of 2–3 may be seated at the counter); private hire for 7–15; smoking allowed; bring-your-own drinks (Tabelog). Opened 15 June 2019 (Tabelog).
places.neighborhood: A third-floor shop (伊勢屋ビル 302) just off Higashi-dori, in the Douyama area — 5 min from Higashi-Umeda, Hankyu Umeda or JR Osaka Stn
places.cuisine: Seafood izakaya with local sake, including kimoto-style and aged sakes, and fresh pasta (Tabelog) · large portions: assorted sashimi, tuna maki, ikura, seafood yukke (August 2026); toro-taku hosomaki that looks like a thick roll, negitoro, a tuna and daikon roll (September–October 2026); shirako with ponzu in season; maitake tempura with spice; sake-steamed clams; spiced fried eggplant; shrimp pasta and a fresh-noodle tomato-cream pasta (2026 reviews) · sakes named in reviews: Dewazakura, Hanamura, Nanamizu, Tamako; a sake list with tasting notes (October 2026) · courses for birthdays, dates and business, and hot-pot courses for groups, to budget (Tabelog)
places.notes: [Izakaya · Umeda, Higashi-dori, fish and sake on a third floor] A fourteen-seat izakaya up in a building just off Higashi-dori, hard to find on a first visit and usually full, where a young, lively crowd orders generous seafood and local sake. The dishes diners keep naming are the toro-taku roll (thin rolls that look like thick ones), shirako with ponzu, a heaped sashimi platter, maitake tempura and, unexpectedly, fresh pasta. Portions are big, so two people should order by halves; spending runs ¥5,000–10,000 with a few drinks. The sake list explains each bottle's character. Downsides in 2026 reviews: smoking allowed, tight seats (one diner sat on a beer crate with a cushion), a bleach smell on entry one October evening, and sashimi that one regular suspected was pre-sliced.

chef_bio.background: Shop text (Tabelog): local sake including kimoto-style and aged sakes; fresh pasta; banquets and private hire for 7–15; creative dishes to hot pots, tailored to budget and requests. Opened 15 June 2019.
chef_bio.philosophy: Accommodate customers' requests as much as possible (Tabelog).
chef_bio.specialty: Toro-taku roll; shirako ponzu; local sake.

anecdotes.text: "What looks like a thick roll turns out to be a thin roll. Everything is served in generous portions, so I recommend ordering half for two people!" — September 2026.
"The menu also includes descriptions of the sake's characteristics, making it easier to choose." — October 2026.
"Sitting on a cushion with the plastic box containing the beer was a bit uncomfortable for my backside, though (laughs)." — October 2026.

cultural_comfort.note: Small, busy counter; a sake list with tasting notes (October 2026). No English evidence found.

places.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information. Courses include a chateaubriand katsu sandwich (bread and breading), cold noodles, beef curry and meat grilled with tare, which is usually soy-based with wheat; ask for salt-grilled cuts.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a yakiniku restaurant of Omi beef, with oxtail soup.
places.hours_raw: Daily from 17:00, closing time not given; lunch on request; open Sundays and holidays; closing days not fixed (Tabelog). Courses can be booked 12:00–24:30 (Tabelog). Reservation only (Tabelog). Service charge 8%; bring-your-own wine ¥3,000 a bottle; free birthday or anniversary plate (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners), e-money, PayPay, d Barai, Rakuten Pay, au PAY, Alipay, WeChat Pay (Tabelog). 16 seats: 4 at the counter, 12 at tables, semi-private rooms for 2 and 4; smoking allowed, though guests may be asked to refrain (Tabelog). Opened 16 October 2022 (Tabelog).
places.neighborhood: Kitashinchi, 杉の家ビル B1F — 3 min from Kitashinchi Stn exit 11-41
places.cuisine: High-end yakiniku of Omi beef where, on courses, staff grill every piece for you (Tabelog) · courses (Tabelog, tax included): Omi Beef Delight course A ¥15,000 (12 dishes: wagyu tongue, strip loin, salt- and sauce-grilled cuts, horumon, appetizers, oxtail soup simmered 12–13 hours, gyudon and cold noodles); course B ¥18,000 (13 dishes) with a rare chateaubriand katsu sandwich · à la carte now available (Tabelog): tongue, sirloin eaten with egg yolk and rice, grilled broccoli salad, cold noodles (June 2026) · kimchi to start, the katsu sandwich, grilled beef over rice (October 2026); rice with meat and egg yolk (January 2026); curry with beef cutlet on request (May 2024); kuzu cold noodles (June 2024) · wines imported from France and Italy (Tabelog)
places.notes: [Yakiniku · Kitashinchi, Omi beef grilled for you] A basement yakiniku room in Kitashinchi where you don't touch the grill: on the courses, staff cook each cut of Omi beef in front of you and bring it to the table at its peak, between appetizers and an oxtail soup simmered for half a day. The ¥15,000 course runs from tongue and strip loin through horumon to gyudon and cold noodles; the ¥18,000 course adds a rare chateaubriand katsu sandwich that diners call the best thing on the menu. À la carte is now possible, and in June 2026 the owner came to grill one table's sirloin. Wines come from France and Italy; 8% service. Semi-private rooms suit business dinners; smoking is allowed, and one December 2025 diner was put off by loud regulars.

roles: Owner (unnamed; grilled at the table in a June 2026 review)
chef_bio.background: Shop text (Tabelog): a high-end yakiniku restaurant a short walk from Kitashinchi Station; top-quality wagyu, Omi beef the speciality; courses in which staff grill the meat in front of the guest; wines sourced directly from France and Italy; a homemade oxtail soup simmered 12–13 hours. Opened 16 October 2022.
chef_bio.philosophy: Great emphasis on the meat selection, cutting technique and grilling (Tabelog).
chef_bio.specialty: Omi beef course; chateaubriand katsu sandwich.

anecdotes.text: "Since it was an attended course, I didn't have to cook, which made it so easy to enjoy my meal." — December 2024, a fifth visit.
"The katsu sandwich was especially outstanding." — October 2026.
"I was particularly impressed by the rice topped with meat and egg yolk—it was simply amazing!" — January 2026, course A.

places.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: soba and udon in a soy-sauce broth, served in sets with katsu-don, tempura bowls or kara-age; the soba's buckwheat ratio is not stated.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: soba and udon in dashi broth, with katsu-don, shrimp tempura or fried chicken in the sets.
places.hours_raw: Mon–Sat 11:00–14:00; closed Sunday and holidays; hours may change (Tabelog). Lunch only. No reservations; cash only (Tabelog). 20 seats (Tabelog): shared tables for four downstairs and a tatami room upstairs (August and September 2026); non-smoking (Tabelog). Full of office workers from just before noon, but tables turn over fast (2025–2026).

places.cuisine: Neighbourhood soba and udon lunch house · set meals with warm or cold soba or udon: "Ume" with a mini tempura bowl ¥960 (June 2025, September 2026); "Take" with a mini katsu-don and kitsune soba ¥960 (February 2025); katsu-don with udon ¥960 (December 2025); katsu-don with mini soba ¥940 (May 2026); katsu-don with zaru soba (October 2026); inari with bukkake udon ¥850 (August 2026); fried-chicken bento with wakame soba ¥980 (October 2026) · zaru soba ¥750 (April 2026) · chilled tanuki soba ¥860, large +¥220 (June 2025) · meat soba with inari (November 2025) · a slightly sweet soy broth, sweet fried tofu (2025–2026)
places.notes: [Soba · Nishinakajima, the office workers' lunch soba house] A busy lunch-only soba and udon shop on a back street behind the APA Hotel in Nishinakajima, filled from before noon with office workers at shared tables and turning them over fast. The draw is the set meal: warm or cold soba or udon with a mini katsu-don, a mini tempura bowl or inari, around ¥850–980 (2025–2026), in portions that leave even big eaters full. The broth is slightly sweet soy, the fried tofu sweet, and the soba has a fair buckwheat flavour (2025). Plain zaru soba is ¥750 (April 2026). Three cooks and four floor staff work the rush (May 2026), and a tatami room upstairs takes the overflow. Cash only; 11:00–14:00, closed Sunday.

chef_bio.background: No shop description on Tabelog. Reviewers: "There were three people in the kitchen and four serving staff, all busy at work" (May 2026); "the charm of a local soba shop" (February 2025).
chef_bio.specialty: Soba or udon set with mini katsu-don or tempura bowl.

anecdotes.text: "Despite it being just before noon, the place was already about 80% full, and it reached full capacity while I was eating." — May 2026, the katsu-don set with mini soba for JPY 940.

"I was impressed by the delicious broth! It had a slightly sweet soy sauce flavor that suited my taste perfectly." — September 2026, the Ume set with warm soba for JPY 960.

places.name: 大屋 (Daiya)
places.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: takoyaki is a wheat batter, and yakisoba and curry udon are wheat noodles.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: takoyaki with octopus, horumon, oden in broth.
places.hours_raw: Daily 18:00–23:00; hours may change (Tabelog). Closed on rainy days (September 2026). Not always open on the dot: one November 2025 diner arrived at opening and waited about 30 minutes while the couple prepared. No reservations; no cards or e-money; PayPay accepted (Tabelog). 4 counter seats inside (Tabelog), plus outdoor counters and about four tables for around ten (2025–2026), with electric blankets and cushions in winter (February 2026); smoking allowed; takeaway (Tabelog). A July 2024 diner waited an hour. Opened 22 November 2010 (Tabelog).
places.neighborhood: 宮原5-2-17 — 1 min from Exit 5 of Higashimikuni Stn (Tabelog), on a Showa-feeling street of small izakaya about 10 min from Shin-Osaka (September 2025)
places.cuisine: Takoyaki: large, crisp outside and creamy inside, by number of pieces, with a choice of flavours: sauce and mayonnaise, dashi soy, ponzu, curry, garlic pepper mayonnaise (2024–2026) · spicy horumon, horumon yakisoba (2025–2026) · oden, curry udon (April 2026) · 6 takoyaki, spicy horumon and two Asahi Super Dry came to ¥1,650 (May 2026) · beer, sake, shochu (Tabelog)
places.notes: [Takoyaki · Higashimikuni, a couple's stand with outdoor tables] A tiny takoyaki stand a minute from Higashimikuni Station, run since 2010 by a warm older couple (2024–2026), with four seats inside and a handful of outdoor tables where you eat and drink under the evening sky, blankets supplied in winter (February 2026). The takoyaki are big, golf-ball size, crisp outside and creamy inside, in flavours from classic sauce and mayonnaise to dashi soy, ponzu, curry and garlic pepper mayo; spicy horumon and horumon yakisoba go with a beer. Six takoyaki, horumon and two beers came to ¥1,650 (May 2026). The walls are covered in signed boards from stage actors, including the cast of The Prince of Tennis, and a railway YouTuber has sent fans here (2025). Evenings only; closed when it rains.

chef_bio.background: No shop description on Tabelog; opened 22 November 2010 (Tabelog). Reviewers: "This takoyaki shop is run by a couple" (September 2026); "The owners, an older gentleman and lady, are very kind" (November 2024); "The owner and the lady of the house are super kind!" (April 2026); the walls are covered with signed boards and goods from stage actors, among them the cast of "The Prince of Tennis" (October 2025, September 2026).
chef_bio.specialty: Large takoyaki in many flavours; spicy horumon.

anecdotes.text: "It felt like outdoor dining" — February 2026; electric blankets, cushions and a lap blanket made it comfortable for drinks.
"I had 6 takoyaki, spicy horumon, and 2 Asahi SUPER DRY for JPY 1,650, which is a great value!" — May 2026.
"This place seems to be a hotspot for fans of 'The Prince of Tennis,' as it displays signatures from the cast." — October 2025.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: 大屋、たこ焼き・焼きそば、大阪市淀川区宮原5-2-17、東三国駅5番出口から徒歩1分、毎日18:00〜23:00、予約不可、カード・電子マネー不可、PayPay 可、4席 (カウンター)、喫煙可、テイクアウト、2010年11月22日オープン。口コミ(2024年7月〜2026年9月): 夫婦で切り盛り、やさしい年配の夫婦、雨の日は休み、外のカウンターとテーブル4つほど、冬は電気毛布とクッション、ゴルフボールより少し大きいたこ焼き、外はカリッと中はとろり、ソースマヨ、だし醤油、ポン酢、カレー、ガーリックペッパーマヨ、辛いホルモン、ホルモン焼きそば、おでん、カレーうどん、6個と辛いホルモンとビール2本で1,650円、舞台の俳優のサイン、「The Prince of Tennis」のキャスト、鉄道の YouTuber のおすすめ、開店時間でもまだ準備中の日も。

places.name: らーめん やまふじ 新大阪本店 (Ramen Yamafuji Shin'osaka honten)
places.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: wheat ramen, tsukemen and mazesoba noodles.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: broths of pork bone, chicken carcass, niboshi and kombu, with chashu.
places.hours_raw: Mon and Wed 11:30–16:00 (last order 15:50); Tue, Thu and Fri 11:30–21:00 (last order 20:45); Sat and holidays 11:30–15:00 (last order 15:00); closed Sunday (Tabelog). No reservations; cash only (Tabelog); a ticket machine that takes new notes (August 2025). 12 seats: 8 at the counter and 2 tables (May 2026); non-smoking (Tabelog). Lunch price ¥950 on weekdays; rice ¥50 or ¥100 extra, self-service and refillable (2025–2026). Opened here 20 December 2019 (Tabelog); a May 2026 diner remembers the shop before it moved.
places.neighborhood: 西宮原2-6-16, ground floor of 新大阪コーポビアネーズ, tucked at the back of the apartment building's entrance (September 2026) — about 13 min from Mikuni Stn (February 2026); parking at Super Life nearby (September 2026)
places.cuisine: Yamafuji ramen ¥950 (2025–2026): a pork-bone and seafood shoyu of pork bones, chicken carcasses, niboshi and kombu, light on oil (May 2026), with thin straight or medium-thick curly noodles and bamboo shoots; egg topping ¥150 · white miso ramen, slightly sweet with a hint of yuzu, ¥950 weekday lunch, ¥1,000 at other times (November 2025, April 2026); special with two kinds of chashu, egg, menma, a spicy paste and citrus peel (April 2026) · Ichikara ramen ¥980 (July 2026) · tsukemen in a seafood dip with curly noodles, served in a metal bowl (August and September 2026) · mazesoba with minced meat and egg (June 2026) · rice self-service and refillable for ¥50–100, with a kombu tsukudani from the broth kombu and a niboshi furikake to top it (2025–2026) · staff-meal rice bowl (April 2026)
places.notes: [Ramen · Nishimiyahara, a ramen made for rice] A 12-seat ramen shop hidden at the back of an apartment building's entrance west of Shin-Osaka, here since 2019, whose idea is ramen that goes with rice. The Yamafuji ramen (¥950) is a pork-bone and seafood shoyu of pork, chicken, niboshi and kombu, with thin or curly noodles, and the rice is self-service and refillable for ¥50–100, with a tsukudani made from the broth's own kombu and a niboshi furikake to pile on (2025–2026). The other house bowl is a slightly sweet white miso ramen with yuzu; there are tsukemen and a mazesoba too. One regular has been back ten times (March 2026); lunch can mean a short wait outside. Cash only; closed Sunday, and only Tuesday, Thursday and Friday run into the evening.

chef_bio.background: No shop description on Tabelog; opened at this address 20 December 2019 (Tabelog). Reviewers: the shop moved here from an earlier site (May and September 2026); its concept is ramen that goes with rice (February 2026); "the rice policy differs between this location and the main store" (November 2025); friendly staff (April 2026). The osaka-kita crawl also lists らーめんやまふじ スープ工房東三国店.
chef_bio.philosophy: Ramen that goes well with rice (a February 2026 review, on "the restaurant's concept").
chef_bio.specialty: Yamafuji ramen with refillable rice; white miso ramen.

anecdotes.text: "I topped it with a tsukudani made from the kombu used for the ramen broth and some niboshi (dried sardine) furikake." — March 2026, a diner on visit ten, the Yamafuji ramen for JPY 950.
"The white miso soup, which has a slightly sweet seafood base with a hint of yuzu, pairs perfectly with the curly noodles." — April 2026, JPY 1,000 on a Saturday.
"The restaurant is located in a somewhat hidden spot at the back of the first floor entrance of the apartment building, so be cautious." — September 2026.

places.name: かつ兵衛 (Katsu Bei)
places.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: breaded, deep-fried pork cutlet in every bowl.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: pork cutlet with egg simmered in dashi.
places.hours_raw: Tabelog: Mon–Wed 11:00–14:00 and 17:00–21:00; Thu–Sat 11:00–14:00; closed Sunday; hours may change. Reviewers find it shorter in the evening: an October 2026 diner says it closes at 19:00 even on weekdays, and at 18:30 one April 2026 evening it was already closing; it sometimes opens before 11:00 (August and September 2026), and once showed "Closed for Preparation" at 13:20 (October 2026). No reservations; cash only (Tabelog); order at the ticket machine (2026). 12 counter seats on Tabelog, 10–11 per reviewers; non-smoking (Tabelog). Lines at lunch; come at opening.
places.neighborhood: 東三国4-17-7 — about 200 m from Higashimikuni Stn (Tabelog), in an old shopping street 2 min from the station and 10 min from Shin-Osaka (October 2026)
places.cuisine: Katsu-don specialist (2024–2026) · the menu, October 2026: katsu-don ¥900, oroshi katsu-don with grated daikon ¥900, sauce katsu-don ¥900, curry katsu-don ¥970, each with red miso soup · add-ons: large rice ¥50, double egg ¥50, double katsu ¥450 (October 2026) · a thick pork-loin cutlet fried to order, cut in eight, laid on rice and topped with egg simmered in dashi, crisp despite the egg (2026) · the sauce katsu-don comes on shredded cabbage with an onsen egg (September 2026) · takuan on the counter (2026)
places.notes: [Katsu-don · Higashimikuni, one cook and a ¥900 bowl] A one-man katsu-don counter in the old shopping street by Higashimikuni Station, with a line at most lunches and Southern All Stars on the stereo. The owner fries each thick pork-loin cutlet to order, slices it into eight and lays it on rice under egg simmered in dashi, so it stays crisp under the egg; ¥900 with red miso soup, or ¥970 with curry (October 2026). Oroshi with grated daikon and a sauce katsu-don on cabbage are the alternatives, and double katsu or double egg is a few hundred yen more for big appetites. A card on the counter explains, with evident love, what is special about the pork (October 2026). Get there at opening; evenings end early, around 19:00 per reviewers, and Thursday to Saturday is lunch only.

chef_bio.background: No shop description on Tabelog. Reviewers: "The restaurant is run solely by the owner, with just counter seating available" (November 2024); "it's a one-person operation" (September 2026); "The owner's passion for Katsu Don shines through" (October 2026); a table card titled "What's Amazing Here!" explains the pork (October 2026).
chef_bio.specialty: Katsu-don; oroshi, sauce and curry katsu-don.

anecdotes.text: "The friendly chef was working solo but was very efficient." — October 2026, the katsu-don for JPY 900.
"Sitting at the counter, the sounds of frying katsu and the crisp slicing of the meat are quite pleasant!" — October 2026, the curry katsu-don.
"You get the flavor absorption of stewed Katsu without losing the crispiness, capturing the best of both worlds." — October 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: かつ兵衛、カツ丼、大阪市淀川区東三国4-17-7、東三国駅から201m、月〜水11:00〜14:00、17:00〜21:00、木〜土11:00〜14:00、日曜休み、予約不可、現金のみ、12席 (カウンター)、禁煙。口コミ(2024年11月〜2026年10月): 店主がひとりで切り盛り、カウンター10〜11席、券売機、昼は行列、カツ丼900円、おろしカツ丼900円、ソースカツ丼900円、カレーカツ丼970円、赤だしつき、ごはん大盛り50円、卵ダブル50円、カツダブル450円、厚いロースのカツを注文ごとに揚げて8切れ、だしで煮た卵をかける、ソースカツ丼はキャベツと温泉卵、テーブルに豚の説明「What's Amazing Here!」、たくあん、Southern All Stars の音楽、夜は19時までという声も、11時前に開くことも。

places.name: ビストロolympic (Bistro Olympic)
places.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information. The carpaccio of five fish with four sauces, ajillo, a bluefin-cheek steak and fried potatoes sit beside pastas, fried pizza and baguette; nothing is described as gluten-free.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a seafood-led Italian bar; the soup of the day served as the appetizer has been a white-fish soup (September 2026) and most plates are fish, meat or cheese.
places.hours_raw: Mon, Tue, Fri–Sun 12:00–24:00; Wed–Thu 17:00–24:00; last orders food 23:00, drinks 23:30; one irregular closing day a month; lunch service may close irregularly (official site; Tabelog). Reservations; tables may be shared at a large table, two-hour limit when busy (Tabelog). A cover charge (お通し) applies; a soup of the day comes as the appetizer (Tabelog; 2026 reviews). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners), IC cards, iD, QUICPay and PayPay (Tabelog). 41 seats at a counter, tables and an open terrace; the doors are thrown open in fine weather (October 2026); a 4th-floor event space, tide pool, for up to 45; non-smoking; children of school age welcome (official site; Tabelog). Opened 22 December 2017 (Tabelog).
places.neighborhood: Namba Sennichimae 4-19, in Ura Namba between Namba and Nihonbashi — 4 min from Nankai Namba Stn
places.cuisine: A casual Italian bar of seafood and wine (official site; 2026 reviews) · the signature carpaccio of five fish (e.g. tuna, yellowtail, kanpachi, returning bonito, salmon, scallop) with four sauces such as balsamic and basil (2026) · soup of the day as the appetizer: chilled potage, white fish and basil, chilled pumpkin (August–October 2026) · ajillo of shrimp or mushroom with baguette, shrimp mayo, fries, octopus and avocado, chicken neck with lotus root and zucchini, lotus root and shrimp in anchovy butter, a bluefin-tuna-cheek steak with onion sauce (2026) · pastas: yam and dashi, bonito and lily bulb in tomato, peperoncino; fried pizza · natural wines including rosé and orange (official site), wines of the day from sweet to dry (October 2026) · courses and all-you-can-drink (Tabelog; September 2026) · about ¥3,000–¥5,000 a head (2026)
places.notes: [Italian · Ura Namba, a noon-to-midnight seafood bistro] A casual, open-fronted Italian bar in Ura Namba, with a counter, tables and a terrace, serving straight through from noon to midnight (from 17:00 on Wednesdays and Thursdays). Reviewers place it in the Hidezo group of fish restaurants, and the fish shows: the dish nearly everyone orders is a carpaccio of five kinds of raw fish with four sauces to mix. Then ajillo, a bluefin-cheek steak, shrimp mayo or a pasta of yam and dashi, with a natural-wine list that runs to orange and rosé. A soup of the day comes as the appetizer. Busy most evenings and fully booked by 18:00 on a Sunday in October 2026, though walk-ins often get in; with the doors open, small insects can find their way in (October 2026). A 4th-floor space hosts parties of up to 45.

roles: Chef (unnamed; "シェフがこだわり抜いた一皿" on the official site)
chef_bio.background: Per the official site: a casual, popular-style Italian bar in Ura Namba, open from noon to midnight, with natural wines and a 4th-floor party space; sister shops listed on the site are bar pond, 立ち飲みピラフ, お料理 だいち, tide pool, Meguri Osaka and ぱどる. Several 2026 reviewers say it belongs to the "Hidezo" (also written "Hidezou") group, and one regular of the neighbouring Hidezo says that shop is next door (October 2026). Opened 22 December 2017 (Tabelog).
chef_bio.philosophy: Casual and authentic at once: photogenic plates for day drinking, dates and parties, any time from noon to midnight (official site).
chef_bio.specialty: Carpaccio of five fish with four sauces; natural wine.

anecdotes.text: "The moment the 'Assorted Carpaccio of 5 Types' arrived, my excitement skyrocketed! You absolutely have to order this dish when you visit!" — October 2026.
"I often visit the neighboring Hidezou, but this was my first time here." — October 2026, fully booked by 6 PM on a Sunday.
"While the open air was nice, it did attract some small bugs, which was a bit unpleasant..." — October 2026.

places.cuisine: Kansai-style "grilled" sukiyaki of Kobe beef and wagyu in square iron pans, the meat seared first and seasoned with sugar and soy sauce, the first slice cooked at the table by the staff (official site) · Kobe beef of the top grade as the main (official site); a domestic-beef sukiyaki or shabu-shabu set ¥5,800 (140 g of loin or ribeye, vegetables, udon to finish, the chef's homemade dessert), booked online (September–October 2026); courses from ¥5,800 to ¥32,800 (October 2026), including Kobe beef, wagyu and a course with sirloin steak (official site; 2026 reviews) · vegetables: green onion, shungiku, tofu, enoki, shirataki, onion (October 2026) · two eggs to compare, Oita's "Ryuu no Tamago" ("Dragon's Egg") and Kyoto's "Dose", with free refills (September–October 2026) · Sapporo Lager ¥715, Kubota Manju 180 ml ¥1,980 (October 2026)
places.notes: [Sukiyaki · Higashi-Shinsaibashi, Kobe beef in private rooms] On the 8th floor of a Higashi-Shinsaibashi building, a sukiyaki house of private rooms decorated with ukiyo-e and ink paintings, opened in May 2025 by the beef-focused restaurant company Dancin' Diner. The style is Kansai sukiyaki: the meat seared in a square iron pan and seasoned with sugar and soy sauce, the first slice cooked in front of you by the staff. Kobe beef is the headline, but most 2026 diners ordered the ¥5,800 domestic-beef set booked online, which comes with udon to finish and a homemade dessert, and enjoyed comparing two dipping eggs. One noted the domestic beef was less marbled than Kobe beef. English menus and English-speaking staff; the room is aimed at overseas visitors as much as business dinners. Closed Thursdays.

roles: Run by 株式会社ダンシンダイナー (Dancin' Diner), a beef-focused restaurant company (official site)
chef_bio.background: Per the brand page on d-diner.net: a Kobe beef and wagyu sukiyaki house drawing on long experience supplying high-quality beef, aiming to "lead the way" in bringing wagyu to the world; Kansai-style "grilled" sukiyaki in square iron pans; top-grade Kobe beef as the main; every seat in a private room decorated with ukiyo-e and ink painting, suited to sightseeing, business entertaining and overseas guests. The company runs yakiniku, shabu-shabu and teppanyaki brands in Kansai and Kanto (d-diner.net brand list); this is its only 牛陣. Opened 23 May 2025 (Tabelog).
chef_bio.philosophy: An unforgettable wagyu experience that blends Japanese culture with Kansai sukiyaki (official site).
chef_bio.specialty: Kansai-style Kobe beef sukiyaki; two-egg tasting.

anecdotes.text: "You can choose between two types of eggs: 'Dragon's Egg' and 'Kyoto Egg,' both of which are available for unlimited refills." — September 2026, the ¥5,800 set.

"The clientele includes many Japanese customers, and recently, there has been an increase in foreign visitors" — October 2026, Halloween decorations in the rooms.

places.cuisine: Sanuki-style udon, firm and chewy (2026 reviews), with a long tablet menu of tempura, sides, kushiage and oden · up to 1.5 servings at no extra charge, or a smaller 0.8 serving (September–October 2026) · kakiage sudachi udon, eaten with soy sauce poured over (March and October 2026); kakiage udon with two large fritters; cold udon with burdock tempura; meat udon; chicken-tempura curry udon; beef-tendon curry udon; duck and chicken paitan udon; limited chicken-miso udon (2026) · lunch sets until 14:00 with a choice of rice: takikomi gohan, white rice, clam rice, takana rice, mentaiko rice; ¥1,100–¥1,400 (September–October 2026); a daily special such as chikuwa-tempura udon ¥1,300 or eel rice ¥1,300 (October 2026) · evenings: kushiage, oden and sake (September 2026)
places.notes: [Udon · Minami-Horie, a big, generous Sanuki-style udon house] Much larger inside than the shopfront suggests, with a counter for solo diners, tables and tatami with sunken seating, this Minami-Horie udon house fills with families, couples, tourists and office workers at weekend lunch. The noodles are firm, chewy Sanuki-style, and you can take up to one and a half servings at no extra cost. Favourites include kakiage udon with two big fritters, a sudachi udon to which you add soy sauce, curry udon with chicken tempura or beef tendon, and duck-and-chicken paitan udon; lunch sets (until 14:00) add a bowl of rice such as takikomi or mentaiko. Evenings bring kushiage, oden and sake. Order on a tablet; food comes fast. Diners differ on the curry, which some found thin. Open daily.

places.notes: [Yakiniku · Amerikamura, charcoal wagyu with a smoker-friendly room] A small, calm yakiniku restaurant on the edge of Amerikamura, grilling kuroge wagyu over charcoal, quieter than the usual noisy yakiniku house (March 2026). The special cuts at ¥2,580 (outside skirt, tongue, brisket, ribeye) are the ones diners recommend, with a warning that the regular grades can be tough (March 2026); the horumon is glossy and fresh, from the five-kind platter to the signature horumon stew and raw omasum. Lunch brings set meals at gentler prices. A June 2026 diner found the owner and staff warm, and an August 2026 diner calls it popular with professional baseball players. Smoking is allowed at the tables. Courses were dropped from July (the site gives no year). Closed Mondays.

places.cuisine: Italian with the motto "affordable and delicious", from starters to pasta, with plenty of red, white and sparkling wine (Tabelog) · pasta lunch from ¥1,500 with a bagna cauda of roasted vegetables and a plate of starters (ratatouille, potato salad, roast duck, carpaccio, quiche, oysters), three pastas a day, e.g. shrimp and basil genovese, squid and nori peperoncino, scallop and gorgonzola cream, fresh fish and shiso genovese (October 2026); homemade mentaiko-cream tagliatelle ¥1,980 (April 2026); a premium lunch course · evening: prosciutto and strawberry with burrata, oysters with Kujo green onion in garlic oil, seafood carpaccio, Quattro Formaggi, fried yam with truffle, Caesar salad, carbonara, trippa, cheesecake, sangria (April–September 2026) · courses: party plan with pizza and pasta ¥3,980; Special course of six dishes ¥4,980; Premium course ¥5,980; two hours of drinks +¥2,200 (Tabelog, tax included)
places.notes: [Italian · Kitashinchi, a late-night Italian counter] A small, tiled-counter Italian restaurant in Kitashinchi, open since 2024 at lunch and then from 18:00 until 5:00 on weekdays, with the motto "affordable and delicious". The pasta lunch is the bargain: from ¥1,500 you get a bagna cauda of roasted vegetables, a plate of starters that may include oysters or roast duck, and one of three daily pastas, sometimes homemade tagliatelle (2026). At night the counter fills with wine drinkers over prosciutto with burrata and strawberries, oysters in garlic oil, fried yam with truffle and Quattro Formaggi, or courses from ¥3,980. One person cooks at lunch, so expect a short wait; one diner found it hard to get water on a busy night (September 2026). A 10% late-night charge applies after 22:00, and smoking is allowed in the evening.

chef_bio.background: Per the shop-maintained Tabelog listing: authentic Italian with the motto "affordable and delicious", from appetizers to pasta, open until 5:00; opened 17 June 2024. An April 2026 diner learned "the owner wants customers to enjoy a lot of food"; an October 2026 diner notes "it's a one-person operation" at lunch.
chef_bio.philosophy: "Affordable and Delicious" (Tabelog).
chef_bio.specialty: Pasta lunch with bagna cauda; fried yam with truffle.

anecdotes.text: "I expected a typical green salad with lettuce, but it turned out to be a delicious roasted vegetable bagna cauda!" — April 2026, homemade mentaiko cream pasta for JPY 1,980.

places.cuisine: One course crossing French, Italian and Japanese technique, built on rare ingredients, with drinks pairings (Tabelog) · IAKU course of ten dishes ¥23,100 including service; with a Japanese-chestnut Basque cheesecake to take home ¥26,340; lunch course of seven of its dishes ¥13,200 (Tabelog, tax included) · autumn 2026 courses: the signature Kagoshima black-wagyu fillet katsu roll to open, bonito or bluefin tartare with caviar and a yurinchi-sauce jelly on brioche, chawanmushi of lotus root (Kadoma), surf clam and sea urchin, sweetfish-pâté bisque or vichyssoise, cold noodles with hamo or hamo tempura with sudachi, Akashi sawara or grouper with saffron sauce, fillet steak with summer truffle and daikoku shimeji, Shine Muscat with stracciatella or burrata, lobster and matsutake rice, peach compote with homemade strawberry ice cream, a French blend tea (August–October 2026) · wine pairing, including two reds for one dish (September 2026)
places.notes: [Innovative · Kitashinchi, an eight-seat cross-genre counter] An eight-seat counter on a sixth floor in Kitashinchi, opened in 2022 and named a Tabelog French WEST 100 in 2025, where one course mixes French, Italian and Japanese technique around big, rich ingredients; a September 2026 diner says it is produced by Yuka Hattori of U.KAI. Everyone starts together, after the cook shows the day's cuts of wagyu, matsutake and lobster. The course opens with its signature, a Kagoshima wagyu fillet katsu sandwich, then caviar tartare on brioche, a sea-urchin chawanmushi, cold noodles with hamo, fish in saffron sauce, truffled fillet steak and a clay-pot rice of lobster and matsutake (autumn 2026). Diners call the portions generous. Lunch is ¥13,200 and dinner ¥23,100, the dinner price including service; give allergies when booking, not on the day.

roles: Producer: Yuka Hattori of U.KAI (per a September 2026 review)
chef_bio.background: Per the shop-maintained Tabelog listing: "beyond the boundaries of genre", dishes using techniques of French, Italian and Japanese cuisine; a dish of wild vegetables raw, boiled, grilled and fried; drinks pairings; Tabelog French WEST 100 2025; opened 1 September 2022. A September 2026 diner calls it "a casual innovative restaurant produced by Yuka Hattori from U.KAI".
chef_bio.philosophy: "Beyond the boundaries of genre" (Tabelog).
chef_bio.specialty: Wagyu fillet katsu roll; lobster and matsutake rice.

anecdotes.text: "Before the meal began, I was shown the large cuts of meat, matsutake mushrooms, and lobster that would be used in the course, which really whetted my appetite!" — September 2026, lunch with wine pairing.

"We started with the classic Kagoshima black-haired Wagyu fillet katsu roll, which was so tender that I finished it in one bite." — September 2026, a second visit after two and a half years.

places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: takoyaki is octopus in a dashi batter; teppan dishes of beef, pork and seafood.

places.cuisine: Takoyaki made with a rich dashi and teppan dishes of seasonal ingredients, with a large range of Japanese whisky at fair prices (Tabelog) · takoyaki, with salt among the options, and limited-time varieties (2024–26); an all-you-can-eat option where you make takoyaki yourself at a griddle on the table (October 2026) · okonomiyaki, buta-tama, negiyaki, akashiyaki (July 2024) · teppan: beef thigh, thick beef tongue, shrimp, scallop and asparagus, grilled vegetables (shiitake, manganji pepper, lotus root), dashimaki, garlic rice (2024–25) · a soft-boiled quail egg as the starter (2024–25)
places.notes: [Takoyaki · Kitashinchi, a takoyaki bar in an old snack bar] A small takoyaki and teppan bar up a flight of stairs in a Kitashinchi building, opened in October 2023 in what still looks like a retro snack bar, with sofa seats and takoyaki-shaped decor. Takoyaki made with a rich dashi come in several kinds, with salt among them and limited-time versions, alongside okonomiyaki, akashiyaki and teppan plates of beef tongue, seafood and vegetables, ending with garlic rice, and there is a cheap list of Japanese whisky. Regulars praise the soft-boiled quail-egg starter and a friendly owner; one October 2026 group cooked takoyaki at the table grill, all you can eat. Open until 3:00 on weekdays; smoking is allowed.

chef_bio.background: Per the shop-maintained Tabelog listing: takoyaki with a rich dashi and teppan dishes of seasonal ingredients, a large range of Japanese whisky, "a cozy retro interior open late into the night"; opened 10 October 2023. A November 2024 diner thought it had been a retro snack bar or lounge; a November 2025 diner calls the owner friendly.

anecdotes.text: "Enjoying different types of takoyaki while chatting with friends is truly the best part of Osaka's B-class gourmet scene." — October 2026, with a friend from Tokyo; an all-you-can-eat option lets you cook takoyaki at the table.
"The soft-boiled quail egg appetizer was incredibly delicious!!" — December 2025, a sixth stop on a business trip.
"Inside, you can still feel the remnants of a snack bar or lounge, making it quite a unique space for a takoyaki izakaya." — November 2024.

places.notes: [Tempura · Kitashinchi, tempura and champagne] A tempura counter on a third floor down a narrow Kitashinchi lane, opened in 2016 and on Tabelog's Tempura 100 lists for 2022 and 2023, built on pairing tempura with champagne chosen by its sommelier. The finish everyone talks about is tamago-kake-gohan with truffle shaved over it at the counter, or with sea urchin. Courses run ¥8,000 at lunch to ¥15,000, with a 5% service charge at dinner only. One regular on a 31st visit singled out a foie gras wrapped in beef and fried (September 2026). There are also sunken-kotatsu private rooms.

places.gf_detail: Not gluten-free in practice: takoyaki is a wheat batter, with sauce and soy-sauce toppings; no gluten-free option described.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: octopus takoyaki in a dashi batter, topped with bonito flakes.

Queues at peak times: about 15 minutes in October 2026, a long line at 17:00 in September 2026. Buy a ticket at the register and hand it over; self-service eat-in (August–September 2026). Cash only (Tabelog; October 2026 review). 40 seats: a counter of 12 and tables, plus 12 terrace seats on the riverside walk, and a cool eat-in floor below street level (Tabelog; September 2026); non-smoking; children welcome (Tabelog).

places.cuisine: Takoyaki cooked on a cast-iron plate rather than copper, for a thin crisp skin and a soft centre, with fresh, never-frozen octopus from the central market and sauce from the shop's own factory in Higashi-Osaka (Tabelog shop text) · 8 pieces ¥800 (October 2026); a September 2026 diner counted 9 pieces a plate · flavours: soy-sauce mayonnaise with free green onion, the most popular (Tabelog), sauce and mayonnaise, salt, ponzu, plain (2026 reviews) · takoyaki and a drink set ¥1,200, beer, Corona or a soft drink (August–October 2026) · free soft drinks for preschool children (October 2026) · sake and shochu
places.notes: [Takoyaki · Dotonbori riverside, until 2 or 3 a.m.] A takoyaki counter on the Dotonbori river walk, east of the Ebisubashi bridge and its Glico sign, that cooks on cast iron rather than copper so the balls come out with a thin crisp shell and a molten centre around a piece of fresh, never-frozen octopus. Order the soy-sauce mayo with green onion (the house favourite) or the classic sauce and mayo; 8 for ¥800, or ¥1,200 with a beer (October 2026). Buy a ticket at the register; eat on the riverside terrace, at the counter or in the cool room below. Expect a short queue in the evening; cash only; open from 9:00 to 2:00 or 3:00.

chef_bio.background: Per the Tabelog shop text: three commitments, to the cast-iron plate (harder to use than copper), to fresh octopus from the central market, never frozen, and to the dashi and a sauce made in the company's factory in Higashi-Osaka. A September 2026 diner first found it some 20 years earlier as a lesser-known stand and has since seen it gain long queues.
chef_bio.philosophy: Commitment to the iron plate, the octopus, and the dashi and sauce (Tabelog shop text).
chef_bio.specialty: Soy-sauce mayo takoyaki with green onion; cast-iron takoyaki.

anecdotes.text: "As a local, I was curious about the fact that these takoyaki are cooked on an old-fashioned teppan rather than copper … the outside was well-cooked, though not exactly crispy, while the inside remained wonderfully gooey." — October 2026.
"About 20 years ago … I discovered Acchichi Honpo and bought their takoyaki. I still can't forget the taste of their salt-flavored takoyaki." — September 2026.
"What I appreciated the most was that there were air-conditioned eat-in seats available on the basement floor." — September 2026, after a long line at 5 PM.

places.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information. The motsunabe comes in soy, miso or salt broth and finishes with ramen; the lunch has hamburg steak, beef katsu and menchi katsu; the stone-grilled wagyu is eaten with sesame and salt, but nothing is described as gluten-free.

places.notes: [Wagyu · Minamikyuhojimachi, a Showa row-house complex] A wagyu restaurant set in renovated Showa-era row houses between Shinsaibashi and Honmachi, where you are led through the lanes to tatami or sunken private rooms. Dinner is the stone grill of A5 black wagyu, which you cook yourself and eat wrapped in green onion with sesame and salt, followed by a motsunabe in soy, miso or salt and ramen to finish; the "Mahoroba" course of both is ¥4,730 (with a drinks option). Lunch is hamburg, beef katsu or the five-a-day Kaname Gozen (¥2,000 in October 2026). Popular for business dinners; book ahead.

chef_bio.background: Per the Tabelog shop text: a renovated Showa-era townhouse; A5 female black wagyu and the best meat available at the time; wines and local sake; fully private rooms for business meetings and anniversaries. A September 2026 diner was led through a passage to a separate building beside a private house.

anecdotes.text: "Limited to just 5 servings of this elusive bento. … featuring a generous 70g of Kuroge Wagyu steak" — October 2026, the Kaname Gozen for JPY 2,000.
"I enjoyed wrapping it in green onions and savoring it with sesame and salt, which allowed me to fully appreciate the flavor of the meat." — September 2026.

"Entering this extraordinary space, which feels like it's in the middle of Honmachi and Shinsaibashi, I was guided to a private room in a traditional Japanese house." — October 2026, the yakiniku course.

places.name: うな茂 (Una Shige)
places.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information. Kabayaki and the eel bowls are glazed in a soy-based tare; the premium kabayaki can be ordered white-grilled (shirayaki) without tare (official menu), but nothing is described as gluten-free.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: an eel restaurant; even the rolled omelette and the soup contain eel.
places.hours_raw: Mon–Fri 11:00–22:00; Sat 11:00–21:00; closed Sunday and holidays (Tabelog). Tabelog says no reservations, though a July 2026 diner phoned ahead on the Day of the Ox; full at lunch at weekends (August 2026). Bento and take-out of bowls, sets and dishes, sold outside the door at busy times (official site; July 2026). Cards (JCB, AMEX, Diners), PayPay and Rakuten Pay; no e-money (Tabelog). 40 seats: a counter, tables and a tatami room; non-smoking; children welcome (Tabelog). places.cuisine: Kansai-style eel, chosen for size and freshness and grilled without steaming, turned many times for a crisp outside and soft inside (official site) · prices from the official menu, tax included: Una Shige set ¥2,160 (eel bowl, uzaku, eel omelette, liver soup, pickles) · unagi set ¥3,530 (kabayaki with rice or as a bowl, uzaku, simmered liver, eel omelette, liver soup) · kabayaki set ¥5,220 (adds carp sashimi) · eel bowls 松 ¥3,960, 竹 ¥2,810, 梅 ¥1,820 · à la carte: premium kabayaki ¥3,240 (or white-grilled), regular kabayaki ¥2,120, yawata-maki ¥1,690, carp sashimi ¥830, simmered liver ¥770, fried bones ¥410, uzaku ¥1,410, grilled liver ¥830, eel omelette ¥770, eel-omelette bento ¥2,810 · hot pots in winter by reservation · beer ¥550
places.notes: [Unagi · Bakuromachi, Kansai-style eel at a fair price] A plain eel house in Bakuromachi, sister to the fugu restaurant ふぐ茂, that grills its eel the Kansai way, without steaming, turning it until the skin crisps. The Una Shige set (¥2,160) is the one regulars order every month: an eel bowl with an eel omelette the size of an inkstone box, uzaku and a rich liver soup; the ¥3,530 set adds kabayaki. Open all afternoon on weekdays, so it is easy outside the lunch rush, and the bowls and bento are sold to take away. One September 2026 diner waited over 20 minutes while the owner was on the phone; most 2026 visitors found it generous and good value. Closed Sundays.

chef_bio.background: Per the official site of ふぐ茂: うな茂 is the sister eel shop of the fugu and hamo restaurant ふぐ茂, grilling carefully chosen eel Kansai-style without steaming. It moved to its current address in August 2009 (Tabelog). A September 2026 diner waited over 20 minutes for an order while the owner talked on the phone at the counter.

anecdotes.text: "It was huge—almost the size of a suzuribako (inkstone)! The fluffy egg was packed with eel" — September 2026, the Una Shige set for JPY 2,160.
"I come here every month!" — October 2026, a fifth visit, the Una Shige set with its rich liver soup.
"They kindly served the grilled eel liver as an appetizer before the set meal arrived." — July 2026.

Reservations accepted, and often needed at peak times, though same-day calls and early walk-ins have found seats (2026 reviews); 2.5-hour limit (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners); no e-money or QR; no service charge (Tabelog). 70 seats over several floors, counter and tables, no private rooms; a fourth-floor bar (Tabelog; 2026 reviews); non-smoking (Tabelog).

places.cuisine: Seafood izakaya of a fish dealer with trading rights at the Eastern Market, which supplies more than 100 restaurants and fish shops (Tabelog shop text) · sashimi platters of five or seven kinds, e.g. seared sawara, bluefin tuna (2026) · simmered kinmedai, grilled kanpachi collar, grilled sawara, sanma in autumn · raw oysters, oysters with ponzu, octopus with ponzu · fried fugu, fried conger eel, corn tempura, kara-age · tuna Caesar salad, fluffy cream cheese, Manganji peppers, water eggplant · clam-dashi chazuke to finish · courses with free drinks (Tabelog) · Sapporo Lager Akaboshi, Carlsberg draft, sake and shochu
places.notes: [Seafood izakaya · Ura-Namba, the fishmonger's annex] The sit-down annex of 魚屋ひでぞう, the hard-to-book fishmonger's izakaya in Namba, round the corner in Ura-Namba, with seats over several floors. The fish comes from the company's own market business, so start with the sashimi platter (five or seven kinds), then simmered kinmedai, a grilled collar, oysters with ponzu or fried fugu, and the clam-dashi chazuke to finish. Prices are moderate: about ¥3,000–6,000 a head in 2026. Book, or try a same-day call or an early arrival at 17:00; stays are 2.5 hours. Closed Tuesdays.

chef_bio.background: Per the Tabelog shop text: Hidezou is a fish shop with rights to trade at the Eastern Market, supplying fresh seafood to over 100 restaurants and fish shops; the annex opened in Ura-Namba for people who cannot get a booking at Hidezo Namba. An August 2026 diner notes Hidezou has many branches; an October 2026 diner found its standing bar closed twice and came here instead.

anecdotes.text: "I hadn't made a reservation in advance, but on a whim, I called in the evening on the same day and was lucky enough to get a table." — October 2026, a fourth visit.
"The clam dashi chazuke had an amazing broth that made me want to have it again" — September 2026, a five-kind sashimi platter on the third floor.
"Some items took so long to serve that I wondered if they had been forgotten." — September 2026.

places.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information. Oden and clay-pot rice are cooked in a broth of chicken stock, bonito-kelp dashi, tomato and shiitake; lunches include fried horse mackerel and fried oysters.

places.cuisine: Oden and clay-pot rice, with cheap drinks (Tabelog) · oden in a broth of chicken stock, bonito-kelp dashi, tomato and shiitake, classic and creative: assorted five ¥1,078, "beautiful skin" oden ¥265 (September 2026) · clay-pot rice of chosen rice, cooked to order; the signature "oyakodon you must eat before you die", in a salt or soy version ¥2,398, with lemon to squeeze (September 2026) · small plates: cream cheese with black-bean honey as the starter ¥438, komatsuna and cream cheese with bonito soy ¥418, fresh kimchi with mizuna ¥528, taro kara-age ¥638, three obanzai ¥858, salt chicken wings ¥49 each (September 2026) · lunch: fried horse mackerel and fried oyster set ¥1,200 (August 2026), sweet shrimp chili (October 2026) · draft beer ¥219, mega mug ¥329, chuhai and highballs ¥329 (Tabelog)
places.notes: [Izakaya · Kitahorie, oden and clay-pot rice with your dog] A small second-floor izakaya in Kitahorie that welcomes dogs at the table, done up like a café with dried flowers, driftwood and a tiled counter. The cooking is oden in a broth of chicken stock, bonito-kelp dashi and tomato, and rice cooked to order in a clay pot; the dish to save room for is the oyakodon 'you must eat before you die', creamy egg over the pot rice, in salt or soy (¥2,398 in September 2026). Drinks are a bargain: draft beer ¥219, a mega mug ¥329, and salt chicken wings are ¥49 each. Lunch sets like fried horse mackerel and oysters run about ¥1,200. Diners in 2026 loved the staff, who even played 'wait' games with one guest's dog. English, Chinese and Korean menus.

chef_bio.background: Shop-maintained Tabelog listing: a dog-friendly izakaya of clay-pot rice from carefully selected rice from professional growers, oden in a broth made in-house from chicken stock, bonito and kelp, tomatoes and shiitake, and very cheap drinks; opened 5 December 2024.

anecdotes.text: "The first dish served was a cute monaka (wafer) shaped like a dog, sitting adorably." — September 2026.
"I was also surprised by the 'Umashio Teba (Delicious Salt Chicken Wings).' At just JPY 49 each, they were incredibly affordable" — September 2026.
"I even got to try the 'wait' challenge." — September 2026, dinner with a dog.

places.cuisine: Chinese tavern of Xi'an and Sichuan cooking, grilled fish, skewers and hot pot (Tabelog) · Xi'an biang biang noodles, said to be the longest in Japan, pulled by noodle chefs; spicy or not, in a bowl about 50 cm across (Tabelog; July–October 2026) · tomato and egg noodles; other noodle dishes can be made with biang biang noodles (2026 reviews) · dim sum and dishes with spices from the owner's home province, Sichuan, numbing and hot (Tabelog) · spicy poached white fish, lamb skewers, spring rolls, hot-and-sour soup dumplings, stir-fried pork lunch with a drink (2026 reviews) · frogs and crayfish on the menu (August 2026) · banquet course of 14 dishes with all-you-can-drink ¥5,000 Mon–Thu, ¥5,300 Fri–Sun, 25% off with a coupon (Tabelog); all-you-can-drink alone ¥1,650 (October 2025) · Qingdao and Harbin beer
places.notes: [Chinese · Shimanouchi, biang biang noodles until 2 a.m.] A Chinese tavern on Shimanouchi's street of Chinese and Korean restaurants, open from 11 a.m. to 2 a.m., built around Xi'an's biang biang noodles, a single long, wide, chewy noodle the shop calls the longest in Japan, served in a bowl about 50 cm across, spicy or mild. The owner is from Sichuan, so the rest of the menu runs to numbing, spicy dishes: poached white fish in chili, lamb skewers, hot-and-sour dumplings, and frogs and crayfish for the curious. Terracotta-warrior figures stand in the room. Diners who know China call it authentic; the spice is strong for some. Banquet courses with all-you-can-drink are ¥5,000–5,300, cheaper with a coupon. Smoking is allowed.

chef_bio.background: Shop-maintained Tabelog listing: a Chinese tavern of Xi'an and Sichuan cooking; biang biang noodles "rumored to be the longest in Japan", made by skilled noodle chefs; spices and herbs from the owner's hometown in Sichuan; many TV and media features. An August 2025 diner noted the staff were from abroad but understood Japanese; an August 2026 diner noticed terracotta-warrior figures in the room.
chef_bio.specialty: Biang biang noodles; spicy poached fish.

anecdotes.text: "The Biang Biang noodles are quite substantial. The bowl is about 50 cm in diameter" — October 2026, a weekend afternoon.
"Each bowl of Biang Biang Noodles contains only one type of noodle! Haha. Some parts are as soft as wontons, while others are similar to udon!" — July 2026.
"... thrilled to see the Terracotta Warriors displayed here." — August 2026, a second visit with a parent who loves the history of Xi'an.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ (店舗会員): 朋友雑穀食府 (パンユウザッコクショクフ)、中華・飲茶・串焼き、大阪市中央区島之内2-6-16 第２右田ビル １Ｆ、長堀橋駅から徒歩6分、毎日11:00〜翌2:00 (料理L.O.1:30)、予約可、カード・PayPay 可、33席 (テーブル)、4〜20名の個室と半個室、貸切20〜50名、喫煙可、英語・中国語・韓国語のメニュー、英語と中国語のスタッフ、写真つきメニュー、テイクアウト。店の紹介 (英訳): 西安と四川の料理、焼き魚、串、鍋の中国居酒屋、日本一長いといわれる西安のbiang biang の麺、オーナーの故郷の四川の香辛料と薬味、麻と辣、テレビなどで紹介、飲み放題つき14品の宴会コース (月〜木5,000円、金〜日5,300円、クーポンで25%引き)。口コミ(2025年8月〜2026年10月): biang biang の麺 (辛いのと辛くないの)、トマトと卵の麺、直径50cmほどの器、白身魚の激辛煮、羊肉の串、春巻、酸辣湯の餃子、豚肉の炒め物のランチ、カエルとザリガニ、terracotta warrior の飾り、本場の味、香辛料が強い、飲み放題1,650円、デリバリーの配達員が多い。

cultural_comfort.note: English menu and English- and Chinese-speaking staff (Tabelog); touch-panel ordering.

places.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information. Sushi with soy sauce, sesame-soy dressings and grilled dishes; a course included fried red-vinegar rice chips.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: sushi and fish dishes, with miso soup.

Reservations accepted (Tabelog). Starter ¥330 (Tabelog).
